picks.title: Divarasib as Compared with Sotorasib or Adagrasib in KRAS G12C-Mutated NSCLC.

sections.objective: Divarasib, a next-generation, oral KRAS G12C inhibitor, is more potent and selective in vitro than the first-generation KRAS G12C inhibitors sotorasib and adagrasib.
sections.methods: In this phase 3, international, open-label trial, patients with previously treated KRAS G12C-mutated advanced or metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) were randomly assigned to receive divarasib orally at a dose of 400 mg once daily or control treatment (sotorasib orally at a dose of 960 mg once daily or adagrasib orally at a dose of 600 mg twice daily) until the occurrence of disease progression, unacceptable adverse events, loss of clinical benefit, withdrawal of consent, death, or trial termination. The primary end point was progression-free survival as assessed by blinded independent central review. Secondary end points included overall survival, confirmed overall response, duration of response, patient-reported outcomes, and safety.
sections.results: A total of 338 patients received divarasib (167 patients) or control treatment (171 patients; 156 received sotorasib and 15 received adagrasib). The median follow-up was 14.3 months. The median progression-free survival was 9.8 months with divarasib and 5.7 months with control treatment (hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.58; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.44 to 0.76; P<0.001). The median overall survival was 17.7 months with divarasib and 12.0 months with control treatment (hazard ratio for death, 0.56; 95% CI, 0.41 to 0.78; P<0.001). Of the 328 patients who could be evaluated for response, a confirmed response occurred in 58.4% in the divarasib group and in 32.3% in the control group. The median duration of response was 11.9 months with divarasib and 6.9 months with control treatment. Fewer grade 3 or 4 treatment-related adverse events were noted with divarasib (24.6%) than with control treatment (34.5%).
sections.conclusion: Among patients with previously treated KRAS G12C-mutated advanced or metastatic NSCLC, divarasib led to significantly longer progression-free and overall survival than control treatment. (Supported by F. Hoffmann-La Roche; Krascendo 1 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06497556.).

picks.title: Osimertinib-Savolitinib in Advanced NSCLC after Progression during EGFR-TKI Therapy.

sections.objective: Savolitinib is an oral, potent, highly selective MET-tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI). Combination therapy with savolitinib and osimertinib, an epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-TKI, has shown activity in patients with EGFR-mutated, advanced non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with MET overexpression, MET amplification, or both, after progression during EGFR-TKI therapy.
sections.methods: In this international, phase 3, open-label trial, we randomly assigned, in a 1:1 ratio, patients with EGFR-mutated, locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC with MET overexpression (staining intensity of 3+ for MET in ≥90% of tumor cells on immunohistochemical analysis), MET amplification (≥10 gene copies on fluorescence in situ hybridization), or both whose disease had progressed during osimertinib therapy to receive osimertinib (at a dose of 80 mg once daily) plus savolitinib (300 mg twice daily) or intravenous platinum-pemetrexed. The primary end point was progression-free survival, as assessed by blinded independent central review. Secondary end points included overall survival and safety.
sections.results: Of the 1746 patients screened, 338 were randomly assigned to receive osimertinib-savolitinib (171 patients) or platinum-pemetrexed (167 patients). Osimertinib-savolitinib led to significantly longer progression-free survival than platinum-pemetrexed (hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.55; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.42 to 0.72; P<0.001), as well as significantly longer overall survival (hazard ratio for death, 0.68; 95% CI, 0.50 to 0.91; P = 0.01; final analysis). The Kaplan-Meier estimate of 12-month progression-free survival was 36% in the osimertinib-savolitinib group and 10% in the platinum-pemetrexed group, and the estimate of 12-month overall survival was 70% and 53%, respectively. The most frequently reported adverse events that occurred during treatment in the osimertinib-savolitinib group were peripheral edema (in 49% of the patients), anemia (in 26%), and diarrhea (in 26%). Grade 3 or higher adverse events during treatment were reported in 64% of the patients in the osimertinib-savolitinib group and in 63% of those in the platinum-pemetrexed group.
sections.conclusion: Osimertinib-savolitinib led to significantly longer progression-free and overall survival than platinum-pemetrexed among patients with EGFR-mutated, locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC with MET overexpression, MET amplification, or both that had progressed during osimertinib therapy (Funded by AstraZeneca; SAFFRON ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05261399.).

picks.title: A single-molecule spin–photon interface
picks.abstract: Optical interfaces that connect long-lived spin qubits to photons are a central requirement for quantum networking and distributed quantum information processing. At present, solid-state atomic defects are leading candidates because of their inherent spin and optical coherence1,2. Building on these advancements, synthetically tailored molecular systems represent a fundamental change in the field, using precise atomic control and consistent bottom-up assembly3,4. However, a molecular platform that concurrently satisfies the demands of a robust spin-photon interface-namely, the combination of bright fluorescence, high spectral stability and long ground-state spin lifetimes-has yet to be realized at the single-molecule level. Here we show that a triplet ground-state carbene molecule, embedded within a structurally matched host crystal, functions as a robust spin-photon interface with single-molecule addressability. The system exhibits narrow ZPLs, spectral stability over more than an hour, spin-selective optical transitions and single-molecule optically detected magnetic resonance. Coherent control yields millisecond-scale dynamical-decoupling coherence and tens-of-milliseconds spin relaxation at a temperature of 4.5 K. These results establish molecular qubits as a viable platform for single-emitter quantum optics5,6 while preserving the advantages of bottom-up chemical design7 and processable materials8-10.

picks.title: Emergence of Chern metal in a moiré Kondo lattice.
picks.abstract: A Chern metal is a two-dimensional metallic state of matter carrying chiral edge states. We report the observation of a Chern metal at the onset of the magnetic Kondo breakdown in a frustrated moiré Kondo lattice--angle-aligned MoTe2/WSe2 bilayers. The state is compressible and is manifested by a nearly quantized Hall resistance and a finite longitudinal resistance arising from a bad metallic bulk. We demonstrate the presence of a chiral edge state by nonlocal transport measurements and current-induced quantum anomalous Hall breakdown. Magnetic circular dichroism measurements further reveal a magnetization plateau for the Chern metal before a metamagnetic transition at the Kondo breakdown. Our results open an opportunity for moiré engineering of exotic quantum phases through the interplay between band topology and Kondo interactions.

picks.title: Impact of a large measles outbreak associated with transmission in the Americas and Canada's loss of measles elimination status: descriptive cohort study.

sections.objective: To describe the epidemiological characteristics, public health response, and evidence of international spread of a large measles outbreak that contributed to the loss of Canada's measles elimination status.
sections.methods: Descriptive analysis of the cohort of measles outbreak cases reported to Ontario's public health surveillance system during the outbreak period: epidemiological week of 28 October 2024 to 6 October 2025. Individuals meeting the outbreak case definition for confirmed or probable measles infection during the outbreak period.
sections.results: The outbreak consisted of 2377 cases (2064 confirmed and 313 probable) over 49 weeks and contributed to the loss of Canada's measles elimination status. Most cases (2146/2377, 90.3%) occurred among members of historically under-vaccinated communities, with limited spillover into the broader population. Among the 2377 cases, approximately three quarters of cases (n=1736, 73.0%) occurred in individuals aged 19 years or younger, 2121 (89.2%) were unvaccinated, and 97 (4.1%) had unknown vaccination status. The outbreak was associated with 166 (7%) admissions to hospital, 13 (<1%) admissions to intensive care unit, 51 (2.1%) infections during pregnancy, 10 (<1%) congenital measles infections, one (<1%) case of encephalitis, and one (<1%) infant death. Sequencing identified a novel N450 distinct sequence identifier that was subsequently detected in countries including the United States of America, Mexico, and the Netherlands. The outbreak strain was designated a World Health Organization named strain (MVs/Ontario.CAN/47.24).
sections.conclusion: These findings highlight the risk of measles re-establishment in countries that have attained elimination and underscore the importance of culturally appropriate community engagement to build trust in immunisation and prevent future outbreaks. This outbreak shows the fragility of measles elimination in the presence of long standing immunity gaps within interconnected communities across the Americas and the population-level protection that limited broader community transmission.
sections.other: Ontario, Canada. Exposure to measles virus associated with the Ontario outbreak and related transmission chains. Demographic characteristics, vaccination status, admission to hospital, complications, pregnancy associated outcomes, mortality, and evidence of international spread based on measles virus genotyping and sequencing. Cases were identified using an outbreak-specific case definition incorporating epidemiological, clinical, laboratory, and viral sequencing criteria. Phylogenetic analysis of measles virus sequences was used to assess evidence of onwards spread to other countries.

picks.title: An mRNA-lipid nanoparticle vaccine against H5N1 influenza virus protects lactating dairy cows from infection.
picks.abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 virus has recently emerged in dairy cattle in the USA, leading to mastitis and sharp reductions in milk production. The main site of H5N1 viral replication is the mammary tissue rather than the respiratory tract and viral transmission between animals is thought to occur through viral shedding in milk. Here, we generate an mRNA-lipid nanoparticle (mRNA-LNP) vaccine encoding the hemagglutinin (HA) of A/dairy cattle/Texas/24-008749-002/2024, representative of circulating bovine H5N1 viruses, and assess its immunogenicity and efficacy in lactating dairy cows. Eight cows were divided into vaccinated and control groups, receiving two intramuscular doses of the vaccine or saline, followed by intramammary viral challenge. Vaccination elicited HA-reactive and neutralizing antibodies in serum and HA-reactive antibodies in milk. Following viral challenge, vaccinated cows had ~1,000-fold lower peak viral RNA in milk and a lower occurrence of mastitis and mammary fibrosis.

picks.title: Prone positioning and high-frequency oscillatory ventilation in early paediatric acute respiratory distress syndrome (PROSpect): an international, two-by-two factorial, response-adaptive, phase 3, randomised controlled trial.

sections.objective: Data on prone positioning and high-frequency oscillatory ventilation (HFOV) used separately or in combination in patients with paediatric acute respiratory distress syndrome (PARDS) are inconclusive, leading to wide practice variability. We aimed to compare the effects of prone positioning with supine positioning and the effects of HFOV with conventional mechanical ventilation on ventilator-free days in children with early, moderate-to-severe PARDS.
sections.methods: PROSpect was an international, two-by-two factorial, response-adaptive, phase 3, randomised controlled trial done in 75 paediatric intensive care units in 18 countries. Eligible patients were aged 2 weeks to 20 years, and were intubated and mechanically ventilated for less than 96 h before meeting criteria for moderate-to-severe PARDS. Patients were centrally randomly assigned using a web-based system to supine positioning and conventional mechanical ventilation, prone positioning and conventional mechanical ventilation, supine positioning and HFOV, or prone positioning and HFOV. Initially, the allocation was 1:1:1:1 stratified by age group and direct or indirect lung injury using a permuted block design with blocks of four and eight. Response-adaptive randomisation updates were planned to adjust allocation probabilities 28 days after 300 patients were randomly assigned and then 28 days after every 100 additional patients. Given the nature of the interventions, masking was not possible. The primary outcome was ventilator-free days through to day 28 among all randomly assigned participants. Safety was assessed prospectively by daily monitoring for the occurrence of prespecified adverse events. This study was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03896763) and is closed to enrolment.
sections.results: Between May 1, 2019 and Jan 13, 2026, 1045 patients were eligible for enrolment. The trial was stopped early for futility and slow enrolment after 424 of 600 planned patients were recruited. 126 patients were randomly assigned to the supine and conventional mechanical ventilation group, 130 to the prone and conventional mechanical ventilation group, 90 to the supine and HFOV group, and 78 to the prone and HFOV group. Median age was 3·3 years (IQR 1·1-10·1), 211 (50%) patients were female, and 213 (50%) were male. There were no significant differences in ventilator-free days between prone and supine positioning (median 17·9 days [IQR 8·9-21·3] vs 17·4 days [6·4-21·9]; Hodges-Lehmann location shift adjusting for ventilation 0·0 [95% CI -0·8 to 1·0]) or between HFOV and conventional mechanical ventilation (17·3 [5·7-21·6] vs 18·0 [9·9-21·5]; Hodges-Lehmann location shift adjusting for positioning -0·3 [95% CI -1·5 to 0·5]). 41 (10%) patients had died at day 28, without group differences. Plugging or obstruction of the artificial airway occurred more frequently with prone than supine positioning (14 events in 12 [6%] of 188 patients vs three events in three [2%] of 197 patients; 0·74 [95% CI 0·44-1·26] vs 0·15 [0·05-0·47] events per 100 artificial airway days; rate ratio 4·83 [95% CI 1·38-16·82]). Stage 2 or worse immobility-related pressure injuries also occurred more frequently with prone versus supine positioning (12 [6%] vs two [1%]; relative risk 6·13 [95% CI 1·45-25·97]). Haemodynamic instability occurred more frequently with HFOV than conventional mechanical ventilation (41 events in 19 [13%] of 141 patients vs 38 events in 22 [9%] of 244 patients; 2·21 [95% CI 1·63-3·00] vs 1·22 [0·89-1·68] events per 100 paediatric intensive care unit days; rate ratio 1·84 [95% CI 1·18-2·87]). One serious adverse event, an unwitnessed self-extubation followed by cardiopulmonary arrest, occurred in a patient in the prone and conventional mechanical ventilation group.
sections.conclusion: We found no evidence to support prone positioning or HFOV as first-line strategies to improve ventilator-free days in patients with early, moderate-to-severe PARDS. Thus, the routine use of these strategies in this population is not recommended.

picks.title: Genetic coupling of floral rewards and signals underlies pollinator attraction.
picks.abstract: Animal pollinators underpin biodiversity and global agriculture, yet the molecular mechanisms that coordinate floral rewards and signals to attract pollinators remain poorly understood. Through phenotyping melon genetic diversity, we identified nectarless1 (nls1), encoding the YABBY-family transcription factor YABBY5 (YAB5), as a central integrator of pollinator-attracting traits. YAB5 interacts with CRABS CLAW (CRC) during nectary initiation to specify nectary identity by repressing alternative floral organ fates. As flowers mature, YAB5 directly activates 4-α-glucanotransferase 2 (DPE2) to promote starch remobilization required for nectar secretion and promotes petal growth and flower opening. In petals, YAB5 directly engages an MYB111-dependent flavonoid pathway that generates UV nectar guides, while indirectly influencing floral volatile emission. Disrupting YAB5, DPE2, or MYB111 reduces pollinator visitation. Together, these findings reveal how a developmental regulator couples organ specification with organ-specific metabolic programs to synchronize floral rewards and signals at anthesis.

items.title: Reframing the manosphere: a public health response to a commercial ecosystem.
items.abstract: The manosphere, a diffuse commercial ecosystem and loose collection of online communities united by shared beliefs about masculinity, misogyny, and male victimisation, is an under-recognised determinant of health harms. This network has been implicated in considerable health harms: widespread mental health impacts, especially in young people; violence against women, girls, and gender minorities; and delegitimising help-seeking in boys and men. In this Viewpoint, we argue that the manosphere is best understood and addressed as a public health problem.

items.title: Charting a course to men's health and wellbeing: applying a lens of power and politics to improve men's health outcomes.
items.abstract: Despite long-standing evidence of poor health and life expectancy outcomes among men, particularly among men who are socially or structurally marginalised, men's health has generally received little and uneven attention in health policy and practice. Its gendered and intersectional aspects have been especially overlooked. This third paper in the Lancet Men's Health Series examines why men's health has received so little policy attention and proposes strategies to raise men's health on national and global agendas. We applied a gender lens to the 3-i theory-based framework and analysed how ideas, interests, and institutions shape the prioritisation of men's health within national and global policy agendas. We review the modest development of men's health policies and assess how power and politics, including the roles of a range of stakeholders from global and national health spaces, commercial actors, and civil society organisations, have shaped the construction of the problem as well as policy attention and framing, resource allocation, and interventions. The scarcity of attention paid to men's health on global and national agendas reflects how power operates through ideas and institutions which contribute to the conflation of gender with women, institutional inertia, and contested constructions of individual versus structural drivers of ill health. We highlight how this has created a space in which commercial actors, including the manosphere, can shape narratives and influence men's health in ways that align with commercial or ideological interests. We conclude by proposing politically informed strategies that recognise how power, institutional arrangements, and competing interests shape men's health policy within prevailing gender and structural orders. We identify entry points for advancing men's health equity and wellbeing that draw on empirical evidence and technical guidance, are grounded in political realities, and are consistent with a commitment to gender justice for all people.

items.title: A global men's health epidemiology within an intersectional framework.
items.abstract: Males have lower life expectancies and greater disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) than females, and particularly poor outcomes are seen among males in marginalised contexts. In this paper, we provide an epidemiological overview and highlight the intersectional nature of men's health. We analyse mortality and DALYs data from the 1990-2023 Global Burden of Diseases, Injuries, and Risk Factors Studies to illustrate our intersectional framework and draw attention to how health varies in men and to show key themes. Conditions that contribute most to the poor health of males include non-communicable diseases (eg, cardiovascular diseases and cancers), substance use, suicide, injuries (eg, road traffic incidents and interpersonal violence), and respiratory infections (eg, tuberculosis and COVID-19). Although cardiovascular disease and cancer make the largest contributions to men's higher mortality rates, determinants of health such as violence and war, migration, economic stagnation, and labour market changes due to automation and new technologies will disproportionally affect their health in the future. Injuries, violence, and other external morbidity causes often occur at a young age and in unequal distributions across the sexes, making a large contribution to DALYs. Although biology plays a role, the pattern of many diseases contributing to health differences reflects the intersection of health behaviours, shaped by patriarchy, ideas of masculinity, and structural drivers (including commercial determinants of health); many of these are preventable. Although improvements in some health behaviours are seen, exceptions occur in marginalising social conditions (eg, incarcerated men, men experiencing homelessness, men with mental illnesses, men with substance use disorders, men with low income, men who have sex with men, and those who are gender non-conforming). Multiple data sources detail men's shorter life expectancies and the drivers compared with women, but going beyond sex disaggregation remains challenging and is an urgent priority for research and health monitoring.

items.title: Men's health: an intersectional and multilevel framework for understanding syndemic patterns of health.
items.abstract: Men occupy a privileged position within gender power relations: the male body has been the default reference point for biomedical research and therapeutic development (with the historical exclusion of women from medical trials), and men dominate health services leadership and exercise well documented medical misogyny. Yet despite their privileged position, many aspects of men's health outcomes are neglected and undertheorised because they are not examined through an intersectional gender lens. Although consideration of gender and masculinity is important for understanding men's health, research thus far has focused predominantly on men's harmful health behaviours, overemphasising individual determinants of health, and a deficit-based approach. Little attention has been paid to the influence of structural determinants of men's health risks and vulnerabilities, or the gender-specific health outcomes of worsening social and economic inequalities. In this first paper of a Lancet Series on men's health, we present a conceptual framework for understanding men's health from an intersectional perspective, highlighting how structural, social, and commercial determinants of health, intersectionality, and syndemic theory can be combined to analyse men's health at different socioecological levels. We illustrate the framework using four selected case studies that show how the health outcomes of marginalised men are influenced by complex interactions. We provide a working definition of men's health that reflects existing literature and builds on the conceptual framework and case studies. Promotion of gender justice and health equity requires moving beyond one-dimensional approaches that construct men as problematic individuals, and towards better understanding and action on the broader set of power systems and structural determinants underpinning men's health.

items.title: Non-invasive tests in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: the LITMUS prospective multicentre diagnostic accuracy study.

sections.objective: The advent of regulatory-approved pharmacological treatments for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) calls for precise, non-invasive biomarkers that facilitate early diagnosis, support therapy selection, and aid clinical trial enrolment. The European multicentre LITMUS study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of a broad range of non-invasive biomarkers for identifying patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), at-risk MASH, advanced fibrosis, and cirrhosis.
sections.methods: In this prospective, multicentre, diagnostic accuracy study, adults with biopsy-confirmed MASLD were prospectively recruited across 13 countries in Europe and the USA. We assessed 12 single markers and 18 multimarker panels. The reference standard was centrally scored liver histology according to the non-alcoholic steatohepatitis Clinical Research Network Scoring System. Target conditions included MASH (Non-Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease Activity Score ≥4 with ≥1 point per component), at-risk MASH (MASH plus significant fibrosis [fibrosis stage F≥2]), advanced fibrosis (F≥3), and cirrhosis (F4). Performance was evaluated by area-under-the-receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), with the minimum acceptable criterion (MAC) of AUC higher than 0·80 to indicate potential biopsy replacement.
sections.results: Between Jan 1, 2018, and June 30, 2023, we analysed data from 1590 participants with centrally scored liver biopsies and at least one biomarker measurement; 609 (38%) had biopsy-confirmed at-risk MASH, 678 (43%) had MASH, 585 (37%) had advanced fibrosis, and 164 (10%) had cirrhosis. For detecting at-risk MASH, SomaSignal showed the highest diagnostic performance (AUC 0·83 [95% CI 0·80-0·85]), significantly exceeding MAC, whereas no other test reached the MAC for MASH only. For advanced fibrosis, SomaSignal showed the highest performance (AUC 0·92 [0·90-0·94]), followed by FibroMeter-VCTE (AUC 0·87 [0·83-0·92]), Agile 3+ and TSP2 (both AUC 0·84 [0·82-0·86]), and NIS4 (0·82 [0·80-0·85]). For cirrhosis, FibroMeter-VCTE showed the highest diagnostic performance (AUC 0·94 [0·90-0·97]) followed by SomaSignal (AUC 0·92 [0·90-0·94]), followed by Agile 3+ (0·88 [0·85-0·91]), Agile 4 (0·87 [0·84-0·90]), ADAPT (0·85 [0·81-0·88]), and ELF, LSM-VCTE, and TSP2 (all 0·84 [0·81-0·87]). Sequential two-step approaches using gamma-glutamyl transferase as a first-line test met the MAC for both advanced fibrosis and at-risk MASH.
sections.conclusion: Although single markers resulted in variable and limited performance when compared to histology for detecting at-risk MASH, multimarker panels showed great potential, with a proteomic panel showing strong diagnostic performance. These findings could support the selection and implementation of non-invasive testing strategies in MASLD and inform future clinical guidelines, regulatory evaluation, and clinical trial design.

items.title: Effect of Endostaple Configuration and Oversizing on Endograft Displacement Force: An In Vitro Evaluation of the Aortoseal Endostapling System.

sections.objective: Proximal endograft fixation remains a key determinant of long-term durability of endovascular aortic repair (EVAR). The Aortoseal Endostapling system consists of a nitinol frame with 6 welded endostaples at the proximal end, intended to enhance fixation and seal of an endograft by mimicking the hand-sewn anastomosis of open aortic repair. This study evaluates the effect of different distributions of activated endostaples on endograft displacement force (EDF), while considering various endograft oversizing options.
sections.methods: An in vitro silicone tube model was used to assess EDF at 2 mm endograft displacement and pull-out force across 11 activated staple configurations of the Aortoseal Endostapling system with 10%, 20%, and 30% endograft oversizing. Interobserver agreement was assessed using the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC), based on a 2-way mixed-effects model for absolute agreement.
sections.results: Intraclass correlation coefficient for interobserver agreement was 0.987. Endograft displacement force ranged from 8.8 N ± 0.15 N to 39.6 N ± 2.96 N across all configurations and oversizing conditions. Incorporation of the Aortoseal frame alone, without staple activation, substantially increased EDF compared with no Aortoseal frame at 10% and 20% oversizing. Furthermore, EDF was mostly influenced by the number of activated staples and the maximum unstapled circumferential angle (MUCA). The 6-activated-staple configuration consistently yielded the highest EDF. The effect of oversizing on EDF was inconsistent across configurations at 10% and 20%, whereas 30% oversizing was associated with lower EDF in most configurations. Pull-out force exceeded EDF in all tested configurations except the 1-activated-staple configuration.
sections.conclusion: In this in vitro study, Aortoseal frame incorporation alone substantially increased EDF relative to the graft-only configuration at 10% and 20% oversizing. Ten percent endograft oversizing yielded EDF values comparable with 20% oversizing across most configurations. Circumferential staple distribution was the primary determinant of EDF in the Aortoseal Endostapling system, with EDF decreasing with increasing MUCA and increasing with staple number across all endograft oversizing conditions, consistent with circumferential load sharing as a potential underlying mechanism. These findings may serve as a mechanistic reference framework for preoperative planning in anatomically challenging cases and warrant further experimental and clinical evaluation.Clinical ImpactThe Aortoseal Endostapling system (Endoron Medical Holdings Ltd., Dublin, Ireland) represents a novel approach to proximal endograft fixation, enabling simultaneous circumferential single-stage activation of 6 nitinol endostaples via balloon activation, providing a uniform and reproducible fixation pattern intended to mimic the longitudinal and radial anchoring of a surgical anastomosis. To support clinical implementation, this study systematically evaluated endograft displacement force across a range of activated staple configurations, including suboptimal deployment scenarios. The findings provide physicians with a mechanistic reference framework for preoperative planning, supporting procedural decision-making in anatomically challenging cases.

items.title: Five-Year Prognostic Outcomes After Paclitaxel-Coated Balloon Treatment According to Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischaemia Status: Insights From the BIOLUX P-III Registry.

sections.objective: Chronic limb-threatening ischaemia (CLTI) carries a high risk of death, limb loss, and impaired functional recovery despite revascularisation. Drug-coated balloons may reduce restenosis and repeat intervention after infrainguinal endovascular therapy, but long-term safety and effectiveness data in patients with CLTI remain limited.
sections.methods: We performed a prespecified subgroup analysis of BIOLUX P-III, a prospective international post-market all-comers registry evaluating the Passeo-18 Lux paclitaxel-coated balloon for infrainguinal peripheral artery disease. Outcomes were compared between patients with and without CLTI through 60 months. Endpoints included freedom from major adverse events, clinically driven target-lesion revascularisation, major target-limb amputation, amputation-free survival and all-cause mortality. Time-to-event outcomes were analysed using Kaplan-Meier methods. Because follow-up completeness declined substantially by 60 months, late estimates were interpreted in the context of censoring, attrition and competing mortality.
sections.results: Among 877 treated patients, 328 (37.4%) had CLTI. Technical success exceeded 98% in both groups. Patients with CLTI had greater baseline comorbidity, more advanced limb threat and more frequent below-the-knee disease. At 60 months, freedom from clinically driven target-lesion revascularisation was 85.3% in patients with CLTI and 78.3% in those without CLTI (P = .59), and freedom from major adverse events was similar (76.5% vs 74.3%; P = .13). In contrast, 5-year survival was substantially lower in patients with CLTI (47.9% vs 76.7%; P < .001). Freedom from major target-limb amputation was lower (93.3% vs 99.3%; P < .001), and amputation-free survival was reduced (47.1% vs 75.7%; P < .001). Patients with CLTI received a lower cumulative paclitaxel dose despite higher mortality.
sections.conclusion: Passeo-18 Lux treatment was associated with preserved lesion-level durability through 5 years, but CLTI identified a high-risk prognostic phenotype with poor survival and limb outcomes. These findings suggest that long-term outcomes in CLTI are influenced by systemic comorbidity, early limb vulnerability, competing mortality and wound-related factors beyond lesion-level device performance alone.Clinical ImpactThis study provides clinically relevant insights into the long-term outcomes of patients with chronic limb-threatening ischaemia (CLTI) undergoing endovascular revascularisation with drug-coated balloons. Despite high procedural success, patients with CLTI experience substantially greater long-term mortality and adverse limb outcomes than those with intermittent claudication. These findings highlight the importance of recognising CLTI as a high-risk clinical phenotype requiring comprehensive cardiovascular risk reduction, multidisciplinary management, and structured postprocedural surveillance. The study's principal contribution is its evaluation of five-year outcomes in a real-world, all-comers population, providing valuable evidence to inform patient counselling, individualised treatment strategies, and long-term clinical decision-making.

items.title: Preoperative Imaging-Derived Factors Associated With Spinal Cord Ischemia After Fenestrated and Branched Endovascular Aortic Repair-A Scoping Review.

sections.objective: Spinal cord ischemia (SCI) after fenestrated and branched endovascular aortic repair (F/B-EVAR) is a devastating complication with a non-negligible incidence, and better risk prediction is necessary. Preoperative imaging allows assessment of anatomical and morphological characteristics that may predispose to SCI. This scoping review aimed to systematically search the literature and provide an overview of the current evidence on the association of preoperative imaging-derived factors with SCI after F/B-EVAR.
sections.methods: This scoping review was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) guidelines. A systematic literature search of PubMed, EMBASE, Cochrane, and Web of Science was performed from database inception to October 21, 2025, to identify studies that reported on the association of preoperative imaging-derived factors with SCI following F/B-EVAR. Only studies published in English were included. Studies were screened by 2 reviewers, and data were charted using a standardized data-extracting form. Identified factors were categorized as aortic-related, aortic side-branch-related, thrombus-related, and miscellaneous factors.
sections.results: A total of 2231 studies were identified, and 45 were included in this scoping review. Included studies consisted of observational cohort studies and nonrandomized investigational device exemption studies, with all studies using univariable and multivariable analyses. A total of 18 imaging-derived factors were identified and categorized into aortic-related (33 studies), aortic side-branch-related (17 studies), thrombus-related (5 studies), and miscellaneous (psoas muscle parameters, median arcuate ligament [MAL]) (6 studies). Aneurysm extent, maximum aortic diameter, and rupture were the most frequently reported investigated factors. Most (n = 39, 87%) studies were performed in cohorts of less than 400 patients. Definitions of similar investigated factors varied, and associations found were variable across studies. Only a limited number of included studies performed a multivariable analysis.
sections.conclusion: This scoping review provides a categorized overview of preoperative imaging-derived factors and their associations with SCI after F/B-EVAR. Identified factors showed heterogeneous associations and inconsistent definitions across studies limited comparability. Large prospective cohort studies, including standardized definitions of parameters, are needed to investigate the influence of preoperative imaging-derived factors on the risk of SCI.Clinical ImpactSpinal cord ischemia (SCI) after fenestrated and branched endovascular aortic repair remains a significant complication despite continual advancements in preventive strategies and identification of clinical risk factors. Preoperative imaging allows assessment of anatomical and morphological characteristics that may predispose to SCI. This scoping review provides a categorized overview of preoperative imaging-derived factors and the evidence on their association with SCI. Identified factors had varying definitions and showed heterogeneous associations with SCI. Recommendations for future research are outlined to further optimize SCI risk prediction using preoperative imaging-derived factors.

items.title: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Determinants of Bowel Ischemia and Associated Risk After Elective Endovascular Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Repair.

sections.objective: Bowel ischemia (BI) is an uncommon but devastating complication of elective endovascular abdominal aortic aneurysm repair (EVAR). We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to identify patient- and procedure-related risk factors for BI after elective EVAR.
sections.methods: We searched PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature, Cochrane Library, Scielo, and Lilacs from database inception through March 31, 2024, without language or date restrictions. We included observational studies of adults who underwent elective EVAR and reported postoperative BI and extractable risk-factor data. Two reviewers independently screened titles, abstracts, and full texts, extracted data, and assessed study quality using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. For factors reported in multiple sufficiently homogeneous studies, random-effects meta-analysis was used to pool risk ratios (RRs) or mean differences (MDs), with heterogeneity assessed using I2.
sections.results: Twenty-three retrospective cohort studies, including 306 344 elective EVAR procedures, met the inclusion criteria, and 10 provided sufficient data for quantitative synthesis. Across all studies, 1535 patients developed postoperative BI, corresponding to an overall incidence of approximately 0.5%. Female sex was associated with increased BI risk (RR, 2.66; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.06-3.43; I2 = 0%). Larger aneurysm diameter was also associated with increased risk (MD, 4.05 mm; 95% CI, 0.09-8.02; I2 = 0%). Renal dysfunction was a consistent predictor, with chronic kidney disease (RR, 2.93; 95% CI, 1.01-8.47; I2 = 29%) and dialysis dependence (RR, 5.35; 95% CI, 2.38-12.05; I2 = 0%) associated with BI. Major intraoperative blood loss >1 L conferred the highest relative risk among pooled factors (RR, 7.45; 95% CI, 2.80-19.85; I2 = 0%). Age, systemic arterial hypertension, and active smoking were not significantly associated with BI in pooled analyses.
sections.conclusion: Bowel ischemia after elective EVAR is uncommon but clinically important because delayed recognition carries substantial morbidity and mortality. Female sex, larger aneurysm diameter, chronic kidney disease, dialysis dependence, and major blood loss identify patients who may warrant heightened perioperative vigilance. The certainty of evidence remains very low, and future studies should standardize reporting of bowel segment, mesenteric vessel involvement, inferior mesenteric artery and internal iliac artery status, endograft configuration, and overlapping registry populations.Clinical RelevanceBowel ischemia after elective endovascular abdominal aortic aneurysm repair (EVAR) is rare, but its low incidence should not be interpreted as low clinical importance because delayed diagnosis is often catastrophic. This systematic review and meta-analysis synthesizes the largest available elective EVAR evidence focused on bowel ischemia and identifies reproducible risk signals, including female sex, aneurysm size, renal dysfunction, dialysis dependence, and major blood loss. The practical gain for readers is not a definitive prediction score, but a clearer framework for perioperative judgment: recognize vulnerable patients, avoid overinterpreting weak or non-poolable associations, and apply heightened postoperative vigilance when embolic, hypoperfusion, pelvic collateral, or renal-risk features coexist.

items.title: Citrulline Supplementation Improves Aortic Vasodilation and Prevents Aortic Thickening Only in Female Rats.

sections.objective: Aging is associated with endothelial dysfunction and vascular remodeling, partly due to reduced nitric oxide (NO) bioavailability. l-citrulline, a precursor of l-arginine and NO synthesis, has been proposed as a therapeutic strategy to improve vascular function. This study evaluated the effects of chronic citrulline supplementation on aortic structure and vasodilatory function in adult male and female rats.
sections.methods: Eight-month-old male and female Sprague-Dawley rats were randomly assigned to control or treatment groups. The treated animals received oral malate citrulline (1 g/kg/d) for 12 weeks. We isolated thoracic aortas for histological and morphometric analyses, including tunica media thickness and intima/media ratio. We assessed vascular reactivity in vitro using isolated aortic rings in an organ bath system, measuring acetylcholine (ACh)-induced relaxation following phenylephrine-induced contraction.
sections.results: Citrulline supplementation significantly improved ACh-induced vasorelaxation in female rats compared with female controls (55.14% ± 4.8% vs 42.4% ± 4.3%, P < .05. No differences in vasorelaxation were observed in males between the treated and control groups. Histological analyses showed that treated females had less disruption of elastic fibers and a thinner minimal intima than controls, whereas males showed no structural differences.
sections.conclusion: Citrulline supplementation improves endothelium-dependent vasodilation and may preserve aortic structural integrity in female rats but not in males. These findings suggest a sex-dependent vascular response to citrulline, potentially mediated by differences in NO signaling and hormonal regulation. Citrulline may represent a therapeutic strategy to improve vascular function during aging, particularly in females.
sections.other: The findings may guide clinical trials investigating how hormonal status and nitric oxide signaling affect the efficacy of citrulline supplementation in female patients. Ultimately, these insights could establish citrulline as a targeted, preventive intervention to preserve aortic structural integrity and reduce cardiovascular disease risk in the aging female population.

items.title: Super-resolution mapping of nuclear stress signaling by probiotic-derived extracellular vesicles in UV-induced skin photodamage.
items.abstract: Ultraviolet (UV)-induced photodamage drives oxidative stress, DNA damage, and chronic inflammation, leading to progressive cellular ultrastructure and skin function degeneration. Despite the potential of probiotics as anti-photodamage agents, their nanoscale action mechanism remains unexplored. Here, we utilize super-resolution fluorescence microscopy to investigate the cellular and molecular basis of Lactobacillus plantarum-derived extracellular vesicles (L. plantarum EVs) in mitigating photodamage. We showed that UV irradiation triggered extensive organellar remodeling along with elevated reactive oxygen species production, DNA damage signaling, and inflammatory activation. Remarkably, pre- and posttreatment with L. plantarum EVs preserved organelle integrity and restored native nanoscale architecture. Additionally, EV treatment delayed UV-induced PARP-1 activation and nuclear condensate clustering, while suppressing NF-κB translocation and downstream inflammatory cytokine expression. These findings establish probiotic-derived EVs as modulators of stress-responsive signaling and structural homeostasis during UV-induced photodamage. By providing a super-resolution mechanistic framework for understanding probiotic EV-mediated modulation of cellular photodamage responses, this study provides a basis for future investigation of EV-based strategies for skin protection.

items.title: Transcriptional and functional profiling reveals a dynamic continuum of beta-cell activation states.
items.abstract: A central question is whether beta-cells respond uniformly to glucose. Using phospho-S6 as an activation marker, this study shows that beta-cells are recruited sequentially as glucose concentrations increase. Recruitment is spatially organized, with high-threshold cells predominantly located in the islet core. Transcriptomic profiling indicates functional heterogeneity among beta-cells. A low-threshold subset is characterized by enhanced stress resilience necessary for sustained secretion. An intermediate subset, enriched for calcium-signaling and vesicle-excitatory genes, modulates postprandial glucose excursions. The high-threshold subset specializes in high-capacity protein synthesis and insulin secretion to manage glucose peaks. Single-cell RNA sequencing reveals that these functional subsets form a continuous spectrum rather than discrete subpopulations. This division of labor is adaptable; under high-fat diet-induced metabolic demand, islets undergo remodeling with a global reduction in activation thresholds and a shift toward high-capacity profiles. Collectively, these findings identify a beta-cell hierarchy that balances metabolic resilience with secretory demand to maintain glucose homeostasis.

items.title: Monolithic and scalable capacitive electrodes leveraging parasitic capacitance for full-body pressure mapping.
items.abstract: Scaling capacitive pressure sensor arrays to large areas remains challenging due to electrode alignment errors, fabrication complexity, and limited dynamic range inherent in conventional parallel-plate architectures. Here, we present a scalable capacitive pressure sensor array based on a monolithic electrode architecture, where transmitter and receiver electrodes are co-integrated into a single substrate. A deformable dielectric and a floating ground (GND) layer are positioned above, eliminating alignment errors and reducing the layer-stacking process by 20%. The parasitic capacitance between the electrodes and GND layer is intentionally incorporated into the sensing mechanism, enabling stable pressure detection with effective electromagnetic interference shielding. The resulting 2911-cell array (1.7 m by 1.0 m) achieves 30 Hz full-body pressure mapping with high linearity (R2 = 0.994). Demonstrations in sleep posture classification, pressure injury prevention, and exercise monitoring validate the platform's versatility for healthcare and human-machine interfaces.

items.title: Influenza virus antagonizes self-sensing by RIG-I to enhance viral replication.
items.abstract: Innate immune sensors must finely distinguish pathogens from the host to mount a response only during infection. RIG-I is a cytoplasmic sensor that triggers a broad antiviral response in response to sensing foreign RNAs. Here, we show that RIG-I not only binds viral RNAs but is activated by host RNAs. These are primarily non-coding RNAs transcribed by RNA polymerase III. They are benign under normal conditions but become immunogenic during influenza virus infection, where they signal via RIG-I to suppress viral replication. These RNAs are also bound by influenza virus nucleoprotein (NP), which normally functions to encapsidate the viral genome. NP interacts with RIG-I via an RNA bridge and antagonizes sensing of self-RNAs to counter innate immune responses. Overall, we demonstrate that self-sensing is strategically deployed by the cell to amplify the antiviral response and reveal a newly identified viral countermeasure that disrupts RIG-I activation by host RNAs.

items.title: Performance of 0/1 h versus 0/3 h pathways in patients with suspected myocardial infarction: a systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.

sections.objective: In patients with suspected myocardial infarction, the 0/1 h pathway (blood draws at 0 h and 1 h) is recommended in current guidelines for early risk stratification. However, individual trials used different safety outcomes, and efficacy outcomes were inconclusive or not assessed. We conducted a systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis of all randomised controlled trials to synthesise the totality of the evidence, assess heterogeneity across trials, and evaluate clinically relevant outcomes using harmonised definitions across trials.
sections.methods: In this systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis, we searched PubMed, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Scopus, and the International Clinical Trials Registry Platform from inception to July 6, 2026, without language restrictions, for randomised trials comparing the safety and efficacy of 0/1 h versus 0/3 h pathways (blood draws at 0 h and 3 h, ie, standard care). Individual participant data were obtained and outcome definitions were harmonised. The primary analysis used a two-stage random-effects meta-analysis. After receipt of the individual participant data but before data harmonisation or analysis, the primary safety outcome was refined to a composite of all-cause death or new type 1 myocardial infarction within 30 days, from the originally specified composite of all-cause death or any new myocardial infarction. The primary efficacy outcomes were emergency department length of stay and direct discharge from the emergency department. This meta-analysis is registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261383452).
sections.results: Our systematic review identified five randomised trials, all of which provided individual participant data. Among these, the definition of the primary safety outcome varied, and in four trials emergency department length of stay was not reported for the whole analysis population. We included 110 933 patient presentations (55 489 managed with the 0/1 h pathway and 55 444 managed with the 0/3 h pathway). Within 30 days, all-cause death or new type 1 myocardial infarction occurred in 446 patient presentations (0·8%) with the 0/1 h pathway versus 562 patient presentations (1·0%) with the 0/3 h pathway (random-effects pooled odds ratio [OR] 0·83 [95% CI 0·45-1·53]; I2=62·9%; τ2=0·143). Emergency department length of stay was 314 min (IQR 211-481) in the 0/1 h pathway group versus 308 min (209-453) in the 0/3 h pathway group (random-effects pooled geometric mean ratio 1·03 [95% CI 0·85-1·25]; I2=99·2%; τ2=0·024). Direct discharge from the emergency department occurred in 37 190 patient presentations (67·0%) with the 0/1 h pathway versus 36 485 patient presentations (65·8%) with the 0/3 h pathway (random-effects pooled OR 1·31 [95% CI 0·79-2·16]; I2=97·8%; τ2=0·156).
sections.conclusion: Across the available randomised trials, short-term adverse event rates were low with both pathways, but the pooled safety estimate remained imprecise. On average, earlier cardiac troponin retesting did not reduce emergency department length of stay or clearly increase direct discharge, and substantial between-study heterogeneity indicates that treatment effects might not translate uniformly across health-care systems. For hospitals considering transitioning from a 0/3 h to a 0/1 h pathway, implementation decisions should take broader diagnostic and organisational considerations into account.

items.title: Irritable bowel syndrome and related disorders of gut-brain interaction.
items.abstract: Irritable bowel syndrome, chronic constipation, and functional diarrhoea are disorders of gut-brain interaction, the symptoms of which include abnormal stool consistency or frequency accompanied by varying degrees of abdominal pain, discomfort, bloating, or distension. These conditions affect 20% of the global population with a relapsing and remitting course. Risk factors include female sex, younger age, a history of common mental disorders, and acute enteric infection. The pathophysiology of irritable bowel syndrome, chronic constipation, and functional diarrhoea remain incompletely understood, but are thought to be secondary to aberrant interactions throughout the gut-brain axis, resulting in disordered gut motility and visceral hypersensitivity. These conditions are diagnosed with a combination of clinical history, absence of alarm symptoms-such as weight loss or rectal bleeding-and targeted investigations. An empathetic management approach improves quality of life and symptoms, reduces health-care use, and enhances treatment adherence. Mainstays of treatment include education, dietary and lifestyle advice, modifying fibre intake, and drugs directed towards predominant symptoms. For severe symptoms, other treatments include specific medical devices, biofeedback, or psychological therapies. However, the effectiveness of most treatments is modest and there is an ongoing need to expand available treatments for bowel disorders, with several novel drugs currently in development.

items.title: Genetic coupling of floral rewards and signals underlies pollinator attraction.
items.abstract: Animal pollinators underpin biodiversity and global agriculture, yet the molecular mechanisms that coordinate floral rewards and signals to attract pollinators remain poorly understood. Through phenotyping melon genetic diversity, we identified nectarless1 (nls1), encoding the YABBY-family transcription factor YABBY5 (YAB5), as a central integrator of pollinator-attracting traits. YAB5 interacts with CRABS CLAW (CRC) during nectary initiation to specify nectary identity by repressing alternative floral organ fates. As flowers mature, YAB5 directly activates 4-α-glucanotransferase 2 (DPE2) to promote starch remobilization required for nectar secretion and promotes petal growth and flower opening. In petals, YAB5 directly engages an MYB111-dependent flavonoid pathway that generates UV nectar guides, while indirectly influencing floral volatile emission. Disrupting YAB5, DPE2, or MYB111 reduces pollinator visitation. Together, these findings reveal how a developmental regulator couples organ specification with organ-specific metabolic programs to synchronize floral rewards and signals at anthesis.

items.title: Innate sensor responses set a supra-unitary threshold for viral replication.
items.abstract: Cells resist viral infection by triggering rapid and sensitive innate immune responses, initiated by cytoplasmic viral sensor proteins (CyVSP), retinoic acid-inducible gene I (RIG-I), melanoma differentiation-associated protein 5 (MDA-5), and protein kinase R (PKR). Our single-cell analysis reveals that viral replication requires a supra-unitary viral genome input, significantly more than one, which we define as the virion input threshold for replication (VITREP). This threshold varies depending on viruses and cell types, independently of viral protein synthesis. Through mathematical modeling and experimental testing, we uncover that supra-unitary viral genome quantities activate negative feedback regulators (NFR) of CyVSP, including death-associated protein kinase 1 (DAPK1), Rio kinase 3 (RIOK3), and protein phosphatase 2 regulatory subunit alpha (PPP2R2A), that suppress innate immune responses and allow replication. We validate key predictions of our model, namely that downregulating NFR reduces replication, whereas upregulating NFR or coinfecting cells promotes replication. Together, these findings reveal a fundamental mechanism governing viral infectivity and tissue tropism.

items.title: Toward planetary microbial systems biology.
items.abstract: Microorganisms underpin Earth's biosphere, sustaining life, shaping biogeochemical cycles, and maintaining ecosystem stability. In an era of scientific and geopolitical fragmentation, we advocate for a "planetary microbial systems biology" (PMSB) framework to uncover the mechanisms and organizational principles governing Earth's interconnected microbial systems across scales of matter, space, and time and in relation to underlying natural and anthropogenic drivers. PMSB combines molecular and cellular technologies, multi-omics data, artificial intelligence (AI), and integrated transdisciplinary research across ecosystems. By federating open data and combining field observations, experimentation, and modeling, PMSB enables predictive understanding of microbiome dynamics across planetary scales, thus filling a critical knowledge gap in our understanding of the co-evolution of life and the Earth-system.

items.title: Roads not taken: The mismatch between safety and regulation of plant breeding innovation.
items.abstract: Meeting global food security goals while reducing agriculture's environmental impact requires continued crop improvement and innovation. Advances in transgenesis, cisgenesis, and genome editing now enable increasingly precise genetic modification with risks comparable to those of conventional breeding, yet regulatory frameworks remain focused on the method used rather than the product. We highlight recent examples, including immune receptor transfer, cisgenesis-based disease resistance stacking, photosynthesis engineering, and AI-guided protein design, that illustrate innovations constrained by current regulatory approaches. A decisive shift toward science-based, proportionate, and product-focused regulation is needed so that improved crops are evaluated on the basis of their properties, not how they were made.

items.title: The delocalized nature of chemical bonding at a catalytic metal surface.
items.abstract: Adsorbate bonding at metal surfaces requires hybridization of localized molecular orbitals with delocalized electronic bands of the metal; hence, the electronic wave function involved in bonding may extend far beyond the adsorption site. We revealed the consequence of this delocalization by determining the distance over which structural variations of the metal surface influence the molecule-metal bond strength. Velocity-resolved kinetics provided adsorption energies for three molecules bound at atomic steps of platinum (Pt), each exhibiting bond-strength changes of up to 0.2 electron volts as the step-step distance varied over 100 angstroms. We observed molecule-specific behavior reflecting the hybridization of molecule-specific orbitals with symmetry-selected orbital bands of the metal that respond differently to structural modifications of the solid. We discuss implications of these observations for adsorption on Pt nanoparticles.

items.title: Stimulated protein degradation to promote mitochondrial function and neuronal survival.
items.abstract: Targeted protein degradation is a promising modality to treat cancer or inflammation, but whether it can provide a similar benefit for disorders caused by pervasive protein dysregulation is unclear. We describe stimulated protein degradation (SPD) as a strategy that leverages agonists of stress-responsive E3 ubiquitin ligases to simultaneously eliminate multiple pathogenic factors. Specifically, we show that activators of the reductive stress response E3 CUL2FEM1B boost degradation of multiple physiological substrates to improve mitochondrial import and electron transport chain assembly. In this manner, CUL2FEM1B agonists preserve mitochondrial function and neuronal survival in models of neurodegenerative COX deficiency syndrome and Friedreich's ataxia. By activating E3 ligases that evolved to safeguard cellular integrity, SPD expands the use of compound-induced protein degradation to complex pathologies of high unmet need.

items.title: Spatial coordination in the codevelopment of the human urogenital system during organogenesis.
items.abstract: The human urogenital system originates from a common embryonic domain, yet the mechanisms guiding its spatiotemporal coordination remain understudied. Here, we combined high-resolution spatial transcriptomics with single-cell multiomics to profile human embryos from Carnegie stages 15 to 23, capturing the codevelopmental dynamics of the urogenital system. We revealed mesonephros- and adrenal primordium-derived signals that promote gonadal specification and enable efficient in vitro generation of cells resembling early gonadal lineages. We also uncovered a possible mesonephric origin of gonadal supporting cells through rete testis or ovarii linking the mesonephros. Finally, we delineate three transcriptionally distinct steroidogenic lineages differing in cholesterol sourcing, cortisol synthesis, and sex hormone production that together orchestrate sex differentiation. These findings deepen our understanding of urogenital system assembly and guide the exploration of coordinated multiorgan development.

items.title: Data-driven discovery and rapid, direct synthesis of MXenes.
items.abstract: MXenes are a rapidly expanding family of two-dimensional transition metal carbides and nitrides, yet scalable synthesis routes remain limited and historical reports suggest a broader, largely unexplored chemical space. We used machine learning-assisted database mining to uncover hidden multilayer MXenes. Screening reveals 33 previously synthesized but unrecognized MXene candidates. Guided by these findings, we synthesized seven multilayer MXenes using a rapid, scalable self-propagating high-temperature method that requires no sustained external heating and completes within minutes. We further realized 11 previously unexplored rare earth-based MXenes (M = praseodymium, neodymium, samarium, gadolinium, terbium, holmium, and thulium). Experiments and modeling suggest semiconducting behavior and diverse magnetic states across this family. Together, these results expand the MXene family and demonstrate a data-driven strategy for accelerating materials discovery through sustainable methods.

items.title: Intrinsic gestational timing governs human cerebellar development after preterm birth.
items.abstract: Intrinsic programs shape brain maturation; however, which of these programs are perturbed by prematurity as well as the molecular pathways involved remain unknown. The human cerebellum serves as a paradigm of extrauterine development-its accelerated growth and circuit formation align with the third trimester, a period disrupted by preterm delivery. Using multimodal datasets encompassing in vivo neuroimaging and neurodevelopmental outcomes with postmortem spatial-transcriptomic and histopathological profiling, we show that prematurity diverts the cerebellar developmental trajectory. Cerebellar growth and functional outcomes scaled with gestational age, despite modifying perinatal exposures. Spatially resolved developmental programs underlying macroscopic trajectories were marked by incomplete granule cell maturation and impaired Purkinje cell structural refinement, which indicate lineage-specific developmental asynchrony. Thus, prematurity constitutes biologically displaced maturation, in which infants of equivalent postmenstrual age occupy divergent developmental states.

items.title: Chiral altermagnon in MnTe.
items.abstract: Altermagnetism has been recognized as a magnetic phase that bridges the properties of ferro- and antiferromagnetism. The momentum-dependent spin splitting observed in these materials reflects their distinctive symmetry characteristics, which also establish the conditions for chiral magnons to emerge. Here we provide direct experimental evidence for a chiral magnon in the altermagnetic candidate manganese telluride (MnTe) revealed by circular-dichroism resonant inelastic x-ray scattering. This mode, which we term chiral altermagnon, exhibits a distinct momentum dependence of its spin polarization consistent with the altermagnetic g-wave symmetry of MnTe. Our polarization-resolved data corroborate the existence of a discrete class of magnetic excitations, demonstrating how altermagnetic order shapes spin dynamics and paving the way for advances in spintronic and quantum technologies.

items.title: The global geography of threats to freshwater biodiversity.
items.abstract: Human activities are eroding biodiversity, especially in freshwater systems. Despite major advances in quantifying species vulnerability and threats, we still lack a crucial understanding of where threats are affecting freshwater species globally. Here, we produced a species-centered spatial assessment of threats, mapping the impact of 45 threats across 21,490 freshwater species of amphibians, fish, mammals, odonates, and reptiles. We found that species in highly developed and water-managed regions are strongly affected by multiple overlapping threats. Although threats vary across taxa and regions, increasing threat probabilities elevate extinction risk and population declines, with freshwater species experiencing greater threat intensity and distinct spatial patterns than terrestrial species. Our findings establish a spatially explicit baseline for targeting the most urgently needed freshwater conservation and management interventions.

items.title: Papaver self-incompatibility is controlled by two multiallelic idiomorphs.
items.abstract: Self-incompatibility (SI) prevents self-fertilization through highly polymorphic genetic recognition at the S locus with multiple alleles. In Papaver rhoeas, the S determinants were previously identified as PrpS and PrsS. However, we found that PrpS-PrsS was absent in many S haplotypes. In this work, we report the identification of an alternative pair of polymorphic S genes, S locus oligopeptide transporter (SOPT) and S locus glycine-rich protein (SGRP), segregating at the S locus when PrpS-PrsS is absent. SOPT and SGRP display hallmark S determinant features and confer SI when heterologously expressed in Arabidopsis thaliana. Therefore, instead of having allelomorphs with homologous variants, the Papaver SI system is determined by two multiallelic idiomorphs sharing no obvious common ancestry. This discovery of a dual-idiomorph system reveals a distinct genetic basis for polymorphism, with implications for the evolution of allorecognition mechanisms.

items.title: A commensally regulated immune rheostat fine-tunes skin barrier fitness.
items.abstract: At the skin's surface, the epidermis must balance stem cell renewal with barrier maintenance to withstand environmental stress and shield against pathogens. In this study, we identify a microbial-immune-epithelial feedback mechanism that integrates environmental information into stem cell regulation in mice. Specifically, we show that Langerhans cells (LCs), an intraepithelial macrophage population, orchestrate this circuit by producing prostaglandin E2, which restrains stem cell proliferation, promotes epidermal differentiation, and maintains barrier integrity during homeostasis. Upon pathway disruption, stem cells become overactivated, hindering terminal differentiation and weakening barrier function. Upstream, LC activity is tuned by the local microbial environment in a rheostat-like fashion, coupling commensal sensing to stem cell dynamics. Our findings provide a general framework for how barrier tissues achieve adaptive homeostasis amid continual external fluctuations.

items.title: Altermagnetism revealed by polarized neutrons in MnF2.
items.abstract: Altermagnets are compensated magnets with symmetry-enforced spin split bands. Direct spectroscopic evidence for their existence has been reported in several materials. For example, inelastic neutron scattering (INS) has recently been used to witness a splitting of magnon bands in MnTe that is compatible with altermagnetism. Here, we present polarized INS results on MnF2 showing that it is altermagnetic. Our data reveal a splitting coming from the long-range dipolar coupling. Furthermore, using a domain-biased sample, the data reveal a nonzero chirality in the neutron scattering cross section that reverses the sign between the two magnon modes. It is this feature that clearly demonstrates altermagnetism in MnF2. This finding highlights the potential for polarized INS to characterize altermagnets through its sensitivity to fine structure in magnon spectra.

items.title: Rapid longitudinal flights cause time shifts and Sun compass error.
items.abstract: Many animals use the Sun compass to guide their movement, sometimes over thousands of kilometers. Consistent use of the Sun compass relies on the endogenous clock to track the Sun's arc, yet animals traveling east-west experience time shifts, potentially causing mismatches between their internal clock and local time. Using GPS, we reveal that Manx shearwaters (Puffinus puffinus) experience such shifts during homing flights, generating predictable errors in Sun compass orientation. Use of the Sun compass persists even when shearwaters have access to compass-independent cues during coast following. Our findings provide a new avenue for chronobiology research in the wild, suggesting that rapid longitudinal movements may affect other processes governed by the endogenous clock and that conserved chronobiological mechanisms impose substantial constraints on navigation.

items.title: Pervasive patterns in bird songs resemble those in human speech and song and are independent of vocal learning.
items.abstract: Bird songs are often described as analogs to human speech and songs, but expansive comparisons are necessary to determine analogy and mechanistic substrates. By analyzing global corpora consisting of 367 bird species (>74,500 vocal elements from ~5900 songs) within two clades of vocal learners (oscines and hummingbirds) and related nonlearners (suboscines and nightjars) and 52 human languages (>15,000 elements in >800 speech or song phrases), we revealed common patterns in bird songs that resemble prevalent patterns in human speech and song with variation in resemblance to speech or song. Vocal learning did not systematically affect acoustic patterning or similarity to human vocalizations. These data underscore the deep analogies between bird and human vocalizations and convergent motor mechanisms shaping communication.

items.title: Genomic erosion across avifauna in a biodiversity hotspot sounds a conservation alarm.
items.abstract: Loss of biodiversity can have a hidden dimension-the cryptic erosion of genetic diversity even in the face of apparent species resilience. We quantified changes in genetic diversity by comparing historical and modern genomes of 62 songbird species from the Gaoligong Mountains, a biodiversity hotspot in southwestern China. We identified genomic loss averaging between 43 and 49%; and, unexpectedly, common species were disproportionately affected. We argue that this loss was driven primarily by habitat fragmentation (and mitigated by dispersal ability) and show that it exceeds prior estimates and conservation policy thresholds. Species identified as having lost diversity continue to be listed as "Least Concern" on the International Union for Conservation of Nature's Red List of Threatened Species, exposing a blind spot in extinction risk monitoring. We call for genomic metrics to be rapidly integrated into global conservation frameworks.

items.title: Whole-body single-cell atlas of an adult vertebrate, Danionella cerebrum.
items.abstract: A complete cell type transcriptome atlas of a vertebrate could promote understanding of animal cell type composition, organization, and evolution. The miniaturized, transparent, and regenerative teleost Danionella cerebrum brings whole-vertebrate single-cell profiling experiments within reach. We performed region-stratified single-cell RNA sequencing across the adult Danionella body and mapped cell types and gene expression at single-cell resolution using spatial transcriptomics. We delineated spatially distinct neural cell types on the basis of their regional gene expression signatures. The body-wide atlas elucidated cell types harboring adult molecular positional memory, uncovered paedomorphic features, and revealed conserved body-region and appendage-specification programs in adult connective tissue. Comparative analyses revealed conserved neural cell types, and regeneration datasets uncovered expression dynamics during telencephalon regeneration. This whole-vertebrate transcriptome atlas yields a comprehensive resource for myriad questions in biology and neuroscience.

items.title: Western Pacific double subduction drives Gulf of California rifting.
items.abstract: Continental rifting reflects the balance between tectonic forces and lithospheric strength, yet the mechanisms of breakup remain debated. Rapid rifting of the Gulf of California oblique rift (GOCOR) ~6 million to 8 million years ago is a key example; it may have resulted from the lithosphere responding to external kinematics or acceleration of long-lived extension. The dynamics of either scenario remain incompletely understood. In this study, we highlight that the rapid rifting of the GOCOR coincides with the initiation of Western Pacific double subduction. Using three-dimensional geodynamic models, we show that such subduction reorganization can transmit extensional stresses of ~5 to 15 megapascals across the Pacific plate, loading the GOCOR and the southern San Andreas fault. Subduction reorganization may represent the missing driver for the initiation of rapid GOCOR rifting within a preconditioned lithosphere and may be an overlooked tectonic force behind other rifting events.

items.title: A Martian meteorite that formed ≳4.1 billion years ago samples Mars' early crust and mantle.
items.abstract: Martian meteorites provide a record of the planet's geological history. However, most are geologically young samples that are not representative of Mars' surface, which is dominated by ancient rocks. We describe the Martian meteorite Teghaza 001 (Teg 001), a slowly cooled igneous rock that formed at least 4.1 billion years ago. Its composition, mineralogy, and texture are distinct from other Martian meteorites. We determine that Teg 001 is a sample of ancient crust, which formed from a geochemically distinct mantle source with primordial composition. The presence of aqueously altered minerals, combined with bulk and mineral-specific oxygen isotope measurements, indicate that Teg 001 experienced reactions with fluids enriched in 18O, before ejection into space by an impact.

items.title: Emergence of Chern metal in a moiré Kondo lattice.
items.abstract: A Chern metal is a two-dimensional metallic state of matter carrying chiral edge states. We report the observation of a Chern metal at the onset of the magnetic Kondo breakdown in a frustrated moiré Kondo lattice--angle-aligned MoTe2/WSe2 bilayers. The state is compressible and is manifested by a nearly quantized Hall resistance and a finite longitudinal resistance arising from a bad metallic bulk. We demonstrate the presence of a chiral edge state by nonlocal transport measurements and current-induced quantum anomalous Hall breakdown. Magnetic circular dichroism measurements further reveal a magnetization plateau for the Chern metal before a metamagnetic transition at the Kondo breakdown. Our results open an opportunity for moiré engineering of exotic quantum phases through the interplay between band topology and Kondo interactions.

items.title: Gram-Negative Bacterial Resistance.
items.abstract: The rapid worldwide spread of antimicrobial resistance among gram-negative bacteria is driven by a complex interplay of human, environmental, and health care-associated factors and accelerated by mobile genetic elements that facilitate the dissemination of resistance genes. Resistance in gram-negative bacteria arises primarily through reduced drug entry, active drug efflux, modification of antibiotic targets, and enzymatic drug inactivation, most notably through β-lactamase production. Clinically important resistant pathogens include extended-spectrum β-lactamase-producing Enterobacterales, carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales, Pseudomonas aeruginosa with difficult-to-treat resistance, and carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii. Limited access to effective antibiotics and the continued emergence of resistance to available agents pose substantial challenges to the management of these infections. Appropriate management requires timely and accurate diagnostics, targeted use of newer β-lactam agents, effective source control, and judicious selection of treatment durations.

items.title: Continuous Glucose Monitoring in Non-Insulin-Treated Type 2 Diabetes.

sections.objective: Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) has been shown to be beneficial in persons with type 1 diabetes and others with insulin-treated type 2 diabetes, but its role in the treatment of persons with type 2 diabetes not being treated with insulin has needed further study.
sections.methods: In a 26-week trial conducted at 22 primary care practices in the United States, we randomly assigned adults with type 2 diabetes who were not using insulin to either CGM or routine care (control). The primary outcome was the glycated hemoglobin level at 26 weeks. Key CGM-measured secondary outcomes were tested hierarchically to control the type I error rate.
sections.results: A total of 145 participants were assigned to the CGM group, and 138 to the routine-care group. Participants ranged in age from 21 to 84 years. The mean (±SD) glycated hemoglobin level decreased from 8.8±1.3% at baseline to 7.2±1.1% at 26 weeks in the CGM group and from 8.7±1.2% to 8.0±1.4% in the routine-care group (adjusted mean difference, -0.9 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -1.1 to -0.6; P<0.001). The mean percentage of time that the CGM-measured glucose level was in the glucose-level range of 70 to 180 mg per deciliter was 21 percentage points higher (95% CI, 16 to 26) with CGM than with routine care (P<0.001). The between-group difference in the percentage of time that the glucose level was below 54 mg per deciliter was -0.17 percentage points (95% CI, -0.27 to -0.11; P<0.001 for noninferiority); the difference in the percentage of time that the glucose level was below 70 mg per deciliter was -0.20 percentage points (95% CI, -0.43 to -0.09; P<0.001 for noninferiority; P = 0.004 for superiority). No severe hypoglycemia events were reported.
sections.conclusion: Among adults with type 2 diabetes that was not being treated with insulin and was being managed in a primary care setting, the use of CGM led to a greater reduction in the glycated hemoglobin level and to a lower risk of hyperglycemia than routine care. (Funded by Dexcom; CONNECT ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06601166.).

items.title: Intermittent or Continuous Renal-Replacement Therapy in Acute Kidney Injury.

sections.objective: The preferred method of renal-replacement therapy for acute kidney injury in critically ill patients remains uncertain.
