sections.methods: In this multicenter, open-label, noninferiority trial, we randomly assigned critically ill adults with acute kidney injury who had indications for renal-replacement therapy to undergo intermittent hemodialysis or continuous renal-replacement therapy as the initial treatment. The primary outcome was a major adverse kidney event - defined as death, dependence on renal-replacement therapy, or a serum creatinine concentration more than 25% above the baseline value - by day 90.
sections.results: The trial was stopped early after sequential interim analyses showed a sustained signal of higher mortality with intermittent hemodialysis than with continuous renal-replacement therapy. A total of 554 patients underwent randomization, with 272 patients assigned to undergo intermittent hemodialysis and 282 to undergo continuous renal-replacement therapy; 535 patients (260 in the intermittent group and 275 in the continuous group) were included in the intention-to-treat population. A major adverse kidney event occurred by day 90 in 203 patients (78.1%) in the intermittent group and in 197 patients (71.6%) in the continuous group (adjusted absolute risk difference, 6.28 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -1.22 to 13.79). Death by day 90 occurred in 164 patients (63.1%) and in 147 patients (53.5%), respectively. Kaplan-Meier mortality estimates at day 90 were 63.3% and 53.6% (hazard ratio, 1.30; 95% CI, 1.04 to 1.63). The most common complication potentially related to acute kidney injury or renal-replacement therapy was hypotension, which occurred in 179 patients (68.8%) in the intermittent group and in 183 patients (66.5%) in the continuous group.
sections.conclusion: Among critically ill patients with acute kidney injury who had indications for renal-replacement therapy, intermittent hemodialysis as the initial treatment approach was not shown to be noninferior to continuous renal-replacement therapy with respect to major adverse kidney events by day 90 and was associated with higher mortality. (Funded by the French Ministry of Health; ICRAKI ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06032884.).

items.title: A fluctuation test for gastruloid heterogeneity.
items.abstract: Stem cells self-organize into models of early development, but even under carefully controlled conditions, the resulting organoids exhibit substantial "inter-individual" heterogeneity. To explore its origins, we generated monoclonal gastruloids, each derived from a single mouse embryonic stem cell (mESC). Molecular profiling revealed extensive heterogeneity: some gastruloids failed to develop, others were biased toward mesodermal or neural fates, and yet others contained cell types atypical of conventional polyclonal gastruloids. Applying DNA Typewriter, a cell lineage recorder, we identified heritable fate biases arising prior to gastruloid induction and found that more closely related founder mESCs give rise to more phenotypically similar gastruloids. Linking mESC subclones to their descendants' fates revealed cryptic, fate-predictive differences in gene expression and chromatin accessibility, including at imprinted, methylation-sensitive loci linked to developmental potency. Intrinsic, heritable fluctuations in mESC state are therefore an important source of organoid heterogeneity, and DNA Typewriter enables high-resolution lineage trees in stem cell models.

items.title: Comprehensive lineage tracing maps the landscape of cell fate decisions in mouse embryogenesis.
items.abstract: A comprehensive cell fate map of mammalian embryogenesis has remained out of reach given the scale, cellular diversity, and non-deterministic nature of development in utero. Here, we use PEtracer to continuously install heritable genetic marks as development progresses, reconstructing lineage trees that resolve ∼75% of cell divisions across >1.4 million cells from 16 replicate embryos. We pair these trees with deep transcriptional profiling to resolve cell fate biases, restriction timing, progenitor pool sizes, and lineage relationships throughout embryogenesis. Using this quantitative reference, we uncover strikingly reproducible lineage architecture between replicate embryos and chart the lineage dynamics driving fate specification across diverse tissues. Specific biological insights include the progressive restriction of neural crest fate, the relative contributions of distinct mesodermal origins to endothelium, and the dynamics of axial elongation. This work provides a foundation for a quantitative and predictive understanding of mammalian development.

items.title: Opposing functions of gut immunomodulatory metabolites on CAR-T therapy.
items.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cell therapy has transformed hematological cancer treatment, yet nearly half of patients still relapse or progress. Increasing evidence implicates the gut microbiome and antibiotic exposure as key modulators of clinical outcomes. In a cohort of 129 patients across three German centers, shotgun metagenomics and targeted mass spectrometry revealed that reduced short-chain fatty acids, particularly valeric acid, prior to CAR-T cell therapy correlated with increased risk of disease progression. Conversely, high levels of indole metabolites, including indole-3-carboxaldehyde and indole-3-acetic acid as well as the branched-chain fatty acid isovaleric acid, were linked to adverse outcomes. Functional validation in human and murine CAR-T cell models demonstrated that valeric acid supplementation enhanced, while indole-3-carboxaldehyde and isovaleric acid impaired, CAR-T cell efficacy. These findings reveal the opposing roles of immunomodulatory metabolites on CAR-T cell therapy, carrying significant implications for the design of metabolite-guided, microbiome-based therapeutics.

items.title: In-cell structures visualize human pre-ribosome assembly in the nucleolus.
items.abstract: In eukaryotes, ribosome biogenesis initiates within the nucleolus, a hallmark multilayered compartment of the nucleus. Structures of pre-ribosomes have been characterized ex situ, but their assembly pathways within human nucleoli have not been described. Here, we used cryogenic correlative light and electron tomography to visualize molecular landscapes within HeLa cell nucleoli and obtained in-cell structural snapshots of both ribosomal subunit precursors, the small subunit processome and the pre-60S. These recapitulate major states resolved previously ex situ and reveal additional critical interaction partners, including the RNA exosome, rixosome, and nuclear export receptor CRM1-RanGTP. We further show how pre-ribosome assembly landscapes are altered upon RNA polymerase I inhibition. Our study combines molecular structures with cellular context to elucidate the spatiotemporal assembly pathway of the human ribosome.

items.title: Copper ion-induced MYH9 polymerization executes cuproptosis.
items.abstract: Cuproptosis is a recently identified form of copper-dependent cell death implicated in various physiological and pathological processes. However, the executive proteins involved and the role of physiological intracellular copper in cuproptosis remain unclear. Herein, we identified myosin heavy-chain 9 (MYH9) as a cuproptosis executioner. Copper binding induced MYH9 polymerization, which disrupted the actin cytoskeleton and led to cuproptotic cell death. Hexyl 2-(3,4,5-trihydroxy-phenyl) acetate (HThPA) was shown to induce cuproptosis by binding to the nuclear receptor Nur77, leading to depletion of copper chelate glutathione (GSH) and release of free copper from intracellular copper stores. Acetylation of MYH9 by acetyltransferase dihydrolipoamide S-acetyltransferase (DLAT) facilitated copper binding, regardless of its extracellular or intracellular origin. Physiological copper levels were higher in drug-resistant tumor cells and clinical samples, which increased the likelihood of HThPA-induced cuproptosis. These results elucidate the mechanisms underlying cuproptosis, establish MYH9 as an executioner, and propose a treatment strategy for drug-resistant tumors.

items.title: Glycocalyx-edited mesenchymal stem/stromal cell therapy in advanced osteoporosis.
items.abstract: Mesenchymal stem/stromal cells (MSCs) are osteoregenerative; however, their therapeutic efficacy for skeletal conditions is hampered by poor bone-homing ("osteotropism"). In preclinical models, this deficit is correctable by MSC glycocalyx editing to enforce sialylated Lewis X (sLeX) expression, thereby programming osteotropism. We conducted a first-in-human clinical trial (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT02566655) involving a single intravenous infusion of glycocalyx-edited autologous bone marrow-derived MSCs in ten women with advanced-stage osteoporosis. The protocol-mandated evaluation spanned 2 years and included clinical assessments, radiographic studies, and measurements of bone turnover markers (BTMs), bone tissue area (BTA), and bone mineral density (BMD). Thereafter, fracture and safety monitoring continued for >3 additional years for each patient. No serious adverse events occurred. Fragility fractures were markedly and durably reduced, amidst increased osteoanabolic BTM levels, BTA, and volumetric BMD. These findings indicate that glycocalyx editing effectuates MSC-based osteoporosis therapy and also refute notions that MSCs derived from older persons and/or diseased-tissue sites are biologically compromised.

items.title: Metax enables accurate cross-domain taxonomic profiling of metagenomes.
items.abstract: Taxonomic profiling is fundamental to microbiome research, yet achieving high species-level accuracy remains challenging for complex communities that span bacteria, viruses, eukaryotes, and archaea, and these limitations are exacerbated in low-biomass, host-dominated samples. We introduce Metax, a cross-domain taxonomic profiler that integrates coverage-based probabilistic modeling with an expectation-maximization framework to distinguish true microbial signals from artifacts. Across >600 samples from host-associated, environmental, wastewater, and low-biomass clinical settings, including benchmarks with limited reference representation, Metax improved profiling accuracy, achieving on average 55% higher F1 scores and 45% lower Bray-Curtis dissimilarity than other methods. Moreover, this broad evaluation demonstrated that Metax resolved bacterial and viral signatures of peri-implantitis in oral microbiomes and revealed signals suggestive of reagent-borne contaminants and reference misassemblies in plasma-cell-free DNA. By leveraging genome-wide coverage evidence, Metax enables robust cross-domain profiling across diverse sample types and sequencing depths, including settings where reference databases are highly incomplete.

items.title: Caloric restriction modulates genome-wide somatic mutation in mice.
items.abstract: Somatic mutations accumulate throughout life in every cell, and this process constitutes one of the hallmarks of aging-genomic instability. Caloric restriction (CR) has been shown to extend lifespan across diverse species. Using high-fidelity duplex DNA sequencing of bulk liver, bulk kidney, hepatocytes, and cerebellar neurons, we found that CR in mice reduces genome-wide somatic mutation burdens across multiple tissues and cell types. CR reduced both substitution and insertion/deletion burdens, with the magnitude of these effects varying across sample types. CR also decreased the activity of the enigmatic single-base substitution (SBS) mutational process SBS5 that gives rise to most mutations in mammals. Surprisingly, the mutation burden reduction from CR was greatest in transcriptionally inactive regions. This work illuminates links between diet, aging, and genomic integrity and establishes genomic integrity as a modifiable axis of aging.

items.title: Structural basis of a SWI/SNF-associated transcription pre-initiation complex.
items.abstract: The mating type switching/sucrose non-fermenting (SWI/SNF) chromatin remodeling complex removes and repositions nucleosomes at promoters for the initiation of transcription. Though long thought to function independently, we find that SWI/SNF is an integral component of the transcription machinery. SWI/SNF associates with an RNA polymerase II pre-initiation complex (PIC), Mediator, and a nucleosome, and the entire assembly dimerizes to form a giant 7-megadalton complex. We present high-resolution cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) structures of both PIC-Mediator-SWI/SNF and PIC-Mediator-SWI/SNF-nucleosome complexes, together with results of cross-linking and mass spectrometry. The structures reveal how SWI/SNF enhances the initiation of transcription through stabilization of PIC organization and concerted remodeling of the so-called +1 nucleosome. The structural model suggests the coordinated actions of two DNA translocases, Snf2 of SWI/SNF and Ssl2 of TFIIH, for the initiation of transcription.

items.title: Tozorakimab to Prevent COPD Exacerbations.

sections.objective: Many patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) have exacerbations despite receiving standard-of-care inhaled maintenance therapy. Dysregulated interleukin-33 signaling is implicated in the pathogenesis of COPD. Tozorakimab is a monoclonal antibody that inhibits the activity of interleukin-33.
sections.methods: In two replicate phase 3 trials (OBERON and TITANIA), we enrolled adults with COPD who were current or former smokers and had a history of exacerbations in the previous year despite receiving stable standard-of-care inhaled maintenance therapy. There were no eligibility criteria related to blood eosinophil count. Patients were randomly assigned to receive add-on subcutaneous tozorakimab (300 mg) or placebo every 4 weeks for 52 weeks. The primary end point was the annualized rate of moderate or severe exacerbations that occurred over a 52-week period among former smokers, and the first key secondary end point was the annualized rate of moderate or severe exacerbations in the overall population. Safety was also assessed.
sections.results: The overall population in OBERON included 446 patients in the tozorakimab group and 431 in the placebo group, and in TITANIA included 438 in the tozorakimab group and 435 in the placebo group. The annualized rate of moderate or severe exacerbations among former smokers was 1.34 events in the tozorakimab group and 1.90 events in the placebo group (rate ratio, 0.71; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.57 to 0.88; P = 0.002) in OBERON, and 1.37 events and 2.07 events, respectively (rate ratio, 0.66; 95% CI, 0.55 to 0.80; P<0.001), in TITANIA. In the overall population, the annualized rate of moderate or severe exacerbations was 1.41 events in the tozorakimab group and 2.00 events in the placebo group (rate ratio, 0.70; 95% CI, 0.58 to 0.85; P<0.001) in OBERON, and 1.44 events and 2.03 events, respectively (rate ratio, 0.71; 95% CI, 0.59 to 0.84; P<0.001), in TITANIA. Adverse events occurred in 70.4% of the patients in the tozorakimab group and in 77.2% of those in the placebo group in OBERON, and in 80.1% and 79.8%, respectively, in TITANIA.
sections.conclusion: Among patients with COPD, treatment with tozorakimab resulted in a significantly lower rate of moderate or severe exacerbations than placebo in the cohort of former smokers and in the overall population of current and former smokers. (Funded by AstraZeneca; OBERON ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05166889; TITANIA ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05158387.).

items.title: Identification of the tendon/ligament stem cell in mice and humans.
items.abstract: Ligamentum flavum (LF) hypertrophy resulting in spinal cord compression is a key cause of lumbar spinal stenosis (LSS). There are no medical therapies for LSS, in part because the identity of the tendon/ligament stem cell (TLSC) mediating LSS remains unclear. Here, we identify the TLSC present in all tendons and ligaments in humans and mice as Lin-Thy1.2-Sca-1-CD73+CD140α- cells that display self-renewal and give rise to all other tenocyte lineage cells. This TLSC also sits at the apex of their differentiation hierarchy, as determined by in vivo somatic-variant-based lineage tracing. LSS induction led to druggable, calcium signaling-dependent, cell-intrinsic reprogramming of the TLSCs to increase their tenocyte output. Overall, this work identifies the TLSC and establishes dysregulated differentiation of this cell as a mechanism contributing to LSS. This TLSC is anticipated to play a central role in other disorders of tendons and ligaments.

items.title: Tabula Sapiens 2.0: A comprehensive transcriptomic atlas of human cell types.
items.abstract: The Tabula Sapiens is a reference human cell atlas containing single-cell transcriptomic data from more than two dozen organs and tissues. Here, we report Tabula Sapiens 2.0, which includes data from nine new donors, doubles the number of cells, and adds four new tissues. These new data include four donors with multiple organs contributed, thus providing a unique dataset in which genetic background, age, and epigenetic effects are controlled for. We illustrate applications of the Tabula Sapiens data in areas as diverse as gene regulation and aging. The Tabula Sapiens contains transcripts from nearly all human transcription factors, thereby providing putative cell-type specificity for nearly every human transcription factor and insights into their potential regulatory roles. We also analyze the transcriptomes of cells expressing canonical genes relating to cellular senescence, revealing the heterogeneity and context-dependent nature of senescence and providing new hypotheses into senescence-associated pathways.
items.authors: Tabula Sapiens Consortium. Electronic address: steve@quake-lab.org

items.title: De novo pan-rhodamine binders for fluorescence microscopy from mammalian cells to extremophiles.
items.abstract: Fluorescent imaging in live cells is a cornerstone of life sciences. While natural fluorescent proteins have been engineered to enhance individual features, no existing tag combines ideal properties into a single system: high brightness, reversible binding, compact size, and stability across diverse conditions. Here, we achieve this through de novo design of rhodamine binders (Rhobin). To harness the broad repertoire of rhodamine fluorophores, we developed a generalizable design strategy for a pan-rhodamine binder compatible with diverse wavelengths and applications. Rhobin enables live- and fixed-cell imaging of various subcellular targets in mammalian cells, showing brightness surpassing existing tags. Its reversible fluorophore binding supports super-resolution stimulated emission depletion (STED) and live-cell single-molecule imaging for extended durations compared with HaloTag. Beyond conventional systems, Rhobin enables live imaging of the extremophile Sulfolobus acidocaldarius at 75°C, previously inaccessible with current tags. Together, these results establish Rhobin as a versatile platform for next-generation imaging and biosensor design.

items.title: Immediate Ambulatory Electrocardiographic Monitoring in Syncope.

sections.objective: In patients with syncope who present to the emergency department for evaluation, diagnosing an underlying cardiac arrhythmia remains difficult.
sections.methods: We conducted an open-label, randomized, controlled trial at 45 hospitals in the United Kingdom to assess the effects of 14-day cardiac monitoring on diagnosis, treatment, and outcomes among patients with syncope. Adults with syncope that remained unexplained after an evaluation in the emergency department were assigned in a 1:1 ratio to undergo 14-day ambulatory electrocardiographic (ECG) monitoring (the intervention group) or to receive the standard care provided for patients with unexplained syncope at each participating site (the standard-care group). The primary outcome was the mean number of patient-reported episodes of syncope at 1 year.
sections.results: A total of 2234 patients underwent randomization: 1123 were assigned to the intervention group and 1111 to the standard-care group. The mean age of the patients was 58.3 years, and 52.1% were male. After the exclusion of patients who did not complete any follow-up, a total of 1970 patients (1004 in the intervention group and 966 in the standard-care group) were included in the primary analysis. The mean (±SD) number of patient-reported syncope episodes at 1 year was 1.37±5.10 in the intervention group and 1.58±8.56 in the standard-care group (incidence rate ratio, 0.89; 95% confidence interval, 0.68 to 1.18; P = 0.42). A total of 49 adverse events were reported in the intervention group, and 8 adverse events were reported in the standard-care group, with 1 serious adverse event in each group.
sections.conclusion: Among patients with syncope that remained unexplained after evaluation in the emergency department, the use of 14-day ambulatory ECG monitoring did not result in significantly fewer patient-reported syncope episodes at 1 year than standard care. (Funded by the British Heart Foundation and National Health Service Research Scotland; ASPIRED ISRCTN Registry number, ISRCTN10278811.).

items.title: Genome-scale perturb-seq in primary human CD4+ T cells maps context-specific regulators of T cell programs and human immune traits.
items.abstract: Gene regulatory networks encode the fundamental logic of cellular functions, but systematic network mapping remains challenging, especially in cell states relevant to human biology and disease. Here, we perturbed all expressed genes across 22 million primary human CD4+ T cells from four donors and developed a probe-based perturb-seq platform to measure the transcriptome effects in cells at rest and after stimulation. These data allowed us to map genes regulating immune pathways, including previously uncharacterized regulators of cytokine production. Importantly, active regulators and the gene programs they control changed dramatically across stimulation conditions. Perturbation signatures enabled us to model T cell states observed in population-scale transcriptomic atlases, nominating regulators of T cell polarization and of age-related phenotypes. Finally, we leveraged perturb-seq to implicate context-specific gene regulatory pathways in autoimmune disease risk. Our study provides a foundational resource and new approaches to decode T cell function and human immune traits.

items.title: Integrative spatial profiling of 3D genome organization and gene expression in tissue.
items.abstract: Three-dimensional genome organization shapes transcriptional regulation, yet measuring its spatial coordination in situ within intact tissues remains challenging. We present Spatial Hi-C-RNA, a multimodal platform that simultaneously maps genome-wide chromatin contacts and transcriptomes from the same tissue section at near-single-cell resolution. Across the mouse brain, developing embryos, and human melanoma, Spatial Hi-C-RNA generated multimodal maps that aligned with tissue anatomy while revealing complementary chromatin- and RNA-defined spatial patterns. Multiscale features, including A/B compartments, topologically associating domains, and chromatin loops, were associated with region- and cell-type-specific transcriptional programs. In mouse embryos, Spatial Hi-C-RNA resolved coordinated chromatin and transcriptional remodeling during neuronal maturation across developmental stages. In human melanoma, chromatin architecture delineated intratumoral subregions not detected by RNA alone and linked tumor-state transitions to changes in compartments, domain boundaries, and regulatory programs. Spatial Hi-C-RNA thus provides a broadly applicable framework for investigating genome structure-function relationships in development and disease within native tissue environments.

items.title: Gut microbiota generate dinitrosyl iron complexes with cardiometabolic benefits.
items.abstract: Gut bacteria affect host physiology, but the underlying mechanisms are not completely understood. We identify a pathway whereby gut microbes convert inorganic nitrate and non-heme iron into mobile bioactive dinitrosyl iron complexes (DNICs) that are distributed systemically and affect host metabolism. Electron paramagnetic resonance detected DNICs in tissues of conventional but not germ-free mice. Mouse and human feces and E. coli generated DNICs from nitrate and iron citrate, whereas a nitrate-reductase-deficient mutant did not. Dietary supplementation with nitrate+iron citrate or synthetic DNICs increased tissue DNIC levels and ameliorated cardiometabolic dysfunction in Western diet-fed mice. Additionally, in HepG2 cells and human hepatocyte spheroids, DNIC reduced fatty acid-induced steatosis. DNIC bioactivity is mediated by the Fe(NO)2 entity, rather than by free nitric oxide (NO), and involves activation of soluble guanylyl cyclase (sGC), inhibition of leucine uptake, and mTORC1 signaling normalization. Modulating DNIC formation by the gut microbiota could be a strategy to support cardiometabolic health.

items.title: RNA structures regulate norovirus life cycle and enable rational attenuation in vivo.
items.abstract: Viral genomes encode regulatory RNA structures that orchestrate key steps of viral replication and gene expression. Although these structures are increasingly recognized as critical regulators of viral function, their systematic characterization in an infection context and roles in regulating viral fitness and immune recognition in vivo remain limited. Here, we systematically map and functionally interrogate structured RNA elements across the murine norovirus genome using orthogonal in-cell chemical probing, revealing conserved motifs that regulate viral function. Targeted disruption of specific structural elements reduces viral replication in cell culture, modulates translation in cis, and decreases viral RNA levels in animal infection models. These findings enabled the rational design of a genetically stable, attenuated virus that elicits protective immunity and limits viral replication upon secondary challenge. Together, this work uncovers essential roles for RNA structure in norovirus biology and establishes a generalizable framework for RNA structure-guided design of antiviral vaccines and therapeutics.

items.title: Multimodal brain cell atlas across the adult macaque lifespan.
items.abstract: High-throughput single-cell omics of non-human primate brain tissue provides a powerful platform to investigate the molecular basis of brain aging. Here, we present a comprehensive transcriptomic and chromatin accessibility atlas of 2,955,873 nuclei from eight brain regions of 23 female cynomolgus macaques spanning the adult lifespan, including exceptionally old individuals. Our analyses reveal dynamic, cell-subtype- and region-specific age-related changes in core brain functions, including synaptic communication and axon myelination. We identify multicellular networks in the pons and medulla as a previously unrecognized hotspot of primate brain aging, highlighting white matter vulnerability as a central feature of aging. Integration with human brain aging and neurodegeneration datasets reveals both shared and divergent molecular mechanisms. We further define transcription factors and age-related chromatin remodeling programs linked to longevity and neurodegeneration. This spatiotemporal atlas establishes a foundational framework for understanding the cellular and regulatory architecture of primate brain aging and its links to disease.

items.title: Brain perivascular macrophages regulate endothelial cell function via a cMAF-dependent transcriptional program in mouse and human.
items.abstract: Brain perivascular macrophages maintain brain physiology, yet their transcriptional regulators and functions in health and disease remain unclear. Using single-cell multi-omics and functional experiments, we identify cellular musculoaponeurotic fibrosarcoma oncogene (cMAF) as a key transcription factor for brain perivascular macrophages, and conditional deletion of cMAF disrupts their phenotype in vivo. Functionally, cMAF drives insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF1) expression in perivascular macrophages, enabling communication with endothelial cells. Consistently, cMAF deletion in perivascular macrophages causes transcriptional alterations in cerebral arteries, affecting vascular functions. Notably, cMAF emerges as the main transcription factor for human perivascular macrophages, suggesting conservation of this transcriptional module. During Alzheimer's disease (AD), human perivascular macrophages upregulate cMAF and IGF1 to enhance communication with vascular cells, and this response is abrogated in APOE4 carriers. Lastly, we explore an uncharacterized polymorphism in cMAF, providing evidence that the cMAF program is protective against AD. Targeting cMAF in perivascular macrophages may offer new therapeutic strategies for neurodegenerative and cerebrovascular diseases.

items.title: Functional atlas of vertebrate viral RNA elements that stabilize RNA and enhance translation.
items.abstract: Viruses encode diverse regulatory elements, but their breadth and mechanisms remain poorly defined. To address this gap, we performed massively parallel reporter assays spanning ∼200,000 genomic segments from 297 vertebrate-infecting viral genera. We identified numerous viral elements that enhance RNA stability and translation through TENT4-mediated mixed tailing, distributed across 19 genera and grouped into six distinct subclasses, indicating extensive convergent evolution. We also found diverse TENT4-independent elements acting through alternative pathways. One such element, Pt1 from Potamipivirus, stabilizes linear mRNA to levels comparable to circular RNA, suggesting its potential for RNA therapeutics. Pt1 directly recruits canonical poly(A) polymerases (PAPγ/α)-previously thought to function exclusively in transcription-coupled nuclear pre-mRNA processing-to drive cytoplasmic polyadenylation. Together, these findings chart the rich landscape of viral regulation, extend the scope of poly(A)-tail biology, and establish the virome as a valuable source for uncovering host RNA regulatory mechanisms.

items.title: In Situ Fenestration-Assisted TEVAR in Patients With Complex Pathology Involving the Aortic Arch.

sections.objective: To assess the feasibility, safety, and short-term clinical outcomes of in situ fenestration during thoracic endovascular aortic repair (ISF-TEVAR) employing an electrocautery-connected guidewire combined with a novel, pump-less, extracorporeal femoro-carotid bypass for cerebral perfusion in patients with complex aortic arch pathology.
sections.methods: This prospective, single-center study included 19 consecutive patients treated between February 2024 and September 2025. A homemade extracorporeal arterio-arterial bypass was constructed using femoral arterial inflow and intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) tubing connected to supra-aortic sheaths to maintain continuous cerebral perfusion during fenestration. Fenestrations were performed with an electrocautery-connected 0.018-inch chronic total occlusion-dedicated guidewire. Patients' demographics, procedural details, perioperative outcomes, and early follow-up data were analyzed, with stratification according to the number of fenestrated supra-aortic branches.
sections.results: A total of 37 supra-aortic branches were targeted: 3-branch fenestrations in 6 patients (31.6%), 2-branch in 6 patients (31.6%), and single-branch in 7 patients (36.8%). Technical success, defined as successful graft fenestration with patent branches on completion angiography, was achieved in 94.5% (35/37). One failed innominate artery fenestration was managed with chimney-assisted TEVAR, and 1 left subclavian artery fenestration was successfully completed in a subsequent procedure. Operative time increased with procedural complexity (140 ± 12 minutes for 1 branch, 152 ± 10 minutes for 2 branches, and 162 ± 13 minutes for 3 branches; P = .004). No intraprocedural mortality occurred. Two perioperative strokes (10.5%) and 2 in-hospital deaths (10.5%) were recorded, 1 death was due to vertebrobasilar stroke and the other due to retrograde type A aortic dissection with rupture. Median hospital stay was 8 days. During a mean follow-up of 9.2 months, there was no aorta-related mortality, with an overall survival rate of 89.5%. All stented branches remained patent, and 2 endoleaks (10.5%) were successfully treated endovascularly.
sections.conclusion: In situ fenestration during thoracic endovascular aortic repair using an electrocautery-connected wire combined with a temporary, pressure gradient-driven extracorporeal femoro-carotid bypass is a feasible, reproducible, and safe technique for complex aortic arch repair. This fully percutaneous approach ensures continuous cerebral perfusion, demonstrates efficient procedural metrics, and yields favorable short-term outcomes, representing a practical alternative when custom-made devices or hybrid surgical procedures are not available.Clinical ImpactIn situ fenestration-assisted TEVAR combined with a temporary pumpless extracorporeal femoral-carotid bypass enables continuous cerebral perfusion during complex aortic arch interventions without the need for cardiopulmonary bypass or surgical debranching. This technique expands the feasibility of fully endovascular multibranch arch repair in urgent or anatomically challenging cases where custom-made devices are unavailable. For clinicians, this approach offers a practical and reproducible strategy to mitigate cerebral ischemic risk while maintaining procedural efficiency and percutaneous access. This technique may facilitate broader adoption of in situ fenestration by providing a cerebral protection strategy using readily available endovascular equipment.

items.title: Alloimmune risk stratification for kidney transplantation.
items.abstract: Alloreactivity after kidney transplantation occurs via both memory responses resulting from prior sensitization and de novo responses that develop due to donor-recipient disparity for the human leukocyte antigen (HLA) complex. HLA compatibility (absence of HLA-DSA) and the degree of HLA matching inform on the likelihood of allorecognition that can cause allograft rejection and allograft loss, and are therefore the two pillars of alloimmune risk assessment. Over the past decades, the detection of anti-HLA antibodies has become more sensitive and specific through single antigen bead testing, and advances in HLA typing from serology to DNA level have been instrumental for more detailed analysis of HLA compatibility. Nonetheless, alloimmune risk stratification using antigen-level HLA data has limited ability to accurately predict the risk of de novo anti-HLA responses and long-term graft outcome after transplantation, especially on the individual patient level. Aiming to improve long-term outcomes by improving HLA matching, HLA molecular mismatch algorithms have been developed. In this review, we discuss the advances, clinical evidence, limitations and clinical implementability of HLA molecular mismatch analysis to increase precision in alloimmune risk stratification in kidney transplantation. In addition, we provide an overview of the different molecular mismatch tools and their potential application in personalized medicine, such as organ allocation, criteria for donor acceptance and individualized immunosuppression.

items.title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists Decrease the Rate of Rupture, Cardiac Events, and Death in Patients with Abdominal Aortic Aneurysms.

sections.objective: Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a degenerative condition involving several processes including inflammation, matrix remodeling, disruptions of vascular smooth muscle cells, and thrombus formation all leading to progressive dilatation of the aorta and eventual rupture. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RA) are now considered part of the frontline therapeutic options to treat type 2 diabetes mellitus and have also been validated as having compelling anti-inflammatory and cardiovascular protective properties. Data is limited on the impact of GLP-1RA on outcomes of patients with AAA. The aim of this study is to examine the association and possible impact of GLP-1RA on patients with AAA.
sections.methods: Data was sourced from the TriNetX research network, encompassing 123 health care organizations. Utilizing ICD-10 and CPT codes, we identified patients with AAA who received abdominal imaging every six months. Group 1 was comprised of patients who were treated with GLP-1RA while Group 2 patients were not. Propensity-score-matching (PSM) was used in a 1:1 fashion using age, sex, diabetes, metformin use, hypertension, cardiac disease, tobacco use, chronic kidney disease, and pulmonary disease as covariates. Primary outcomes were aneurysm rupture or repair. Secondary outcomes include mortality and major adverse cardiac events (MACE; myocardial infarction, stroke, and heart failure). Standard statistical methods were used as appropriate.
sections.results: We identified 412,490 patients with diagnosis of AAA who were undergoing 6-month surveillance between June 1, 2010 and April 16, 2024. After PSM, the GLP-1RA group (N=13,722) underwent fewer elective repairs at each timepoint (1.5% vs 2.3% at 2 years, 2.1% vs 3.0% at 5 years, P<.01) and had significantly fewer ruptures at two years (1.1% vs 1.8%, P<.01) and five years (1.6% vs 2.4%, P<.01) when compared to Group 2 (N=13,722). Group 1 also experienced significantly fewer MACE and all-cause mortality at two and five years. On multivariate analysis, GLP-1RA significantly reduced the risk of undergoing elective repair (HR 0.757, 95% CI [0.636-0.902], P<.01), rupture (HR 0.538, 95% CI [0.418-0.691], P<.01), all-cause mortality (HR 0.474, 95% CI [0.439-0.511], P<.001), and MACE (HR 0.825, 95% CI [0.794-0.857], P<.01) at 5 years.
sections.conclusion: The use of GLP-1RA in patients with AAA is associated with fewer ruptures, elective repairs, and improved rates of MACE and death. A prospective analysis may further elucidate if GLP-1RA should be prescribed to reduce the rate of aneurysm growth.

items.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Paracentral Acute Middle Maculopathy for Arteritic Anterior Ischemic Optic Neuropathy.

sections.objective: The purpose of this study was to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of paracentral acute middle maculopathy (PAMM) detected on optical coherence tomography (OCT) macula for differentiating arteritic anterior ischemic neuropathy (AAION) from nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION) in a multicenter United States cohort.
sections.methods: Retrospective, multicenter diagnostic accuracy analysis. This study included patients diagnosed with AAION or NAION at the University of Minnesota, Mayo Clinic, and Johns Hopkins Wilmer Eye Institute between January 2020 and January 2025. Inclusion criteria consisted of patients older than 50 years who had obtained OCT macula within 14 days of symptom onset. AAION diagnoses were confirmed by temporal artery biopsy or positron emission tomography/computed tomography. Two masked fellowship-trained neuro-ophthalmologists independently evaluated OCT images for the presence of acute PAMM.
sections.results: A total of 119 patients were included, consisting of 27 patients with AAION and 92 patients with NAION. PAMM was identified in 18.5% of patients with AAION and 5.4% of patients with NAION (p = 0.032). The sensitivity, specificity, PPV, and NPV of PAMM for AAION was 19% [95% CI: 0.08-0.37], 94.6% [95% CI: 0.88-0.98], 50% [95% CI: 0.24-0.76], and79.8% [95% CI: 0.71-0.86] respectively. Three of five NAION patients with PAMM had provoked NAION associated with severe systemic hypoperfusion.
sections.conclusion: PAMM is a highly specific but insensitive OCT marker for AAION. Although its presence should increase clinical suspicion for AAION, PAMM may rarely occur in patients with NAION particularly in the setting of systemic hypoperfusion and should be interpreted within the overall clinical context.
sections.other: Sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), and negative predictive value (NPV) of PAMM for AAION were calculated.

items.title: Constructing an Objective Defocus Curve from Pyramidal Wavefront Aberrometry: Mapping Objective-to-Subjective Through-Focus Response.

sections.objective: To construct an objective defocus curve from pyramidal wavefront aberrometry and map it onto the subjective through-focus response.
sections.methods: Prospective multicenter case series with external validation. Pyramidal aberrometry (Osiris) with numerically introduced defocus from +1.00 to -4.00 diopters (D); the second-moment radius of the geometrical point spread function was mapped to acuity by a rational function and compared with monocular ETDRS defocus curves.
sections.results: Internal test set: RMSE 0.095 logMAR (95% CI, 0.078-0.110), bias 0.016 logMAR (LoA, -0.168 to +0.201); external cohort: RMSE 0.092 logMAR (0.079-0.103), bias -0.021 logMAR (LoA, -0.197 to +0.155). Objective minus subjective DOFi at 0.20 logMAR was -0.10 D (LoA, -1.44 to +1.25 D) and -0.15 D (LoA, -0.98 to +0.69 D). Cohort-mean subjective DOFi was 2.43 D (Full-DOFi, continuous); corrected distance acuity was 20/20 or better in 88.8%.
sections.conclusion: An objective defocus curve from one pyramidal wavefront acquisition estimated the subjective through-focus response with small bias and limits of agreement of about ±0.2 logMAR in a test set and an independent cohort of refractive IOLs; individual precision, diffractive designs, and pupil-specific curves need further work.
sections.other: 98 eyes of 63 patients implanted with the RayOne Galaxy spiral refractive intraocular lens (IOL) at three centers (Italy, UK); 81 eyes with a wavefront pupil ≥ 4 mm were split by patient into training (56) and test (25) sets; 19 eyes with other refractive extended-depth-of-focus IOLs from a fourth center formed an external cohort. Root-mean-square error (RMSE), bias, and 95% limits of agreement (LoA) between mapped objective and subjective acuity; objective versus subjective depth of field (DOFi).

items.title: Retinal phenotypes and longitudinal clinical courses in patients with NPHP1-associated Senior-Løken syndrome.

sections.objective: This study aimed to describe retinal phenotype, longitudinal clinical course, and genetic findings in Japanese patients with NPHP1-associated Senior-Løken syndrome and their siblings.
sections.methods: Retrospective, multicenter case series. This study included 12 patients with biallelic pathogenic NPHP1 variants, comprising 10 probands with symptomatic retinal dystrophy recruited from six ophthalmic centers across Japan and 2 affected siblings identified through family screening. Clinical and genetic findings were analyzed. Retinal dystrophy was diagnosed using fundus photography, fundus autofluorescence (FAF), optical coherence tomography, and electroretinography. Genetic testing was performed using whole-exome and/or whole-genome sequencing. Follow-up ranged from 0 to 44 years (mean, 14.6 years).
sections.results: Retinal phenotypes included cone/cone-rod dystrophy (4 patients), retinitis pigmentosa (4 patients), sector retinitis pigmentosa (2 patients), pigmented paravenous retinochoroidal atrophy (1 patient), and normal retina (1 patient). FAF images showed a descending tract in 5 patients. Retinopathy preceded nephropathy in 9 patients, all of whom were initially diagnosed with Leber congenital amaurosis or early-onset retinal dystrophy. Genetic testing showed that 11 patients harbored a homozygous whole-NPHP1 deletion, whereas 1 carried compound heterozygous NPHP1 and EYS variants.
sections.conclusion: Patients with NPHP1-associated Senior-Løken syndrome showed considerable inter- and intrafamilial variability in retinal phenotype. Pigmented paravenous retinochoroidal atrophy can be associated with NPHP1 variants. A descending tract on FAF imaging may be a characteristic feature of retinal degeneration in Senior-Løken syndrome. Retinopathy, which commonly manifests as Leber congenital amaurosis or early-onset retinal dystrophy, often precedes nephropathy in patients with NPHP1-associated Senior-Løken syndrome.
sections.other: Retinal phenotype, onset of retinopathy and nephropathy, and genotype.

items.title: Choroidal Thickness and Axial Length as Independent Correlates of AMD: Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2017-2020.

sections.objective: To examine how choroidal thickness and axial length relate to age-related macular degeneration (AMD) across disease stages in a nationwide Korean population.
sections.methods: Cross-sectional, population-based study. We analyzed the Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey, 2017-2020, including 15,388 adults aged 40 years or older with gradable fundus photographs; ocular analyses included 13,807 after excluding coexisting macular disease. Axial length (AL), central macular thickness (CMT), and subfoveal choroidal thickness (SFCT) were measured by partial coherence interferometry and optical coherence tomography. Associations were assessed by survey-weighted logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, and systemic factors.
sections.results: Weighted AMD prevalence was 14.41% (95% CI, 13.67-15.15; early, 13.46%; late, 0.95%). In multivariable models, greater SFCT was associated with early AMD (OR per 10 µm, 1.03; 95% CI, 1.02-1.03; P < .001), and shorter AL with early AMD (OR per 1 mm, 0.76; 0.71-0.82; P < .001) and late AMD (0.74; 0.57-0.97; P = .030). Greater CMT was associated with late AMD (OR per 10 µm, 1.10; 1.01-1.19; P = .030) and neovascular AMD (1.23; 1.12-1.35; P < .001). SFCT and AL remained associated with early AMD after mutual adjustment (both P < .001). Older age, male sex, non-white-collar occupation, and rural residence were associated with AMD, and anemia with late AMD (1.78; 1.06-2.96; P = .028).
sections.conclusion: Greater SFCT and shorter AL were independently associated with early AMD. These findings suggest that choroidal thickness and axial length may reflect distinct structural correlates.

keywords: Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey

items.title: Outcomes of Calcanectomy in Diabetic Foot Ulcers and Calcaneal Osteomyelitis: A Systematic Review.

sections.objective: Diabetic Foot Ulcers (DFU) and calcaneal osteomyelitis present a formidable management challenge in limb reconstruction and preservation. Calcanectomy has emerged as an intermediate limb-preserving option. It aims to eliminate infection and allows wound closure without a need for major amputation. The aim of this review is to evaluate the outcomes of calcanectomy performed for DFU and osteomyelitis.
sections.methods: A systematic search of MEDLINE and Embase. Studies were restricted to English-language publications from 2020 onwards. The primary outcomes were limb salvage and major amputation rates. Secondary outcomes included wound healing, time to complete healing, post-operative complications, re-operation and mortality.
sections.results: Fifteen studies published between 2020 and 2025 were included, encompassing 503 patients undergoing partial, total, or vertical contour calcanectomy. Calcanectomy was associated with favourable rates of limb preservation with limb salvage exceeding 80% in 9 of the 15 studies (range: 40.0% to 100%). The highest reported major amputation rate was 60.0%. Complete wound healing rates ranged from 33.4% to 100%, with healing times ranging from 3.6 weeks to 7 months. Re-operation rates ranged from 0% to 62.8%, while postoperative infection spanned from 0% to 83.3%. Mortality ranged from 0% to 37.5%, reaching 43.3% at the five-year mark. Included literature carried a low-to-moderate risk of bias.
sections.conclusion: These findings support calcanectomy as a potentially valid alternative to major lower-limb amputation. Considerable heterogeneity in technique, outcome definitions and follow-up limits direct comparison. Prospective, multicentre studies with standardised reporting are needed to refine patient selection, optimal technique and confirm long-term functional benefit.

items.title: The prevalence and long-term clinical significance of left common iliac vein compression by the right common iliac artery in an asymptomatic population.

sections.objective: To investigate the prevalence of left common iliac vein (LCIV) compression between the right common iliac artery and L5 vertebra in an asymptomatic cohort, and determine whether individuals with ≥50% LCIV stenosis develop chronic venous insufficiency (CVI) or deep venous thrombosis (DVT).
sections.methods: Retrospective cohort study with prospective long-term clinical follow-up METHODS: Iliac venous anatomy was analysed on protocolised computed tomography (CT) in healthy individuals assessed for live related kidney donation at a tertiary referral centre between January 2012 and January 2019, with follow-up until January 2026. Scripted phone interviews assessed left leg venous symptoms, signs, investigations and treatment.
sections.results: Of 102 participants, 60 were female (58.8%), median age was 38 years (IQR 30-45), mean body mass index was 26.6 ± 4.2. Mean LCIV compression was 39.2% ± 18.5. Female sex (OR 3.52, CI 1.36-10.1, p=0.009) and younger age (OR 0.91, CI 0.86-0.96, p<0.001) were independently associated with ≥50% LCIV compression. 39 participants (38.2%) had ≥50% LCIV compression; one participant (1%) had ≥70% LCIV compression. One participant developed a right leg DVT. No others underwent venous imaging for CVI or DVT over a median 11-year follow-up (IQR 9.1-12.7). Of 13 participants with ≥50% LCIV compression surveyed, three reported left leg varicosities and three reported an episode of isolated leg swelling without investigation or treatment.
sections.conclusion: LCIV compression is common on supine CT in healthy, asymptomatic individuals, particularly young females. On long term follow-up, no clinically significant left leg venous sequelae were identified in those with ≥50% LCIV compression. Hence, caution is advised when reporting this finding on CT to avoid unnecessary investigation or intervention.

items.title: Ultrasound-Guided Thrombin Injection for Iatrogenic Femoral Artery Pseudoaneurysms: Predictors of Failure and Recurrence.

sections.objective: Ultrasound-guided thrombin injection (UGTI) is effective for iatrogenic femoral artery pseudoaneurysms, but factors associated with early failure and recurrence remain incompletely defined. We evaluated treatment outcomes and their predictors.
sections.methods: This retrospective single-center study included 216 patients treated with UGTI between November 2023 and May 2026. Technical success was defined as immediate complete thrombosis after the first injection, clinical success as complete thrombosis at 24-hour Doppler follow-up, and recurrence as recanalization at 24 hours after technical success. Independent associations with clinical failure and recurrence were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression.
sections.results: Technical success was achieved in 204 patients (94.4%), clinical success in 176 (81.5%), and recurrence occurred in 31 of 204 patients (15.2%). Overall success without surgical or endovascular repair was 94.0%. Therapeutic index procedures (OR, 6.368; 95% CI, 2.037-19.910), INR >1.5 (OR, 5.286; 95% CI, 1.681-16.625), shorter neck length (OR per mm, 0.879; 95% CI, 0.802-0.964), a longer procedure-to-UGTI interval (OR per day, 1.041; 95% CI, 1.008-1.074), and platelet count 1.5 (OR, 3.653; 95% CI, 1.114-11.982) independently predicted recurrence. No procedure-related complications occurred.
sections.conclusion: UGTI was highly effective for iatrogenic femoral artery pseudoaneurysms, with high immediate and overall success and no observed complications. Procedural, anatomical, temporal, and hemostatic factors were associated with outcomes, while clinical failure and recurrence represented distinct treatment phases. These findings may support risk-adapted surveillance.

items.title: Effect of a Nurse-Driven Early Mobilization Protocol on Biomarker Levels and Incidence of Deep Vein Thrombosis After Lower Extremity Fracture Surgery: A Retrospective Cohort Study.

sections.objective: To evaluate the effect of a nurse-driven early mobilization protocol on the incidence of deep vein thrombosis (DVT), biomarker levels, and clinical outcomes in patients after lower extremity fracture surgery.
sections.methods: This retrospective cohort study included 205 patients who underwent surgery for traumatic unilateral lower extremity fractures (January 2023-June 2025). Patients were divided into a control group (conventional care, n=107) and an early mobilization group (nurse-driven protocol, n=98) using July 2024 as the implementation cutoff. Outcomes included postoperative DVT incidence, changes in D-dimer and C-reactive protein (CRP), bed rest duration, pain scores, length of stay, and complications. Repeated-measures ANOVA compared biomarker changes; binary logistic regression identified DVT risk factors.
sections.results: The early mobilization group had a significantly lower incidence of postoperative DVT than the control group (7.14% vs. 19.63%, P=0.009), with an absolute risk reduction of 12.49% and a relative risk reduction of 63.6%. Repeated-measures ANOVA showed significant between-group effects (F=22.33, P<0.001) and interaction effects (F=6.36, P<0.001) for CRP levels. After Bonferroni correction, the early mobilization group had significantly lower D-dimer and CRP levels at one week postoperatively and at discharge than the control group (P<0.0125). The early mobilization group also had significantly better outcomes in terms of bed rest duration (5.86±1.69 days vs. 6.38±1.54 days, P=0.021), NRS score on postoperative day 3 (3.27±1.15 vs. 4.54±1.47, P<0.001), and length of hospital stay (median 11.00 days vs. 13.00 days, P<0.001), as well as a lower complication rate (6.12% vs. 14.95%, P=0.041). Multivariate logistic regression analysis identified the early mobilization protocol (OR=0.27, 95%CI: 0.10-0.73, P=0.009), age (OR=1.05, 95%CI: 1.02-1.08, P=0.001), and postoperative day 1 D-dimer level (OR=1.25, 95%CI: 1.05-1.47, P=0.011) as independent factors influencing postoperative DVT.
sections.conclusion: A nurse-driven early mobilization protocol effectively reduces the incidence of DVT after lower extremity fracture surgery, improves coagulation and inflammatory biomarker levels, shortens hospital stay, and does not increase complication risks. The protocol is safe and feasible and can be recommended as an adjunctive measure for venous thromboembolism (VTE) prevention after lower extremity fracture surgery.

items.title: Ophthalmic Encounters After Tamoxifen Initiation.

sections.objective: Tamoxifen can cause retinal toxicity and vision loss, yet no formal screening guideline exists in the US. To characterize ophthalmic use after tamoxifen initiation, identify predictors, and compare 12-month use between those with breast cancer taking tamoxifen and those taking aromatase inhibitors.
sections.methods: This was a retrospective cohort study conducted May to June 2026 using All of Us data with 365-day minimum follow-up. The setting was a US multisite research program. Participants included adults with a first tamoxifen prescription recorded in All of Us, excluding those taking hydroxychloroquine. The comparator included those with breast cancer taking aromatase inhibitors.
sections.results: Among 2327 individuals taking tamoxifen (mean [SD] age, 53.8 [10.6] years; 2232 [95.9%] female), 162 (7.0%) had an ophthalmic encounter within 12 months, and 39 (1.7%) underwent retinal OCT or fundus photography. Among participants with preexisting glaucoma or diabetic retinopathy, 22 of 88 (25.0%) had an encounter vs 140 of 2239 (6.3%) without either condition (difference, 18.7 percentage points; 95% CI, 10.8-28.8 percentage points; P < .001). Preexisting glaucoma (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 3.87; 95% CI, 2.12-7.06; P < .001), greater preindex health care use (aOR, 1.43; 95% CI, 1.24-1.63; P < .001), and older age (aOR per 10-year increase, 1.21; 95% CI, 1.04-1.42; P = .02) were associated with greater use. Among participants with breast cancer, 126 of 1886 individuals taking tamoxifen (6.7%) had an encounter vs 240 of 2809 individuals taking aromatase inhibitors (8.5%; difference, -1.9 percentage points; 95% CI, -3.4 to -0.3 percentage points; P = .02). After adjustment, tamoxifen use was not associated with greater ophthalmic use (aOR, 1.10; 95% CI, 0.85-1.42; P = .46).
sections.conclusion: Results of this cohort study suggest that ophthalmic use after tamoxifen initiation was uncommon, and retinal-specific testing was rare. Tamoxifen use was not associated with greater adjusted 12-month use than aromatase inhibitor use. Additional evidence on retinopathy incidence, natural history, screening strategies, and clinical benefit is needed to inform guidance.
sections.other: Tamoxifen or aromatase inhibitor initiation. The primary outcome was any ophthalmic encounter within 12 months, identified from eye examination, retinal procedure, and eye visit codes. Retinal optical coherence tomography (OCT) or fundus photography was secondary. Logistic regression assessed predictors and compared treatment groups after adjustment for demographics, preexisting conditions, preindex health care use, region, and initiation year.

items.title: Bi-Allelic PRKCZ Loss-of-Function Variants and Adult-Onset Retinitis Pigmentosa.

sections.objective: Inherited retinal diseases are genetically heterogeneous disorders, with retinitis pigmentosa (RP) representing the most common form; although more than 90 genes have been implicated, many RP cases remain molecularly unsolved. To describe an adult-onset RP phenotype associated with loss-of-function variants in PRKCZ, profile the clinical features of this disorder, and investigate the underlying disease mechanism.
sections.methods: In this case series study, genomic analyses were performed in individuals with unsolved childhood- and adult-onset retinal disease recruited through international research and diagnostic programs. Detailed clinical characterization was conducted in affected individuals. In vitro analyses were carried out to validate the genomic findings using primary and transduced cell-based experimental approaches. Genomic analyses were performed from October 2023 to December 2025; functional studies were carried out from January 2024 to May 2026.
sections.results: Among approximately 4500 individuals with unsolved childhood- and adult-onset retinal disease tested, 6 bi-allelic PRKCZ variants were identified in 13 affected individuals from 10 unrelated families, 5 of which were predicted to lead to loss of function (frameshift, nonsense, or splice-altering variants). Six of 13 affected individuals (46%) were female. Most cases carried a recurrent frameshift variant (c.139_140del; p.Met47Valfs*19). All variants selectively affected the long PRKCZ transcript encoding the N-terminal Phox and Bem1 (PB1) domain. Clinically, PRKCZ-associated RP showed adult onset (18-49 years), progressive night blindness, peripheral visual field constriction, and eventual central vision loss. Four individuals exhibited adult-onset sensorineural hearing loss. Functional studies in patient-derived fibroblasts demonstrated selective loss of the long PRKCZ isoform, impaired ciliogenesis, and altered mitochondrial organization, which were validated in stable PRKCZ knockdown cell lines. Structural modeling and coimmunoprecipitation assays indicated that the missense variant was associated with the disruption of PB1 domain-mediated protein-protein interactions.
sections.conclusion: In this case series study, bi-allelic inactivating variants in PRKCZ were associated with adult-onset RP with an isoform-specific mechanism involving the long retinal-enriched transcript. These findings expand the genetic spectrum of RP and highlight PRKCZ as a potentially clinically relevant gene implicated in adult-onset retinal degeneration.
sections.other: Bi-allelic likely pathogenic variants in a novel RP disease gene candidate, PRKCZ. The primary outcome was genetic, clinical, and functional effects of bi-allelic PRKCZ inactivating variants associated with adult-onset RP. A detailed ophthalmologic assessment was conducted to characterize the clinical phenotype. Functional analyses in patient-derived fibroblasts and transduced cell lines were performed to validate the consequence of disruptive variants on PRKCZ transcript processing and PKCζ function.

items.title: Visual Field and RNFL OCT Testing Among Rural and Urban Residents With Glaucoma.

sections.objective: Rural populations face disparities in eye care; therefore, understanding the utilization of structural imaging and visual field (VF) testing for glaucoma monitoring among rural compared with urban patients is important. To evaluate whether rural residence and sociodemographic factors are associated with patterns of VF testing and retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) optical coherence tomography (OCT) in patients with glaucoma.
sections.methods: This retrospective longitudinal cohort study used data from the Sight Outcomes Research Collaborative (SOURCE) consortium, a multi-institutional repository of US academic ophthalmic clinical data, from May 2012 to January 2025. Included patients had at least 2 separate dates of glaucoma billing codes, at least 3 years of follow-up data, and at least 1 VF or RNFL OCT test.
sections.results: Among 48 196 patients, 45 843 (95.1%) lived in urban areas (25 613 [55.9%] female; mean [SD] age, 67.78 [12.71] years) and 2353 (4.9%) lived in rural areas (1272 [54.1%] female; mean [SD] age, 67.3 [12.03] years). Mean (SD) VF testing frequency was 0.91 (0.52) tests per year among rural patients and 0.91 (0.56) among urban patients; rural residence was not associated with regular VF monitoring (adjusted odds ratio [AOR], 0.95; 95% CI, 0.88-1.04; P = .28). Rural residence was associated with lower RNFL OCT frequency (mean [SD], 0.57 [0.45] vs 0.63 [0.47] tests per year; difference, -0.06 [95% CI, -0.08 to -0.04] tests per year; adjusted incidence rate ratio, 0.93 [95% CI, 0.88-0.98]; P = .004) and lower odds of regular RNFL OCT monitoring (AOR, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.74-0.90; P < .001). Medicaid insurance was associated with lower odds of regular monitoring with VF (AOR, 0.35; 95% CI, 0.30-0.40; P < .001) and RNFL OCT (AOR, 0.62; 95% CI, 0.52-0.74; P < .001).
sections.conclusion: In this cohort study, rural residence was associated with lower utilization of RNFL OCT but not VF testing, while Medicaid insurance was associated with lower odds of monitoring for both modalities. The findings suggest that ophthalmologists should be aware that rural patients with glaucoma may require additional attention to continuity of structural imaging.
sections.other: Rural vs urban residence, categorized by Rural-Urban Commuting Area codes. Primary outcomes were utilization frequency (tests per year) and regular monitoring (≥1 test every 18 months) for VF and RNFL OCT. Testing frequency was analyzed using multivariable negative binomial regression, and regular monitoring was analyzed using logistic regression adjusted for sociodemographic characteristics and baseline visual acuity.

items.title: Healthy Dietary Patterns and Incident Cardiovascular Disease in Cancer Survivors: A Prospective Cohort Study.

sections.objective: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of noncancer mortality among cancer survivors. The potential influence of healthy dietary patterns on CVD risk among cancer survivors remains poorly understood. This study aims to investigate the association between healthy dietary patterns and incident CVD among cancer survivors.
sections.methods: We analyzed data from 8,716 cancer survivors initially free of CVD in the UK Biobank cohort. We used 24-hour dietary recall data to calculate 8 dietary pattern scores. Cox proportional hazards models and Fine-Gray competing risks models were used to investigate the association between dietary patterns and incident CVD.
sections.results: During a median follow-up of 12.3 (Q1-Q3: 11.6-13.0) years, 1,116 individuals experienced incident CVD events. When comparing the top quintile with the bottom quintile, HRs (95% CI) for total CVD were 0.72 (0.58-0.88) for Mediterranean diet score, 0.74 (0.61-0.89) for Mediterranean-Dietary Approaches to stop Hypertension Diet Intervention for Neurodegenerative Delay score, 0.63 (0.52-0.76) for Alternate Healthy Eating Index-2010, 0.65 (0.53-0.79) for Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension score, 0.82 (0.68-0.99) for healthful Plant-Based Diet Index, 0.67 (0.55-0.80) for reversed energy-adjusted diet inflammatory index, and 0.80 (0.67-0.96) for healthy low-fat diet score. The findings remain robust after fitting the generalized propensity score model. At age 45, participants with the highest adherence to healthy dietary patterns gained an estimated life expectancy of 1.66 to 3.32 years more than those with the lowest adherence.
sections.conclusion: Adherence to healthy dietary patterns is associated with reduced CVD risk among cancer survivors, underscoring the potential for diet to support cardio-oncology care.

items.title: Autophagy in macrophages curtails IL-1α-mediated immune priming against lung infections.
items.abstract: Host resistance to infection is initially determined by how well primed the innate immune system is to respond on first exposure to an invader, yet the mechanisms underlying this priming remain incompletely understood. Here we found that basal autophagy suppressed the expression of Il1a in alveolar macrophages (AMs) and an otherwise protective innate immune priming against Staphylococcus aureus and influenza A virus (IAV), independently of the microbiome and adaptive immunity. Inactivating autophagy genes in AMs led to elevated expression of IL-1α in AMs, which subsequently enhanced IL-1R-MyD88 signaling in neutrophils and increased the recruitment of myeloid cells to the lung. As a result, autophagy-deficient mice showed more efficient clearance of S. aureus along with reduced lung damage and inflammation. Similar to genetic inactivation of autophagy, overexpression of IL-1α in AMs conferred broad spectrum protection against S. aureus and IAV, suggesting a possible strategy to fine-tune immune responses to combat important respiratory infections.

items.title: Optimal closed-loop feedback control of blood flow after spinal cord injury with norepinephrine.
items.abstract: After spinal cord injury, clinical management aims to support tissue perfusion, but current methods rely on the indirect control of arterial blood pressure without direct measurement of the local blood flow. This limits the ability to tailor drug delivery to the injured tissue. Here, we show that spinal cord blood flow can be regulated using a closed-loop controller that adjusts vasopressor infusion on the basis of real-time ultrasound flow measurement. We characterize the dynamic relationship between drug infusion, arterial pressure and spinal cord blood flow, and we use these data to design a feedback controller that targets a predefined flow level. We validate the system in simulations, implement the controller in real time in rodents and translate it to pigs. We show that the controller reduced blood flow deviations and variability compared with constant dosing and supported functional recovery in a rodent survival model. These results show a closed-loop spinal cord perfusion control strategy that leverages clinically available measurements and pharmacological interventions, supporting its translation to clinical settings for the management of acute spinal cord injury.

items.title: Long-term safety and efficacy of twice-yearly depemokimab in type 2 asthma with an eosinophilic phenotype: 2-year integrated analysis of the phase 3a SWIFT-1 and SWIFT-2 studies and AGILE open-label extension.

sections.objective: Depemokimab is the first ultra-long-acting biologic, with enhanced interleukin-5 binding affinity, high potency, and extended half-life, enabling twice-yearly dosing. The double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3a SWIFT-1 and SWIFT-2 studies demonstrated depemokimab efficacy and safety over 52 weeks in patients with asthma with type 2 inflammation and an eosinophilic phenotype. Here, we present long-term safety and efficacy outcomes over the 52-week, phase 3a open-label extension (OLE) of SWIFT-1 and SWIFT-2 (AGILE) alongside an integrated post-hoc analysis of the 104-week SWIFT and AGILE period.
sections.methods: In SWIFT-1 and SWIFT-2, patients (aged ≥12 years) with asthma with type 2 inflammation, an eosinophilic phenotype (≥150 cells/μL at screening or ≥300 cells/μL during the previous 12 months), and a history of at least two exacerbations in the previous 12 months despite receiving medium-dose or high-dose inhaled corticosteroids were randomly assigned (2:1) to subcutaneous depemokimab 100 mg or placebo every 26 weeks in addition to standard of care for 52 weeks. Patients who completed SWIFT-1 or SWIFT-2 could join the single-arm, 52-week AGILE OLE study, conducted at 156 centres across 14 countries. Patients continued depemokimab (depemokimab-depemokimab group) or switched to depemokimab from placebo (placebo-depemokimab group). The primary endpoints for the 52-week AGILE OLE period were the incidence of adverse events and serious adverse events, and immunogenicity as measured by the presence of anti-drug antibodies and neutralising antibodies. Secondary efficacy outcomes, including exacerbation rate, St George's Respiratory Questionnaire (SGRQ) total score, Asthma Control Questionnaire-5 (ACQ-5) score, and pre-bronchodilator forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1), were also assessed. Additional post-hoc analyses were carried out to assess safety and efficacy over the 104-week integrated SWIFT and AGILE analysis period. AGILE OLE is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05243680. The SWIFT-1 and SWIFT-2 trials are registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04719832 and NCT04718103.
sections.results: Between March 1, 2022, and May 19, 2025, 629 patients were included in the AGILE OLE study (419 patients in the depemokimab-depemokimab group and 210 patients in the placebo-depemokimab group). During the 52-week AGILE OLE period, adverse events occurred in 297 (71%) of 419 patients in the depemokimab-depemokimab group and 146 (70%) of 210 patients in the placebo-depemokimab group; serious adverse events were infrequent (37 [9%] of 419 in the depemokimab-depemokimab group and 19 [9%] of 210 in the placebo-depemokimab group), with no treatment-related or fatal serious adverse events reported. In the depemokimab-depemokimab group, the reduced annualised exacerbation rate was sustained over 2 years (0·51 [95% CI 0·43-0·61] in the 52-week SWIFT-1 and SWIFT-2 period and 0·56 [0·47-0·66] in the AGILE OLE). Improvements in SGRQ total score, ACQ-5 score, and FEV1 were maintained over 2 years. In the placebo-depemokimab group, improvements in clinical outcomes were observed after the switch to depemokimab during the AGILE OLE.
sections.conclusion: Twice-yearly depemokimab was well tolerated and demonstrated sustained efficacy over the 2-year SWIFT and AGILE period, supporting its long-term therapeutic benefit and safety profile.

items.title: Long-term evaluation of the effectiveness and safety of autologous haematopoietic stem-cell transplantation for systemic sclerosis (NISSC1-LTE): a cohort study.

sections.objective: Systemic sclerosis is a rare and heterogeneous chronic autoimmune disease. It has the highest mortality of the rheumatic diseases and few treatment options exist. Autologous haematopoietic stem-cell transplantation (HSCT) is an effective and established therapeutic option in selected patients with early severe systemic sclerosis. This study aimed to evaluate the long-term safety and effectiveness of autologous HSCT in patients with systemic sclerosis in real-life clinical practice.
sections.methods: This cohort study (NISSC1-LTE) followed up patients with systemic sclerosis included in the prospective European Society for Blood and Marrow Transplantation NISSC1 study who had undergone their first autologous HSCT for severe progressive systemic sclerosis. Follow-up data were collected from 13 participating centres in France, Germany, Netherlands, Italy, Spain, Switzerland, and Brazil. Participating centres completed a yearly case report form for each patient alive after 2 years and up to 10 years after autologous HSCT. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival, defined as survival from baseline without evidence of systemic sclerosis progression. Late complications after autologous HSCT, including malignancies, secondary autoimmune diseases, infections, and major adverse cardiovascular events were also analysed. People with lived experience of systemic sclerosis were involved in the design and conduct of this study. The NISSC1 study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT02516124) and is complete.
sections.results: All 80 patients with systemic sclerosis who had an autologous HSCT between Dec 4, 2012, and Jan 19, 2016, were included in this long-term extension study. 12 patients were lost to follow-up, including five patients with a follow-up less than 5 years. Median age at autologous HSCT was 43 years (IQR 33-51), 57 (71%) of 80 patients were female, 23 (29%) were male, and median follow-up was 9·2 years (IQR 8·9-9·6) after autologous HSCT. Progression-free survival was 81% (95% CI 71-88) at 2 years, 72% (61-81) at 5 years, and 60% (47-71) at 10 years. 18 patients died during the study; causes of death were autologous HSCT-related in five (6%) of 80 patients, disease progression in nine (11%) patients, post-autologous HSCT malignancy in two (3%) patients, and late serious infection in two (3%) patients. 34 (43%) of 80 patients maintained remission without immunosuppressive treatment over 10 years.
sections.conclusion: This study provides long-term follow-up data after autologous HSCT in patients with systemic sclerosis allowing robust assessment of response rate, late complications, and sustained treatment benefit. The extended timeframe might serve as an important comparator for all upcoming, cellular treatment options.

items.title: Prevalence and spectrum of skin diseases in adults in China: a nationwide cross-sectional study.

sections.objective: Skin diseases have been identified as a public health priority at the 78th World Health Assembly, with a call for strengthened national surveillance and evidence-based responses. However, in China, comprehensive national epidemiological data on the prevalence of skin diseases have been lacking. We aimed to bridge this data gap by conducting the China Skin Health study, a large-scale, population-based, cross-sectional study.
sections.methods: In this study, we used a multistage stratified cluster random sampling design to obtain a nationally representative sample of adults aged 18 years or older from diverse geographical regions of China. We collaborated with provincial centres for disease control and prevention to establish a survey team comprising public health workers and ten to 12 certified dermatologists in each of the five provinces selected for the study. Residents' committees disseminated study information through posters and WeChat groups to recruit participants, and data were collected at local community health centres. Standardised electronic questionnaires were administered by trained interviewers to collect information on demographic and other characteristics. Certified dermatologists examined sun-exposed areas (eg, scalp, face, neck, and extremities) in all participants, as well as unexposed areas reported as concerns by respondents, for common skin diseases spanning 12 categories and more than 60 specific conditions. Clinical diagnoses were made on the basis of observed skin manifestations. The total number of skin conditions was recorded for each participant, and the mean number of skin conditions was calculated. Point prevalence of skin diseases was defined as the proportion of participants with a dermatologist-confirmed diagnosis of any listed condition at the time of the survey. Sampling weights derived from the study sampling framework and the 2020 National Population Census were applied when calculating prevalence and conducting logistic regression analyses. The absolute number of dermatological cases nationwide was estimated by applying prevalence estimates to the 2020 Chinese census data.
sections.results: From July 1, 2022, to June 27, 2024, 153 593 participants completed the survey and were included in the analysis. The study population had a mean age of 48·5 years (SD 16·8), with 75 512 (49·2%) men and 78 081 (50·8%) women; 98 926 (64·4%) participants resided in urban areas. The age-standardised prevalence of skin diseases was 55·6% (95% CI 51·2-59·9), corresponding to an estimated 618 million (95% CI 567-666) affected adults in China, with a mean of 0·98 (SD 1·22) skin diseases per person. Prevalence increased with age, from 42·0% (95% CI 35·3-48·6) in those aged 18-29 years to 79·5% (75·8-83·1) in those aged 80 years or older (p<0·0001 for trend). Skin diseases were more common in women (56·5%, 51·8-61·1) than in men (54·6%, 50·5-58·7; p=0·023) and more prevalent in southern China (62·5%, 56·2-68·9) than in northern China (47·4%, 43·2-51·7; p<0·0001). Benign cutaneous tumours were the most prevalent type of condition (31·1%, 28·7-33·5), followed by superficial fungal infections (15·0%, 12·5-17·5); dermatitis, eczema, and allergic dermatoses (9·0%, 7·8-10·1); pigmentary dermatoses (7·9%, 6·3-9·6); and sebaceous and sweat gland dermatoses (5·7%, 5·0-6·4). Factors associated with skin diseases included female sex, increasing age, residence in southern China, current or former smoking, current or former alcohol consumption, overweight or obesity, a history of allergies, and a history of photosensitivity. Despite the substantial burden, only 5·8% (4·5-7·3) of affected individuals had sought medical care, and 18·2% (16·7-19·9) had used over-the-counter medications in the past year.
sections.conclusion: Skin diseases could affect more than half of Chinese adults. These findings highlight a substantial unmet need and should inform national priorities.

items.title: Novel dengue serotype 4 live virus human challenge: a phase 1 dose optimisation and homologous rechallenge study.

sections.objective: Dengue live virus human challenges (LVHCs) are key in dengue vaccine and pharmacological development, to down-select candidates and provide a useful platform for understanding viral-host immunology in a controlled setting. The primary aim of this study was to assess the safety, reactogenicity, and immunogenicity of a newly derived underattenuated dengue virus serotype-4-LVHC (DENV-4-LVHC) strain intended for future dengue challenge studies.
sections.methods: We conducted a first-in-human, phase 1, non-randomised, open-label study that evaluated the safety and optimised dose of the DENV-4-LVHC strain H-241 in flavivirus-naive healthy adult volunteers.
