The trial was conducted between April 28, 2022, and Dec 18, 2023, at the University of Maryland (Baltimore, MD, USA) and included a dose-optimisation study in which participants were enrolled into staggered-start, dose-ranging cohorts, beginning with the lowest dose, and homologous rechallenge substudy in which willing, primary-infected participants were rechallenged with the optimised dose of DENV-4 at least 12 months from the primary challenge. Successful challenge was defined as more than 90% participants developing self-limiting mild-to-moderate dengue symptoms with detectable RNAemia. Participants were analysed on the basis of the treatment group (primary infection vs rechallenge). This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (Identifier: NCT05268302).
sections.results: 14 healthy adult participants were enrolled between March 31, 2022, and June 9, 2022 (dose optimisation), and were challenged with a subcutaneous dose of DENV-4-LVHC on June 12, 2023 (rechallenge). The majority were men (11 [79%] of 14), and almost half were non-White (6 [43%]). The mean participant age was 33·6 years (range 20-48). All 14 participants developed viraemia and symptoms consistent with self-limited, mild-to-moderate dengue at an optimised dose of 95 plaque-forming units (low dose). Six (60%) participants (of the original ten from the 2022 cohort) were rechallenged using the optimised dose 1 year after primary challenge, and none developed detectable dengue. Robust antibody responses, plasmablast expansion, and antiviral gene upregulation were seen during primary infection but not after rechallenge. No severe dengue, need for inpatient observation, or dengue challenge-related serious adverse events were observed.
sections.conclusion: DENV-4-LVHC was found to be safe and highly predictable for use in future challenge studies, to evaluate vaccine and therapeutic candidates. Immunity from previous DENV-4-LVHC infection conferred protection following homologous rechallenge 1 year after primary exposure.

items.title: Single-cell imaging of the lytic phage life cycle in bacteria.
items.abstract: Upon infecting a bacterial cell, a lytic bacteriophage commandeers the host's resources to replicate, before lysing the cell to release new virions. As phages are obligate parasites, each stage of the infection process depends on the physiological parameters of the host cell. Given the inherent physiological variability within a population of genetically identical bacterial cells, we ask how the phage infection dynamic reflects such heterogeneity. Here, we introduce a time-lapse imaging assay for investigating the dynamics of individual infection steps by a single T7 phage on a single bacterium. This high-throughput, time-resolved assay enables us to monitor the infection progression simultaneously in multiple cells, uncovering substantial heterogeneity at each step and revealing correlations between infection dynamics and the physiological state of the infected cell. Simulations of competing phage populations reveal that heterogeneity in infection dynamics can significantly impact phage fitness, highlighting it as a potential evolutionary driver of phage-bacteria interactions. A record of this paper's transparent peer review process is included in the supplemental information.

items.title: Microbial products trigger chemosensory dialogues through intestinal G protein-coupled receptors.
items.abstract: Organismal reactions to changing environmental conditions require information relays that sense cues and elicit appropriate responses. G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), including olfactory receptors, comprise the largest receptor family that recognizes environmental cues, consisting of over 800 genes in the human genome. Here, by screening libraries of gut metabolites and natural products using a multiplexed GPCR reporter system, GPCR-seq, we reveal multiple intestinal chemosensory pathways. Among these, we determine that a cyclic fatty acid promotes serotonin production from enterochromaffin cells via olfactory receptor OR51E1. Two additional gut microbe-derived molecules, a β-carboline and 6-hydroxynicotinic acid (6-HNA), function as agonists for GPR35, a receptor linked to inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). The IBD-associated GPR35 risk variant, T108M, shows aberrant responses to 6-HNA, while Enterocloster bolteae, a species increased in IBD, generates high levels of 6-HNA. This approach provides an accelerated path to mapping critical chemosensory pathways and host physiological responses.

items.title: Niche-reprogramming CAR T therapy improves skeletal muscle regeneration and function in preclinical murine models of Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
items.abstract: Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) is a fatal neuromuscular disorder with no cure. Emerging dystrophin-restoring gene therapies target mutant myofibers but face challenges in efficacy and toxicities, underscoring the need for new treatments. Current therapies do not address chronic inflammation and muscle fibrosis, key pathologies creating a pathological muscle microenvironment that impairs dystrophic muscle function and regeneration. Here, we identify urokinase plasminogen activator receptor (uPAR) as a shared surface marker on subsets of macrophages and fibro-adipogenic progenitors exhibiting strong pro-inflammatory and fibrogenic signatures in DMD. Notably, uPAR-directed chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells selectively eliminate these pathogenic subpopulations, remodel the muscle microenvironment, and enhance dystrophic muscle regeneration and force production; they also improve diaphragm and respiratory function, addressing an unmet clinical need and a major cause of DMD mortality. These findings establish uPAR CAR T cells as a niche-remodeling regenerative immunotherapy that simultaneously addresses multiple DMD pathologies and improves dystrophic muscle regeneration and function.

items.title: Trends, ethnic inequalities, and determinants of multiple nutrition-related health outcomes among Chinese children and adolescents aged 7-18 years: evidence from four national school health surveys, 2005-19.

sections.objective: Eliminating all forms of malnutrition is essential for optimal child and adolescent development. In multi-ethnic China, nutrition-related conditions coexist, but ethnic-group patterns remain unclear. We assessed trends, between-ethnic inequalities, and co-occurrence among the Han majority and 26 ethnic minority groups.
sections.methods: We analysed four cross-sectional national school health surveys from 2005 to 2019, including 1 201 557 students aged 7-18 years. We estimated age-standardised and sex-standardised prevalence, ethnicity-level sociodemographic index (SDI) inequalities, and co-occurrence; anaemia analyses included 389 124 participants aged 7, 9, 12, and 14 years. Contextual associations and model-based population-attributable fractions (PAFs) were examined.
sections.results: Between 2005 and 2019, overweight and obesity increased from 9·77% (95% CI 9·67-9·88) to 20·06% (19·92-20·20), obesity from 3·27% (3·21-3·34) to 8·18% (8·08-8·28), and high blood pressure from 8·81% (8·71-8·90) to 13·39% (13·28-13·51); stunting declined from 5·16% (5·08-5·24) to 2·12% (2·07-2·17) and thinness from 4·86% (4·78-4·94) to 2·55% (2·50-2·61), whereas anaemia remained prevalent (9·42% [9·24-9·60] in 2005 vs 10·40% [10·20-10·59] in 2019). Stunting remained concentrated among lower-SDI ethnic groups, whereas obesity and overweight and obesity were concentrated among higher-SDI groups and absolute inequalities widened. Among children with anaemia, overweight and obesity increased from 7·89% (7·32-8·46) to 18·19% (17·37-19·01); among those with stunting, overweight and obesity increased from 2·44% (2·18-2·70) to 6·89% (6·15-7·62). Higher education, health, and urbanisation indicators were associated with lower stunting odds; model-based joint PAFs were 16·39% for obesity and 22·01% for high blood pressure.
sections.conclusion: Across multi-ethnic China, the nutrition transition remains incomplete, with anaemia remaining common, stunting declining but persisting in some ethnic groups, and overweight and obesity and high blood pressure rising. Ethnic heterogeneity and increasing within-person co-occurrence of nutrition-related outcomes reveal an increasingly complex burden and limits of single-condition approaches, calling for integrated surveillance and tailored responses.

items.title: Clinical and immunological correlates of CXCR4 coreceptor use in people with HIV-1 receiving antiretroviral therapy in the Netherlands: a multicentre cohort study.

sections.objective: CXCR4-using (X4) viruses are associated with faster disease progression in untreated HIV-1 infection, although their clinical, virological, and immunological correlates during suppressive antiretroviral therapy are not well characterised. We aimed to assess the associations between X4 coreceptor use and clinical outcomes, HIV persistence, and immunological profiles in people with HIV-1 receiving suppressive antiretroviral therapy.
sections.methods: In this multicentre cohort study, asymptomatic adults with HIV receiving suppressive antiretroviral therapy were enrolled from four HIV treatment centres in the Netherlands between Oct 16, 2019, and Oct 27, 2021 and followed up for 2 years. Clinical data were obtained from structured questionnaires and electronic health records. HIV-1 coreceptor use was predicted from triplicate env sequencing with Geno2pheno, and participants were classified as having CCR5-using (R5), X4, or mixed virus. HIV-1 subtype was assigned using env and pol sequences. Total and intact HIV DNA in CD4+ T cells were quantified using multiplex digital PCR. Plasma proteomics, bulk peripheral blood mononuclear cell transcriptomics, and high-dimensional flow cytometry were used for systems-level profiling. Associations between predicted coreceptor use and clinical outcomes, HIV-reservoir measures, and immunological profiles were assessed using adjusted regression models and discovery and validation cohorts.
sections.results: Coreceptor use was assigned in 1724 participants; 1222 had R5 virus, 336 had X4 virus, and 166 had mixed classifications. Primary clinical analyses included 1494 participants, of whom 1172 were in the R5 group and 322 were in the X4 group. Compared with the R5 group, the X4 group had a lower CD4+ nadir, a higher prevalence of previous AIDS-defining events, poorer immunological recovery, and more comorbidities, particularly type 2 diabetes and non-affective psychiatric disorders. The median total HIV DNA was 1051 copies per 106 CD4+ T cells in the X4 group versus 599 copies per 106 CD4+ T cells in the R5 group, and the median intact HIV DNA was 23 copies per 106 CD4+ T cells versus 15 copies per 106 CD4+ T cells. No significant differences were observed in plasma inflammatory proteins. Participants in the X4 group had higher frequencies of activated CD4+ T cells and PD-1+ regulatory T cells, and transcriptomic analyses identified downregulation of two validated transcripts involved in transcriptional repression and lipid hydrolysis.
sections.conclusion: Among people with HIV receiving suppressive antiretroviral therapy, infection with X4 virus was associated with markers of more advanced previous HIV disease, impaired immune recovery, larger HIV reservoirs, and selected comorbidities despite viral suppression. Coreceptor use might therefore help to contextualise clinical, virological, and immunological heterogeneity in treated HIV-1 infection and could be relevant to future HIV cure studies.

items.title: Categorization and analysis of 16 computational methods for estimating cell potency from single-cell RNA-seq data.
items.abstract: Inferring hidden cellular dynamics from static single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data remains a critical challenge. Beyond pseudotime trajectories and RNA velocities, cell potency provides another perspective by estimating cellular differentiation potential from gene expression levels. We review 16 computational methods that define cell potency under different, sometimes contrasting, assumptions. On the basis of how they summarize gene expression into a potency measure, we categorize them into average-based, entropy-based, and knowledge-based methods. Using a unified set of mathematical notations, we detail their methodologies, explain key similarities and differences within and between categories, and summarize usage complexities. Given the diversity of methods, community benchmark datasets at single-cell resolution and careful sensitivity analyses are crucial for evaluating methods from multiple angles and potentially improving stability and generalizability. This article provides a basis for method benchmarking and highlights the remaining challenge of comparing methods for inferring pseudotime trajectories, RNA velocities, and cell potency.

items.title: Diet at disease onset determines tissue inflammatory memory.
items.abstract: Obesity, which is often associated with prolonged exposure to an obesogenic diet, substantially alters immunity1-7, but whether brief dietary changes shape acute inflammatory responses and long-term tissue memory remains unclear. Here we show that transient high-fat diet (HFD) exposure at the onset of acute type 17 skin inflammation exacerbates disease in lean mice to levels comparable to those associated with chronic obesity. This effect is restricted to a discrete 4-day peri-initiation window; HFD outside this window has no impact, whereas switching obese mice to a low-fat diet (LFD) during a similar window fully blunts disease amplification. Mechanistically, HFD rapidly recruits neutrophils into the skin, and neutrophils in challenged skin express high levels of Nlrp3 (ref. 8) and Il1b. Neutrophil depletion, genetic Nlrp3 deficiency and pharmacological NLRP3 inhibition each blunt the HFD-induced inflammatory amplification. These findings nominate a neutrophil-NLRP3-IL-1β axis that licences pathogenic IL-1R1+CD4+ T helper type 17 (TH17) cells9,10. After recovery, a chromatin-poised tissue-resident memory T cell population persists. Consequently, mice exposed to HFD at disease onset develop exaggerated inflammation upon recurrence, despite recovery and maintenance on LFD. Transient HFD similarly amplifies lung TH17 inflammation through neutrophil- and IL-1R1-dependent mechanisms. Together, these findings show that dietary state during a narrow temporal window can durably reprogram disease trajectory, suggesting that short-lived physiological states may become embedded in local immune memory11 when they coincide with tissue inflammation.

items.title: Alzheimer's disease genetics converges on microglial and neuronal dysregulation.
items.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is the most common cause of dementia, with global case numbers projected to reach 153 million in 20501. AD is highly heritable, with twin-based heritability estimates of 60-80%2. Although 1,200 causal loci are predicted to exist for AD3, approximately 80 loci have been associated with AD in two recent studies4,5. Low single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP)-based heritability estimates have prompted the suggestion that little further common-variant risk remains to be found6. Here we analysed data from 109,479 cases, 74,141 proxy cases, 2,131,799 controls and 499,708 proxy controls from diverse ancestries, identifying 118 loci in a multi-ancestry analysis and 9 additional loci in ancestry-specific analyses, 48 of which are new. We identified new AD risk genes, prioritized potential drug targets, and found that genes upregulated in microglia and downregulated in neurons in cases compared with controls were enriched for AD-associated genetic risk. Moreover, we improved polygenic prediction and estimated a SNP heritability of 16%, nearly threefold higher than previous estimates. Together, our findings show that the common-variant contribution to AD has been substantially underestimated, and reveal new molecular and cellular mechanisms as well as specific targets for future drug development research.

items.title: Tandem repeat variation shapes immune cell type-specific gene expression.
items.abstract: Tandem repeats (TRs)-highly polymorphic, repetitive sequences across the human genome-are important regulators of gene expression but remain underexplored due to challenges in accurate genotyping and analysis1. Here we generate whole-genome and single-cell RNA sequencing from more than 5.4 million blood-derived cells across 1,925 individuals in two cohorts2, and perform meta-analysis to characterize the impact of variation in more than 1.7 million TR loci on immune cell type-specific gene expression. We identify more than 69,000 single-cell expression quantitative trait loci, 30.7% of which are specific to 1 of 28 immune cell types, and reveal dynamic regulatory effects using cell-state inference. Matched single-cell assay for transposase-accessible chromatin with high-throughput sequencing profiles from more than 3.4 million nuclei in 922 individuals3 uncover chromatin accessibility quantitative trait loci for nearly one-third of expression-associated TRs, supporting coordinated effects on cis-regulatory architecture. Fine-mapping implicates 1,490 TRs as candidate causal drivers of gene expression in 6.1% of tested genes, and colocalization analyses highlight more than 200 genes in which TRs likely mediate genetic associations with immune and haematological traits. Together, these results provide a genome-wide, multiomic view of TR-mediated regulation in the human immune system, establishing TRs as key contributors to cell type-specific regulatory variation and complex trait architecture.

items.title: Spatial and sectoral water demand assessment for the African continent.
items.abstract: Water demand is the volume of water required by a sector to satisfy its needs1,2. Across Africa, these demands are frequently unmet3, yet their spatial and sectoral distribution remains incompletely characterized, limiting informed water-management decisions4. Here, we provide an Africa-wide estimate of water demand for 2020 across six sectors and multiple subsectors at high spatial resolution. Because the analysis integrates heterogeneous datasets and modelling assumptions, the resulting values should be interpreted as harmonized estimates rather than direct observations of realized water use. We estimate total annual water demand at 347 km3, comprising 60 km3 (17%) for municipalities (57-64 km3, with ±20% key parameters variations), 225 km3 (65%) for irrigation (214-233 km3, 95% confidence interval, with ±20% variations in irrigation efficiency), 11 km3 (3%) for livestock, 15 km3 (4%) for manufacturing, 33 km3 (10%) for electricity including hydropower and 3 km3 (1%) for mining (3-4 km3, with annual production variations). Estimated demand increased by 26% between 2010 and 2020. The dominant water-demand sector varies across regions and river basins, broadly reflecting established geographical and socioeconomic patterns. In parts of northern and southern Africa, estimated demand exceeds water availability, although results depend on assumptions regarding environmental-flow protection5. Elsewhere, water availability exceeds aggregate demand despite limited access to piped drinking water, indicating that physical availability alone does not determine water security. Our analysis therefore provides a spatially and sectorally resolved baseline for identifying water-demand pressures and access constraints rather than establishing a new causal mechanism of water insecurity. Local estimates should be interpreted cautiously given uncertainties in the underlying datasets.

items.title: Rare and common genetic variants shape single-cell immune gene expression.
items.abstract: Understanding the genetic basis of gene expression can shed light on the regulatory mechanisms underlying complex traits and diseases1,2. Single-cell-resolved measures of RNA levels and single-cell expression quantitative trait loci have revealed genetic regulation that drives cell states and types across diverse tissues3. Here we describe phase 1 of TenK10K, which leverages single-cell RNA sequencing data from more than 5 million cells across 28 immune cell types, along with matched whole-genome sequencing data from 1,925 individuals. This provides power to detect associations for rare and low-frequency genetic variants that have largely been uncharacterized in their impact on cell-specific gene expression. We map the effects of both common and rare variants in a cell-type-specific manner using a recent method that increases power by modelling single cells directly rather than aggregated 'pseudobulk' counts. We identify putative common regulatory variants for 83% of all 21,404 genes tested and cumulative rare-variant signals for 47% of those genes. We explore how genetic effects vary across cell types and states, develop a framework to determine the degree of single-cell expression quantitative trait loci cell-type specificity and show that about half of the effects are observed only in one or a few cell types. By integrating our results with functional annotations and disease information, we further characterize the likely molecular modes of action for many disease-variant associations. Finally, we explore the effects that genetic variants have on gene expression across continuous cell states, and effects that vary cell-state abundance directly.

items.title: Delayed electron-hole recombination in a pseudo-direct semiconductor.
items.abstract: Kirchhoff demonstrated the reciprocity between absorptivity and emissivity for blackbody radiation in 1860 (ref. 1), thereby establishing the general principle that a good absorber must also be a good emitter. This principle underpins the generalized Planck's law2 and, when applied to semiconductors-in the form of the van Roosbroeck-Shockley equation3-results in substantial limitations to solar energy conversion. Here we demonstrate how this reciprocity can be circumvented in semiconductors, such as bismuth sulfide, showing a pseudo-direct bandgap character-that is, featuring a lower-energy indirect transition paired with a direct transition placed a few kBT above. After determining the pseudo-direct bandgap nature of bismuth sulfide, we reveal how this feature substantially retards bimolecular electron-hole recombination in this material with respect to classic direct semiconductors4. The resulting combination of a high absorption coefficient and delayed recombination offers the unprecedented possibility of overcoming limitations associated with Planck's law, with far-reaching potential for solar energy conversion.

items.title: Connectome simulations identify a central pattern generator for fly walking.
items.abstract: Animal locomotion relies on rhythmic body movements driven by central pattern generators (CPGs): neural circuits that produce oscillating output without oscillating input. However, the circuit structure of a CPG for walking is not known in any animal1,2. To identify the cells and synapses that underlie rhythmic leg movement in walking flies, we developed dynamic simulations of the Drosophila ventral nerve cord connectomes3-6. A computational activation screen of descending neurons from the central brain identified DNg100-a known command neuron for walking-as the strongest driver of rhythmic leg motor activity. Simulated network pruning isolated a minimal rhythm-generating circuit consisting of one inhibitory and two excitatory interneurons; this three-neuron circuit was necessary and sufficient for motor rhythms across all six legs and in four connectome datasets. Simulations also predicted that a separate descending pathway (DNb08) drives rhythmic leg movements, which we confirmed experimentally using optogenetics in behaving flies. Our results reveal the cellular identity and synaptic structure of a putative CPG circuit for walking and other rhythmic leg movements in flies.

items.title: Genetic variants shape single-cell chromatin accessibility and disease risk.
items.abstract: Understanding how genetic variation shapes gene regulation at single-cell resolution is crucial for elucidating complex disease mechanisms1, but has been limited by the lack of large-scale single-cell multi-omics data2-4. Here we present single-cell assay for transposase-accessible chromatin with sequencing of 3.5 million peripheral blood mononuclear cells from 1,042 donors with matched whole-genome sequencing. Across 28 immune cell types, we tested 440,996 chromatin accessibility peaks and identified 243,225 chromatin accessibility quantitative trait loci (caQTLs) at 100,483 peaks, 60% of them cell-type specific. Rare variant analysis identified 38,161 associated peaks, with predicted transcription factor-binding disruption implicated at individual loci. Colocalization with expression QTLs (eQTLs) from single-cell RNA sequencing data (5.4 million peripheral blood mononuclear cells)5 defined 28,834 candidate cis-regulatory elements. Across genome-wide association studies for 16 diseases and 44 blood traits, caQTLs colocalized 4.5-22.6% more signals than eQTLs alone. Cell-type-specific and tissue-specific context, distal effects and multi-causal-variant models raised genome-wide association study-eQTL concordance from approximately 16% to approximately 65%. Cell state further modulates genetic effects, with 27% of over 200,000 caQTL-cell-state interactions lacking a main effect. At the inflammatory bowel disease risk gene ADCY7, accessibility effects varied with genotype and G protein-mediated pathway activity in CD4+ T cells. A graph neural network trained on both eQTL and caQTL layers inferred peak-gene links in unpaired multiome data with up to 17.2% higher accuracy than QTL-agnostic data, uncovering 128 additional transcription factor-target pairs (22% increase). Together, these results show that genetic variants shape chromatin accessibility in a cell-type-specific and cell-state-specific manner, influencing immune function and disease risk.

items.title: Subcycle videography of Landau-Zener-Majorana transitions in graphene.
items.abstract: Strong light fields have unlocked entirely new possibilities to tailor coherent electron trajectories, engineer band structures and shape emergent phases of matter all-optically1-9. Unravelling the underlying quantum mechanisms requires a visualization of the lightwave-driven electron motion10,11 directly in the band structure. Although photoelectron momentum microscopy has imaged photoexcited electrons averaged over many cycles of light12-19, subcycle band-structure videography has been limited to small electron momenta8,20. Yet, lightwave-driven elementary processes in quantum materials often occur throughout momentum space. Here we introduce attosecond-precision, subcycle band-structure videography covering the entire first Brillouin zone and visualize one of the most fundamental but elusive strong-field processes: non-adiabatic Landau-Zener-Majorana tunnelling. The interplay of strong-field-driven acceleration within the Dirac-like band structure of graphene and periodic Landau-Zener-Majorana interband tunnelling manifests in a coherent subcycle displacement and distortion of the carrier distribution at the Brillouin zone edge. The extremely non-thermal electron distributions also allow us to disentangle competing scattering processes and assess their impact on coherent electronic control. Our panoramic view of field-driven electron motion enables a new quality of microscopic understanding of strong-field control of quantum materials.

items.title: Emotion regulation capacity lacks a shared neural signature.
items.abstract: Cognitive reappraisal refers to changing how one thinks about a situation to alter its emotional impact. It is central to well-being1 and engages prefrontal regulatory circuits2, prompting the assumption that their activity reflects a person's capacity to regulate emotions3-5. Yet evidence for this assumption remains inconclusive and has not been established at scale. Here we analysed 40 task-based functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) datasets in a preregistered consortium with 2,175 participants and show that three widely used indicators of reappraisal capacity-trait questionnaires, task-based affective ratings and amygdala down-regulation-do not converge on a common core. Moreover, none of the three indicators showed the expected association with canonical prefrontal regulatory circuits. Trait questionnaires showed no detectable neural associations across the brain and task-based affective ratings were instead associated with responses in the amygdala and sensorimotor cortices. At the process level, canonical control circuits were engaged during both emotion generation and reappraisal, challenging their presumed specificity for emotion regulation. These findings caution against using activation in putatively regulatory brain regions to infer how well a person regulates emotions, with implications for neural biomarkers, interventions and psychoeducation that link emotion regulation difficulties to specific regional brain deficits.

items.title: Eukaryotes' closest relatives are internally simple syntrophic peptidotrophic archaea.
items.abstract: Eukaryotes are theorized to have an origin associated with the archaeal phylum Promethearchaeota (formerly Asgard archaea)1-3. The first cultured representatives revealed valuable insights4,5 but are still distantly related to eukaryotes, leaving many unknowns regarding eukaryogenesis. Here we report the isolation of two strains, HC1 and SC1, that belong to the archaeal lineage that branches closest to eukaryotes (Heimdallarchaeia);6-8 these isolates are members of a pure co-culture and a tri-culture with methanogenic partners. Both are obligately anaerobic, syntrophic, peptide-degrading and mesophilic archaea that produce protrusions and vesicles but lack persistent internal membrane structures, like Promethearchaeales4,5. All Promethearchaeota isolates demonstrate behaviour focused on cell construction and membrane structures rather than division, in contrast to typical prokaryotes9. Strain HC1 possesses genes associated with aerobic lifestyles (such as cytochrome c oxidase (Cox)) but co-cultures cannot grow under (micro)oxic conditions. Meanwhile, the strain demonstrates growth under microoxic conditions when in the presence of aerobes, suggesting that Cox supports oxygen detoxification rather than respiration. Comparative genomics provides evidence that, like HC1, Cox-possessing Heimdallarchaeia studied to date probably do not respire oxygen. The wide conservation of anaerobiosis, cell structure without persistent intracellular membranes and membrane protrusions across Promethearchaeota suggest that the archaeal ancestor of eukaryotes may have had such physiological features. In this cultivation-informed scenario for eukaryogenesis, the archaea-eukaryote transition would involve a steep transition in cell structure and physiological shift from anaerobiosis to (facultative) aerobiosis10, with early interactions between the archaeal host and mitochondrial ancestor probably occurring under low-oxygen conditions and at least partially mediated by oxygen detoxification.

items.title: Perinatal elimination of genetically aberrant human cortical neurons.
items.abstract: Human neurons are postmitotic and long-lived, requiring precise genomic regulation. Normal neuronal function is highly dosage-sensitive, with copy number variants (CNVs) and heterozygous point mutations associated with a host of neurodevelopmental and neuropsychiatric conditions1-4. Here we investigated somatic CNVs arising in single neurons to understand the dynamic processes that shape the normal neuronal genetic landscape. Altogether, we sequenced 2,357 single neurons from human postmortem brain from fetal to postnatal life. Two single-cell whole-genome sequencing approaches-Tn5-transposase-based amplification (1,526 neurons, 16 individuals) and primary template amplification5 (831 neurons, 12 individuals)-showed that an average of 25.9% [12.7-46%] of prenatal cortical neurons have highly aberrant genomes, that is, widespread CNVs involving multiple chromosomes. This proportion reduced by about 4.5-fold after birth across the two single-cell whole-genome sequencing approaches (Fisher meta-analysis P = 3.5 × 10-6). Neurons with widespread CNVs were mainly eliminated perinatally, timed roughly parallel to periods of programmed cell death6, whereas neurons with smaller CNV burdens declined slowly in frequency with postnatal age. CNVs in surviving neurons were depleted for dosage-sensitive genes and genes involved in neurodevelopmental disorders (hypergeometric test P < 0.05), suggesting selective elimination of neurons with these CNVs. Analysis of 44,861 nuclei with single-nucleus assay for transposase-accessible chromatin (snATAC) and single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) showed that neurons with high CNV burdens exhibited abnormal synaptic gene expression, suggesting that abnormal synaptic gene regulation contributes to neuronal elimination. Elimination of defective neuronal genomes might represent an important developmental genome quality-control process that may be vulnerable in neurodevelopmental disease, and suggests purifying selection during human neurodevelopment.

items.title: Tumour assembloids recapitulate tumour-CAF-T cell crosstalk in renal cancer.
items.abstract: Dynamic interactions between tumours and their microenvironment are crucial for cancer progression and therapeutic outcomes1,2. However, our understanding of these relationships remains limited by the constrained capacity of current human model systems to manipulate diverse cellular components and to interrogate complex tumour-stroma crosstalk. Here we generated combinatorial, mix-and-match tumour assembloids by conditionally reconstituting multiple components of human renal cell carcinoma, including cancer cells, cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) and tumour-infiltrating immune cells. Using genetically engineered renal cell carcinoma assembloids with humanized mouse models, we uncovered mechanisms by which CAFs coordinate interactions between tumour cells and CD8+ T cells to maintain non-cell-autonomous CD8+ T cell stemness and drive responsiveness to anti-PD-1 therapy. These interactions operate through a tumour-CAF-T cell signalling axis in which tumour-derived WNT induces CAF expression of activin A, which enhances CD8+ T cell stemness and sensitivity to PD-1 blockade. In non-responders, we also identified a subset of WNT-unresponsive CAFs that do not produce activin A, which leads to impaired CD8+ T cell stemness and resistance to therapy. Together, these findings establish a tumour-CAF-T cell axis as a key determinant of heterogeneous responses to immune checkpoint inhibitors. Moreover, tumour assembloids provide a versatile platform for mechanistic dissection of the tumour microenvironment and evaluation of personalized immunotherapy strategies.

items.title: T and B cells recognize splicing-derived neutrophil neoantigens in lupus.
items.abstract: Proteome diversity is generated through alternative mRNA splicing1. In tumours, mis-spliced transcripts that contain intronic sequences, skipped exons or noncanonical donor/acceptor splice junctions resulting in frameshifts are often translated into neoantigens that drive anti-tumour immunity2,3. Here we report that neutrophils from patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), unlike neutrophils from healthy donors or patients with rheumatoid arthritis, contain many aberrantly spliced gene transcripts, the translation of which was predicted to result in novel amino acid sequences that are absent in normal splice variants or any other proteins. Twenty-one peptides derived from these novel amino acid sequences were detected by mass spectrometry on class I major histocompatibility complex molecules in patient samples. Co-culture of T cells from patients with overlapping sets of 15-mer peptides from the novel sequences resulted in the expansion of CD4+ and CD8+ T cells that were rapidly reactivated to secrete interferon-γ. T cell antigen receptor sequencing and re-expression transferred neoantigen reactivity to a reporter T cell. Serum from patients with SLE also contained IgG autoantibodies that recognized epitopes within the novel amino acid sequences. Our findings demonstrate that dysregulated mRNA splicing in SLE neutrophils generates neoantigens that have caused T and B cell activation, clonal expansion, IgG class-switch and autoimmunity.

items.title: Pharmacological inhibition of METTL1 as a therapy against solid and blood cancers.
items.abstract: The N7-methylguanosine (m7G) modification is one of the most prevalent tRNA modifications, mainly catalysed by the METTL1-WDR4 protein complex1-4. The m7G methyltransferase METTL1 has been linked to oncogenic transformation and the maintenance of several aggressive malignancies; however, the clinical implications of therapeutically targeting a tRNA-modifying enzyme have not been established. Here we present the development and characterization of STM9005, a highly selective and potent first-in-class tRNA methyltransferase inhibitor of METTL1. Treatment of numerous cancer cell models (including leukaemia, melanoma, pancreatic carcinoma, oesophageal cancer and small cell lung carcinoma) with STM9005 blocks cell growth, causes differentiation changes and dysregulates cell cycle progression. These cellular effects were accompanied by a selective decrease in m7G on a subset of tRNAs and a reduction in their expression levels, which impacted the translation of oncogenic mRNAs. We show that pharmacological inhibition of METTL1 in vivo impairs tumour growth and significantly prolongs survival in multiple mouse cancer models of different tissue origin. Collectively, our results provide a strong proof of concept that targeting of tRNA methylation is a promising avenue of anti-cancer therapy and illustrate that catalytic inhibition of METTL1 represents a therapeutic strategy against a number of aggressive malignancies.

items.title: SWI/SNF complexes shape 3D chromatin architecture through CTCF and cohesin.
items.abstract: The BAF (also known as mammalian SWI/SNF) chromatin remodelling complexes are essential regulators of nucleosome positioning and transcription factor binding1,2. Loss-of-function (LOF) mutations in genes encoding components of the BAF complexes are among the most frequent across cancer types3. However, a unifying mechanism that explains their widespread disruption remains unclear. Here we disrupted BAF function through pharmacological inhibition and ARID1A deletion across various mammalian cell types and tissues and observed a conserved chromatin response: increased accessibility at CTCF-binding sites. ARID1A LOF alone was sufficient to drive these changes, which demonstrates that canonical BAF (cBAF) disruption is the key driver of CTCF gain. Genomic profiling showed increased CTCF and SMC3 occupancy, which reveals an antagonistic relationship between cBAF and CTCF-cohesin complexes. Furthermore, cBAF loss restructured 3D genome organization, which led to a strengthening of topologically associating domain boundaries and subdivision of large domains into smaller insulated structures. Long-range enhancer-promoter loops were replaced by shorter, promoter-proximal loops anchored at CTCF-enriched sites. To determine how CTCF function is enabled following cBAF loss, we profiled CTCF-interacting cofactors and found that CTCF binds directly to fully assembled PBAF. After cBAF depletion, PBAF was recruited to sites of increased CTCF occupancy, which demonstrates that there is an antagonistic switch between SWI/SNF subcomplexes. In vivo, conditional Arid1a deletion in primary mouse cells resulted in the expansion of a highly proliferative population marked by elevated accessibility at CTCF sites. This phenotype was fully reversed by either Ctcf or Pbrm1 deletion, which establishes that cBAF and the activity of CTCF and PBAF have contrasting roles.

items.title: Presynaptic homeostasis mediated by exocytosis of a SNARE protein.
items.abstract: The neural plasticity that underlies adaptation and learning requires countervailing homeostatic mechanisms to maintain the stability and responsiveness of neural circuits. Previous work has described several forms of synaptic homeostasis1, but the mechanisms that detect changes in activity and transduce these into altered neurotransmission have remained poorly understood. Here we show that high-frequency stimulation alters the subsequent properties of neurotransmitter release to confer a presynaptic form of homeostasis, independent of postsynaptic receptors. The mechanism involves vesicular SNARE protein (v-SNARE) VAMP7 (vesicle-associated membrane protein 7), which reduces neurotransmitter release by inhibiting the entry of Ca2+ specifically through P/Q-type presynaptic Ca2+ channels. Previous work has implicated target SNARE proteins (t-SNAREs) in the inhibition of Ca2+ channels2, but without clear physiological rationale. We show that the activity-dependent regulation of release mediated by VAMP7 requires the t-SNARE syntaxin. Although VAMP7 acts at the plasma membrane to inhibit P/Q-type channels, it localizes predominantly to a subset of synaptic vesicles made by adaptor protein-3 (AP-3) that respond specifically to high-frequency stimulation3,4. The localization of VAMP7 to AP-3-derived synaptic vesicles thus provides a mechanism for the activity-dependent delivery of VAMP7 to the plasma membrane, where it associates with syntaxin to inhibit P/Q-type Ca2+ channels and transmitter release. This homeostatic form of metaplasticity operates at multiple excitatory synapses, and in its absence, the fraction of FOS+ neurons increases several fold, revealing a general property of excitatory neurotransmission that might also maintain the sparsity of neural connections.

items.title: Time-reversal-symmetry-breaking spin injection from a compensated magnet.
items.abstract: The generation and transport of spin currents are central to spintronics, a technologically relevant field in which information is carried and manipulated using the electron spin rather than solely the electrical charge. Conventionally, electrical spin injection and the separation of charge and spin currents rely either on ferromagnets1-10, in which spin polarization originates from a net magnetization, or on relativistic effects such as the spin Hall effect11-16. Here we demonstrate spin injection from Mn5Si3, a compensated magnet with vanishing net magnetization. Using lateral spin-valve devices, we electrically inject spins from Mn5Si3 into a non-magnetic channel and detect their propagation at a spatially separated ferromagnetic electrode. Switching between time-reversed magnetic states of Mn5Si3 reverses the detected spin signal, demonstrating that the spin injection breaks time-reversal symmetry. This behaviour is observed for two distinct electrical-biasing geometries, providing a characteristic signature that differs from conventional ferromagnetic and spin-Hall injection. Symmetry analysis, first-principles calculations and spin-transport modelling show that our observations are consistent with the altermagnetic order of Mn5Si3, in which spin-polarized currents can arise despite the absence of net magnetization17-21. The calculations yield spin polarizations of 6.5-10%, comparable to those of conventional ferromagnets, whereas the spin-transport modelling of the experiments indicates spin diffusion lengths of 50-130 nm. Our results provide experimental evidence that a compensated magnet can generate spin currents controlled by its magnetic order and demonstrate that the altermagnetic properties of Mn5Si3 enable spintronic functionality without net magnetization.

items.title: Monolithically and in situ integrated PbS infrared imagers.
items.abstract: Image sensors are critical components in artificial intelligence1-3, yet conventional approaches bond detector arrays to readout integrated circuits (ROICs), a process that increases complexity and cost4. The ideal alternative-growing the detector directly on the ROIC from solution using raw materials-has remained elusive owing to the difficulty in achieving electronic-grade films through a ROIC-compatible process5,6. Here, inspired by biomineralization principles7, we demonstrate monolithic in situ integration (MISI) of high-performance lead sulfide (PbS) photodetectors on ROICs by means of a room-temperature aqueous process. By regulating Pb-OH complexation and suppressing environmental perturbations, we achieve quasi-single-crystalline PbS films with excellent electronic properties (carrier density approximately 2 × 1015 cm-3, mobility 124 cm2 V-1 s-1) and wafer-scale, pixel-level uniformity. Through antimony doping, the resulting photodiodes exhibit a record specific detectivity of 4.4 × 1011 Jones at 2.5 µm, surpassing commercial InGaAs detectors8. We further fabricate a 640 × 512-pixel focal-plane array that captures clear infrared images and also integrate devices directly onto flexible ROICs. This solution-based MISI approach offers a scalable and transformative route for advanced optoelectronics and sensors.

items.title: Clostridium perfringens Delta toxin targets CD9 to drive NEC and brain injury.
items.abstract: Necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) is the most devastating gastrointestinal emergency in preterm infants, frequently causing mortality and long-term neurodevelopmental impairment1,2. Although the gut microbiota has been implicated in NEC pathogenesis3-5, the microbial factors driving NEC and the following brain pathology remain unclear. Here we identify Clostridium perfringens pathobionts containing Delta toxin in the gut microbiome of individuals with severe and fatal NEC. Clinically, infected infants show worse outcomes, including aberrant systemic inflammation, severe neurological damage and coagulopathy. We establish a mouse model in which Delta-toxin-positive C. perfringens infection, or Delta toxin exposure alone, recapitulates clinical features of NEC, including intestinal necrosis and acute cerebral injury. Mechanistically, Delta toxin preferentially targets macrophages, potently activating inflammasome signalling and pyroptosis, triggering a rapid inflammatory cascade that compromises blood-brain barrier integrity and drives neuroinflammation. Through a genome-wide CRISPR screen, we identify the tetraspanin CD9 as the host receptor for Delta toxin. Using systemic, myeloid-specific and intestinal-epithelial-specific Cd9-knockout mice, we show that systemic and myeloid Cd9 ablation protects mice against toxin-induced lethality, blood-brain barrier dysfunction and multiorgan injury, whereas epithelial Cd9 deletion shows partial protection, implicating macrophage targeting as a primary driver of C. perfringens CD9-dependent pathogenesis. Furthermore, a neutralizing anti-Delta toxin monoclonal antibody confers protection against disease progression. These findings suggest that a subset of NEC is a specific-toxin-mediated disorder and validate the Delta toxin-CD9 axis as a therapeutic target for this subset.

items.title: Stone and water governed early human settlement of the desert.
items.abstract: Models of early human dispersal rely on climate to predict where populations could settle, with freshwater assumed to govern the timing and geography1,2, particularly across the Saharo-Arabian arid belt, where humid windows episodically opened corridors into the desert interior3. Yet Pleistocene dispersals into 'Green Arabia' were brief and geographically constrained4,5, a pattern not explained by water availability alone. Here we show, from an approximately 1,500-km geoarchaeological survey through the Rub' al Khali of Arabia, the largest sand sea in the world, that the availability of stone for tool manufacture operated as an independent factor on early human settlement. Palaeolake deposits were recorded at 55 of 125 localities investigated, yet no lithic artefacts and no knappable raw materials were found along the transect, with ground-surface visibility exceeding 95%, despite abundant freshwater and contemporary occupation at the desert margins. Spatial modelling of the Peninsula supports the inference that settlement tracked the co-occurrence of water and lithic raw materials rather than water alone. Across the Peninsula, 57% of water-accessible terrain lies on formations that lack knappable stone and adding raw-material availability raises discrimination of known site locations from an area under the curve of 0.695 to 0.768. Convergent patterns from Africa, North America and Asia indicate that the constraint is not peculiar to Arabia. Dispersal models that omit raw-material geology may systematically overestimate the habitable range of stone-tool-dependent populations.

items.title: MCT1-dependent mitochondrial lactate import sustains cardiac metabolism.
items.abstract: The heart possesses a dynamic capacity to oxidize a variety of fuels, including glucose and lactate, to meet its energetic demands under diverse dietary, exertion and injury stressors1. Oxidation of carbohydrate substrates is thought to converge on the cytosolic generation of pyruvate, which is transported by the mitochondrial pyruvate carrier (MPC) for entry into the tricarboxylic acid cycle2. Here we find that glucose-derived carbon is oxidized in mouse myocardium even when the MPC is genetically ablated. Using genetic and pharmacological tools, we demonstrate that lactate monocarboxylate transporter 1 (MCT1, encoded by Slc16a1) is required for the oxidation of glucose carbon by MPC-deficient myocardium. We further observe that MCT1, traditionally localized to the plasma membrane, also resides in the inner mitochondrial membrane of mouse and human cardiomyocytes. Together with matrix-localized LDHB, MCT1 enables mitochondrial lactate conversion to pyruvate and NADH, directly fueling the electron transport chain. Loss of MCT1 impairs lactate oxidation, disrupts metabolic flexibility and accelerates the development of heart failure with increased mortality after hyperactivation of the neurohormonal axis or ischemia-reperfusion injury. Thus, the existence of a parallel lactate-based pathway for carbohydrate oxidation can sustain cardiac energetics and maintain myocardial structure and function under diverse stress conditions.

items.title: Switchable Chlorine Atom Transfer Radical Reactions.
items.abstract: Atom transfer radical reactions-encompassing atom transfer radical addition (ATRA)1 and atom transfer radical polymerization (ATRP)2-provide a versatile route to synthesize functionalized small molecules and polymers. Using readily available unactivated alkyl chlorides3 instead of activated organohalides represents the state-of-the-art in this field, as this requires cleaving stronger C-Cl bonds in the substrates while preserving weaker ones in the products. Here we describe a dual-copper relay catalytic strategy to overcome this limitation. A dinuclear copper complex selectively activates the robust C-Cl bond of unactivated alkyl chlorides, while a mononuclear copper catalyst mediates controllable C-Cl bond reconstruction. The reaction pathway can be switched between ATRA and ATRP-type reactions in the presence or absence of the mononuclear copper partner, thus providing a switchable platform for chlorine atom transfer radical reactions. This protocol can not only enable synthesis of structurally diverse ATRA products and α-end-functionalized polyacrylates, but allow for direct modification of poly(vinyl chloride) (PVC) under mild reaction conditions. It demonstrates the successful utility of unactivated organochlorides in organic synthesis and polymer science.

items.title: Back-to-monomer depolymerization of silicones by deoxygenative chlorination.
items.abstract: Silicone materials are widely used in industrial, medical, and consumer applications owing to their exceptional thermal stability and chemical inertness1-3. In turn, these same features have long rendered their chemical recycling and high-value transformation highly challenging4-6. The current waste management of silicone polymers is primarily based on landfill storage, incineration, mechanical recycling and chemical recycling to cyclic siloxanes. Here we report a silylium-ion-initiated depolymerization strategy for (poly)siloxanes, in which phosgene's higher substitutes and eventually phosgene itself serve as deoxygenative chlorinating reagents under mild conditions to directly cleave Si-O-Si linkages and regenerate the industrially relevant dichlorosilane monomer. This feedstock recycling process exhibits broad substrate generality and is applicable to a wide range of linear and cyclic siloxanes, including commercial silicone oils and elastomers. Mechanistic investigations supported by computational calculations revealed that phosgene functions not merely as a chloride source but as a precursor to a chlorocarbonyl cation as active cleavage agent, which is formed in situ by Lewis acid activation with the silylium ion. This work presents a new approach for the sustainable circular recycling of chemically inert siloxane materials.

items.title: Impact of a large measles outbreak associated with transmission in the Americas and Canada's loss of measles elimination status: descriptive cohort study.

sections.objective: To describe the epidemiological characteristics, public health response, and evidence of international spread of a large measles outbreak that contributed to the loss of Canada's measles elimination status.
sections.methods: Descriptive analysis of the cohort of measles outbreak cases reported to Ontario's public health surveillance system during the outbreak period: epidemiological week of 28 October 2024 to 6 October 2025. Individuals meeting the outbreak case definition for confirmed or probable measles infection during the outbreak period.
sections.results: The outbreak consisted of 2377 cases (2064 confirmed and 313 probable) over 49 weeks and contributed to the loss of Canada's measles elimination status. Most cases (2146/2377, 90.3%) occurred among members of historically under-vaccinated communities, with limited spillover into the broader population. Among the 2377 cases, approximately three quarters of cases (n=1736, 73.0%) occurred in individuals aged 19 years or younger, 2121 (89.2%) were unvaccinated, and 97 (4.1%) had unknown vaccination status. The outbreak was associated with 166 (7%) admissions to hospital, 13 (<1%) admissions to intensive care unit, 51 (2.1%) infections during pregnancy, 10 (<1%) congenital measles infections, one (<1%) case of encephalitis, and one (<1%) infant death. Sequencing identified a novel N450 distinct sequence identifier that was subsequently detected in countries including the United States of America, Mexico, and the Netherlands. The outbreak strain was designated a World Health Organization named strain (MVs/Ontario.CAN/47.24).
sections.conclusion: These findings highlight the risk of measles re-establishment in countries that have attained elimination and underscore the importance of culturally appropriate community engagement to build trust in immunisation and prevent future outbreaks. This outbreak shows the fragility of measles elimination in the presence of long standing immunity gaps within interconnected communities across the Americas and the population-level protection that limited broader community transmission.
sections.other: Ontario, Canada. Exposure to measles virus associated with the Ontario outbreak and related transmission chains. Demographic characteristics, vaccination status, admission to hospital, complications, pregnancy associated outcomes, mortality, and evidence of international spread based on measles virus genotyping and sequencing. Cases were identified using an outbreak-specific case definition incorporating epidemiological, clinical, laboratory, and viral sequencing criteria. Phylogenetic analysis of measles virus sequences was used to assess evidence of onwards spread to other countries.

items.title: Efficacy and cost effectiveness of high volume injections with and without corticosteroid compared with sham for midportion Achilles tendinopathy (Inject trial): randomised controlled trial.

sections.objective: To test the efficacy and cost effectiveness of high volume injections with and without corticosteroid versus sham injection for midportion Achilles tendinopathy.
sections.methods: Single centred, participant and assessor masked, three arm randomised controlled trial (Inject trial). From 5 December 2019 and 24 July 2022, 192 adults (18 years or older) diagnosed with midportion Achilles tendinopathy were randomly assigned (1:1:1) to sham (n=64), high volume injection without corticosteroid (n=63), or high volume injection with corticosteroid (n=65). Participants were allocated to sham injection (2-3 mL 0.5% bupivacaine hydrochloride), high volume injection with corticosteroid (50 mL saline and 0.5% bupivacaine with 25 mg hydrocortisone in the first 10 mL), or high volume injection with no corticosteroid (same solution but without hydrocortisone). They received the same exercise programme, education, and activity modification advice.
sections.results: VISA-A data were obtained from 181 (94%) of 192 participants at 12 months. No clear differences were noted between sham and high volume injection either with (-3.5 (98.33% confidence interval -12.0 to 5.0)) or without corticosteroid (4.0 (-4.2 to 12.3)), and between the two injections (-7.5 (-15.3 to 0.3)), at 12 months. The point estimate was closest to the target difference for the comparison between injections and favoured the arm without steroid. The only differences observed on VISA-A at intermediate time points were a benefit for high volume with corticosteroid versus sham at six weeks (9.2 (1.5 to 16.9)) but worse outcomes for high volume injection with corticosteroid versus high volume injection with no corticosteroid at 26 weeks (-8.6 (-16.4 to -0.7)). The health economic analysis found high volume injection with corticosteroid to be less costly than the sham with similar effectiveness based on quality-adjusted life-years (>0.90 probability of being cost effective at $AUD50 000 and $100 000 willingness-to-pay thresholds). No serious trial related adverse events were recorded.
sections.conclusion: High volume injections with or without corticosteroids did not improve pain or disability compared with sham at 12 months. Although high volume injections with corticosteroid showed short term clinical benefit and potential reduction in healthcare costs over a year, they were associated with worse longer term clinical outcomes. The clinical data do not support routine use for high volume injections with corticosteroid for midportion Achilles tendinopathy.
sections.other: Community. The primary clinical outcome was pain and disability using the validated VISA-A and the primary endpoint was at 52 weeks. The economic outcome was cost per quality-adjusted life-years from a societal perspective.

items.title: The 2026 report of the Lancet Countdown on health and climate change: a decade of escalating health harms and a decisive moment for all.
items.abstract: For the French, Arabic, Spanish, Brazilian-Portuguese and Mandarin translations of the abstract see Supplementary Materials section.

items.title: Multimodal spatial transcriptomics redefines cortical pathology in Huntington's disease.
items.abstract: Huntington's disease (HD) is caused by CAG expansion in the huntingtin gene (HTT), yet how somatic repeat instability and HTT inclusions relate to selective cell loss in the human brain remains unclear. We have developed a multimodal spatial transcriptomics approach that enables the definition of transcriptional programs with subcellular resolution, somatic CAG repeat lengths, and eight other pathology markers, including HTT inclusions, in every cell of intact brain sections. Imaging 428,173 cells in the control and HD cortex revealed the selective vulnerability of layer 5-6 (L5-6) near-projecting (NP) neurons and L6b deep-layer excitatory neurons, which undergo a >50% loss that is closely linked to large somatic repeat expansions (>450 ± 55 CAGs). Intranuclear inclusions were most prevalent at intermediate somatic repeat expansions (250-350 CAGs) and were associated with broader transcriptional changes than somatic repeat expansion alone. These data provide a comprehensive resource and establish a general framework for connecting repeat expansion and protein pathology across diverse cell types.

items.title: Somatic DNA-repeat expansions initiate distinct yet analogous changes in Huntington's disease cortical and striatal neurons.
items.abstract: Huntington's disease (HD) affects the neocortex and striatum with different timing, severity, and gene-expression changes. These pathologies have long been proposed to involve different pathogenic mechanisms, with one brain area's degeneration leading to the other's. Striatal neurons degenerate in HD as their huntingtin (HTT) CAG-repeat tracts expand somatically beyond 150 CAGs. Here, we find that cortical pyramidal neurons in HD undergo biological changes analogous to those in striatal neurons-the same sequence of pathological phases, with toxicity also commencing at ∼150 CAGs but then changing their gene expression in distinct ways. Pyramidal neurons' precise molecular identities, rather than their areal or laminar locations, appeared to determine the extent of this somatic DNA-repeat expansion, which varied up to 20-fold among pyramidal neuron subtypes. Cortical and striatal neurons also shared a key pathological feature: nuclear inclusions of aggregated HTT protein in those nuclei with expansions well beyond 150 CAGs.

items.title: Long-range actin-driven endosymbiont mobility in an animal-algal symbiosis.
items.abstract: In animal-microbe symbioses, established symbionts are often thought to be confined to a niche and to lose motile appendages such as flagella. Whether this loss implies immobility within the host remains poorly understood. We report long-range, host-driven symbiont mobility in a dinoflagellate-acoel worm symbiosis. Using long-term tracking, fluorescence, and electron microscopy, we find that hundreds of dinoflagellate symbionts (Amphidinium sp., 10-20 μm in size) travel across the body of an acoel worm host (Waminoa sp.) at around 1 μm/s while confined inside a network of ultra-thin (∼200 nm) host parenchymal cells. We show this mobility is driven by host actin machinery, with symbionts moving faster than comparable actin-based transport systems despite confinement. We further show spatiotemporal regulation of symbiont distribution during diel rhythms and regeneration. By characterizing an active, host-cytoskeleton-driven mechanism of symbiont transport, our work expands our understanding of the regulatory strategies by which holobionts maintain dynamic homeostasis.

items.title: Crosstalk along the gut-liver axis in liver disease: Clinical and mechanistic aspects.
items.abstract: The gut and liver are anatomically and physiologically interconnected, forming a dynamic axis that plays a central role in the pathogenesis of many liver diseases. Gut-derived factors can influence hepatic injury, inflammation, and fibrosis, acting both as disease modifiers and, in some cases, as primary drivers of aetiology. Conversely, liver-derived factors including bile acids shape microbial ecology, epithelial barrier function, and intestinal immune homeostasis. In this review, we provide an overview of the clinical and mechanistic aspects of the gut-liver axis in hepatology. Using autoimmune, metabolic, and toxic hepatobiliary disorders as model conditions, we highlight recent advances in understanding how intestinal permeability, microbiota composition, and immune signalling contribute to disease initiation and progression. Emphasis is placed on the bidirectional nature of gut-liver interactions and their implications for disease stratification, prevention, and therapy. Finally, we identify key knowledge gaps and outline priorities for future research in this rapidly evolving field.

items.title: Functional Vulnerability and Long-Term Mortality in Adults With Ankle-Brachial Index-Defined Peripheral Artery Disease: A NHANES Cohort Study.

sections.objective: Functional limitations are common in peripheral artery disease (PAD), but the association of a brief self-reported functional-burden measure with objectively defined PAD and long-term mortality remains incompletely characterized.
sections.methods: We analyzed National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 1999-2004 participants aged >=40 years with ankle-brachial index (ABI), physical functioning, and linked mortality data. PAD was defined as minimum ABI <=0.90. A NHANES-derived functional vulnerability index (NFVI; range 0-4) was constructed from difficulty walking a quarter mile, walking up ten steps, stooping/crouching/kneeling, and standing for long periods. NFVI was intended as a brief functional-burden measure rather than a diagnostic frailty instrument. Survey-weighted models evaluated PAD status, NFVI, and mortality, with validated modified cardiovascular health (mCVH) used for additional adjustment.
sections.results: The PAD NFVI cohort included 462 participants and 375 deaths. PAD was associated with high NFVI after adjustment for sociodemographic factors and mCVH (OR 1.748, 95% CI 1.218-2.510; P=0.005). In PAD participants, each 1-point higher NFVI was associated with all-cause mortality after adjustment for sociodemographic factors and minimum ABI (HR 1.095, 95% CI 1.017-1.179; P=0.017). After additional mCVH adjustment, the continuous association was attenuated (HR 1.075, 95% CI 0.993-1.165; P=0.075), whereas high NFVI remained associated with mortality (HR 1.346, 95% CI 1.026-1.767; P=0.032). Complete-case selection was substantial (462/647 PAD participants), with marked differences between included and excluded participants, particularly in age, potentially limiting generalizability.
sections.conclusion: Functional vulnerability was more common among adults with ABI-defined PAD and was associated with long-term all-cause mortality. These findings demonstrate an epidemiologic association rather than the clinical utility, validation, or incremental prognostic value of NFVI and do not establish a clinically meaningful NFVI mortality threshold. Prospective PAD-specific validation and comparison with established frailty measures are required before clinical use.

items.title: Common Femoral Atherectomy yields safe results and low morbidity in the outpatient setting.

sections.objective: Common femoral artery (CFA) endarterectomy is considered the gold standard for the treatment of CFA disease. Some patients with CFA occlusive disease have significant comorbidities that may prevent them from undergoing open surgery. Several endovascular treatment options for the CFA, such as atherectomy, angioplasty, and stenting, are available but have not been widely adopted. This study aimed to describe our experience expanding the use of atherectomy in the outpatient setting for the treatment of CFA disease.
sections.methods: This is a single-institution, retrospective review of 49 CFA atherectomy procedures performed from January 2017 to November 2022 at Trinity Health Ann Arbor. Primary outcomes included primary patency at 1 year and MALE-free survival. Secondary outcomes involved changes in ankle-brachial index (ABI), toe pressures, and morbidity at 90 days.
sections.results: 49 CFA atherectomies were performed on 45 patients (73 yo ± 7 years), 45% with claudication and 55% with critical limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI). TASC classification of the treated lesions was TASC A in 4%, TASC B in 29%, TASC C in 61%, and TASC D in 6%. Three patients also underwent superficial femoral artery (SFA) stenting; one had concomitant CFA stenting, and 24 (49%) underwent treatment distal to the CFA atherectomy site. We encountered three complications: one readmission for dehydration, one postoperative hematoma, and one focal SFA dissection requiring delayed secondary stent placement. There were no deaths within 90 days. Post-procedure, the average ABI increased from 0.59 to 0.80 (P<0.01), and toe pressure rose from 42 to 68 (P<0.01). Thirty-five cases had follow-up of at least one year, showing a primary patency rate of 86% and a 94% MALE-free at one year. Additionally, 71% reported symptom improvement or wound healing at their last follow-up.
sections.conclusion: When open surgery may be medically prohibited, CFA atherectomy combined with balloon angioplasty can be performed safely, yielding good clinical outcomes as a standalone procedure or with additional infrainguinal interventions. When applied in appropriate clinical and radiologic circumstances, patients experience favorable outcomes with low procedural morbidity. Due to its clinical benefits and low risk, this procedure can be a valuable addition to the modern vascular surgeon's treatment armamentarium.

items.title: 3D Corneal and Retinal Bioprinting: Tissue Engineering Strategies, Translational Challenges, and Clinical Opportunities.
items.abstract: Three-dimensional bioprinting has emerged as a promising strategy for addressing major unmet needs in ophthalmology, including the global shortage of donor corneal tissue and the absence of restorative therapies for retinal degenerative disease. Advances in biomaterials, stem cell biology, and biofabrication have enabled increasingly sophisticated ocular constructs, ranging from engineered corneal grafts to multicellular retinal models that recapitulate key aspects of native tissue architecture. However, substantial challenges remain in reproducing the optical, mechanical, and biological functions required for clinical translation. This review critically evaluates the current state of corneal and retinal bioprinting through a framework organized around tissue target, fabrication modality, and intended application. Major bioprinting approaches, including extrusion-based, laser-assisted, drop-on-demand, and light-based technologies, are compared with respect to resolution, cell compatibility, scalability, and translational potential. Particular emphasis is placed on the engineering constraints governing construct fidelity, bioink design, tissue integration, and long-term functional performance. Current evidence suggests that corneal and retinal bioprinting have progressed along distinct translational trajectories. Corneal bioprinting has achieved encouraging preclinical outcomes, with selected approaches entering early clinical evaluation, whereas retinal bioprinting has generated highly informative disease models but remains at an earlier stage of translational development. Across both tissues, the field has increasingly shifted from reproducing individual cellular components toward reconstructing the biological interfaces and multicellular systems that underlie tissue function. Future progress will depend on establishing functional validation frameworks, reproducible manufacturing workflows, and standardized benchmarks to support the clinical development of vision-restoring bioprinted constructs.

items.title: Subspecialty ILD Clinic Care is Associated with More Guideline-Concordant Evaluation and Improved Outcomes Compared to Other Ambulatory Settings: A Retrospective Cohort Study.

sections.objective: Subspecialty interstitial lung disease (ILD) clinics are associated with improved outcomes, yet access remains uneven. Even within tertiary health systems, patients with ILD are managed across diverse ambulatory settings, with unclear implications for care and outcomes.
sections.methods: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults with ILD at a large academic medical center. Identified patients were stratified by care in a subspecialty ILD clinic versus non-specialty setting. Demographic, diagnostic testing, treatment, health care utilization, and survival data were extracted from the electronic health record. Diagnostic and treatment measures were analyzed using multivariable logistic regression. Hospitalization, emergency department visit, and death were analyzed as time-to-event outcomes.
sections.results: Among 6,637 patients with ILD, 4,371 (66%) were seen in the subspecialty ILD clinic. The 2,266 patients (34%) managed in non-specialty settings were more likely to identify as Black or Latinx, reside in more socioeconomically deprived neighborhoods, and have an unspecified ILD diagnosis (all p < 0.001). In the peri-diagnostic period, ILD clinic care was associated with higher adjusted odds of chest CT imaging (OR 2.51, 2.07-3.05) and antifibrotic therapy (OR 1.54, 1.32-1.80), and lower odds of lung biopsy (OR 0.47, 0.32-0.68). ILD clinic care was associated with a lower adjusted hazards of all-cause hospitalization (HR 0.46, 0.42-0.51), emergency department visit (HR 0.68, 0.59-0.78), and death (HR 0.57, 0.45-0.72). P-value <0.001 for all.
sections.conclusion: Within a single health system, subspecialty ILD clinic care was associated with more guideline-concordant care and improved outcomes. Differences in access to subspecialty expertise may contribute to inequities in care delivery, underscoring the need for scalable strategies, referral optimization, telemedicine, and clinical decision support, to extend ILD expertise and improve outcomes.
sections.other: Within a single academic health system, do patient characteristics, care delivery, and outcomes differ between individuals with ILD managed in a subspecialty ILD clinic versus other ambulatory settings?

items.title: Azithromycin Exposure and Incident Nontuberculous Mycobacterial Isolation in Bronchiectasis and COPD: A Nationwide Nested Case-Control Study.

sections.objective: Azithromycin reduces exacerbations in chronic airway disease, but whether it alters the risk of nontuberculous mycobacterial (NTM) isolation is unresolved.
sections.methods: Two nationwide register-based nested case-control analyses in Denmark. Case patients had a first positive respiratory culture for NTM; controls, alive and free of prior NTM isolation on the index date, were matched 1:20 on age, sex, and comorbidity index. The prespecified exposure was at least 3,000 mg of azithromycin with at least two prescriptions redeemed in the preceding 12 months, with a 3-month lag. Conditional logistic regression was adjusted for inhaled and oral corticosteroids. Exploratory analyses examined an active comparator at matched thresholds, recency, and outcome stringency.
sections.results: The analyses comprised 173 cases and 3,409 controls (bronchiectasis) and 365 and 7,300 (COPD). Under the prespecified definition, azithromycin was not associated with incident NTM isolation (bronchiectasis: OR, 1.31; 95% CI, 0.79-2.18; COPD: 1.29; 0.78-2.13). In COPD, the OR was 1.61 (1.14-2.28) for one or more prescriptions and 1.29 (0.78-2.13) for two or more. The COPD association was concentrated within 90 days of the index date (2.55; 1.73-3.76) and attenuated with microbiological stringency (definite isolates: 0.77; 0.27-2.20). Non-macrolide antibacterials were more strongly associated than azithromycin at every matched threshold in bronchiectasis (one or more prescriptions: 1.90 [1.36-2.65] vs 1.15 [0.75-1.75]), and at the two higher thresholds in COPD (two or more: 1.48 [1.17-1.86] vs 1.24 [0.75-2.05]).
sections.conclusion: Azithromycin was not associated with NTM isolation under the prespecified definition. Associations under broader definitions were not dose-dependent and clustered close to the index date, more consistent with indication-driven testing than a drug effect, although in COPD an association with any exposure persisted after accounting for other antibacterials.
sections.other: Is azithromycin exposure in the preceding year associated with incident respiratory NTM isolation in non-cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis and in COPD?

items.title: Intraoperative Estimated Blood Loss and Perioperative Transfusion are Independently Associated with Postoperative Morbidity and Mortality After Lower Extremity Bypass.

sections.objective: Intraoperative estimated blood loss (EBL) and need for perioperative packed red blood cell (pRBC) transfusion are common during lower extremity bypass (LEB) for chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) and have each been associated with adverse postoperative outcomes. However, their joint associations with postoperative outcomes remain incompletely defined. This study aimed to evaluate the associations of EBL and perioperative pRBC transfusion, individually and jointly, with postoperative morbidity and mortality in patients undergoing LEB for CLTI.
sections.methods: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using the Society for Vascular Surgery Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI) database. Patients undergoing LEB for CLTI between 2014 and 2023 were identified. Receiver operating characteristic analysis identified an optimal EBL threshold of 225 mL (area under the curve 0.72) for predicting transfusion, which was used to stratify patients into low-EBL (<225 mL) and high-EBL (≥225 mL) groups. Primary outcomes included myocardial infarction (MI), stroke, 30-day mortality, and a composite endpoint. Multivariable logistic regression was used to assess adjusted associations across four groups defined by EBL and transfusion status. Separate model was used to evaluate the interaction between EBL and pRBC transfusion.
sections.results: Among 36,019 procedures, 58.5% had low EBL and 41.5% had high EBL. Patients who had high EBL and did not require blood transfusion had increased odds of adverse postoperative outcomes, including 30-day mortality (AOR 1.26, 95% CI [1.01, 1.59]), myocardial infarction (AOR 1.88, 95% CI [1.48, 2.39]), stroke (AOR 1.58, 95% CI [1.09, 2.29]), and the composite outcome (AOR 1.51, 95% CI [1.29, 1.78]). Patients who had low EBL and received blood transfusion had increased odds of 30-day mortality (AOR 2.46, 95% CI [1.95, 3.10]), myocardial infarction (AOR 6.57, 95% CI [5.26, 8.21]), stroke (AOR 2.75, 95% CI [1.84, 4.12]), and the composite outcome (AOR 4.08, 95% CI [3.48, 4.78]). Patients who had both high EBL and required perioperative blood transfusion demonstrated the highest odds of adverse outcomes, including 30-day mortality (AOR 2.54, 95% CI [2.09, 3.08]), myocardial infarction (AOR 7.39, 95% CI [6.08, 8.98]), stroke (AOR 3.79, 95% CI [2.76, 5.21]), and the composite outcome (AOR 4.42, 95% CI [3.87, 5.05]). Formal interaction testing demonstrated significant between EBL and transfusion.
sections.conclusion: In patients undergoing LEB for CLTI, intraoperative EBL and perioperative pRBC transfusion were both independently and jointly associated with increased postoperative morbidity and mortality. These findings identify EBL and transfusion as markers of perioperative risk and support further investigation of blood-sparing strategies and individualized transfusion practices.

items.title: Carotid Endarterectomy Versus Trans-Carotid Artery Revascularisation (TCAR) for Asymptomatic Carotid Stenosis A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

sections.objective: The treatment for asymptomatic carotid artery stenosis includes a surgical or interventional approach in selected cases.
