Although endarterectomy should be considered over stenting for selected patients, according to the latest European Society of Vascular Surgery (ESVS) guidelines, the Carotid Revascularization and Medical Management for Asymptomatic Carotid Stenosis Trials (CREST-2) suggested that carotid stenting would be associated with low rates of perioperative stroke or death. The transcarotid artery revascularization (TCAR) technique is a relatively new endovascular method, which involves placing a stent at the carotid bifurcation through direct carotid artery access, performed under a flow reversal system. This approach avoids manipulation of the aortic arch, potentially reducing embolic events. The aim of this systematic review is to compare TCAR with carotid endarterectomy (CEA) in asymptomatic patients undergoing carotid intervention. It seeks to evaluate whether TCAR is associated with improved perioperative outcomes, such as lower rates of stroke and death, compared with CEA, given its potentially less invasive approach.
sections.methods: The review was performed according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) on the platforms PubMed/Medline, OVID/Embase, and Scopus. The following MeSH terms were used: "asymptomatic carotid stenosis" AND "carotid endarterectomy", "transcarotid artery revascularization" OR "TCAR". Full-text screening and data extraction were performed with the support of the COVIDENCE platform. Six studies were selected for this systematic review, comprising a total of 132,684 patients (30,581 undergoing TCAR and 102,103 undergoing CEA). Statistical analysis was performed using R software.
sections.results: The selected studies for this systematic review showed similar results in terms of perioperative stroke and death for asymptomatic patients who underwent carotid endarterectomy and TCAR.
sections.conclusion: Our results suggest that there are no significant differences between CEA and TCAR for the treatment of asymptomatic patients who require a surgical or interventional approach. Further studies are necessary to provide more robust data in this field.

items.title: Vascular Surgery is Overrepresented by Multiple Medical Societies Compared to its Peers.
items.abstract: Medical societies play an important role in representing physicians and their interests. Our objective was to compare the number, size, and fiscal strength of vascular societies compared to other cardiovascular specialties. All information was found via a systematic Internet search and with publicly available data (i.e. www.aamc.org). Medical societies representing vascular surgery (VS), cardiology (CARD), cardiothoracic surgery (CTS), and interventional radiology (IR) in the United States were compared. Board-certified physicians (www.abms.org) and publicly available financial information were tabulated (www.ProPublica.org). Board-certified vascular surgeons (n=4464) can choose to join 30 VS societies (4 national, 10 regional, 12 city/state, 4 other). In comparison, 12 societies (2 national) represent CTS (n=5869) and 16 (1 national) represent IR (n=4032) physicians. Cardiologists (n=22843) are represented by 14 (5 national) societies and an additional 27 chapters of a parent national society. The available number of vascular surgeons per national society is markedly lower than comparative specialties. Vascular societies generated $23M in revenue compared to $52M for CTS, $6M for IR, and $1.03B for CARD. CARD societies have 93% of total revenue for these four specialties and 52 times the revenues compared to VS societies. Compared to similar specialties, VS has few surgeons, yet a high number of medical societies. This segmentation may dilute the educational, governmental, societal, and patient advocacy impact of VS compared to its peers.

items.title: Ultrasound-guided selective nerve block promotes perioperative vascular remodeling and early maturation of radiocephalic arteriovenous fistulas.

sections.objective: Autogenous arteriovenous fistula (AVF) is the preferred vascular access for maintenance hemodialysis, but its successful maturation depends on adequate perioperative vascular remodeling. We evaluated whether ultrasound-guided selective nerve block (SNB) promotes vascular remodeling and improves AVF maturation after radiocephalic AVF creation.
sections.methods: This was a retrospective analysis based on a prospectively-maintained single-center vascular-access clinical follow-up database. We included 163 patients with stage 5 chronic kidney disease undergoing primary radiocephalic AVF creation between January 2023 and January 2024. Patients received ultrasound-guided selective nerve block (SNB, n=72) or local infiltration anesthesia (LA, n=91). Perioperative changes in radial artery and cephalic vein diameters were evaluated, postoperative brachial artery blood flow was recorded, and AVF maturation was assessed at 1, 2, and 3 months. Linear mixed-effects models and multivariable logistic regression were used for analysis.
sections.results: Compared with LA, SNB significantly increased radial artery and cephalic vein diameters after anesthesia, whereas both vessels constricted in the LA group (both P<0.001). Linear mixed-effects analysis demonstrated significant time effects and group-by-time interactions for both vessels, while a significant group effect was observed only for the cephalic vein (all P<0.001). Postoperative brachial artery blood flow was significantly greater in the SNB group (P<0.001). The 2-month AVF maturation rate was significantly higher in the SNB group than in the LA group (60% vs. 35%, P=0.002), whereas no between-group differences were observed at 1 or 3 months. Younger age, larger preoperative radial artery diameter, and SNB were independent predictors of AVF maturation.
sections.conclusion: Ultrasound-guided selective nerve block promotes perioperative vascular remodeling, increases postoperative blood flow, and independently facilitates early AVF maturation after radiocephalic AVF creation. These findings support SNB as a promising perioperative strategy to optimize vascular access outcomes in patients undergoing AVF creation.

items.title: Long-term outcomes of cyanoacrylate closure alone versus combined high saphenous ligation and cyanoacrylate closure in large-diameter great saphenous veins.

sections.objective: Long-term evidence regarding the effectiveness of cyanoacrylate closure (CAC) in large-diameter great saphenous veins (GSVs) is limited. This study aimed to compare the long-term outcomes of CAC alone with those of combined high saphenous ligation and cyanoacrylate closure (HSL + CAC) for large-diameter GSV insufficiency.
sections.methods: This single-center retrospective cohort study evaluated 198 extremities in 180 patients treated for symptomatic GSV insufficiency between January 2018 and December 2022 who had a preoperative GSV diameter of ≥8 mm. CAC was performed in 127 extremities and HSL + CAC in 71. Clinical and long-term duplex outcomes were compared using generalized estimating equation (GEE) models that accounted for within-patient clustering and prespecified confounders. Propensity score overlap weighting (PSOW) was used as a sensitivity analysis.
sections.results: Long-term duplex follow-up data were available for 186 extremities (93.9%). HSL + CAC was associated with greater GSV occlusion (84.1% vs 65.8%; P = .007), less saphenofemoral junction (SFJ) reflux (5.8% vs 47.0%; P < .001), a lower postoperative Venous Clinical Severity Score (VCSS; 2.45 ± 2.04 vs 3.15 ± 1.89; P = .019), and greater VCSS improvement (3.45 ± 2.21 vs 1.47 ± 1.93; P < .001). Reoperation was performed in 8.7% of extremities treated with CAC alone but in none treated with HSL + CAC (P = .008). In adjusted GEE analyses, HSL + CAC was associated with a lower postoperative VCSS (β, -1.15; 95% CI, -1.71 to -0.59), greater GSV occlusion (OR, 3.05; 95% CI, 1.31-7.14), and less SFJ reflux (OR, 0.06; 95% CI, 0.015-0.223). PSOW estimates were consistent with the primary analyses. Complication rates were low and similar in both groups.
sections.conclusion: In large-diameter GSVs, HSL + CAC was associated with better long-term anatomic and clinical outcomes than CAC alone, without an appreciable increase in complications. These findings suggest that adding HSL to CAC may improve long-term outcomes in selected patients with large-diameter GSVs.

items.title: Interpreting High-Sensitivity Cardiac Troponin in Clinical Practice and Emerging Directions: Detection Is No Longer Diagnosis.
items.abstract: High-sensitivity cardiac troponin (hs-cTn) assays have solved the problem of detecting myocardial injury and, in doing so, created the problem of classifying it. Abnormal troponin concentrations are now known to be common across a wide spectrum of cardiac and systemic disease, and the central challenge of contemporary practice is no longer whether myocardial injury can be detected, but whether it can be correctly classified. Misclassification occurs in both directions and with real consequence: nonischemic myocardial injury is frequently mislabeled as secondary myocardial infarction (MI), contributing to the overdiagnosis of MI, and chronic myocardial injury, which carries a risk of subsequent MI or cardiovascular death approaching that of primary MI, is routinely dismissed once infarction has been excluded. This narrative review argues that accurate classification cannot be delegated to an algorithm and instead requires integrated, context-aware interpretation grounded in 4 domains: 1) the analytical and biological properties of hs-cTnI and hs-cTnT, including assay-specific and sex-specific thresholds, clearance kinetics, and sources of analytical interference and false-positive results; 2) the capabilities and limitations of guideline-endorsed serial testing, including the European Society of Cardiology 0/1h and 0/2h algorithms, point-of-care platforms, and artificial intelligence-based decision support; 3) rigorous application of the Fifth Universal Definition of Myocardial Infarction, in particular the distinctions between myocardial injury, necrosis, and infarction, and between diagnosis and risk stratification; and 4) recognition of the non-acute coronary syndrome conditions-chronic kidney disease, heart failure, sepsis, tachyarrhythmias, pulmonary embolism, takotsubo syndrome, and others-in which troponin elevation is expected rather than anomalous. We provide explicit bedside guidance for the situations that clinicians find most difficult, including suspected secondary MI, the observe zone, and troponin elevation without a dynamic pattern. Finally, we review emerging understanding of troponin biology, clearance, proteolysis and fragmentation, macrotroponin, antitroponin autoantibodies, and extracellular vesicle-associated troponin, which may eventually allow the assay itself to carry more of the interpretive burden. Until then, that burden rests with the clinician.

items.title: Serotonin signaling enhances phagocytosis by brain macrophages through Htr2b and alleviates brain injury after stroke.
items.abstract: Brain myeloid cells, including infiltrating monocyte-derived macrophages (MDMs) and microglia, play critical roles in ischemic brain injury, clearing debris and shaping neuroinflammation and neurological outcomes. Yet the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, using single-cell RNA sequencing and fate mapping with an MDM-specific Ms4a3creERT2-Ai14 mouse line, we identified serotonin receptor Htr2b+ MDMs as a crucial cell population involved in resolving neuroinflammation within the ischemic penumbra. Htr2b+ MDMs significantly accumulate in the peri-infarct region and exhibit enhanced phagocytosis and inflammation-resolving gene signatures. Mechanistically, Htr2b activation promotes nuclear translocation of Tfe3, a key lysosomal regulator, enhancing lysosomal biogenesis and supporting phagocytic activity. MDM-specific Htr2b ablation impairs debris clearance, exacerbates neuroinflammation and ischemic injury, whereas pharmacological agonism or Tfe3 activation restores lysosomal biogenesis in brain MDMs and improves post-stroke outcomes. Thus we demonstrate a previously unrecognized Htr2b+ MDM subset that integrates serotonin signaling to license intrinsic phagocytic function, alleviating ischemic brain injury.

items.title: An mRNA-lipid nanoparticle vaccine against H5N1 influenza virus protects lactating dairy cows from infection.
items.abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 virus has recently emerged in dairy cattle in the USA, leading to mastitis and sharp reductions in milk production. The main site of H5N1 viral replication is the mammary tissue rather than the respiratory tract and viral transmission between animals is thought to occur through viral shedding in milk. Here, we generate an mRNA-lipid nanoparticle (mRNA-LNP) vaccine encoding the hemagglutinin (HA) of A/dairy cattle/Texas/24-008749-002/2024, representative of circulating bovine H5N1 viruses, and assess its immunogenicity and efficacy in lactating dairy cows. Eight cows were divided into vaccinated and control groups, receiving two intramuscular doses of the vaccine or saline, followed by intramammary viral challenge. Vaccination elicited HA-reactive and neutralizing antibodies in serum and HA-reactive antibodies in milk. Following viral challenge, vaccinated cows had ~1,000-fold lower peak viral RNA in milk and a lower occurrence of mastitis and mammary fibrosis.

items.title: Population-scale single-nucleus multi-omic profiling of skeletal muscle reveals extensive context-specific genetic regulation.
items.abstract: Skeletal muscle tissue underlies several polygenic metabolic traits and diseases. Identifying their genetic mechanisms requires pinpointing cell types, regulatory elements, target genes and causal variants. Here we use genetic multiplexing to generate population-scale single-nucleus chromatin accessibility (single-nucleus assay for transposase-accessible chromatin using sequencing (snATAC-seq)) and transcriptome (single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq)) maps across 287 frozen human skeletal muscle biopsies. We identify 13 cell types and integrate genetic variation to discover >7,000 expression quantitative trait loci (eQTLs) and >100,000 chromatin accessibility QTLs (caQTLs) across cell types, including context-specific eQTL/caQTL with significant G × C interaction. We identify nearly 2,000 eGenes colocalized with caQTL and construct causal directional maps for chromatin accessibility and gene expression. Almost 3,500 genome-wide association study (GWAS) signals across 38 relevant traits colocalize with sn-eQTL/caQTL, most in a cell-specific manner. These signals typically colocalize with caQTL and not eQTL, highlighting the importance of population-scale chromatin profiling for GWAS functional studies. The results of this study illuminate the genetic regulatory architecture of human skeletal muscle.

items.title: Pupillary Diameter and Image Count in Telemedicine ROP Parameter Classification.
items.abstract: We examined whether pupillary diameter (PD) and image count (IC) are associated with detection of ICROP3 parameters in 10,503 eye-sessions from 1,131 infants in the SUNDROP telemedicine program. PD was graded on the anterior segment image as Large (8 mm), Medium (6-7 mm), or Small (≤5 mm). In mixed-effects models adjusted for gestational age, birth weight, and postmenstrual age, smaller PD was associated with Plus disease (Small vs Large: OR 2.41, 95% CI 1.36-4.29) and P-score, and each additional image with higher graded Stage, Plus, and P-score. Among Small pupils, additional images did not improve detection of any parameter.

items.title: Talazoparib plus enzalutamide versus placebo plus enzalutamide in metastatic androgen pathway modulator-resistant (castration-resistant) prostate cancer (TALAPRO-2): a biomarker analysis of circulating tumour DNA and cells for prognosis and molecular profiling.

sections.objective: The TALAPRO-2 trial showed improved radiographic progression-free survival and overall survival with first-line talazoparib plus enzalutamide versus placebo plus enzalutamide in patients with metastatic androgen pathway modulator-resistant prostate cancer (APMR; also referred to as castration-resistant prostate cancer) unselected for homologous recombination repair (HRR) gene alterations treated. We aimed to assess HRR gene alteration status agreement between prospective solid tumour tissue and circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) testing, the potential complementary value of prospective and retrospective ctDNA testing, and the prognostic utility of baseline ctDNA burden, changes in ctDNA burden, and circulating tumour cell (CTC) reductions.
sections.methods: In TALAPRO-2, a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial, men aged 18 years or older (≥20 years in Japan) with asymptomatic or mildly symptomatic metastatic APMR prostate cancer and no previous life-prolonging systemic therapy for APMR disease were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive once daily, oral talazoparib 0·5 mg plus enzalutamide 160 mg or placebo plus enzalutamide and stratified by HRR gene alteration status and previous treatment for androgen pathway modulator-naive/sensitive disease. The sponsor, patients, and investigators were masked to allocation of talazoparib or placebo; enzalutamide was open label. In this exploratory analysis, HRR gene alteration status agreement was evaluated in the unselected intention-to-treat cohort between solid tumour tissue prospectively tested using a clinical trial assay based on FoundationOne CDx and retrospectively tested ctDNA samples, collected at screening and assessed using an assay based on FoundationOne Liquid CDx. Tumour burden was categorised as positive or negative (ctDNA tumour fraction detectable or not detectable). Reductions in CTCs, enumerated using CELLSEARCH, were defined as conversion (from five or more cells per 7·5 mL of blood to four or fewer cells per 7·5 mL of blood) or CTC0 (from one or more cells per 7·5 mL of blood to zero). Radiographic progression-free survival was assessed for patients with baseline ctDNA positivity (positive vs negative) and for patients with ctDNA conversion and CTC conversion and CTC0 at week 9 (and week 17 for CTC conversion and CTC0) by treatment group. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrial.gov, NCT03395197 and is active, not recruiting.
sections.results: Between Jan 7, 2019, and Sept 17, 2020, 805 patients were enrolled and randomly assigned (402 to talazoparib plus enzalutamide; 403 to placebo plus enzalutamide); median follow-up for radiographic progression-free survival was 24·9 months (IQR 21·9-30·2) for the talazoparib group and 24·6 months (14·4-30·2) for the placebo group. A high concordance in HRR gene alteration status was observed between results from prospectively tested solid tumour tissue samples and retrospectively tested screening ctDNA samples (reported for 739 [92%] of 805 enrolled patients), with 84% (421 of 501) agreement in patients evaluable as either HRR-deficient or HRR-non-deficient by both tests. Median radiographic progression-free survival for positive versus negative ctDNA burden was 21·0 months (95% CI 16·5-not reached [NR]) versus NR (NR-NR), respectively (hazard ratio [HR] 2·46; 95% CI 1·68-3·60; p<0·0001) with talazoparib plus enzalutamide, and 11·0 months (8·4-13·8) versus 33·2 months (30·3-NR), respectively (HR 4·03; 2·85-5·72; p<0·0001) with placebo plus enzalutamide. In both groups, week 9 conversion from positive to negative ctDNA was prognostic of improved radiographic progression-free survival versus remaining ctDNA positive. Patients remaining ctDNA negative had more favourable radiographic progression-free survival versus conversion from positive to negative ctDNA. CTC conversion and CTC0 at week 9 were prognostic for radiographic progression-free survival benefit in both groups.
sections.conclusion: Our results support broad prognostic utility of ctDNA burden and CTC enumeration in metastatic APMR prostate cancer, including in the context of poly(ADP) ribose polymerase inhibitor therapy.

items.title: B cell subsets are associated with durable responses in distinct cancer types after immune checkpoint inhibition.
items.abstract: B cells are a critical arm of the adaptive immune system. However, the impact of B cells and antibody responses on overall cancer survival remains understudied. Here, we report results from a prospective randomized phase 2 trial of 106 patients treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) and identify that B cell antibody responses are associated with exceptional complete responses to ICI in certain cancer types. To further dissect the impact of B cell subtypes, we generated a comprehensive single-cell RNA sequencing database of intratumoral B cells in 12 tumor types from 152 patients. We found a context-dependent role for B cells, in which they are beneficial in certain cancer types and potentially unfavorable in others, with germinal center and memory B cells enriched in favorable prognosis cohorts and immunoglobulin A-positive plasma cells enriched in unfavorable prognosis cohorts. Depletion of B cells using rituximab in patients before surgery affected intratumoral T cell frequency and diversity. Furthermore, we show that B cells improve long-term overall survival even when T cell infiltrates are already high, indicating that a coordinated dual-arm T cell and B cell adaptive immune response is key to long-term tumor control. Overall, these results demonstrate that B cells and antibody responses in the proper context play an important role in durable complete responses in multiple tumor types.

items.title: An engineered, compact Cas12m variant for multiplexed gene activation in vivo.
items.abstract: Achieving coordinated CRISPR-based transactivation (CRISPRa) regulation in vivo remains challenging, as the requisite genetic elements frequently exceed the packaging capacity of AAV vectors. Here we report the identification and engineering of the Cas12m protein family, a naturally nuclease-dead CRISPR system that possesses intrinsic self-processing activity for its precursor crRNA. We develop an optimized variant, denCas12m, and leverage it in the smCRISPRa platform. We show that a single transcriptional unit encoding a multi-gRNA array can be processed into individual functional guides within a target cell, enabling efficient synergistic activation of a single gene through multiple sites or simultaneous activation of distinct endogenous genes from a single all-in-one AAV vector. We demonstrate phenotypic rescue in mouse models of Duchenne muscular dystrophy and Scn1a haploinsufficiency. Furthermore, a single all-in-one AAV vector supports the simultaneous activation of multiple distinct endogenous genes in mice, with a single vector delivering up to eight crRNAs for activation of six different genes, demonstrating the platform's high-order multiplexing.

items.title: Electroconductive patch promotes heart repair by directing epicardial cells toward endothelial fate.
items.abstract: Whether epicardium-derived cells (EPDCs) can differentiate into endothelial cells after myocardial infarction (MI) remains unclear. Considering the heart's electrical dependence, we asked if restoring electrical conduction could direct this potential. Using cardiac patches with tunable electroconductivity and genetic fate-mapping approaches in mice, we found that patches matching native myocardial electroconductivity (10-4-10-3 S/cm) specifically promoted proliferation and endothelial differentiation of WT1+ EPDCs, rescuing cardiac function. Single-cell transcriptomic sequencing revealed that electroconductive patches drove WT1+ EPDCs into a distinct WT1+TRPC3+CD93+ transitional state. These cells differentiated into endothelial cells via TRPC3-Ca2+ signaling and integrated into functional vessels. Inhibiting TRPC3 blocked differentiation and reduced infarct vascularization. Thus, improving electrical conduction unlocks and directs the endothelial differentiation of WT1+ EPDCs, offering a strategy for post-MI repair.

items.title: T cell-mediated depletion of intratumoral regulatory T cells using a CCR8xCD3 T cell-engaging bispecific antibody (TCB) promotes antitumor immunity in preclinical mouse models.
items.abstract: T cell-engaging bispecific antibodies (TCBs) have seen notable successes in hematologic malignancies, and emerging data demonstrate their potential for the treatment of solid tumors. Most oncology applications of TCBs have focused on targeting tumor cells via tumor-specific antigens; however, TCBs have been underutilized for strategic depletion of immunosuppressive cells in the TME. Regulatory T cells (Treg cells) play a crucial role in suppressing antitumor immune responses, making them an attractive target for immune-based therapies. Treg cells express several surface markers that can serve as potential targets for antibody-mediated depletion, including C-C chemokine receptor type 8 (CCR8), which is highly enriched on tumor-infiltrating Treg cells. Monoclonal antibody (mAb)-mediated Treg cell depletion relies on natural killer (NK) cells, which can be scarce in some solid tumors, whereas TCBs can broadly engage the T cell compartment by overwriting antigen specificity and redirecting potent T cell cytotoxicity against target cells. Here, we have developed a CCR8xCD3 TCB and show that it effectively depletes CCR8-expressing Treg cells in a T cell-mediated manner. CCR8xCD3 TCB led to the selective depletion of intratumoral Treg cells from human solid tumor samples in vitro and mediated inhibition of tumor growth in multiple syngeneic tumor models with variable levels of T cell infiltration alone or in combination with anti-PD-L1. In cynomolgus monkeys, CCR8xCD3 TCB was well tolerated without evidence of acute phase inflammation or cytokine release syndrome and led to effective and durable depletion of the CCR8-expressing subset of Treg cells.

items.title: Validation of the TWO-ROP Algorithm in the Shenzhen Prematurity Eye Study.

sections.objective: To evaluate the performance of the TWO-ROP algorithm in a large Chinese cohort under alternative United States (US) and Chinese retinopathy of prematurity (ROP) screening criteria.
sections.methods: Multicenter retrospective cohort study. A total of 14,198 infants screened for ROP between 2011 and 2025 across 56 centers in China. Infants were identified through the Eyecare-Cloud platform as part of the Shenzhen Prematurity Eye Study. The TWO-ROP algorithm aims to reduce screening examinations by recommending a single examination at 36 weeks or later postmenstrual age (PMA) for lower-risk infants. Its performance was evaluated under the US and Chinese ROP screening criteria within the same cohort, with alternative 35- and 38-week rules also explored.
sections.results: Overall, 10,024 infants were eligible for TWO-ROP under the US screening criteria and 6,750 under the Chinese criteria. The rates of TR-ROP were 2.94% and 1.32%, respectively. Under the US criteria, the 36-week screening rule identified 275 of 295 TR-ROP cases with sensitivity of 93.2% (95% confidence interval [CI], 89.7%-95.8%). Among 20 potentially missed cases, 14 (70%) had aggressive ROP. Advancing the screening time point to 35 weeks increased sensitivity to 98.6% (95% CI, 96.6%-99.6%). Under the Chinese criteria, the 36-week rule identified all 89 TR-ROP cases with sensitivity of 100% (95% CI, 95.9%-100%). Among infants born from 2021 to 2025, the exploratory 38-week rule identified 22 of 25 TR-ROP cases, with a sensitivity of 88.0% (95% CI, 68.8%-97.5%); all three potentially missed cases occurred in local hospitals.
sections.conclusion: The performance of the TWO-ROP algorithm varied under the US and Chinese ROP screening criteria. These findings highlight the importance of adapting screening strategies to local criteria and individualizing screening timing according to clinical settings and levels of care.
sections.other: Rates of any ROP and TR-ROP, potentially missed TR-ROP cases, and sensitivity for detecting TR-ROP.

items.title: In Vitro Fertilization or Intrauterine Insemination in Unexplained Infertility.

sections.objective: Although international guidelines recommend intrauterine insemination (IUI) with ovarian stimulation as first-line treatment for unexplained infertility, evidence from comparisons of this method with in vitro fertilization (IVF) is limited.
sections.methods: We conducted a sequential, multicenter, randomized, controlled trial involving couples with unexplained infertility. Stage 1 was a noninferiority comparison between IUI with ovarian stimulation (up to four cycles) and IVF (one complete cycle, with transfer of all embryos). After 7 months, couples without live birth or ongoing pregnancy could proceed to stage 2: couples in the IUI group could undergo up to two IVF cycles, and those in the IVF group could undergo one further IVF cycle. The primary outcome was the cumulative live-birth rate resulting from stage 1. Couples who were in stage 1 during lockdowns due to coronavirus disease 2019 were omitted from the analysis of the primary outcome. A secondary outcome was the cumulative live-birth rate resulting from stages 1 and 2. Live births were included in analyses if day 1 of the treatment cycle that led to pregnancy or day 1 of the last menstrual period before conception occurred within 7 months (stage 1) or 20 months (stage 2) after randomization. The noninferiority margin for the primary outcome was a between-group difference of 10 percentage points.
sections.results: A total of 737 couples underwent randomization: 365 couples were assigned to undergo IUI with ovarian stimulation before IVF, and 372 were assigned to undergo first-line IVF (1 couple in the IVF group withdrew consent for the use of data). The primary-outcome analysis included 585 couples (288 in the IUI group and 297 in the IVF group). The cumulative live-birth rate from stage 1 was 31% (89 births among 288 couples) with IUI with ovarian stimulation and 55% (164 births among 297 couples) with IVF (adjusted risk difference, -24 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -31 to -16). The cumulative live-birth rate from stages 1 and 2 among all the couples who had undergone randomization and provided consent was 70% (257 births among 365 couples) and 71% (265 births among 371 couples), respectively (adjusted risk difference, 0 percentage points; 99% CI, -9 to 8). Overall, serious adverse events occurred in 6 couples in the IUI group and in 14 couples in the IVF group; most serious adverse events were related to oocyte retrieval or hyperstimulation.
sections.conclusion: In couples with unexplained infertility, treatment with four cycles of IUI with ovarian stimulation was not noninferior to treatment with one complete cycle of IVF with respect to the cumulative live-birth rate. (Funded by the Health Research Council of New Zealand and others; FIIX Australian New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry number, ACTRN12619001003167.).

items.title: Comparative effectiveness of three splints for rehabilitation after finger flexor tendon repair (FIRST): randomised controlled trial.

sections.objective: To compare the clinical effectiveness of three splints after repair of zone 1 and 2 flexor tendons: forearm based (long), Manchester short (short), and relative motion flexion (mini) splints.
sections.methods: Prospective, randomised, parallel group, pragmatic, superiority, clinical trial. 430 participants (aged ≥16 years) requiring rehabilitation after primary repair of zone 1 and 2 flexor tendons in one or two fingers of the hand according to British Society for Surgery of the Hand guidelines. Participants were randomly assigned 1:1:1 to the long, short, or mini splint. Splints were worn continuously for five weeks and intermittently for a further week at night and in vulnerable situations such as public environments. Masking participants was not possible owing to the nature of the intervention.
sections.results: 430 participants were randomised to the long splint (n=143), short splint (n=140), or mini splint (n=147) and 403 were included in the intention-to-treat analysis. Adherence, defined as wearing the splint for a minimum of five weeks, was 83% (118/143) for the long splint, 76% (106/140) for the short splint, and 78% (115/147) for the mini splint. Mean post-randomisation PRWHE scores were 24.5 (standard deviation 15.5) in the long splint group, 23.5 (16.7) in the short splint group, and 22.4 (15.0) in the mini splint group, with adjusted between group differences of 0.3 (98.3% confidence interval -4.0 to 4.6, P=0.88) for the long versus short splint, 2.3 (-1.9 to 6.5, P=0.19) for the long versus mini splint, and 2.0 (-2.2 to 6.3, P=0.25) for the short versus mini splint. Serious adverse event rates occurred in 10% (14/143) of participants in the long splint group, 11% (15/140) in the short splint group, and 11% (16/147) in the mini splint group.
sections.conclusion: This trial found no statistically significant difference in clinical effectiveness between the long, short, and mini splint. Apart from some small differences, secondary outcomes were comparable across all three groups.
sections.other: 26 UK hospitals. The primary outcome was the mean post-randomisation score on the patient-rated wrist and hand evaluation (PRWHE) instrument at 6, 12, 26, and 52 weeks, analysed by intention to treat.

items.title: Deep sequencing of 3,367 maize genomes uncovers substantial contribution of rare variants to agronomic traits.
items.abstract: Rare variants are highly abundant, yet their genome-wide contributions to agronomic traits remain elusive in plants. Here, we performed deep whole-genome sequencing of 3,367 diverse elite maize inbred lines, uncovering 75.3 million variants, of which 79.2% were rare. Overall, we identified 411 independent association signals for 10 agronomic traits, including 359 attributable to globally rare variants, with rare variants showing effect sizes approximately 2.4 times those of common variants. Frequency-stratified genome-based restricted maximum likelihood (GREML) analyses indicated that rare variants captured a substantial proportion of phenotypic variance for traits under strong adaptive selection, consistent with the allele frequencies of trait-associated variants shifting from common in tropical to rare in temperate maize. Complementing conventional variant-level genome-wide association studies (GWAS), gene-based tests identified an additional 94 candidate gene-trait associations. Our study highlights rare variants as important components of the genetic architecture of complex agronomic traits in maize and provides much-needed resources for future functional studies and breeding.

items.title: Prospective circulating tumour DNA surveillance in patients with early high-risk hormone receptor positive, HER2-negative breast cancer in the TRAK-ER study.

sections.objective: CtDNA detection during adjuvant endocrine therapy (ET) strongly associates with recurrence in oestrogen receptor (ER) positive early breast cancer (EBC), with potential to direct switches in adjuvant treatment.
sections.methods: TRAK-ER is a multicentre study for patients with high-risk, ER-positive, HER2-negative EBC, who undergo 3 monthly ctDNA surveillance for up to 3 years during adjuvant ET. High-risk included ≥4 involved lymph nodes; tumour >5 cm; 1-3 involved lymph nodes with additional high-risk features. Upon ctDNA detection, patients have staging scans and in the absence of radiological recurrence, are randomised to receive palbociclib plus fulvestrant or standard ET. ctDNA analysis was performed using a tumour informed assay (Labcorp). We report a protocol-specified analysis of ctDNA detection during surveillance, and results of contemporaneous radiological recurrence.
sections.results: 1133 patients were registered by September 2025, 928 had panels designed (design failed in 16.1% (178/1106), and 912 started ctDNA surveillance including results from 5810 tests (median 7 per patient). ctDNA detection rate was 5.0% (45/897) in the first test, and 1.3% (66/4913) in subsequent tests (P<0.001). Patient level detection rate was 12.0% (109/912), with 1.1% (10/912) of patients having a clinical recurrence without prior ctDNA detection. Detection positively associated with nodal burden (P<0.001) and grade (P=0.04) and negatively associated with increasing time from surgery (P=0.01). Estimated cumulative ctDNA detection rate at 5 years post-surgery was 23.7% (95%CI 14.5-31.9%). In patients with ctDNA detected on the first test, 65.9% (29/44) had radiological recurrence compared to 26.6% (17/64) in patients first detected on subsequent tests (P<0.001).
sections.conclusion: Results from TRAK-ER inform implementation of ctDNA surveillance in ER-positive EBC, including molecular relapse rates, factors associating with ctDNA detection and contemporaneous radiological recurrence. Ultrasensitive assays detecting ctDNA at low levels, are required to robustly identify patients prior to clinical recurrence. TRAK-ER is ongoing to assess the impact of treatment after molecular relapse detection.

items.title: Fundus torsion in strabismus: Measurement, clinical interpretation, and emerging imaging approaches.
items.abstract: Fundus torsion is an important but underused anatomical marker in strabismus evaluation, particularly for cyclovertical disorders. Unlike subjective cyclodeviation testing, fundus-based assessment provides an objective reference based on retinal landmarks, though it remains influenced by image acquisition, head position, ocular anatomy, and measurement conventions. We synthesize the anatomical basis of ocular and fundus torsion, contemporary qualitative and quantitative assessment methods, and disease-specific evidence across superior oblique palsy, pattern strabismus, pediatric and adult strabismus, and surgical follow-up. The review emphasizes 3 clinically important issues: the frequent dissociation between objective fundus torsion and subjective cyclodeviation, the need for method-specific interpretation using reproducibility and minimal-detectable-change data, and the importance of avoiding isolated treatment decisions based on anatomical torsion alone. Recent optical coherence tomography-based and artificial intelligence-assisted approaches may improve measurement consistency and scalability, but current evidence supports their use as adjunctive tools rather than autonomous decision systems. Fundus torsion should therefore be interpreted within a multimodal clinical framework that integrates motility findings, sensory status, age, chronicity, fixation behavior, and surgical history. Treatment options include observation and symptom relief in selected patients, inferior oblique weakening for associated overaction, and torsion-directed surgery for persistent symptomatic excyclotorsion; comparative evidence remains limited. Prospective comparative treatment studies are a clinical research priority. Standardized acquisition protocols, explicit reporting conventions, age- and population-specific normative data, externally validated automated methods, and prospective studies linking torsional change to symptoms and functional outcomes are needed to strengthen the clinical utility of fundus torsion assessment.

items.title: Long-term patency outcomes after first autogenous arteriovenous fistula creation in patients aged 80 years or older: a competing-risk analysis.

sections.objective: Whether chronological age predicts arteriovenous fistula (AVF) durability remains uncertain. We compared primary patency between patients aged ≥80 and <80 years using competing-risk analysis and examined relevant vascular characteristics.
sections.methods: This single-center retrospective cohort included 416 consecutive patients undergoing first autogenous AVF creation during 2017-2020, with follow-up through March 2025. Intraoperative vessel diameters, macroscopic arterial atherosclerosis and preoperative ankle-brachial and toe-brachial indices were prospectively recorded. Death before primary patency loss was treated as a competing event. Cumulative incidence was estimated using Aalen-Johansen and compared using Gray's test. Associations were assessed using Fine-Gray and cause-specific Cox regression, with age modeled continuously in a sensitivity analysis.
sections.results: Among 416 patients, 109 (26.2%) were aged ≥80 years. Median follow-up was 48 months. Older patients had more macroscopic arterial atherosclerosis (67.0% vs 47.9%; P<.001), lower ankle-brachial (1.09 vs 1.16; P<.001) and toe-brachial indices (0.69 vs 0.76; P=.002), and more venous diameters <2.5 mm (22.0% vs 13.4%; P=.030). The cumulative incidence of primary patency loss did not differ between groups (Gray P = .710), with 36-month estimates of 43.2% and 38.0%. Age ≥80 years was not independently associated with primary patency loss (subdistribution hazard ratio [sHR], 1.12; 95% CI, 0.74-1.70), whereas each 10-year increase was associated with higher risk in a sensitivity analysis (sHR, 1.20; 95% CI, 1.04-1.39). Proximal anastomosis was associated with lower risk (sHR, 0.57; 95% CI, 0.37-0.88), and venous diameter <2.5 mm with higher risk (sHR, 1.70; 95% CI, 1.05-2.75). Assisted primary and secondary patency did not differ. Fewer than 10% of fistulas were permanently abandoned by 60 months in either group, and 60-month survival among older patients was 82.0%.
sections.conclusion: Among patients selected for autogenous AVF creation, age ≥80 years was not independently associated with primary patency loss, whereas a continuous-age sensitivity analysis suggested a modest increase in risk per decade. These findings suggest that an age threshold alone should not determine AVF candidacy in otherwise suitable patients, although interpretation is tempered by loss to follow-up.

items.title: Autologous Anterior Lens Capsule as an Intrascleral Spacer in Deep Sclerectomy: A Randomized Clinical Trial.

sections.objective: To compare deep sclerectomy (DS) combined with phacoemulsification (PE), with versus without an autologous anterior lens capsule spacer.
sections.methods: Prospective, randomized, parallel-group clinical trial. Sixty eyes of 60 adults with medically uncontrolled glaucoma and visually significant cataracts underwent PE-DS with an autologous anterior capsule spacer (Spacer group) or PE-DS alone (Control group). Follow-up was at least 12 months. The primary outcome was change in intraocular pressure (IOP) from baseline through 12 months. Secondary outcomes included glaucoma medication use, surgical success according to prespecified IOP-based criteria, and adverse events.
sections.results: Baseline IOP was similar (25.14 ± 9.62 vs 23.77 ± 5.18 mmHg) and both study groups had significant IOP reduction at all visits. IOP was significantly lower in the spacer group at month 6 (11.90 ± 1.82 vs 13.13 ± 2.20 mmHg; P = 0.022) and month 12 (12 ± 2.20 vs 13.29 ± 2.68 mmHg; P = 0.042). Medication use was lower in eyes with an autologous spacer at months 6 (0.14 ± 0.45 vs 0.48 ± 0.85; P= 0.063) and 12 (0.29 ± 0.66 vs 0.68 ± 1.04; P =0.094). Under stringent success definitions, survival favored the spacer (e.g., Definition C: IOP≤12 mmHg: 47.5% vs 15.5%; log-rank test P = 0.025).
sections.conclusion: Adding an autologous anterior capsule spacer during PE-DS was associated with lower IOP at 6 and 12 months and higher cumulative success under stringent IOP thresholds. Medication use was lower in the spacer group, although the between-group differences showed a trend toward statistical significance.

items.title: Time Course of Resolution of Diabetic Macular Edema by Sustained Suppression of VEGF-A with the Port Delivery Platform with Ranibizumab.

sections.objective: To determine the incidence of poor responsiveness to VEGF-A suppression in eyes with diabetic macular edema (DME) by evaluating the effect of continuous delivery of ranibizumab via the Port Delivery Platform with ranibizumab (PDS) in individual patients enrolled in the Pagoda clinical trial.
sections.methods: Retrospective analysis of prospective clinical trial data SUBJECTS: DME patients enrolled in Pagoda (NCT04108156). Change in central subfield thickness (CST) and best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) over time was evaluated for the adjusted intent-to-treat (aITT) population in the Pagoda trial. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) images obtained at each visit were analyzed for 56 PDS subjects from 8 sites to determine the time course of changes in intraretinal and subretinal fluid.
sections.results: In the aITT population the mean duration of follow up was 107.7 weeks in the PDS arm (n=272) and 100.7 weeks the IVT-PDS arm (n=238). The percentage of eyes with CST improvement into the normal range (≤325 µm) by the last visit was 87.9% in the PDS group and 85.3% in the IVT-PDS arm with mean time to normalization of 21.3 weeks and 20.6 weeks, respectively. All eyes in both arms showed reduction in CST over time although some exhibited periods of CST fluctuation and a few in each arm showed initial improvement followed by worsening at last follow up. In the eyes of 56 PDS patients that had detailed analysis of OCTs, normalization of CST occurred in 93% at a median of 17 weeks and elimination of intraretinal fluid in the central 1mm occurred in 84% at a median of 68 weeks. Only 3 of 56 eyes had poorly controlled DME at last follow up.
sections.conclusion: Sustained suppression of VEGF-A is sufficient to effectively treat DME in the vast majority of patients, but edema resolution may be slow in some patients giving the false impression of poor response to anti-VEGF-A treatment. In DME, the term unresponsive to anti-VEGF-A treatment should be replaced by slowly responsive.
sections.other: CST, BCVA, and time to resolution of edema.

items.title: Glioma regulates GABAergic signaling to drive hyperactivity and tumor progression.
items.abstract: Recent studies have identified bi-directional communication between neurons and glioma tumors as a key driver of hyperexcitability and malignant progression. Although much of this work has focused on the activity of excitatory neurons, the roles of inhibitory neurons remain poorly defined. Using in vivo screening approaches in autochthonous glioma models, we found that the loss of a γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) transporter (Slc6a1) enhanced glioma progression, promoted network hyperactivity, and influenced tonic GABA release by tumors. Mechanistically, we show that glioma tumors influence the activity of inhibitory neurons and that their subsequent stimulation suppresses tumor growth. Further screening of these phenomena identified diazepam binding inhibitor (DBI), a secreted negative allosteric modulator of GABA-A, as a link between glioma-related hyperexcitability and proliferation that functions through modulating inhibitory neuronal signaling. Collectively, our findings indicate that glioma tumors utilize multiple mechanisms to manipulate the activity of inhibitory neurons as a means to drive network hyperactivity, which ultimately facilitates malignant progression.

items.title: Trait-linked brainstem circuit resilience balances tau pathology-induced cellular vulnerability in Alzheimer's disease.
items.abstract: Although tau pathology correlates with cognitive decline in Alzheimer's disease (AD), some individuals exhibit resilience by maintaining cognitive function. The mechanisms enabling this protection, particularly before widespread cortical degeneration occurs, remain elusive. Here, we identify a dynamic interplay between cellular vulnerability and circuit-level resilience that shapes cognitive outcomes in AD. Tau accumulation in the Edinger-Westphal nucleus (EW) impairs attention by inducing hypoexcitability in CART+ neurons via Kcnma1 upregulation, a vulnerability predictive of future decline in both 3×Tg-AD mice and AD patients. Conversely, a subset of AD mice with heightened exploratory behavior activates a compensatory medial parabrachial (mPB)-EW circuit, mediated by substance P-Tacr1 signaling, which sustains CART+ neuron function and delays cognitive deterioration. These findings reveal resilience as an active state enabled by trait-linked circuit plasticity that balances cellular vulnerability, defining multilevel targets for early intervention.

items.title: Natural Missplicing Events Amplified by an Elusive Deep-Intronic MYBPC3 Variant Cause Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy.

sections.objective: Disruption of MYBPC3 precursor mRNA splicing is a frequent genetic cause of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM). Most often, it reflects changes at canonical sites or the creation of novel splice sites. Prediction tools usually prioritize splice variants with lower efficiency when they are distant from canonical sites. These elusive variants may explain HCM in patients considered genotype-negative after DNA testing.
sections.methods: Massively parallel sequencing identified the previously unreported deep-intronic variant MYBPC3 c.2308+227G>A in a cohort of genotype-negative patients with HCM from Salamanca, Spain. SpliceAI predicted a benign effect (Δ score, 0.03). However, its recurrent detection prompted us to conduct extensive analyses to investigate its pathogenicity, including genetic testing, clinical assessment, family studies, splicing assays, and haplotype reconstruction.
sections.results: We identified 35 unrelated HCM probands carrying c.2308+227G>A, plus 46 relatives from 27 families, yielding 81 confirmed carriers. Of these, 56 (69%) met diagnostic criteria for HCM (66% male; mean age, 53±15 years). By age 60 years, cumulative penetrance was estimated to be 81% in women and 96% in men. The combined logarithm of the odds score of 5.51 across 20 informative families provided strong evidence of cosegregation. During follow-up of probands, no significant differences were observed in heart failure, arrhythmic events, atrial fibrillation, or mortality when compared with cohorts carrying other pathogenic MYBPC3 variants. Blood splicing assays, confirmed in cardiac tissue, showed that c.2308+227G>A disrupts splicing by the use of pre-existing cryptic donor (c.2308+299) and acceptor (c.2309-580) splice sites, generating 2 misspliced mRNAs with partial intron retention or cryptic exon inclusion, which encode truncated proteins. These cryptic sites are the leading natural, unannotated missplicing events in intron 23, and some of the most frequent across the whole MYBPC3 precursor mRNA, as revealed by SpliceVault analysis of RNA sequencing databases. This deep-intronic variant does not alter essential splice motifs but promotes the use of pre-existing cryptic sites, likely through gain of splicing regulatory enhancer elements. The identification of a shared haplotype among HCM probands carrying this variant explains its recurrent detection, consistent with an ancient founder effect.
sections.conclusion: MYBPC3 c.2308+227G>A is a pathogenic splice-altering variant that causes HCM by amplifying natural missplicing events. These background splicing errors help explain how this elusive variant disrupts splicing without creating novel essential splice sites, thereby expanding the known mechanisms by which deep-intronic variants alter MYBPC3 splicing and ultimately contribute to HCM pathogenesis. Elusive MYBPC3 splice-altering variants should be considered in HCM patients with an unresolved genetic origin of disease.

items.title: Correlation Between EMS Agency Rates of Survival to Hospital Admission and Hospital Survival Outcomes for Cardiac Arrest.

sections.objective: Survival to hospital admission for out-of-hospital cardiac arrest is an important resuscitation outcome to gauge emergency medical service (EMS) agency performance. However, its correlation with EMS rates of survival to hospital discharge and favorable neurological survival is unclear.
sections.methods: Using the Cardiac Arrest Registry to Enhance Survival (CARES), we identified adults with nontraumatic out-of-hospital cardiac arrests during 2 periods: 2015 through 2019 (before the COVID-19 pandemic) and 2022 through 2024 (after the peak pandemic years). Multivariable hierarchical logistic regression was used to derive EMS agency-level risk-standardized survival rates for hospital admission, hospital discharge, and favorable neurological survival during each period. We then assessed the correlation between EMS agency rates of survival to admission versus discharge and favorable neurological survival using weighted linear regression, and whether the correlations differed by neighborhood income (above versus below median household income) and race and ethnicity (categorized as predominantly White [>80% of residents], majority Black or Hispanic [>50% of residents], or integrated).
sections.results: A total of 544 296 events from 1838 EMS agencies met inclusion criteria (252 137 pre-COVID; 292 159 post-COVID). During the period of 2015 to 2019, EMS rates of survival to admission were strongly correlated with survival to discharge (weighted r=0.68 [95% CI, 0.64-0.72]) and favorable neurological survival (weighted r=0.54 [95% CI, 0.43-0.59]). These correlations were similar during the period of 2022 through 2024 (weighted r=0.63 [95% CI, 0.59-0.66] and weighted r=0.48 [95% CI, 0.44-0.53], respectively). Neighborhood racial and ethnic composition modified the correlation between EMS rates of survival to admission and survival outcomes at discharge in both periods (all interactions <0.05), but the correlations remained strong in each neighborhood group. Similar findings were found for the interactions by neighborhood income strata.
sections.conclusion: EMS agency rates of survival to hospital admission are strongly correlated with their rates of survival to hospital discharge and favorable neurological survival. These findings support the use of survival to hospital admission as a performance metric for EMS systems.

items.title: LDLR Variant Classification Through Activity-Normalized Prime Editing Screening.

sections.objective: Inherited variants in the LDL (low-density lipoprotein) receptor (LDLR) gene are the most common cause of familial hypercholesterolemia, significantly increasing coronary artery disease risk. Early identification of pathogenic LDLR variants enables prompt lipid-lowering therapy and cascade testing of at-risk relatives; however, most LDLR variants observed in the population have uncertain or absent clinical classifications, leaving many patients without actionable information.
sections.methods: We developed the first activity-normalized prime editing screening pipeline to measure the impact of 5184 LDLR coding variants on LDL-cholesterol (LDL-C) uptake. Each prime editing guide RNA is paired with a genotypic outcome reporter to correct for variable editing efficiency, overcoming a key limitation of previous pooled genome editing screens. A statistical framework further improves variant effect estimates by jointly analyzing all missense variants at each amino acid position.
sections.results: We show that prime editing of the reporter construct correlates with endogenous variant installation frequency, validating the activity normalization approach. The resulting scores capture a continuous spectrum of functional effects, robustly separate pathogenic versus benign ClinVar variants, and show concordance with LDL-C levels in UK Biobank participants. We calibrate functional evidence strengths to the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics/AMP variant interpretation framework, enabling integration into a clinical variant classification workflow. By combining functional, computational, population, and contextual evidence, 322 of 434 LDLR variants currently classified as variants of uncertain significance, conflicting, or absent from ClinVar appear to meet evidence thresholds for reclassification and can be prioritized for expert review, substantially expanding the pool of actionable variant classifications. The screen also reveals a cluster of gain-of-function variants in LDLR class A repeat 5, at least some of which enhance LDL-C uptake through increased apolipoprotein B interaction, with implications for therapeutic genome editing. Last, prime editing uniquely detects splice-altering coding variants missed by cDNA-based screens and pathogenicity predictors, revealing an advantage of endogenous variant installation.
sections.conclusion: Altogether, activity-normalized prime editing provides a scalable framework for LDLR variant classification that substantially expands the proportion of variants with evidence for genetic diagnosis and reveals novel biology with therapeutic relevance.

items.title: Effectiveness of Nurse-Coordinated, Digital-Supported Collaborative Care Model in Reducing Hospital Stay and Mortality Among Patients With Heart Failure: TIME-HF Cluster RCT (India).

sections.objective: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction causes high mortality and recurrent hospitalizations in India. We evaluated the effectiveness of the collaborative care model in improving days alive and out of the hospital and overall survival.
sections.methods: We conducted a parallel-group, cluster-randomized controlled trial involving 1507 adults with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction across 22 centers in India (CTRI/2021/11/037797). Centers were randomized 1:1 to the intervention or usual care. Participants were followed up for 2 years. The intervention included risk stratification, lifestyle and pharmacological optimization, and a nurse-coordinated, mobile health-supported disease management program with self-care education, active follow-up, and continuous outpatient monitoring throughout the study period. The primary outcome was days alive and out of the hospital, and all-cause mortality was assessed as a secondary outcome. Days alive and out of the hospital was analyzed with a one-inflated β model. All-cause mortality was analyzed with Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for the clustered study design.
sections.results: Among 1507 participants (752 usual care; 755 intervention), the mean age was 61.9 years, and 77.6% were men. All participants except one completed 24 months of follow-up. Most participants (70%) had low educational attainment; 57.3% lived in rural areas; and ischemic heart disease was the predominant cause (77.4%). Baseline characteristics were comparable between the intervention and usual care groups. In the one-inflated β model, the probability of surviving up to 730 days without hospitalization was 34.7% (95% CI, 31.2%-38.1%) in the usual care group and 46.5% (95% CI, 42.6%-49.9%) in the intervention group. Participants in the intervention group had 78% higher odds of achieving a percent days alive and out of the hospital of exactly 1 (730/730 days) compared with those in the usual care group (odds ratio, 1.78 [95% CI, 1.42-2.23]). There were 201 deaths (26.73%) in the usual care group compared with 163 deaths (21.59%) in the intervention group (risk ratio, 0.80 [95% CI, 0.67-0.97]). In the multivariable Cox proportional hazards model, the intervention group had a 22% lower mortality risk than the usual care group (hazard ratio, 0.78 [95% CI, 0.63-0.95]; P=0.028).
sections.conclusion: A nurse-coordinated, mobile health-supported collaborative care model for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction in India increased the number of days alive and out of hospital, raised the absolute probability of remaining out of hospital by 11.8 percentage points, and reduced all-cause mortality by 22%.

items.title: Vitamin K2 and D3 Supplementation in Patients With Severe Coronary Artery Calcification: The DANCODE Trial.

sections.objective: Coronary artery calcification (CAC) progression is a strong predictor of cardiovascular events. We investigated whether supplementation with vitamin K2 and vitamin D3 reduces CAC progression in patients with severe coronary calcification.
sections.methods: In this multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized trial, 400 participants with a CAC score ≥400 Agatston units (AU) were randomly assigned to vitamin K2 (720 μg/d) plus vitamin D3 (25 μg/d) or placebo for 24 months. Participants were enrolled from February 2023 to February 2024. Noncontrast cardiac computed tomography was performed at baseline, 12 months, and 24 months. The primary end point was change in CAC score at 24 months. Subgroup analyses by sex and baseline CAC subgroups (400-999 and ≥1000 AU) were performed. Change in plaque composition was assessed in a subset with CAC score <1000 AU who underwent coronary computed tomography angiography at baseline and 24 months.
sections.results: A total of 398 participants (30% women; median age, 71 years) were included. Median baseline CAC was 903 AU, and 44% had CAC ≥1000 AU. In the intention-to-treat analysis, the mean CAC increase was 196 AU (95% CI, 178-214) with vitamin K2 and D3 and 248 AU (95% CI, 225-271 AU) with placebo (between-group difference, -52 AU [95% CI, -79 to -24]). The treatment effect was consistent across sex and baseline CAC subgroups. In the 143 participants who underwent coronary computed tomography angiography, there were a similar increase in total plaque volume and no change in noncalcified plaque volume between groups; progression of calcified plaque volume was attenuated in the intervention group (between-group difference, -8 mm3 [95% CI, -13 to -2]).
sections.conclusion: Among patients with severe CAC, supplementation with vitamin K2 and vitamin D3 reduced progression of CAC over 24 months. The reduction in calcification progression was not associated with an increase in noncalcified plaque volume.

items.title: Acute Effects of Cannabis Inhalation on Cardiac Ectopy, Physical Activity, Sleep, and Glucose.

sections.objective: Inhaled cannabis is widely legal in the United States. Data regarding cardiovascular effects are conflicting and generally arise from observational studies. The goal was to evaluate the acute effects of cannabis inhalation on cardiac ectopy.
sections.methods: We conducted a prospective, randomized, crossover trial to assess effects of inhaled cannabis on cardiac ectopy, mean glucose levels, step counts, and sleep durations. Adults who smoked or vaped cannabis on a regular basis without a history of cardiac arrhythmias were enrolled. Participants were randomly assigned each day to inhale vs abstain from cannabis via text messages for 14 days. Adherence was assessed using time-stamped Zio patch button presses at the time of cannabis use, daily surveys, and, in a subset, salivary mass spectrometry. The primary outcome was daily cardiac ectopy (daily premature atrial contractions and premature ventricular contractions).
sections.results: Of 108 participants (mean age 32 ± 10 years, 59% women, and 37% non-Hispanic White) experiencing a total of 713 days randomized to inhaled cannabis and 616 days randomized to abstinence, randomization adherence was imperfect but generally supportive of assignment adherence. Inhaled cannabis resulted in a statistically significant 9% reduction in ectopic beats (rate ratio [RR]: 0.91; 95% CI: 0.85-0.98; P = 0.02). Daily premature atrial contractions decreased by 10% (RR: 0.90; 95% CI: 0.82-0.97; P = 0.012), whereas premature ventricular contractions showed no significant change. Each cannabis inhalation was associated with a 2% reduction in ectopic beats (RR: 0.98; 95% CI: 0.97-0.99; P = 0.043). No significant differences were observed for step counts, sleep duration, or glucose levels.
sections.conclusion: In a pragmatic crossover design including habitual cannabis users, randomization to inhaled cannabis was associated with less cardiac ectopy, driven by fewer premature atrial contractions. Potential withdrawal effects, moderate adherence, and co-intervention limit interpretation of causal mechanism. (Marijuana and Acute Risk of Arrhythmia-Joint Abstinence and Exposure [MARY-JANE]; NCT06021613).

items.title: Combined LDL-C, Lp(a), and hsCRP Assessment Predicts ASCVD in the Multiethnic HELIUS Cohort.

sections.objective: Low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), lipoprotein(a) (Lp[a]), and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP) capture different pathways driving atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD). However, it is unknown whether their combined assessment provides reliable risk stratification in different ethnic populations with markedly different distributions of these biomarkers as well as background risk of ASCVD. The goal was to evaluate independent and joint associations of LDL-C, Lp(a), and hsCRP with incident ASCVD and to formally assess additive and multiplicative interaction of these biomarkers in a multiethnic cohort, and to determine whether these associations are consistent across participants of African, European, and South Asian Surinamese descent.
sections.methods: Among 15,676 HELIUS (HEalthy Life In an Urban Setting) participants without prior myocardial infarction or ischemic stroke (mean age 44.4 ± 13.2 years; 56.0% women), incident ASCVD was identified through linkage to nationwide registries. Fine-Gray competing-risk models were used to assess associations across increasing biomarker quintiles and joint elevations. Additive interaction was assessed using the relative excess risk due to interaction, attributable proportion, and synergy index. Incremental predictive value of Lp(a) and hsCRP beyond a PREVENT-ASCVD (Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease EVENTs-Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease)-based clinical model was evaluated using time-dependent area under the curve and continuous net reclassification improvement.
sections.results: Over median 8.9-year follow-up (138,375 person-years), 378 ASCVD events occurred. Top vs bottom quintile adjusted subdistribution HRs were 1.39 (95% CI: 1.09-1.79) for LDL-C, 1.86 (95% CI: 1.54-2.25) for Lp(a), and 1.51 (95% CI: 1.34-1.71) for hsCRP. Formal interaction assessment showed no interaction on either the multiplicative or additive scale. Risk increased with the number of elevated biomarkers, reaching a 2.44-fold increase (95% CI: 1.46-4.09) among those with all 3 elevated. Consistent dose-response patterns were observed across ethnic groups (Pinteraction = 0.75), although absolute ASCVD risk was approximately 3-fold higher in South Asian Surinamese participants. Addition of Lp(a) and hsCRP to a clinical model modestly improved discrimination at 10 years (Δ area under the curve: 0.006; P = 0.030) and reclassification (continuous net reclassification improvement: 0.165; 95% CI: 0.050-0.289).
sections.conclusion: In a multiethnic primary prevention cohort, combined assessment of LDL-C, Lp(a), and hsCRP identified individuals at elevated long-term risk through independent pathways, with consistent relative risk gradients but divergent absolute risks across ethnicities.

items.title: Resistance Training, Aerobic Activity, Television Viewing, and Risk of Major Cardiovascular Events in U.S. Women.

sections.objective: Long-term resistance training may influence cardiovascular health, but evidence in women, particularly in the context of aerobic activity and sedentary behavior, remains limited. This study sought to examine the association between long-term resistance training and risk of major cardiovascular disease (CVD) in women, and to evaluate joint associations with aerobic activity, sedentary television viewing, and key training-related characteristics.
sections.methods: We conducted a prospective cohort study among 117,025 women from the Nurses' Health Study (N = 45,669; 2002-2020) and Nurses' Health Study II (N = 71,356; 2003-2017), with up to 5 repeated assessments of physical activity. Resistance training was reported every 4 years, and time-varying cumulative averages were calculated to represent long-term exposure. The primary outcome was incident major CVD, defined as nonfatal or fatal myocardial infarction (MI), stroke, coronary artery bypass grafting, or percutaneous coronary intervention.
sections.results: Over a mean of 14.5 years of follow-up (1,630,964 person-years), 5,459 incident major CVD events occurred. Compared with no resistance training, women performing ≥2 h/wk had a 20% lower risk of major CVD (HR: 0.80; 95% CI: 0.69-0.92; P for trend = 0.007), and each additional 1 h/wk was associated with a 5% lower risk (HR per 1 h/wk: 0.95; 95% CI: 0.92-0.99). The inverse association was stronger for MI (HR for ≥2 h/wk vs none: 0.56; 95% CI: 0.41-0.76) but not evident for stroke (HR: 0.99; 95% CI: 0.80-1.23). Women who met recommendations for aerobic activity (≥15 metabolic equivalent of task hours per week), resistance training (≥1 h/wk), and low sedentary television viewing (<2 h/d) had a lower risk of major CVD (HR: 0.60; 95% CI: 0.53-0.69), than those meeting aerobic and low sedentary television viewing recommendations but not resistance training (HR: 0.73; 95% CI: 0.67-0.80). Greater consistency in maintaining resistance training (≥75% of follow-up) and engaging in both upper and lower limb training were associated with stronger inverse associations.
sections.conclusion: In this large prospective study of U.S. women, consistent resistance training, especially when integrated with recommended levels of aerobic activity and reduced sedentary television viewing, was associated with a substantially lower risk of major CVD, particularly MI.

items.title: Anti-Inflammatory Effects of Oral NLRP3 Inhibition With Ruvonoflast Among Individuals at Elevated Cardiovascular Risk.

sections.objective: The nucleotide oligomerization domain-, leucine-rich repeat-, and pyrin domain-containing protein 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome is a key sensor of diverse exogenous stimuli linked to noncommunicable diseases including atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. Early clinical data with the oral NLRP3 inhibitor ruvonoflast suggested lowering of biomarkers of systemic and central nervous system inflammation. The purpose of this study was to assess anti-inflammatory efficacy and safety of ruvonoflast in participants with residual inflammatory risk and high atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk.
sections.methods: In a double-blind Phase 1b trial, we randomly allocated individuals with high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP) ≥2.5 mg/L and body mass index ≥30 to ≤40 kg/m2, plus dyslipidemia, hypertension, or type 2 diabetes, to oral ruvonoflast (225 mg twice daily; n = 40) or matching placebo (n = 23). Both groups were maintained on a 2,000 kcal/d diet. The primary endpoint was change in hsCRP at Day 28 (ratio to baseline), analyzed using a Bayesian analysis of covariance. Additionally, change in hsCRP ratio to baseline over time was analyzed using a mixed-effects model with repeated measures. Change from baseline in inflammatory biomarkers and body weight were secondary endpoints analyzed with mixed-effects model with repeated measures and ANCOVA, respectively. Safety and tolerability were analyzed descriptively.
sections.results: Of 63 participants (mean age: 52.6 years; 71.4% female; 69.8% White) randomized, 59 completed the study. Median hsCRP at baseline was 5.7 mg/L (IQR: 3.9-9.8 mg/L). The primary endpoint of hsCRP reduction was met with a posterior probability of >99% for superiority of ruvonoflast over placebo at Day 28. Between-group differences favoring ruvonoflast were significant from Day 3 onward (P ≤ 0.001); at Day 28, geometric least-squares mean reduction in hsCRP was 82.2% (95% CI: 75.9%-86.8%) with ruvonoflast vs 37.2% (95% CI: 7.0%-57.6%) with placebo. hsCRP returned to baseline 7 days post-treatment discontinuation. Ruvonoflast significantly lowered key secondary biomarkers interleukin-6 and fibrinogen vs placebo at Day 28 (P < 0.001). Treatment groups had comparable mean percentage body weight reductions at Day 28. Serious treatment-emergent adverse advents were similar between groups, but 4 (10%) ruvonoflast-treated participants discontinued treatment due to transient, reversible treatment-emergent adverse advents, vs none in placebo.
sections.conclusion: Oral NLRP3 inhibition with ruvonoflast significantly reduced hsCRP with concurrent reductions in inflammatory biomarkers in participants with elevated inflammatory risk. Ongoing Phase 2 trials of larger size and longer duration will further characterize the therapeutic potential of ruvonoflast. (Effects of NT-0796 in Obese Participants at Risk of Cardiovascular Disease; NCT06129409).

items.title: Videolaryngoscopy versus direct laryngoscopy for nasotracheal intubation in infants undergoing cardiac procedures (NasoVISI): a multicentre, randomised controlled trial.

sections.objective: Nasotracheal intubation is a common procedure for infants undergoing surgery, and successful intubation at first attempt reduces the risk of complications. First-attempt success is improved with videolaryngoscopy compared with direct laryngoscopy in infants requiring orotracheal intubation, but the value of videolaryngoscopy in infants requiring nasotracheal intubation is unknown. We aimed to compare first-attempt success of nasotracheal intubation by videolaryngoscopy and direct laryngoscopy in infants undergoing cardiac procedures.
sections.methods: In this multicentre, parallel group, randomised controlled trial across eight paediatric cardiac centres in the USA, we enrolled infants aged 365 days or younger without anticipated difficult airways requiring nasotracheal intubation for elective cardiothoracic surgery or cardiac catheterisation. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) to videolaryngoscopy or direct laryngoscopy using permuted block randomisation stratified by site. The primary outcome was first-attempt intubation success rate. Analysis was by modified intention to treat using generalised estimating equations to account for clustering within intubating clinicians. Complications associated with first attempt and across all attempts were compared between groups with the same marginal models as the primary outcome analysis. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05433155) and is closed to new participants.
sections.results: Between July 1, 2022, and March 31, 2024, 684 infants were randomly assigned, of whom 673 were included in the primary outcome analysis: 340 in the videolaryngoscopy group and 333 in the direct laryngoscopy group. 311 (46%) participants were female, 362 (54%) were male, and 457 (68%) were White. The median age was 14·04 weeks (IQR 1·48-22·89) and the mean weight was 4·77 kg (SD 1·74). First-attempt success was higher in the videolaryngoscopy group than in the direct laryngoscopy group (281 [83%] vs 249 [75%]; adjusted risk difference 8·2% [95% CI 2·0-14·3], p=0·0093). First-attempt complications occurred in 85 (13%) participants overall, with similar incidences between groups (45 [13%] vs 40 [12%]; 0·4% [-3·5 to 4·3], p=0·83). Considering all attempts cumulatively, any complication occurred in 94 (14%) participants overall, with similar incidences between groups (46 [14%] vs 48 [14%]; -1·9% [-6·0 to 2·3], p=0·38). No cases of cardiac arrest or death occurred in either group.
sections.conclusion: Improved first-attempt success rates with videolaryngoscopy for nasotracheal intubation in infants undergoing cardiac procedures add to growing evidence favouring videolaryngoscopy as the first-line technique for tracheal intubation in infants. Key remaining questions for ongoing research include whether this benefit extends to infants with difficult airways and at non-specialist centres or urgent settings, and how clinician training should evolve as videolaryngoscopy becomes standard practice.

items.title: Prioritising environmental determinants in health technology assessment: a framework for integrating environmental considerations into health-care decision making.
items.abstract: Environmental determinants, such as air pollution, climate change, water quality, and waste, substantially influence population health, yet health technology assessment (HTA) rarely considers how health-care technologies affect these determinants and their downstream health consequences. In this Personal View, we propose a four-step prioritisation framework to identify the environmental determinants that should be prioritised for consideration in HTA. The framework maps causal pathways linking health-care technologies to environmental determinants across the lifecycle; assesses potential population health impacts; evaluates feasibility across five domains-strength of evidence, data availability, measurement standardisation, continuity of data collection, and alignment with existing HTA processes; and positions determinants within an impact-feasibility matrix to inform prioritisation. We demonstrate application of our framework using fine particulate matter (PM2·5) associated with vaccine packaging as an illustrative worked example. By considering potential population health impact alongside feasibility for HTA, the framework can help identify the environmental determinants that warrant detailed assessment and those for which current evidence or data are insufficient to support assessment within HTA.

items.title: Global, regional, and national burden of unintentional poisoning, 1990-2023: results from the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.

sections.objective: Unintentional poisoning is a preventable cause of injury-related morbidity and mortality, yet global patterns, trends, and inequalities remain incompletely characterised. Within the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) framework, unintentional poisoning includes poisoning by carbon monoxide and poisoning by other means, a category largely informed by pesticide poisoning codes plus some indirect capture of other poisoning as part of the GBD re-distribution process. Poisonings by pharmaceuticals and illicit substances are not captured in the GBD definition of poisoning. We aimed to quantify this GBD-defined burden and assess regional variation, sociodemographic gradients, and case fatality between 1990 and 2023.
sections.methods: We analysed GBD 2023 estimates for 204 countries and territories, modelling deaths, incidence, and disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) using standard GBD cause-of-death and non-fatal estimation methods with 95% uncertainty intervals. We stratified results by age, sex, region, and Socio-demographic Index (SDI), and derived case fatality from modelled deaths and incidence.
sections.results: In 2023, unintentional poisoning from carbon monoxide and other means caused 2·54 million incident poisonings, 69 805 deaths, and 3·68 million DALYs globally, with age-standardised DALY rates declining by 47·5% since 1990. Carbon monoxide accounted for 641 932 poisonings, 30 890 deaths and 1·34 million DALYs, with the highest burdens in central and eastern Europe and central Asia. Most regions showed substantial long-term declines, and the global age-standardised DALY rate for carbon monoxide poisoning declined by 58·2% since 1990. Poisoning by other means caused 1·90 million incident cases, 38 914 deaths, and 2·34 million DALYs, with the greatest burden in sub-Saharan Africa. Most regions showed declining age-standardised DALY rates for poisoning by other means; however, there was no clear change (with the 95% uncertainty interval including zero) in the global estimate, driven by wide uncertainty intervals in several regions (including sub-Saharan Africa). Mortality and DALYs were inversely associated with SDI, and derived case fatality was highest in low-SDI regions.
