sections.conclusion: Global reductions in GBD-defined unintentional poisoning by carbon monoxide and other means are consistent with decades of regulatory and environmental interventions. These include bans of highly toxic pesticides, improved heating and ventilation systems, emissions controls, and adoption of carbon monoxide alarms. Stark inequalities persist in some regions and in low-SDI settings. Compared with previous GBD publications, this study provides a detailed global assessment of unintentional poisoning by carbon monoxide and other means up to 2023, integrating incidence, DALYs, and comparative case fatality across regions.

items.title: Pazopanib alternating with bevacizumab in patients with metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma naive to treatment: a multicentre, single-arm, phase 1/2 trial.

sections.objective: VEGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) are considered the backbone for the treatment of metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma. We hypothesise that the administration of bevacizumab during scheduled breaks in pazopanib (TKI) treatment can improve tolerability and prolong progression-free survival compared with historical controls.
sections.methods: In this single-arm, phase 1/2 trial in five US academic cancer centres, patients (aged ≥18 years) with histologically confirmed metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 1 or less, and adequate organ functions were included. The phase 1 portion included patients with up to one previous therapy with high-dose IL-2 or an anti-PD-1 compound alone or in combination with a CTLA-4 inhibitor. The phase 2 portion enrolled only patients with treatment-naive metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma. The primary endpoint of phase 1 was to find the recommended phase 2 dose (RP2D). We tested a novel regimen using four dose levels: oral pazopanib (600 or 800 mg daily on days 1-28, followed by a 7 day break) alternating with intravenous bevacizumab (5, 7·5, or 10 mg/kg, one on day 36 and one on day 50) on a 10-week cycle in patients with metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma naive to TKI treatment. The primary endpoint of phase 2 was median progression-free survival, assessed by a masked central statistician review. Dose selection (in patients who had completed 15 weeks) and activity (in patients who had completed one full 10-week cycle of the novel regimen) were analysed in the per-protocol population. Safety analyses included all patients who received any treatment. This trial was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT01684397) and is ongoing but closed to new participants.
sections.results: Between Nov 21, 2012, and June 11, 2018, phase 1 enrolled 25 patients, with 18 patients evaluable for dose-limiting toxicity during the extended 15-week safety assessment period. The RP2D was established as pazopanib 800 mg daily (days 1-28) and bevacizumab 10 mg/kg on days 36 and 50 of a 10-week cycle. Between Jan 23, 2019, and Oct 19, 2023, phase 2 enrolled 53 patients, of whom 51 (including six from phase 1) were evaluable for activity and 59 were evaluable for safety. 36 (71%) patients were male and 15 (29%) were female, and 48 (94%) patients were White. 33 (65%) patients in phase 2 had favourable risk per the International Metastatic Renal Cell Carcinoma Database Consortium categories. After a median follow-up of 63·7 months (IQR 16·2-73·5), median progression-free survival was 24·8 months (95% CI 17·2-34·3). The most common grade 3-4 treatment-related adverse events were hypertension (20 [34%] of 59) and elevated aspartate aminotransferase (seven [12%]) and alanine aminotransferase (ten [17%]). Five (8%) patients discontinued the study for drug-related serious adverse events. No treatment-related deaths occurred.
sections.conclusion: The phase 1 portion identified the safe RP2D. The phase 2 portion showed that this novel regimen has promising antitumour activity in patients with metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma in the predominantly favourable risk group who are naive to treatment. Phase 3 randomised controlled trial data are needed to confirm these findings.

items.title: Cartilage-binding coacervate with therapeutic payload delivery and biomimetic lubrication alleviates osteoarthritis by reducing joint friction and inflammation.
items.abstract: Healthy articular cartilage maintains ultralow friction through the lipid/hyaluronic acid/lubricin complex lubrication layer, in which the zwitterionic lipids mediate lubrication and the hyaluronic acid and lubricin anchor to cartilage matrix. However, in osteoarthritis this lubrication system is progressively degraded, leading to increased cartilage wear and joint dysfunction. Therefore, early and lubrication-based intervention is urgently needed. Here we present biomimetic polyzwitterionic coacervates (pZCOs) that recapitulate both the lubrication and cartilage-binding functionalities of the natural boundary lubrication layer. pZCOs exhibit strong binding affinity to fibronectin, establish a stable and ultralow-friction lubrication layer on the cartilage surface, facilitate the sustained release of anti-inflammatory drugs, and preserve the viability and anti-inflammatory paracrine secretion of encapsulated mesenchymal stem cells. In both rat and mini-pig models of osteoarthritis, intra-articular administration of drug/MSC-laden pZCOs effectively reduces cartilage degradation, suppresses inflammation and promotes cartilage integrity, outperforming clinical hyaluronic acid lubricants in lubrication performance, in vivo retention and therapeutic efficacy. These findings highlight the translational potential of engineered biomimetic coacervates as next-generation joint lubricants for integrated management of osteoarthritis.

items.title: Stimulus-specific recruitment of human amygdala neurons predicts episodic memory encoding success.
items.abstract: Controlling whether an experience is encoded into long-term memory and thus later remembered is a crucial aspect of memory. Here we examined single-neuron activity in the human brain while participants formed memories for novel visual stimuli and later retrieved them with confidence ratings. Category-selective amygdala neurons exhibited elevated firing during encoding of later remembered items relative to later forgotten items. This effect was predictive of the episodic aspect of the memory, was restricted to the preferred category of each cell, emerged earlier and was stronger in the amygdala compared to the hippocampus, and did not depend on stimulus valence and arousal. Successful memory formation was accompanied by enhanced spike-field coherence between the activity of amygdala category cells and hippocampal field potentials. These findings demonstrate that stimulus-specific recruitment of the amygdala predicts memory formation and suggest category cells in the right amygdala as a target for interventions to treat disorders affecting episodic memory in humans.

items.title: Advances in the management of renal cell carcinoma.
items.abstract: Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) is the most common form of kidney cancer, with 435 000 patients newly diagnosed worldwide each year. In addition to morphology and histology, molecular subtyping has advanced the diagnostic classification of RCC. Contemporary diagnosis relies on cross sectional imaging in the form of computed tomography or magnetic resonance imaging and selective biopsy. For localised disease, nephrectomy remains the standard of care, with partial nephrectomy being an option for smaller tumours. Ablation or stereotactic radiation is appropriate for selected patients. Adjuvant pembrolizumab provides improved disease-free and overall survival in high risk clear cell RCC. In metastatic disease, the introduction of immune checkpoint inhibitor based combinations has extended overall survival, providing a durable response in some patients. Despite these advances, primary and secondary resistance, along with the lack of predictive and prognostic biomarkers, remain a challenge.

items.title: Izalontamab brengitecan versus platinum-based chemotherapy in EGFR-mutated advanced non-squamous non-small-cell lung cancer after progression on third-generation EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (PANKU-Lung01): a multicentre, randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial in China.

sections.objective: Izalontamab brengitecan (iza-bren) is a first-in-class bispecific antibody-drug conjugate targeting epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) and human epidermal growth factor receptor 3 (HER3) and has shown antitumour activity in EGFR-mutated non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC). We compared iza-bren with platinum-based chemotherapy in participants with EGFR-mutated advanced non-squamous NSCLC after progression on third-generation EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs).
sections.methods: In this multicentre, randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial (PANKU-Lung01) conducted at 73 sites in China, eligible participants had EGFR-mutated locally advanced or metastatic non-squamous NSCLC, disease progression after third-generation EGFR TKIs, and had received no previous chemotherapy for advanced disease. Participants were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive iza-bren (2·5 mg/kg intravenously on days 1 and 8 of each 3-week cycle) or pemetrexed plus carboplatin or cisplatin for four to six cycles, with pemetrexed maintenance permitted in participants without progression. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival assessed by blinded independent central review (BICR). The primary analysis included all randomly assigned participants who received at least one dose of study treatment (modified intention-to-treat population). We report the prespecified final progression-free survival and interim overall survival analyses. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06382116.
sections.results: Between May 22, 2024, and Sept 1, 2025, we screened 654 participants. After 222 (34%) were excluded, 432 (66%) participants were randomly assigned to iza-bren (n=217 [50%]) or chemotherapy (n=215 [50%]); 422 (98%) received study treatment (216 [51%] in the iza-bren group and 206 [49%] in the chemotherapy group) and comprised the modified intention-to-treat population. At the data cutoff (July 15, 2026; median follow-up for progression-free survival 14·6 months [95% CI 12·9-16·7] in the iza-bren group vs 15·2 months [11·2-18·2] in the chemotherapy group), median BICR-assessed progression-free survival was 11·1 months (9·2-12·7) with iza-bren versus 5·7 months (5·5-5·9) with chemotherapy (hazard ratio [HR] 0·40 [95% CI 0·31-0·51]; one-sided p<0·0001). Treatment-related adverse events of grade 3 or worse occurred in 170 (79%) of 216 participants in the iza-bren group and 128 (62%) of 206 in the chemotherapy group (predominantly haematological); treatment-related adverse events led to permanent discontinuation of at least one study-treatment component in four (2%) participants in each group and treatment-related deaths occurred in one participant in each group. Treatment-related interstitial lung disease occurred in two (1%) participants in the iza-bren group and none in the chemotherapy group.
sections.conclusion: In participants with EGFR-mutated advanced non-squamous NSCLC after progression on third-generation EGFR TKIs, iza-bren significantly prolonged progression-free survival, although treatment-related adverse events of grade 3 or worse were more frequent than with chemotherapy. To our knowledge, these findings provide the first phase 3 evidence for a bispecific antibody-drug conjugate and support iza-bren as a potential treatment option in this population.

items.title: Sacituzumab tirumotecan versus treatment of physician's choice in previously treated endometrial cancer (TroFuse-005/ENGOT-en23/GOG-3095): a randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial.

sections.objective: Therapeutic options for patients with endometrial cancer who progress after platinum-based chemotherapy and immunotherapy are scarce, and prognosis is poor. Sacituzumab tirumotecan (sac-TMT) is a trophoblast cell-surface antigen 2-directed antibody-drug conjugate with a unique, bifunctional linker that maximises delivery of a belotecan-derived topoisomerase I inhibitor payload to tumour cells. This study aimed to compare sac-TMT with the treatment of physician's choice (TPC) in patients with endometrial cancer who had been previously treated with platinum-based chemotherapy and immunotherapy.
sections.methods: In this randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial, patients were recruited from 242 gynaecological oncology centres across 31 countries and regions. Participating centres were selected based on established expertise in gynaecological oncology and an adequate volume of potentially eligible patients. Eligible patients were female and aged 18 years or older with histologically confirmed advanced or recurrent endometrial carcinoma or carcinosarcoma, who had received up to three previous lines of therapy, including systemic platinum-based chemotherapy and anti-programmed death 1 or anti-programmed death ligand 1 therapy. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) via central interactive response technology to receive intravenous sac-TMT (4 mg/kg on days 1 and 15 of each 28-day cycle) or TPC (intravenous doxorubicin 60 mg/m2 every 3 weeks or intravenous paclitaxel 80 mg/m2 on days 1, 8, and 15 of each 28-day cycle). Investigators and patients were not masked to treatment; radiologists performing blinded independent central review were fully masked. Randomisation was stratified by mismatch repair status (deficient vs proficient), trophoblast cell-surface antigen 2 expression by immunohistochemistry (TROP2 EPR20043 Formulation Locked Assay [Roche Tissue Diagnostics, Tucson, AZ, USA]; low [0% to <50% of tumour cells with moderate (2+) or strong (3+) membrane staining intensity] vs medium-high [≥50% tumour cells with moderate (2+) or strong (3+) membrane staining intensity]), number of previous lines of systemic therapy (≤2 vs 3), and baseline disease status per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (version 1.1) by blinded independent central review (measurable vs non-measurable). Dual primary endpoints were progression-free survival per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (version 1.1) assessed by blinded independent central review and overall survival, analysed in the intention-to-treat population. The data cutoff date was March 23, 2026. Progression-free survival and overall survival were evaluated as dual primary endpoints using a graphical multiple-testing approach with prespecified alpha allocation. Progression-free survival was assessed every 8 weeks through to week 56, then every 12 weeks thereafter; overall survival was assessed continuously. The safety analysis included all randomly assigned patients who received at least one dose of study treatment. For progression-free survival, missing radiographic assessments were handled using prespecified censoring rules; no imputation was performed for missing overall survival or safety data. The trial was registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06132958) and is ongoing.
sections.results: Between Jan 5, 2024, and Sept 17, 2025, 776 patients were randomly assigned to sac-TMT (n=386) or TPC (n=390). 384 (99%) of 386 patients in the sac-TMT group and 367 (94%) of 390 in the TPC group received at least one dose of study treatment. At data cutoff, median follow-up was 14·0 months (IQR 11·0-16·9). Median progression-free survival was 7·2 months (95% CI 5·6-7·6) in the sac-TMT group and 3·9 months (3·7-5·3) in the TPC group (hazard ratio 0·59 [95% CI 0·50-0·70]; p<0·0001) and median overall survival was 19·0 months (16·1-not reached) in the sac-TMT group and 12·1 months (11·0-15·2) in the TPC group (0·68 [0·55-0·84]; p=0·0001). 265 (69%) of 384 patients in the sac-TMT group and 210 (57%) of 367 in the TPC group had a grade 3 or higher adverse event. Serious adverse events were reported in 133 (35%) patients in the sac-TMT group and 117 (32%) patients in the TPC group. Treatment-related adverse events led to death in three (<1%) patients in the sac-TMT group and three (<1%) in the TPC group.
sections.conclusion: Sac-TMT significantly improved progression-free survival and overall survival versus TPC in patients with advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer previously treated with platinum-based chemotherapy and immunotherapy. These findings support sac-TMT as a new standard of care for patients with endometrial cancer who have received chemotherapy and immunotherapy and have few effective treatment options.

items.title: Izalontamab brengitecan for HR+/HER2- breast cancer in China (PANKU-Breast01): a randomised, phase 3 trial.

sections.objective: Patients with heavily pretreated hormone receptor-positive and human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-negative (HR+/HER2-) breast cancer have few treatment options. Izalontamab brengitecan (iza-bren) is a first-in-class, epidermal growth factor receptor and HER3 bispecific antibody-drug conjugate that contains a potent topoisomerase I inhibitor payload (Ed-04). The aim of PANKU-Breast01 was to compare the efficacy and safety of iza-bren versus chemotherapy in patients with pretreated HR+/HER2- breast cancer.
sections.methods: In this randomised, phase 3, open-label, multicentre study in 72 hospitals in China, patients with HR+/HER2- breast cancer who had disease progression after endocrine therapy, cyclin-dependent kinase (CDK) 4/6 inhibitors, and one or two lines of chemotherapy were randomly assigned (1:1) to iza-bren (2·5 mg/kg, administered by intravenous infusion on day 1 and day 8 every 3 weeks) or physician's choice chemotherapy (eribulin, 1·4 mg/m2; vinorelbine, 25 mg/m2; or gemcitabine, 1000 mg/m2, all administered by intravenous infusion on day 1 and day 8 every 3 weeks; or capecitabine, 1000-1250 mg/m2, administered orally twice daily on days 1-14 of each 3-week cycle). Stratified block randomisation was performed by an independent vendor using an interactive web response system, with stratification factors of number of previous lines of chemotherapy, CNS metastasis, and HER2 expression status. Patients, investigators, and site personnel involved in patient care and performing trial procedures were not masked to treatment assignment. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival assessed by Blinded Independent Central Review per RECIST (version 1.1) in the modified intention-to-treat population, which consisted of all randomly assigned participants who had at least one dose of study drug. Median progression-free survival was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method and hazard ratios (HRs) were calculated using a stratified Cox proportional hazards model. The trial was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06343948, and is closed to recruitment.
sections.results: Between April 24, 2024, and June 6, 2025, 560 patients were screened, 177 were excluded, and 383 patients were randomly assigned and treated (190 were assigned to the iza-bren group and 193 were assigned to the chemotherapy group). All 383 participants in the study were female and of Chinese ethnicity. Median age was 54·0 years (IQR 47·0-60·0). At data cutoff (July 21, 2026), median follow-up for progression-free survival was 15·2 months (95% CI 13·9-16·8). Iza-bren significantly improved progression-free survival versus chemotherapy (log-rank p<0·0001), and median progression-free survival assessed by Blinded Independent Central Review was 8·2 months (95% CI 6·9-8·6) versus 4·0 months (2·9-4·3; HR 0·41 [95% CI 0·33-0·53]). Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in 162 (85%) patients in the iza-bren group versus 127 (66%) patients in the chemotherapy group, and haematological adverse events were the most common in both groups. For the treatment of haematological adverse events, 138 (73%) patients in the iza-bren group received platelet-elevating agents, 28 (15%) patients in the iza-bren group received platelet transfusion, and 18 patients (10%) in the iza-bren group received a blood transfusion. Two patients in the iza-bren group died due to treatment-related adverse events.
sections.conclusion: Iza-bren showed a significant improvement in progression-free survival versus chemotherapy in patients with HR+/HER2- breast cancer previously treated with endocrine therapy, CDK4/6 inhibitors, and one or two lines of chemotherapy (including taxanes). The overall survival data were immature, and an overall survival benefit has not been established. These results suggest that iza-bren could be a new treatment option for this population in China; however, further evaluation of iza-bren in global populations and in earlier lines of therapy for HER2-negative breast cancer is warranted.

items.title: First-line pembrolizumab versus carboplatin plus paclitaxel in participants with mismatch repair-deficient advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer (KEYNOTE-C93/GOG-3064/ENGOT-en15): interim analysis of a multicentre, open-label, randomised, active-comparator controlled, phase 3 trial.

sections.objective: A need exists for first-line chemotherapy-free options in advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer. We therefore assessed the efficacy, quality of life, and safety of first-line pembrolizumab versus carboplatin plus paclitaxel in mismatch repair-deficient (dMMR) advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer.
sections.methods: The KEYNOTE-C93/GOG-3064/ENGOT-en15 multicentre, open-label, randomised, active-comparator controlled, phase 3 trial was conducted at 122 centres in 24 countries in the Americas, Asia, Europe, and Oceania. Adult participants (≥18 years) with inoperable, stage III or IV, persistent, advanced, or recurrent dMMR endometrial cancer were randomly assigned 1:1 to intravenous pembrolizumab 400 mg every 6 weeks for up to 18 cycles or intravenous carboplatin area under the curve 5 mg/mL or 6 mg/mL per min plus paclitaxel 175 mg/m2 on day 1 of each 3-week cycle for six cycles. Randomisation was stratified by disease status, histology, and previous receipt of (neo)adjuvant chemotherapy. Primary endpoints were progression-free survival per RECIST version 1.1, by blinded independent central review, and overall survival. This trial is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05173987, and is ongoing.
sections.results: Between Feb 22, 2022, and Dec 12, 2023, 299 participants were assigned to pembrolizumab (n=149) or carboplatin plus paclitaxel (n=150). At the cutoff for the prespecified interim analysis in the intention-to-treat population (April 24, 2026), median progression-free survival was 38·2 months (95% CI 17·9 months-not reached) in the pembrolizumab group versus 8·4 months (6·8-10·4) in the carboplatin plus paclitaxel group (hazard ratio [HR] 0·57, 95% CI 0·42-0·79; p=0·0002). Estimated progression-free survival was 75% (95% CI 67-81) versus 76% (68-82) at 6 months, 67% (59-74) versus 40% (32-48) at 12 months, and 53% (44-61) versus 30% (22-38) at 36 months. The prespecified statistical significance criterion for overall survival was not met at the interim analysis (medians not reached; HR 0·77, 95% CI 0·52-1·15; p=0·10). Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in 27 (18%) of 149 participants in the pembrolizumab group and 73 (51%) of 144 in the carboplatin plus paclitaxel group. Treatment-related adverse events of any grade that occurred in at least 25% of participants in either group included alopecia (three [2%] of 149 in the pembrolizumab group, 72 [50%] of 144 in the carboplatin plus paclitaxel group), anaemia (seven [5%], 71 [49%]), nausea (seven [5%], 41 [28%]), decreased neutrophil count (five [3%], 40 [28%]), peripheral neuropathy (none, 38 [26%]), and fatigue (20 [13%], 37 [26%]). Treatment-related adverse events led to treatment discontinuation in 14 (9%) of 149 participants in the pembrolizumab group and 21 (15%) of 144 participants in the carboplatin plus paclitaxel group; they resulted in death in two participants in the pembrolizumab group (hepatic failure and bacterial meningitis [n=1 each]) and one participant in the carboplatin plus paclitaxel group (pulmonary embolism).
sections.conclusion: First-line pembrolizumab showed a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in progression-free survival, with lower frequency of overall and grade 3 or above treatment-related adverse events. The study did not compare pembrolizumab monotherapy with the current standard of care (immunotherapy plus chemotherapy).

items.title: Ruzaltatug rezetecan versus chemotherapy for EGFR-mutated advanced non-small-cell lung cancer progressing after EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor therapy (HERON-Lung01): interim analysis of a randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial in China.

sections.objective: Ruzaltatug rezetecan is a novel HER3-directed antibody-drug conjugate that has shown promising antitumour activity and manageable safety in pretreated EGFR-.mutated non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) in a phase 1 trial. We aimed to compare the efficacy and safety of ruzaltatug rezetecan with chemotherapy in patients with EGFR-mutated advanced NSCLC that had progressed after EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) therapy.
sections.methods: HERON-Lung01 is a randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial conducted at 62 sites in China. Eligible patients were aged 18-75 years, with locally advanced or metastatic non-squamous NSCLC harbouring an EGFR activating mutation (exon 19 deletion or L858R mutation), and had progressed during or after EGFR-TKI therapy. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive ruzaltatug rezetecan 8·0 mg/kg or chemotherapy comprising pemetrexed 500 mg/m2 plus carboplatin (area under the curve 5) or cisplatin 75 mg/m2 for four cycles, followed by maintenance pemetrexed. All treatments were administered intravenously on day 1 of each 3-week cycle. Block randomisation was stratified by presence of brain metastases, EGFR mutation subtype, and use of a first-line third-generation EGFR-TKI. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS), as assessed by blinded independent central review (BICR), in the intention-to-treat population. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06671379). Recruitment is complete, with the trial ongoing.
sections.results: Between Nov 29, 2024, and Jan 29, 2026, 498 patients were randomly assigned to receive ruzaltatug rezetecan (n=250) or chemotherapy (n=248). The median age was 60·0 years (IQR 54·0-68·0); 276 (55%) patients were female and 222 (45%) male. At the prespecified interim PFS analysis, median follow-up was 7·7 months (95% CI 7·1-8·3). BICR-assessed PFS was significantly longer with ruzaltatug rezetecan than with chemotherapy (median 8·3 months vs 5·4 months; hazard ratio 0·47 [95% CI 0·36-0·60]; one-sided p<0·0001). Grade 3 or worse treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) occurred in 101 (41%) of 248 patients receiving ruzaltatug rezetecan and 93 (39%) of 239 patients receiving chemotherapy, most commonly decreased neutrophil count (64 [26%] of 248 patients vs 46 [19%] of 239 patients), decreased white blood cell count (29 [12%] vs 29 [12%]), and anaemia (15 [6%] vs 26 [11%]). TRAEs led to treatment discontinuation in three (1%) patients in the ruzaltatug rezetecan group and three (1%) in the chemotherapy group. One death (unknown cause) in the ruzaltatug rezetecan group was considered by the investigator to be possibly treatment related.
sections.conclusion: Ruzaltatug rezetecan significantly prolonged PFS compared with chemotherapy, with a manageable safety profile, in EGFR-TKI-resistant, EGFR-mutated advanced NSCLC. These data support ruzaltatug rezetecan as a potential treatment option in this setting.

items.title: In vivo genome-editing therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy: Preclinical studies and first-in-human trial.
items.abstract: We report the preclinical and early clinical evaluation of in vivo genome editing for Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD), delivered via a single AAV9 vector. In humanized DMD mice, systemic administration achieved targeted genome editing, partial dystrophin restoration, and improved muscle function. In non-human primates, efficient on-target editing was achieved with no dose-limiting toxicity identified under the conditions tested. In an open-label, dose-escalation, first-in-human clinical trial (NCT06594094), post-treatment muscle biopsies provided early molecular evidence of hfCas12Max-mediated genome editing and detectable dystrophin expression in participants with DMD. However, at the higher dose level (1.0 × 1014 vg/kg), one participant experienced a treatment-related fatal serious adverse event, characterized by marked complement activation and systemic cytokine response shortly after dosing. This work provides initial human proof-of-concept for muscle genome editing while crucially highlighting the critical role of immunologic risks and the narrow therapeutic window of systemic adeno-associated virus (AAV)-CRISPR therapies, underscoring the need to develop safer dosing and immunomodulation strategies.

items.title: Effect of Activin Type II Receptor Signaling in Patients With HFpEF and Pulmonary Hypertension: A Critical Analysis of Biological Mechanisms and Clinical Trials.
items.abstract: The totality of evidence indicates that the mechanisms underlying the increase in pulmonary vascular resistance in patients with combined postcapillary and precapillary pulmonary hypertension (CpcPH) associated with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) differ meaningfully from those responsible for the increase in pulmonary vascular resistance in patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension. CpcPH-HFpEF is a complex disorder involving the pulmonary veins, left atrium, and pulmonary arterioles, but recent evidence has highlighted a potentially central role for pulmonary venous and left atrial (LA) dysfunction. Epicardial adipose tissue occupies anatomical proximity to both structures, allowing derivative secretory products to influence their structure and function. The most well-characterized proinflammatory adipokine released from an expanded epicardial fat mass is activin A, which causes fibrosis and cardiomyocyte stiffness and senescence in underlying tissues by signaling through activin type II receptor signal transduction. Such signaling regulates pulmonary venular responses to mechanical stretch, and circulating activin A is elevated in patients with HFpEF who have enlarged LA chambers, pulmonary venous hypertension and increased pulmonary vascular resistance. The adipokine hypothesis of HFpEF identified activin A and activin type II receptor signaling as key adipokine mediators in the pathogenesis of HFpEF. Experimentally, activin A signaling promotes the development of both atrial myopathy and HFpEF, and activin type II receptor ligand traps alleviate HFpEF and ameliorate both the pulmonary vascular and left heart abnormalities in experimental models in which CpcPH-HFpEF is induced by obesity. These collective observations led to the prospective hypothesis that adipokine modulation by sotatercept would mediate benefits on the left heart in patients with CpcPH-HFpEF. These expectations were validated when the CADENCE trial showed that sotatercept decreased both pulmonary artery wedge pressures and left atrial volume index in patients with CpcPH-HFpEF, which are effects that could not explained by a decrease in pulmonary vascular resistance. Activin A released from an expanded epicardial adipose tissue promotes both pulmonary venous and left atrial remodeling and fibrosis in vivo, which (in turn) are effects that can be attenuated by an activin A decoy. The efficacy of sotatercept to slow the progression of CpcPH-HFpEF is now being tested in a phase III outcomes trial.
keywords: heart failure with preserved ejection fraction

items.title: Management of Patients with High-risk Localised, Locally Advanced, and Biochemically Recurrent Prostate Cancer: Report from the 2026 Advanced Prostate Cancer Consensus Conference.

sections.objective: Innovations have improved outcomes in high-risk localised, locally advanced, and biochemically recurrent prostate cancer (PC), yet high-level evidence remains limited for many management decisions. The 2026 Advanced Prostate Cancer Consensus Conference (APCCC) surveyed an international panel on key clinical questions to complement evidence-based guidelines. Here we present the voting results for the questions on high-risk localised, locally advanced, and biochemically recurrent PC from APCCC 2026.
sections.methods: Before the conference, a multidisciplinary panel of 144 international PC experts used a modified Delphi process to develop 313 multiple-choice consensus questions, of which 134 covered high-risk localised and locally advanced PC, including prostate-specific antigen (PSA) persistence and PSA recurrence, and side effects of treatment. These questions were administered to the 133 voting panel members "panellists" via a web-based survey prior to the conference.
sections.results: Consensus was defined a priori as ≥75% agreement, with strong consensus defined as ≥90% agreement. Overall, consensus was reached for 44 of the 134 questions (32.8%), with seven questions reaching a strong consensus. Results and limitations The voting results show varying degrees of consensus, as discussed in this article and as detailed in the Supplementary Material. An interactive heat map for the questions can be found at https://apccc.org/APCCC2026-votings-localised-and-locally-advanced-prostate-cancer/. These findings do not include a formal literature review or meta-analysis.
sections.conclusion: The voting results can help physicians and patients navigate controversial areas of clinical management for which evidence is scant or conflicting. The findings can also help funders and policymakers in prioritising areas for future research. Importantly, APCCC 2026 once again identified important gaps (areas of no consensus) that merit evaluation in specifically designed trials.

items.title: Intestinal Candida albicans promotes HCC progression and anti-PD-1 resistance via IL-17A and Trem2+ macrophages.

sections.objective: Whether intestinal fungal dysbiosis contributes to hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) progression and resistance to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) remains unclear. We investigated how gut Candida albicans influences HCC progression, immune remodeling, and response to ICI therapy.
sections.methods: Fecal and tumor samples from patients with HCC, liver cirrhosis, and healthy controls were analyzed using ITS2 sequencing, immune profiling, and correlation analyses. Mechanistic studies focused on four complementary autochthonous murine HCC models and cell-based assays, integrating single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing, genetic and pharmacologic perturbations, Kaede photoconversion, fungal antigen recall assays, antifungal treatment, and anti-PD-1 therapy.
sections.results: Fecal C. albicans abundance was higher in HCC patients and was associated with advanced disease, shorter overall survival, and reduced durable clinical benefit. Across HCC models, C. albicans gavage increased tumor burden and induced a Th17/IL-17A-skewed microenvironment characterized by Trem2+ macrophage accumulation and impaired CD8+ T cell infiltration and function. Antifungal treatment attenuated tumor progression, whereas IL-17A blockade or deficiency largely abrogated C. albicans-associated tumor promotion. Mechanistically, IL-17A induced tumor-derived MCP-1 through ACT1-TRAF6-TAK1 signaling to recruit macrophages and upregulated PAI-1, which activated TGF-β/Smad3 signaling to promote an immunosuppressive Trem2+ macrophage state. These macrophages limited CD8+ T cell recruitment and effector function through coordinated CXCL10 repression and GAL-1 induction, while potentially reinforcing Th17 responses through IL-1β and IL-6. Kaede photoconversion demonstrated enhanced mesenteric lymph node-to-liver Th17 trafficking, while fungal antigen recall assays revealed preferential Th17 responsiveness to C. albicans. C. albicans also impaired anti-PD-1 efficacy in vivo, whereas antifungal treatment partially restored therapeutic responsiveness.
sections.conclusion: Intestinal C. albicans promotes HCC progression and anti-PD-1 resistance through an IL-17A-Trem2+ macrophage circuit, supporting its potential as a biomarker and therapeutic target.
sections.other: Intestinal fungal dysbiosis is increasingly recognized as a component of the gut-liver axis, but its functional contribution to HCC has remained poorly defined. Our study identifies intestinal Candida albicans as a promoter of HCC progression in experimental models and delineates an IL-17A-MCP-1/PAI-1-Trem2+ macrophage circuit that links fungal exposure to impaired CD8+ T-cell immunity and reduced response to PD-1 blockade. These findings are relevant to researchers and clinicians seeking microbiome-associated determinants of HCC progression and immunotherapy resistance. Fecal C. albicans abundance and components of this immune circuit may warrant evaluation as biomarkers for patient stratification and as potential targets for combination therapy. However, the clinical associations reported here are based on modest observational cohorts, and antifungal treatment was tested as a proof-of-concept intervention in mice. Larger prospective studies and more selective therapeutic approaches will therefore be required before these findings can inform clinical management.

items.title: Clinical Phenotypes and Prognostic Heterogeneity of Mild-to-Moderate Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease: A Prospective Community-Based Cohort Study.

sections.objective: The clinical phenotypes, prognosis, and heterogeneity of mild-to-moderate chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) have not been systematically evaluated.
sections.methods: We analysed the baseline and 3-year follow-up data of participants with mild-to-moderate COPD from a prospective community-based cohort study. Mild-to-moderate COPD was defined as a forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1) / forced vital capacity ratio of < 0.70 and FEV1 ≥ 50% of the predicted value. The clinical phenotypes included respiratory symptoms, exacerbation history, emphysema, air trapping, and airway remodelling. Respiratory health outcomes included exacerbations and lung function decline over the 3-year follow-up.
sections.results: Overall, 806 participants with mild-to-moderate COPD were included, of whom 712 (88%) completed the 3-year follow-up. Participants with mild-to-moderate COPD had more severe emphysema, air trapping, and airway remodelling; increased exacerbation risk; and faster annual FEV1 decline than those with preserved spirometry. The severity of airflow obstruction, respiratory symptoms, emphysema, and air trapping, as well as the eosinophilic phenotype, had low overlap in mild-to-moderate COPD. There was significant individual variation in the annual FEV1 decline rate and exacerbation incidence among participants with mild-to-moderate COPD. Emphysema and air trapping were associated with faster FEV1 decline and higher exacerbation risk. Respiratory symptoms and exacerbations in the previous year were associated with a higher acute exacerbation risk but not with faster lung function decline.
sections.conclusion: Mild-to-moderate COPD exhibited distinct clinical phenotypes with significant prognostic heterogeneity. Accurate phenotype identification is essential for targeted intervention, clinical precision management, and prognostic improvement.
sections.other: Do different clinical phenotypes of mild-to-moderate COPD have different prognoses?

items.title: Efficacy and safety of risvutatug rezetecan versus gemcitabine plus docetaxel in relapsed/refractory advanced osteosarcoma: Primary results from the ARTEMIS-011 phase 3 trial.

sections.objective: Patients with relapsed/refractory (R/R) osteosarcoma have a poor prognosis and high unmet needs for effective therapies. Herein, we report primary results from ARTEMIS-011, the multicenter, open-label, randomized phase 3 trial of risvutatug rezetecan (Ris-Rez), a B7-H3-directed antibody-drug conjugate, in Chinese patients with R/R osteosarcoma after ≥2 prior lines of systemic treatment.
sections.methods: Patients (≥12 years) were randomized 2:1 to Ris-Rez 12.0 mg/kg or gemcitabine plus docetaxel (GD), every 3 weeks, stratified by age and lung metastasis. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS) by blinded independent central review (BICR); secondary endpoints included overall survival (OS) and safety.
sections.results: At data cutoff (June 17, 2026), 80 patients were treated with Ris-Rez and 42 with GD; median follow-up was 7.1 months. Median age was 21 years (IQR, 17-34) with 31 (25%) adolescents (12 to <18 years). BICR-assessed PFS significantly improved with Ris-Rez compared with GD (median, 5.5 vs 1.4 months; HR, 0.33; 95% CI, 0.20-0.55; P<0.0001). OS data were immature, with a HR of 0.51 (95% CI, 0.21-1.23). With longer treatment duration with Ris-Rez than GD (median, 4.5 vs 1.5 months), adverse events (AEs) were reported in all patients. No treatment-related AEs (TRAEs) led to death. Grade ≥ 3 TRAEs occurred in 93% of patients with Ris-Rez and 83% with GD, and serious TRAEs in 64% versus 29%, which were predominantly hematologic. TRAEs led to dose reductions in 71% versus 26% of patients with Ris-Rez versus GD, respectively, and permanent discontinuation was infrequent (3.8% vs 2.4%).
sections.conclusion: In ARTEMIS-011, Ris-Rez demonstrated a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in BICR-assessed PFS compared to GD, alongside a numerical trend toward improved OS and manageable safety profile with dose modifications and supportive care, offering a promising new treatment option for patients with R/R advanced osteosarcoma.

items.title: Extended follow-up of tarlatamab in patients with small-cell lung cancer after platinum-based chemotherapy in the randomized phase III DeLLphi-304 study.

sections.objective: In the DeLLphi-304 trial, at a median follow-up of <12 months, tarlatamab significantly improved overall survival (OS; P < 0.001), progression-free survival (PFS; P = 0.002), and patient-reported outcomes (PROs), and demonstrated a favorable safety profile versus chemotherapy. We report efficacy and safety outcomes after extended follow-up in patients with small-cell lung cancer (SCLC).
sections.methods: In this phase III, open-label trial, patients with SCLC whose disease had progressed on or after platinum-based chemotherapy were randomly assigned (1 : 1) to receive either tarlatamab or chemotherapy (topotecan, lurbinectedin, or amrubicin) until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, or death. The primary endpoint was OS. Secondary endpoints included investigator-assessed PFS, objective response, disease control, duration of response per RECIST v1.1, PROs, and safety.
sections.results: As of data cut-off (18 February 2026), median OS was 13.6 and 8.4 months with tarlatamab and chemotherapy, respectively (median follow-up, 23.3 and 22.8 months). Median PFS was 4.2 and 3.2 months, respectively (median follow-up, 22.2 and 21.9 months). Kaplan-Meier estimated OS rates at 12 and 24 months were 55.9% and 30.3% with tarlatamab versus 39% and 14.9% with chemotherapy; corresponding PFS rates at 12 and 24 months were 20.6% and 14.2% versus 5.9% and 2.3%. Objective response rate was 35.4% with tarlatamab, including six confirmed complete responses versus 20.4% with chemotherapy; at data cut-off, ongoing responses were observed in 31.1% (28 of 90) versus 3.8% (2 of 52) of responders, respectively. Sustained disease control for ≥52 weeks was observed in 24.4% versus 4.3%. Treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) led to treatment discontinuation in 3.2% versus 6.6%; grade ≥3 events decreased over time, with no serious TRAEs with onset ≥12 months. Cytokine release syndrome and immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome occurred early in treatment and were predominantly low grade.
sections.conclusion: With extended follow-up, tarlatamab continues to demonstrate sustained and durable clinical benefit and a favorable long-term tolerability profile versus chemotherapy, in patients with SCLC after first-line platinum-based chemotherapy, supporting its use as the standard of care in this setting.

items.title: Update of a Living Network Meta-Analysis Comparing Non-compounded Polidocanol 1% Endovenous Microfoam (Varithena) Ablation versus Endovenous Thermal Ablation in Chronic Venous Insufficiency.

sections.objective: We previously published a network meta-analysis showing no statistically significant difference between commercially manufactured polidocanol 1% endovenous microfoam and endovenous thermal ablation for vein closure or deep vein thrombosis, when polidocanol endovenous microfoam was distinguished from physician-compounded foam. This living network meta-analysis updates the previous analysis comparing the effectiveness and safety of polidocanol endovenous microfoam ablation versus endovenous thermal ablation for the primary treatment of adult patients with venous insufficiency caused by lower-extremity truncal vein incompetence.
sections.methods: Systematic review searches following the prespecified protocol were conducted quarterly through March 2026. No changes were made to selection criteria. Vein closure, deep venous thrombosis, and ulcer healing were summarized as odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals. A composite outcome of disease-specific quality of life or symptom improvement scales was summarized with Hedges' g standardized mean difference.
sections.results: The updated search yielded 507 new citations and 11 new eligible studies, for a total of 24 studies (235,413 patients). Polidocanol endovenous microfoam was not statistically different from endovenous thermal ablation for vein closure (odds ratio 0.71, 95% confidence interval 0.42 to 1.21). A sensitivity analysis at longest follow-up (mean 28 months, range 12-72 months) showed similar results (odds ratio 0.71, 95% confidence interval 0.45 to 1.11). There was no evidence of increased deep venous thrombosis risk with polidocanol endovenous microfoam versus endovenous thermal ablation (odds ratio 0.83, 95% confidence interval 0.29 to 2.43). Post-treatment improvement in disease-specific quality of life or venous insufficiency symptoms showed no statistically significant difference between polidocanol endovenous microfoam and endovenous thermal ablation (standardized mean difference [Hedges' g] 0.04, 95% confidence interval -0.16 to 0.25), though the network was not fully connected. Finally, ulcer healing data was limited, but an exploratory analysis found no evidence of a statistically significant difference.
sections.conclusion: This living network meta-analysis update reinforced the original findings that polidocanol 1% endovenous microfoam is not statistically different from endovenous thermal ablation for venous closure or deep venous thrombosis in the treatment of chronic venous insufficiency, and adds new preliminary information on outcomes relevant to the patient experience. There was no evidence of a statistically significant difference between polidocanol endovenous microfoam ablation and endovenous thermal ablation for a composite of disease-specific quality of life and symptom improvement, or for ulcer healing. The living approach maintains rigor and efficiently keeps evidence current as new studies emerge.

items.title: Remak bundle size, structure, and function are regulated by the Schwann cell basal lamina.
items.abstract: Remak bundles are groups of small-diameter unmyelinated nociceptive axons ensheathed by Schwann cells (SCs). Whereas the development and maturation of myelinating SCs have been extensively studied, the formation of Remak bundles remains poorly understood. By preventing the secretion of type IV collagen from SCs, we observe normal myelin but abnormal Remak bundles. There is a decrease in Remak bundle density, an increase in bundle size, improperly ensheathed axons, and a decrease in mechanosensitivity. While Remak bundle formation appears to be independent of integrin signaling, the loss of type IV collagen leads to a decrease in postnatal SC proliferation. Inducing the emergence of supernumerary SCs rescues Remak bundle architecture and mechanosensitivity. Taken together, our results demonstrate that SC-secreted basal lamina critically regulates Remak SC number, bundle size, and structure. Our findings provide insight into the functional role of Remak bundles and highlight their potential involvement in peripheral neuropathies and neuropathic pain.

items.title: NT-proBNP and Clinical Outcomes in Patients With HFrEF According to Atrial Fibrillation: Insights From QUEST.

sections.objective: The Chinese traditional medicine qiliqiangxin (QLQX) improves outcomes in patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) when added to guideline-directed medical therapy. This post hoc analysis of the QUEST (Qiliqiangxin in Heart Failure: Assessment of Reduction in Mortality) trial assessed the efficacy and safety of QLQX according to baseline N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) levels, and examined whether the prognostic value of baseline NT-proBNP varied by atrial fibrillation (AF) status.
sections.methods: QUEST enrolled 3,110 patients with HFrEF and NT-proBNP ≥450 pg/mL, and followed them for a median of 18 months. The primary outcome was cardiovascular (CV) death or heart failure (HF) hospitalization. NT-proBNP was analyzed by quartiles and as a continuous variable.
sections.results: Median baseline NT-proBNP was 1,731 pg/mL. Higher baseline NT-proBNP independently predicted greater risk of the primary outcome (adjusted HR for Q4 vs Q1: 4.03 [95% CI: 3.12-5.20]). The prognostic value of baseline NT-proBNP for all outcomes was consistent irrespective of AF status. At 3 months, QLQX reduced NT-proBNP by 10% compared with placebo. The HRs for the primary composite with QLQX vs placebo were 1.13 (95% CI: 0.73-1.76), 0.76 (95% CI: 0.54-1.06), 0.73 (95% CI: 0.55-0.95), and 0.75 (95% CI: 0.59-0.95) from the lowest to the highest NT-proBNP quartiles, respectively (Pinteraction = 0.48). Results were consistent for CV death, HF hospitalization, and total HF hospitalizations, and when NT-proBNP was modeled continuously (all Pinteraction ≥ 0.30).
sections.conclusion: The treatment effect of QLQX on CV events was consistent across the spectrum of baseline NT-proBNP in HFrEF. Baseline NT-proBNP strongly predicted the risk of CV outcomes and mortality, irrespective of AF status. (Qiliqiangxin in Heart Failure: Assessment of Reduction in Mortality [QUEST]; ChiCTR1900021929).

items.title: Liver Extracellular Volume in Patients With Tricuspid Regurgitation: A Novel Prognostic Marker.

sections.objective: Liver extracellular volume (L-ECV), a novel cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) parameter of systemic venous congestion, might help to stratify tricuspid regurgitation (TR) patients at higher risk, but its role in this context is unexplored. The aim of this study was to assess the incremental prognostic relevance of L-ECV in a large TR cohort.
sections.methods: Data were collected from patients with TR referred to CMR between 2019 and 2024 who had parametric mapping analysis for L-ECV quantification. The primary endpoint was the composite of all-cause mortality and heart failure (HF) hospitalization, under medical management.
sections.results: In 462 patients included (median age: 67 years; 43% female), median left ventricular ejection fraction was 51% (Q1-Q3: 40%-59%), median tricuspid regurgitant fraction was 21% (Q1-Q3: 14%-33%), and median L-ECV was 31% (Q1-Q3: 28%-35%). When dividing the cohort according to median L-ECV value, patients with high L-ECV (≥ median) showed worse baseline status with more clinical and imaging signs of right HF and (after a median follow-up of 2.1 years) poorer survival free from the primary outcome (P < 0.001) compared with patients with low L-ECV. High L-ECV independently predicted the outcome even after multivariable adjustment accounting for TR severity, biventricular ejection fraction, and pulmonary pressure (adjusted HR: 1.82; 95% CI: 1.03-3.18; P = 0.030). Finally, L-ECV showed incremental prognostic value compared with TRI-SCORE when assessed in a nested Cox model.
sections.conclusion: In our large real-world TR cohort, L-ECV appeared as a novel, powerful CMR marker of right HF with an independent and incremental prognostic value to stratify patients with TR at higher risk of events.

items.title: A deep learning model for detection and staging of osteonecrosis of the femoral head on x-ray images: a retrospective, large-scale, multicentre study in China.

sections.objective: Accurate detection and staging of osteonecrosis of the femoral head (ONFH) are essential for effective treatment yet frequently require specialist expertise and advanced equipment. To address this requirement, we aimed to develop a deep learning-based diagnostic model for the automatic detection and staging of ONFH using x-ray images, and compared its performance with clinicians to allow them to improve their diagnostic performance.
sections.methods: In this retrospective, large-scale, multicentre study, we developed our deep learning model, Osteonecrosis Artificial Intelligence Diagnostician (OsteoAID), which was based on the You Only Look Once version 8 (YOLOv8) detection network and trained on a multicentre x-ray dataset. The dataset, dated from Jan 1, 2015, to Dec 31, 2023, and obtained from 16 399 patients across six Chinese tertiary hospitals, included 20 722 anteroposterior hip x-ray images of 28 785 hips, including hips with ONFH, healthy hips, and hips with other conditions radiographically similar to ONFH. To establish a rigorous ground truth for model training and evaluation, expert orthopaedists annotated each image to differentiate ONFH from confounding diseases and additionally classified the confirmed ONFH lesions on the basis of the Ficat and Arlet staging system. To verify the diagnostic performance of OsteoAID, we compared the model's accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, F1 score, and area under the curve (AUC) with those of the original YOLOv8 model on the internal testing set for both the staging and detection tasks. Furthermore, the performance of OsteoAID was compared with the performance of radiologists and orthopaedists on two external testing sets, and its diagnostic performance was also benchmarked against MRI-the gold standard for ONFH diagnosis-with a third external testing set in which x-ray images were staged by corresponding MRI scans. Diagnostic metrics were compared with those of clinicians using t tests and McNemar's tests, with significance set at p<0·05.
sections.results: On the internal testing set, OsteoAID improved the staging accuracy from 87·42% (95% CI 85·88-89·20) to 96·44% (94·73-97·17) and the AUC from 88·54% (86·74-90·37) to 96·94% (95·75-97·98) compared with the original YOLOv8 model. For detection the model had a mean average precision of 92·97% (91·73-94·43) at an intersection-over-union threshold of 50%. In comparisons with clinicians on the external testing set I, the model showed staging accuracy of 96·60% (94·27-97·81), which was significantly higher than radiologists (74·96% [73·38-76·85]; p<0·0001) and junior orthopaedists (83·98% [81·27-84·06]; p<0·0001) and similar to that of expert orthopaedists (96·54% [94·18-97·79]; p=0·20). Furthermore, model-assisted diagnostics improved the accuracy of junior orthopaedists by an absolute difference of 12·70% and of radiologists by 21·47%. Although the accuracy improvement for expert orthopaedists was non-significant (an absolute difference of 0·74%; p=0·080), the diagnostic time was substantially reduced across all groups. On external testing set II (which included challenging cases: low-quality x-ray images affected by improper exposure, poor contrast, incomplete field of view, or foreign-object shadows, as well as smartphone photographs of x-ray films), the model showed robust performance even under extreme conditions, achieving an overall staging accuracy of 93·76% (93·09-95·82). Additionally, combining x-ray imaging with the deep learning model produced diagnostic results similar to MRI on external testing set III with an overall accuracy of 96·63% (95·68-97·86) and an AUC of 97·33% (96·65-98·75).
sections.conclusion: The developed deep learning model shows expert-level diagnostic performance in the dual tasks of detecting and staging ONFH by use of anteroposterior x-rays, which can substantially enhance both the diagnostic proficiency and efficiency of clinicians. Consequently, the model could serve as a highly accessible decision-support tool to optimise clinical triage and guide appropriate treatment strategies.

items.title: Two-Year Outcomes of the Prospective THRILLER Registry on Popliteal and Infrapopliteal Endovascular Interventions for CLTI.

sections.objective: Over 70% of patients with chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) present with below-the-knee disease, and there is a growing trend towards endovascular revascularization. The Dutch Chronic Lower Limb-Threatening Ischemia Registry (THRILLER) aimed to provide real-world data on outcomes after popliteal and infrapopliteal endovascular revascularization to guide revascularization strategies.
sections.methods: This prospective multicenter registry included consecutive CLTI patients undergoing popliteal or infrapopliteal endovascular revascularization in seven Dutch hospitals. Primary outcomes were limb salvage and amputation-free survival (AFS) at 24 months, estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method.
sections.results: Between February 2021 and December 2023, a total of 1,119 interventions in 1,060 limbs (938 patients) were included, treating 551 popliteal, 1,352 tibial, and 239 pedal lesions. The median follow-up was 43.6 months (Q1-Q3: 35.5-52.7 months). Overall, 78.4% (831/1,060) of the limbs were Rutherford 5 and 8.1% (86/1,060) were Rutherford 6; 41.3% (382/926) were WIfI (Wound, Ischemia, and foot Infection) stage 4. Technical success was achieved in 92.3% (1,033/1,119). Limb salvage and AFS decreased significantly after technical failure and with increasing WIfI stage and Rutherford category. Compared to Rutherford 5, Rutherford 6 limbs had significantly worse limb salvage (HR: 3.07; 95% CI: 1.89-4.99; P < 0.001) and AFS (HR: 2.07; 95% CI: 1.50-2.86; P < 0.001). For AFS, the excess risk of Rutherford 6 was greatest in the first 3 months (HR: 14.13; 95% CI: 4.94-40.38 vs Rutherford 4; P < 0.001).
sections.conclusion: Endovascular revascularization for popliteal and infrapopliteal disease in patients with CLTI is safe and effective in preventing limb loss and mortality at 2 years, although patients with Rutherford 6 limbs face significantly worse outcomes, particularly in the first 3 months.

items.title: Multimorbidity among older people in three African countries: a population-based cross-sectional study in The Gambia, South Africa, and Zimbabwe.

sections.objective: Multimorbidity is intricately associated with global ageing and presents a key challenge for health systems and individuals. Despite growing recognition of this challenge, the gap in robust, comparable, population-level evidence on multimorbidity in Africa remains substantial. We aimed to describe multimorbidity among older people across five African sites in three countries representing different epidemiological and health-care contexts.
sections.methods: In this population-based cross-sectional study, we recruited adults aged at least 40 years in rural and urban The Gambia, rural and urban South Africa, and urban Zimbabwe (Feb 10, 2022 to Sept 2, 2024). Participants were stratified by site, age-band (40-54 years, 55-69 years, and ≥70 years), and sex. We included 5296 adults (median age 60 years, 53% were women) and recorded their self-reported medical conditions and current medications. We further assessed their height, weight, blood pressure, blood glucose, mental health symptoms, HIV status, and health-related quality of life (HRQoL). We defined multimorbidity as having two or more of 26 chronic conditions. Multimorbidity prevalence was calculated weighted to each country's national population. We evaluated the risk factors for multimorbidity and associations of multimorbidity with HRQoL; multimorbidity clusters were described using latent class analysis.
sections.results: 1926 (36%) of 5296 adults had multimorbidity. The weighted prevalence of multimorbidity was 36% (95% CI 35-37), ranging from 6·6% (5·1-8·1) in rural The Gambia to 62·0% (58·7-65·3) in urban South Africa. Across the three countries, education level, wealth, smoking, alcohol consumption, and BMI were the lowest in The Gambia and the greatest in South Africa, with a rural-urban gradient. Diabetes, hypertension, HIV, mood disorders, arthritis, and fragility fractures were the most common multimorbidity components. People with multimorbidity had lower HRQoL than those without multimorbidity. In Zimbabwe and South Africa, cardiometabolic (42-57% of the population) and HIV-related (25-48% of the population) multimorbidity clusters emerged, characterised by component diseases, risk factors, and associations with HRQoL.
sections.conclusion: Multimorbidity was found to be common among older people in five study settings in three African countries, with notable trends across sites. The high prevalence of multimorbidity in urban South Africa might foreshadow future trends across the African region as the continent's demographic and health transition advances, underscoring the urgent need for coordinated multisectoral strategies to address multimorbidity.

items.title: Accounting for global carbon dioxide production from human metabolism between 1985 and 2015: a modelling study.

sections.objective: Human activity is a dominant driver of global carbon emissions, yet one universal source-human metabolism-has never been quantified using free-living measurements of carbon dioxide (CO2) production at scale. We aimed to describe the contribution of human metabolism to global CO2 emissions between 1985 and 2015.
sections.methods: In this modelling study, we used the largest available database of doubly labelled water (DLW) measurements from 1986 to 2019. The other data sources comprised WHO Global Health Observatory, United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs, and Non-communicable Disease Risk Factor Collaboration. We first allometrically modelled human CO2 production (kg per year) using measurements available for 4479 female and 2277 male participants from the International Atomic Energy Agency DLW database to derive predicted estimates of human CO2 production adjusted for differences in body mass and sex. Second, by combining predicted estimates based on allometric scaling of CO2 production for body mass with available population demographic information, generalised additive models were used to describe the 30-year progression of human body mass and per capita and global CO2 production. We used the time-series country-specific measurements from 1985 to 2015 with population-level global human metabolic CO2 production summarised as cumulative sum for the progression analyses.
sections.results: Data were collected between 1986 and 2019. Mean ± SD (range) participant age was 40 ± 26 (0 to 101) and body mass was 63.3 ± 27.8 (2.4 to 101.9). 9006 measurements from 6756 participants (4479 women and 2277 men) from the DLW database were used to derive estimates of human CO2 production adjusted for differences in body mass and sex. We observed that human metabolic CO2 production approximately doubled over a 30-year period, from 1·18 Gt per year to 2·05 Gt per year. This increase was driven mostly by population growth (>60%) with a minor contribution from increases in body mass. Per capita sex differences equalised at the population level, and continental differences reflect population shifts rather than physiological differences, with Asia accounting for the majority of human metabolic CO2 production among all continents.
sections.conclusion: Our findings suggest that human metabolism is a quantitatively important component of the fast carbon cycle and should be accounted for in carbon system modelling to enhance precision and fidelity. With a projected peak global population in the mid-to-late 21st century, metabolic CO2 production will increasingly contribute to global carbon fluxes.

items.title: Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex strain discordance among people with tuberculosis and a history of household contact: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

sections.objective: Tuberculosis disease clusters within households, but the proportion of disease among household contacts that results from recent within-household transmission remains unclear. We aimed to estimate the prevalence of Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex strain discordance among pairs of individuals with tuberculosis and a history of household contact, and the proportion of all tuberculosis disease attributable to recent household transmission.
sections.methods: In this systematic review and meta-analysis, we included empirical studies or systematic reviews published in English from Jan 1, 1985, to Jan 26, 2024, that described at least ten pairs of individuals with a history of household contact, in which both people had active tuberculosis and their isolates were strain-typed using RFLP, mycobacterial interspersed repetitive unit-variable-number tandem repeat, or whole-genome sequencing. We excluded studies that only collected data on residence for isolates of the same strain and studies that used preselection for both index and secondary cases. Searches of MEDLINE, Embase, Global Health, Web of Science, and POPLINE databases were updated on Jan 26, 2024. Titles and abstracts and then full texts were screened, and data were extracted independently, by two reviewers, with disagreements resolved by consensus. Summary data were extracted from published reports; when necessary, we contacted study authors, some of whom reanalysed data. The main outcome was the prevalence of strain discordance among pairs of individuals with tuberculosis and a history of household contact. Our main analyses excluded studies using 12-loci or 15-loci mycobacterial interspersed repetitive unit-variable-number tandem repeat and studies performed during tuberculosis outbreaks, as these were considered to be at high risk of bias. We used an inverse variance heterogeneity model applying a double-arcsine transformation to stabilise variance. The proportion of total variability due to between-study heterogeneity was estimated using I2. We estimated the proportion of all tuberculosis attributable to recent household transmission as the product of strain concordance and the proportion of all cases in the community with a history of household exposure to a putative index case, which we derived from external data. Sensitivity analyses assessed robustness to the choice of model and to varying assumptions about household size when estimating the attributable fraction. Our PROSPERO registration number was CRD42024504096.
sections.results: The updated searches identified an additional 3735 unique records. Thirty studies from 18 countries met the inclusion criteria. Four studies were omitted from the meta-analysis because they were at high risk of bias. The remaining 26 studies comprised 1544 index-secondary patient pairs. A high proportion of total variability was due to between-study heterogeneity (I2 90·3, 95% CI 69·0-95·3%). The overall pooled estimate of the prevalence of strain discordance was 0·47 (95% CI 0·32-0·62). Pooled estimates differed by tuberculosis incidence: 0·30 (0·25-0·34) in low-incidence settings, 0·25 (0·15-0·36) in moderate-incidence settings, and 0·59 (0·41-0·76) in high-incidence settings (p=0·003). The median proportion of tuberculosis disease attributable to recent household transmission was 10·8% (range 1·4-21·1%).
sections.conclusion: Strain discordance is common, particularly in high-incidence settings. These findings suggest that recent household transmission makes a small contribution to the overall burden of tuberculosis disease. In this study, the number of household pairs and geographical diversity of the studies were strengths. Between-study heterogeneity limited precision. Our estimates of attributable fraction relied on external data. Strain discordance does not necessarily imply discordance in drug susceptibility. These results should motivate a greater focus on social protection and interrupting community transmission.

items.title: Ageing in place: how to evaluate current practices following long-term care reforms.
items.abstract: Governments worldwide are investing in ageing in place-that is, policies and programmes that enable older adults to remain in their homes and communities irrespective of income level or functional ability. However, there have been few concerted evaluation efforts to keep up with these reforms. Drawing on country examples from the Netherlands, Norway, and Japan, this Personal View identifies three recurring reform tensions: decentralisation versus coordination, personal versus collective responsibility, and cost containment versus investment. Each reform tension produces unintended consequences that evaluations can detect, prompting midcourse corrections. Importantly, existing evaluation frameworks remain narrowly focused on care expenditure, missing the wider societal consequences of reforms. These frameworks also overlook structural inequities that shape who can and cannot age in place with dignity. We therefore propose an integrated, equity-stratified framework to assess whether ageing in place reforms achieve their stated goals or instead widen the disparities they purport to address.

items.title: Efzofitimod versus placebo in patients with pulmonary sarcoidosis (EFZO-FIT): a multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial.

sections.objective: Oral corticosteroids are currently standard-of-care therapy for pulmonary sarcoidosis, but they are associated with substantial toxicity and reduced health-related quality of life (HRQoL). The EFZO-FIT trial aimed to assess the efficacy and safety of efzofitimod, a novel immunomodulatory fusion protein targeting the neuropilin 2 receptor, as a steroid-sparing agent in pulmonary sarcoidosis.
sections.methods: In this multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial, adults aged 18-75 years with pulmonary sarcoidosis requiring treatment were enrolled at 85 study centres across nine countries (Brazil, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, Netherlands, Spain, UK, and USA). Participants were randomly assigned 1:1:1 using stratified block randomisation to receive monthly intravenous infusions of efzofitimod 3 mg/kg, efzofitimod 5 mg/kg, or placebo over a 48-week treatment period, including a 12-week oral corticosteroid taper targeting 0 mg per day (starting on day 15). Oral corticosteroid dose could be adjusted upwards in the event of worsening sarcoidosis. The primary endpoint was change from baseline in mean daily oral corticosteroid dose at week 48. Outcome and safety analyses were done in participants who received at least one dose of the study drug and had at least one post-baseline efficacy assessment. This study was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05415137) and is complete.
sections.results: Between Sept 22, 2022, and Aug 14, 2025, 331 patients were screened for inclusion. 63 were excluded and 268 participants were randomly assigned to receive placebo (n=91), efzofitimod 3 mg/kg (n=89), or efzofitimod 5 mg/kg (n=88). Four patients were excluded after random assignment (one in the placebo group and three in the efzofitimod 3 mg/kg group). 264 patients who received at least one dose of study treatment and had at least one post-baseline assessment were included in the outcome analysis and safety population (90 in the placebo group, 86 in the efzofitimod 3 mg/kg group, and 88 in the efzofitimod 5 mg/kg group). Among the 264 participants, the mean age was 53·8 years (SD 10·6); 114 (43%) of 264 patients were female and 150 (57%) were male. 168 (64%) identified as White. Mean steroid dose was 10·7 mg per day (SD 4·4) at baseline and 2·9 mg per day (4·5) at week 48. No difference was seen in the magnitude of oral corticosteroid taper between the active and placebo dose groups; the placebo-adjusted change from baseline was 0·02 mg per day in the efzofitimod 3 mg/kg group (95% CI -1·49 to 1·52, p=0·98) and -0·73 mg per day in the efzofitimod 5 mg/kg group (-2·21 to 0·75, p=0·33). The percentage of participants with serious treatment-emergent adverse events was similar between groups. Malaise was more common in the placebo group (five [6%] of 90 patients vs zero in both efzofitimod groups). TEAEs that were more common in the efzofitimod groups included headache (17 [19%] of 88 patients in the efzofitimod 5 mg/kg group, 11 [13%] of 86 patients in the efzofitimod 3 mg/kg group, and four [4%] of 90 patients in the placebo group), sinusitis (nine [10%], six [7%], and two [2%] patients, respectively), wheezing (seven [8%], two [2%], and zero patients, respectively), and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) increased (five [6%], one [1%], and zero patients, respectively). Most adverse events were grade 1 or 2. Two participants died, both in the efzofitimod 3 mg/kg group (one respiratory failure and one incarceration of a pre-existing inguinal hernia). Neither event was considered to be causally related to the treatment.
sections.conclusion: Efzofitimod was well tolerated but did not result in lower steroid doses at week 48 compared with placebo. The results from steroid tapering indicate that oral corticosteroid doses can be more aggressively reduced in many patients with pulmonary sarcoidosis.

items.title: Quantification method affects replicability of eQTL analysis, colocalization and TWAS.
items.abstract: Expression quantitative trait loci (eQTL) mapping, colocalization and transcriptome-wide association studies (TWAS) are widely used to contextualize genome-wide association study loci, yet the impact of upstream RNA-sequencing processing choices on these analyses remains critically unexplored. Two poorly characterized decisions include the transcriptomic reference annotation used for quantification of short-read RNA-sequencing samples, which defines transcript composition and structure, and the quantification method itself. Here, through a comprehensive analysis spanning 48 tissues in GTEx and 7 widely studied and diverse phenotypes, we find that these choices substantially affect eQTL detection and gene expression prediction with significant downstream impacts on colocalization and TWAS results. Concordant results across pipelines are further enriched for longer genes, genes with more isoforms, and greater expression heritability. Our findings demonstrate that seemingly minor methodological decisions substantially affect these common analyses, highlighting the need for standardized practices to ensure reproducible genetic association studies.

items.title: A CD4-lineage erythro-myeloid progenitor within the adult bone marrow defines an alternative pathway for macrophage generation.
items.abstract: Tissue-resident macrophages originate from distinct developmental sources, but their adult replenishment is thought to depend exclusively on circulating monocytes. Here we identify a previously unrecognized CD4-lineage erythro-myeloid progenitor (EMPROR) in the adult bone marrow that provides an alternative pathway for macrophage generation. EMPROR cells are phenotypically and transcriptionally distinct from hematopoietic stem cells, common myeloid progenitors and monocyte precursors, lacking Csf1r and Ccr2 while expressing Cd4 and Kit. Single-cell RNA sequencing, RNA velocity analysis and lineage assays reveal macrophage, neutrophil, megakaryocytic and erythroid potential. EMPROR cells generate perivascular and tumor-associated macrophages independently of CCR2-mediated monocyte recruitment and contribute to erythroid and granulocytic lineages under inflammatory and neoplastic conditions. Transcriptomic comparisons position EMPROR cells closest to embryonic erythro-myeloid progenitors, indicating the persistence of an embryonic-like program in adult bone marrow. These findings reveal an alternative pathway of adult myelopoiesis that sustains macrophage diversity beyond the classical monocyte lineage.

items.title: Impact of Recurrent Mitral Regurgitation Following Mitral Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair on Long-Term Outcomes.

sections.objective: Residual mitral regurgitation (MR) after mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER) is a major determinant of outcome. However, the prognostic impact of recurrent mitral regurgitation (recMR) after initially successful M-TEER remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the association between recMR after successful M-TEER and long-term mortality across degenerative mitral regurgitation (DMR) and functional mitral regurgitation (FMR).
sections.methods: This retrospective cohort included 461 consecutive patients with MR undergoing successful M-TEER (residual mitral regurgitation ≤2+ at discharge) between 2008 and 2021. recMR was defined as ≥1-grade increase in mitral regurgitation severity at follow-up compared with discharge. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality.
sections.results: Among 461 patients with MR undergoing M_TEER (mean age 75.0 ± 9.1 years; 60.7% male [280 of 461]; 29.3% [135 of 461] had DMR), recMR occurred in 31.7% (146 of 461) (FMR in 31.9% [104 of 326]; DMR in 31.1% [42 of 135]). The median follow-up time was 3.44 years (Q1-Q3: 1.51-3.99 years). In a 12-month landmark analysis, absence of recMR was associated with improved survival (log-rank, P = 0.0088). At 4 years, all-cause mortality was 44.8% (95% CI: 38.7%-50.3%) in patients without recMR and 56.3% (95% CI: 47.2%-63.9%) in those with recMR. In multivariable Cox regression, recMR independently predicted higher mortality (HR: 1.43; 95% CI: 1.06-1.93; P = 0.019). The survival difference was significant in patients with DMR (log-rank, P = 0.014) but not with FMR (P = 0.11).
sections.conclusion: recMR is common and independently associated with increased mortality after M-TEER, with a more pronounced effect in patients with DMR. Identification of patients at risk may inform closer surveillance and timely reintervention.

items.title: Sacituzumab Tirumotecan plus Pembrolizumab in PD-L1-Negative Advanced NSCLC.

sections.objective: Pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy with a platinum-based agent and pemetrexed is a widely used standard first-line treatment option for patients with programmed death ligand 1 (PD-L1)-negative advanced nonsquamous non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) without targetable genomic alterations, but outcomes remain suboptimal.
sections.methods: In this phase 3, open-label, randomized trial, we evaluated sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab in patients with previously untreated locally advanced or metastatic nonsquamous NSCLC without targetable genomic alterations and a PD-L1 tumor proportion score of less than 1%. Patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab or chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab. The primary end point was progression-free survival as assessed by blinded independent central review. Overall survival was a secondary end point.
