items.abstract: For more than two millennia, Archimedean screws have been used for water pumping and, more recently, as turbines in hydroelectric power stations[1]. Their helical-blade structure, essential to their function, is also found in chiral molecules and nanostructures, where injected electric current has been proposed to generate torque-mediated rotation[2,3]. Here, we present a torque-driven molecular machine with a rotor actuated by electric current and conductance enhanced by its rotation. Suspending a helicene molecule between two electrode tips, we show that an applied voltage induces cyclic molecular motion with 100% directional preference that can be inverted by the voltage's polarity. Above a voltage threshold, the current through the rotating molecule is significantly enhanced, and the enhancement onset is tuned by stretching or compressing the helical molecule. Such effects were absent in previous helical molecular junctions, likely due to structural and operational differences[4-6]. Calculations show that molecular rotation by current-induced forces explains both the observed cyclic motion and current enhancement. This mechanism predicts a transition from stepwise to continuous rotation at a threshold voltage, yielding a current increase as rotation allows adopting highly conducting configurations not accessible at rest. Our work introduces a prototype for a new class of torque-driven molecular machines with perfect rotor unidirectionality and significant current modulation.

items.title: Imaging electron-hole asymmetry in the quantum melting of generalized Wigner crystals.
items.abstract: Two-dimensional moiré materials provide a versatile platform to explore phase transitions in strongly correlated systems. Using scanning tunneling microscopy, we imaged the density-driven melting of generalized Wigner crystals (GWCs) and Mott insulators (MIs) in electron-doped, near-60°-twisted molybdenum diselenide bilayers featuring a triangular moiré superlattice. We observed notable electron-hole asymmetry in GWC melting: Hole-doped GWCs yielded interaction-driven disordered states, whereas electron-doped GWCs melted into delocalized liquid-like states. This asymmetry arose from the broken particle-hole symmetry of the moiré superlattice, which produced electron and hole Fermi pockets with different momentum geometries upon GWC condensation. MI states melted without such asymmetry, consistent with the absence of a symmetry-breaking density modulation. This work provides direct visualization of the emergent phases that appear as GWCs undergo quantum melting transitions.

items.title: Ultrarapid decision-making in an avian brain.
items.abstract: Perceptual decision-making is well studied in mammals, but its operation in other vertebrates remains unclear. We show that carrion crows (Corvus corone) make deliberate decisions in a classic visual motion discrimination task with unprecedented speed, reporting choices in approximately 235 milliseconds on average, which is roughly twice as fast as has been observed in monkeys or humans and without sacrificing accuracy. Recordings from the pallial endbrain reveal that direction-selective neurons encode the upcoming choice as early as about 70 milliseconds after stimulus onset and about 170 milliseconds before the response, with ramping activity scaling with sensory evidence and converging at response onset. These findings highlight the extraordinary efficiency of avian decision-making circuitry, possibly shaped by evolutionary pressures for rapid visuomotor control.

items.title: Dynamic functionality-enabled fast and selective transport in nanochannels.
items.abstract: Nanochannels capable of fast and selective mass transport are central to applications in energy, resources, biomedicine, and the environment. However, extreme nanoscale confinement, often coupled with rigid channel environments, imposes substantial frictional and adhesive barriers, causing sluggish transport and constrained selectivity. We identified nanochannel dynamics as a key to addressing these challenges by harnessing the intrinsic mobility (e.g., self-rotation) of confined functionalities to enhance molecular transport. Through a combination of experiments and simulations, we demonstrated that such dynamics reshape transport by promoting kinetic energy transfer and enabling more efficient molecular relays, thereby improving separation performance beyond current benchmarks. Our findings highlight the role of nanochannel dynamics in regulating mass transport under confinement and provide a framework for designing advanced nanochannel systems.

items.title: Sibeprenlimab in IgA Nephropathy - Final Phase 3 Trial Analysis.

sections.objective: Sibeprenlimab, a humanized monoclonal antibody, selectively inhibits the cytokine A proliferation-inducing ligand (APRIL), a key driver of IgA nephropathy. Preliminary trial results with regard to the primary end point of the 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio at 9 months after treatment as compared with baseline have been reported, but secondary end points, including outcomes regarding estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), have not.
sections.methods: We randomly assigned adults with IgA nephropathy to receive subcutaneous sibeprenlimab (at a dose of 400 mg) or placebo every 4 weeks. The key secondary end point was the annualized slope of the eGFR over 24 months. Other secondary end points included the change in eGFR from baseline to 24 months, a composite kidney end point of kidney-function decline or kidney failure, and pharmacodynamic and safety end points.
sections.results: A total of 510 patients underwent randomization - 259 to receive sibeprenlimab and 251 to receive placebo. The annualized eGFR slope over 24 months was 0.3 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 of body-surface area per year (95% confidence interval [CI], -0.4 to 0.9) with sibeprenlimab and -4.2 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 per year (95% CI, -4.9 to -3.6) with placebo (between-group difference, 4.5 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 per year; 95% CI, 3.6 to 5.4; P<0.001). The least-squares mean treatment difference for the change in eGFR from baseline to 24 months was 9.2 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 (95% CI, 7.1 to 11.4; P<0.001). A composite kidney end-point event occurred in 1 patient (0.4%) in the sibeprenlimab group and in 28 patients (11.2%) in the placebo group (adjusted difference, -10.8 percentage points; hazard ratio, 0.029; 95% CI, 0.004 to 0.214; P<0.001). Adverse events occurred in 235 patients (90.7%) in the sibeprenlimab group and 226 patients (90.0%) in the placebo group; serious adverse events occurred in 21 patients (8.1%) and 32 patients (12.7%), respectively; and serious infections in 5 patients (1.9%) and 10 patients (4.0%). No deaths were reported.
sections.conclusion: Among patients with IgA nephropathy, treatment with sibeprenlimab stabilized the eGFR slope over 24 months, a finding consistent with a reduced risk of kidney-function decline. (Funded by Otsuka Pharmaceutical Development and Commercialization; VISIONARY ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05248646.).

items.title: Atacicept in IgA Nephropathy - Phase 3 Trial Final Efficacy Analysis.

sections.objective: Atacicept resulted in a significantly greater reduction in the urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio than placebo in a previously published analysis of this trial, ORIGIN 3. Final prespecified efficacy results are reported here.
sections.methods: We randomly assigned adults with biopsy-confirmed IgA nephropathy to receive weekly subcutaneous atacicept at a dose of 150 mg or placebo. We carried out final analyses of two secondary end points: the change in the estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) at week 52 and the annualized eGFR slope through week 104; additional hierarchically tested end points and safety were assessed.
sections.results: Of 431 patients who underwent randomization, 428 received atacicept or placebo (214 per group). At week 52, the mean change in the eGFR was -0.11 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 of body-surface area (95% confidence interval [CI], -1.44 to 1.22) with atacicept and -5.69 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 (95% CI, -7.04 to -4.35) with placebo (mean difference, 5.58 ml per minute per 1.73 m2; 95% CI, 3.68 to 7.48; P<0.001). Through week 104, the mean annualized eGFR slope was -0.60 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 (95% CI, -1.62 to 0.41) with atacicept and -5.60 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 (95% CI, -6.64 to -4.57) with placebo (difference, 5.00 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 per year; 95% CI, 3.55 to 6.45; P<0.001). Composite kidney-disease progression occurred in 11 patients (5.1%) in the atacicept group and in 38 patients (17.8%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.24; 95% CI, 0.12 to 0.48; P<0.001); no patients in the atacicept group had progression to dialysis, transplantation, or death, as compared with 7 patients in the placebo group. Adverse events occurred in 160 of 214 patients (74.8%) in the atacicept group and in 167 of 214 patients (78.0%) in the placebo group; serious adverse events occurred in 7.0% and 15.4%, respectively. One patient (in the placebo group) died.
sections.conclusion: Atacicept slowed and stabilized the decline in the eGFR as compared with placebo. (Funded by Vera Therapeutics; ORIGIN 3 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04716231.).

items.title: Helicobacter pylori Infection - Advances, Challenges, and the Road Ahead.
items.abstract: The discovery of Helicobacter pylori has revolutionized the prevention and treatment of gastritis, peptic ulcers, and, most important, gastric cancer. In the past 40 years, enormous progress has been achieved in the clinical and basic research on H. pylori infection. However, challenges in preventing and treating H. pylori infection exist owing to the lack of an H. pylori vaccine and the ever-increasing resistance to antibiotics worldwide. This review summarizes the history of and key milestones in H. pylori research, provides an update on the understanding of the pathogenesis and global burden of H. pylori infection and the screening strategy for the primary prevention of gastric cancer, and focuses on the emerging trends in the management of H. pylori infection.

items.title: Ianalumab for the Treatment of Patients with Sjögren's Disease.

sections.objective: Sjögren's disease is a complex, systemic autoimmune disease with no approved targeted therapies. Ianalumab is an IgG1 monoclonal antibody with a dual mechanism of action, depleting B cells through antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity and inhibiting B-cell activation and survival through blockade of B-cell activating factor receptor.
sections.methods: We conducted two 52-week, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trials involving patients with active Sjögren's disease. Patients in the NEPTUNUS-1 trial were assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive subcutaneous ianalumab (300 mg monthly) or placebo; patients in the NEPTUNUS-2 trial were assigned in a 1:1:1 ratio to receive 300 mg of ianalumab monthly or every 3 months or placebo. The primary end point was the change from baseline in the score on the European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology (EULAR) Sjögren's Syndrome Disease Activity Index (ESSDAI) at week 48 (scores range from 0 to 123, with higher scores indicating greater disease activity). The first key secondary end point in the hierarchical plan for the NEPTUNUS-1 trial was an ESSDAI response (≥5-point reduction) at week 48; for the NEPTUNUS-2 trial, it was the change from baseline in the score on the Sjögren's Syndrome Symptom Diary (SSSD) or EULAR Sjögren's Syndrome Patient Reported Index (ESSPRI) at week 48.
sections.results: Overall, 275 patients underwent randomization in the NEPTUNUS-1 trial (ianalumab monthly, 137 patients; placebo, 138 patients) and 504 in the NEPTUNUS-2 trial (ianalumab monthly, 168 patients; ianalumab every 3 months, 167 patients; and placebo, 169 patients). In both trials, ianalumab monthly led to a significantly greater decrease in the ESSDAI score at week 48 than placebo, with a between-group difference of -1.3 points (95% confidence interval [CI], -2.6 to 0.0; P = 0.0496) in NEPTUNUS-1 and -1.0 points (95% CI, -2.0 to 0.0; P = 0.04) in NEPTUNUS-2. No significant differences in the incidence of an ESSDAI response or in the change from baseline in SSSD or ESSPRI scores were observed at week 48. The incidence of serious adverse events was similar with ianalumab and placebo. Nonserious local injection-site and systemic injection-related reactions were more common in the ianalumab groups.
sections.conclusion: In these two trials involving patients with active Sjögren's disease, ianalumab at a dose of 300 mg monthly resulted in a significantly greater decrease in disease activity at week 48 than placebo, although there were no significant differences in the incidence of an ESSDAI response or in the change from baseline in SSSD or ESSPRI symptom scores. (Funded by Novartis Pharma; NEPTUNUS-1 and NEPTUNUS-2 ClinicalTrials.gov numbers, NCT05350072 and NCT05349214, respectively.).

items.title: Tambotatug Pelitecan in Small-Cell Lung Cancer after Platinum-Based Therapy.

sections.objective: Tambotatug pelitecan (known as Tam-Peli, a new antibody-drug conjugate that targets the immune-checkpoint molecule B7-H3) showed promising clinical efficacy in patients with relapsed extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer in early-phase trials.
sections.methods: In this phase 3, multicenter, open-label, randomized trial, we assigned eligible patients with small-cell lung cancer that had progressed after first-line platinum-based therapy in a 1:1 ratio to receive tambotatug pelitecan or topotecan. The primary end point was overall survival. The key secondary end points were progression-free survival and objective response as assessed by investigators. Here, we report the results from the prespecified interim analysis.
sections.results: A total of 451 patients underwent randomization: 225 were assigned to receive tambotatug pelitecan and 226 to receive topotecan. Overall survival was significantly longer with tambotatug pelitecan than with topotecan - a median of 13.3 months (95% confidence interval [CI], 12.1 to could not be estimated), as compared with 9.4 months (95% CI, 7.7 to 10.5); the stratified hazard ratio for death was 0.46 (95% CI, 0.35 to 0.62; P<0.001). Treatment with tambotatug pelitecan also resulted in significantly longer progression-free survival than treatment with topotecan (median, 7.4 months [95% CI, 6.1 to 7.6] vs. 2.8 months [95% CI, 1.8 to 3.0]; stratified hazard ratio, 0.29 [95% CI, 0.23 to 0.37]; P<0.001). A confirmed objective response occurred in 59.1% of the patients in the tambotatug pelitecan group, as compared with 9.7% of those in the topotecan group (P<0.001). The overall incidence of adverse events of grade 3 or higher was lower with tambotatug pelitecan than with topotecan (55.4% vs. 77.9%).
sections.conclusion: Among patients with relapsed small-cell lung cancer after platinum-based therapy, treatment with tambotatug pelitecan resulted in longer overall survival, longer progression-free survival, and a higher percentage of patients with an objective response than treatment with topotecan, with a lower incidence of adverse events of grade 3 or higher. (Funded by the Innovative Drug Research and Development National Science and Technology Major Project and MediLink Therapeutics; TAISHAN-302 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06612151.).

items.title: Milvexian with Antiplatelet Therapy after Acute Coronary Syndrome Event.

sections.objective: Patients are at increased risk for recurrent ischemic events after an acute coronary syndrome event. Milvexian, an oral factor XIa inhibitor, may reduce the risk of major adverse clinical events with minimal bleeding risk.
sections.methods: In this phase 3, randomized, placebo-controlled trial, we evaluated the efficacy and safety of milvexian when added to standard antiplatelet therapy within 7 days after an acute coronary syndrome event. Patients were assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive oral milvexian (25 mg twice daily) or matched placebo. The primary efficacy outcome was a composite of cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, or ischemic stroke as evaluated in a time-to-event analysis. The principal safety outcome was Bleeding Academic Research Consortium (BARC) type 3c or 5 bleeding (intracranial or intraocular bleeding that compromises vision or fatal bleeding).
sections.results: After a planned interim analysis that was based on 556 adjudicated efficacy end points, the trial was terminated for futility. A total of 14,194 patients had been enrolled, with 7094 assigned to receive milvexian and 7100 to receive placebo. After a median follow-up of 12.2 months, a primary efficacy outcome event had occurred in 384 patients (5.4%) in the milvexian group and in 365 patients (5.1%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 1.05; 95% confidence interval, 0.91 to 1.21; P = 0.50). BARC type 3c or 5 bleeding occurred in 23 patients (0.3%) in the milvexian group and in 22 patients (0.3%) in the placebo group (P = 0.88).
sections.conclusion: Among patients with a recent acute coronary syndrome event, milvexian did not decrease the risk of cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, or ischemic stroke but did not increase the risk of intracranial or fatal bleeding, as compared with placebo. (Funded by Janssen Research and Development and Bristol Myers Squibb; LIBREXIA ACS ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05754957.).

items.title: Response-Tailored or Standard-Duration Antibiotic Treatment for Infective Endocarditis.

sections.objective: In patients with infective endocarditis on the left side of the heart, the current recommendation of up to 6 weeks of antibiotic therapy is based largely on expert consensus opinion. Whether a clinical response-tailored antibiotic management strategy can shorten treatment duration without compromising safety is unclear.
sections.methods: In this international, open-label, randomized trial, we assigned adults in stable condition with infective endocarditis caused by Staphylococcus aureus, Enterococcus faecalis, or streptococcus species to receive either response-tailored or standard-duration antibiotic therapy. Before randomization, all the patients received at least the prespecified 2 to 4 weeks of therapy and met criteria for clinical stabilization. After randomization, patients in the tailored-therapy group discontinued antibiotics and those in the standard-therapy group continued standard treatment (total duration, 4 to 6 weeks). The primary efficacy end point was days alive without antibiotic treatment for infective endocarditis or bacteremia within 6 months after randomization (tested for superiority). The primary safety end point was a composite of death from any cause, unplanned cardiac surgery, or symptomatic embolic events within 6 months after randomization (tested for noninferiority; margin, 7.5 percentage points). Relapse of bacteremia or infective endocarditis was a key secondary end point.
sections.results: A total of 508 patients underwent randomization, with 255 assigned to response-tailored therapy and 253 to standard-duration therapy. The median time alive without antibiotic treatment was 183 days (interquartile range, 181 to 183) with tailored therapy and 169 days (interquartile range, 166 to 171) with standard therapy (Hodges-Lehmann estimated difference, 13 days; 95% confidence interval [CI], 12 to 13; P<0.001 for superiority). A primary safety end-point event occurred in 21 patients (8.2%) with tailored therapy and in 27 patients (10.7%) with standard therapy (absolute between-group difference, -2.4 percentage points; 95% CI, -7.7 to 2.7; P<0.001 for noninferiority), indicating noninferiority. Relapse occurred in 13 patients (5.1%) with tailored therapy and in 4 patients (1.6%) with standard therapy (P = 0.04).
sections.conclusion: Among patients with infective endocarditis on the left side of the heart, the use of a response-tailored antibiotic strategy resulted in a longer time alive without antibiotic therapy than standard-duration therapy and met the criterion for noninferiority with respect to safety but was associated with a higher incidence of relapse of bacteremia or infective endocarditis. (Funded by Sygeforsikringen "danmark" and others; POET II ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT03851575.).

items.title: Surgery in Motion: Different Surgical Techniques for Inguinal Lymph Node Dissection in Penile Cancer.
items.abstract: Inguinal lymph node dissection (ILND) remains a cornerstone of nodal management in penile cancer, providing definitive treatment for clinically node-positive disease and surgical staging for high-risk clinically node-negative patients when dynamic sentinel node biopsy (DSNB) is unavailable. Despite its oncological importance, ILND is associated with substantial morbidity. Over the past decade, minimally invasive (MI) approaches have emerged as alternatives to open ILND, with the potential to reduce wound-related complications while maintaining oncological efficacy. This Surgery in Motion article provides a practical overview of contemporary open, video-endoscopic (VEIL), and robot-assisted (RAVEIL) ILND techniques, integrating anatomical principles, technical variations, and current clinical evidence. Open ILND remains the reference approach, particularly in patients with advanced nodal disease, while MI techniques may be considered in selected patients with limited nodal disease at experienced centres. Across all approaches, meticulous adherence to anatomical templates, appropriate patient selection, and preservation of lymphatic and vascular structures where oncologically feasible are key principles for minimising morbidity. Emerging robotic and image-guided technologies may further refine ILND, although their clinical benefits and long-term oncological outcomes require further evaluation. This stepwise educational review and accompanying surgical video aim to support surgical training, standardisation, and safe implementation of contemporary ILND techniques.

items.title: Diagnostic Contribution of Endobronchial Optical Coherence Tomography in the Multidisciplinary Diagnosis of Interstitial Lung Disease.

sections.objective: Less-invasive, lower-risk alternatives to surgical lung biopsy (SLB) have emerged for interstitial lung disease (ILD) diagnosis, such as transbronchial lung cryobiopsy (TBLC) and Envisia Genomic Classifier (EGC), but suffer from limited sampling and simplified binomial classification, respectively. Endobronchial optical coherence tomography (EB-OCT) is a low-risk, large-volume bronchoscopic imaging modality with microscopic resolution, which accurately detects features and patterns for ILD diagnosis as previously validated against SLB.
sections.methods: Patients with low-confidence ILD diagnosis clinically referred for both TBLC with EGC were enrolled to undergo concurrent EB-OCT imaging. Each modality was interpreted independently by blinded pathologists. Separate MDD sessions were conducted at two independent sites, including one without prior EB-OCT experience.
sections.results: Fifteen patients were included (9 male; mean age: 70.6 years) with final diagnoses of UIP/IPF (n=5), secondary UIP (n=2), and various non-UIP ILDs (n=8) in agreement at both MDDs. EB-OCT provided diagnostic data that was in agreement with final MDD diagnosis for 100% of subjects (15/15), including in the 40% of subjects (6/15) where TBLC was non-diagnostic. In the subjects where TBLC yielded diagnostic data (60%, 9/15), EB-OCT diagnosis was in agreement. EB-OCT combined with TBLC/EGC increased diagnostic confidence and/or narrowed the differential diagnosis from baseline clinical/radiologic data review in all subjects, with replication across both independent MDDs.
sections.conclusion: In this pilot study, we demonstrate EB-OCT is a safe, large-volume imaging method that detects microscopic features and patterns for ILD diagnosis, which increases diagnostic confidence in the context of MDD and complements TBLC and EGC. Future multicenter studies are needed to further validate these findings.
sections.other: How does EB-OCT contribute to ILD diagnosis and diagnostic confidence at multidisciplinary discussion (MDD) when paired with clinically indicated TBLC and EGC?

items.title: Determinants of lung cancer screening follow-up care in community care settings: A qualitative multi-case study in the ACCELL trial.

sections.objective: Adherence to lung cancer screening (LCS) follow-up is essential to achieve mortality benefits from screening. However, population-based studies demonstrate follow-up is <50% in clinical settings. Determinants (barriers and facilitators) of LCS follow-up in community settings are under-studied.
sections.methods: This qualitative multi-case study informed a pre-post intervention trial, testing pragmatic interventions to address LCS follow-up in community settings. We conducted rapid ethnographic assessments (REA) through virtual and in person site visits of LCS delivery in three community-based healthcare systems in Washington state. Additionally at the two future intervention sites, we conducted provider and patient interviews. Interview transcripts were analyzed using Rapid Group Analysis Process. All data were triangulated according to Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research and National Institute on Minority Health and Health Disparities Research Framework domains.
sections.results: Twenty-eight organizational leaders, providers, and staff participated in REA. Thirty-one patients and 15 providers from the future intervention sites participated in interviews. Determinants of LCS follow-up in the intervention domain included role of primary care, LCS complexity and care process standardization. In the inner setting domain (organization and clinic), screening prioritization, EHR use, radiology support, and context of wellness visits affected LCS. The main theme in the outer setting domain was the influence of social determinants of health on LCS. In the individuals domain, shared beliefs in LCS and LCS education and information sharing were key. In the process implementation domain, clinical champions and use of data and metrics were crucial.
sections.conclusion: Integrated findings suggest determinants related to LCS complexity, care fragmentation, socioeconomic status and language, and limitations of PCPs could be overcome through more centralized approaches. However, increased use of EHR tools, increased education and standardizing LCS performance metrics may enable follow-up in decentralized settings.
sections.other: What are determinants of LCS follow-up in community settings? NCT06324110.

items.title: Psoriasis: Which therapy for which patient, updated, part II. Focus on special populations and chronic infections.
items.abstract: Choosing systemic therapy for psoriasis remains challenging in populations underrepresented in clinical trials, including pregnant and pediatric patients, patients with chronic infections, and those with difficult-to-treat phenotypes. Since the 2019 version of this article, therapeutic options have expanded substantially, including new pediatric approvals, oral targeted agents, and biologics with increasingly phenotype-specific evidence. This second article in the continuing medical education series reviews systemic treatment selection for moderate-to-severe psoriasis in pregnancy, pediatric patients, hepatitis, HIV, latent tuberculosis, nail psoriasis, erythrodermic psoriasis, generalized pustular psoriasis, and palmoplantar psoriasis. Emphasis is placed on balancing efficacy, safety, monitoring burden, infection/reactivation risk, reproductive considerations, and disease phenotype. Traditional agents remain useful in selected scenarios, while IL-17, IL-23, IL-36, TNF-α, TYK2, JAK, and other targeted therapies offer expanding options. Available evidence is summarized with expert-opinion recommendations where comparative data are limited.

items.title: Early Outcomes of Thoracic Branch Endoprosthesis in Aortic Arch Pathologies: A Nordic Multicentre Study.

sections.objective: This study evaluated the feasibility and early clinical outcomes of the Gore thoracic branch endoprosthesis (TBE) in the treatment of aortic arch pathologies.
sections.methods: This multicentre retrospective study, conducted and reported in accordance with the STROBE statement, included consecutive patients undergoing thoracic endovascular aortic repair with TBE between February 2024 and July 2025. No restrictions were applied regarding the type or extent of aortic disease, use of staged procedures, or concomitant adjunctive endovascular interventions. Primary endpoints were technical success, thirty day mortality, and overall survival, while endoleak occurrence, primary target vessel patency, stroke, and spinal cord ischaemia (SCI) were secondary.
sections.results: Sixty-four patients (median age 73 years [interquartile range 59, 77]; 69% men) were included. Indications for treatment included degenerative aneurysm (n = 26; 41%), chronic dissection (n = 18; 28%), subacute dissection (n = 11; 17%), and acute dissection (n = 9; 14%). The left subclavian artery was the target vessel in 59 cases (92%), followed by the brachiocephalic trunk in three (5%) and the left common carotid artery in two (3%). Technical success was achieved in 95% of cases (n = 61), with failures attributed to two type Ia endoleaks and one type IIIa endoleak. Thirty day mortality was 3% (n = 2). Early unplanned re-interventions occurred in four patients (6%). No strokes or SCI were observed. Median follow up was 6 months (2, 10). No late mortality was observed, and primary patency of all branches was 100%. One late unplanned re-intervention, unrelated to the TBE device, was required. During follow up, 12 patients (19%) had endoleaks, including type II (n = 4), type Ia (n = 4), type Ib (n = 2), type III (n = 1), and type V (n = 1). Estimated freedom from type Ia endoleak at 12 months was 93 ± 3%, while estimated overall survival at 12 months was 97 ± 2%.
sections.conclusion: TBE demonstrated high technical success and acceptable early outcomes across a range of aortic arch pathologies. However, the relatively high rate of endoleaks and need for early re-interventions highlight the importance of careful patient selection and close continuous post-operative surveillance.

items.title: A vagal gut-brain axis for feeding-induced gastric secretion in mice.
items.abstract: Feeding begins with food-seeking and ends with nutrient absorption and waste elimination. Although meal-related sensory cues shape feeding behavior, how they engage neural circuits to control digestion remains unclear. We dissected vagal gut-brain-gut pathways mediating meal-induced gastric secretion. Stomach-innervating vagal afferents were necessary and sufficient for secretion. Among them, Glp1r+ and Sst+ neurons drove acid, pepsin, and gastrin secretion, whereas Oxtr+ and Vip+ neurons had little effect. Piezo2 was expressed in Glp1r+ mechanosensory afferents, and conditional deletion of Piezo2 attenuated distension-evoked secretion. On the efferent limb, genetically defined vagal motor-neuron subsets showed distinct secretory effects: Cck+ neurons broadly increased acid, pepsin, and gastrin, whereas Grp+ neurons preferentially affected acid secretion. Finally, enteric circuit dissection revealed modular output control, with Calb2+ neurons driving secretion with minimal motility effects. Together, these results define a cell-type-resolved vagal-enteric architecture for gastric control.

items.title: Covered Stent Assisted Coil Embolisation of a Rare Splenomesenteric Artery Aneurysm - A Case Report and Literature Review.
items.abstract: BackgroundSplenomesenteric artery aneurysms are a rare clinical entity occurring in <1% of the population, where the splenic artery originates from the superior mesenteric artery (SMA). These aneurysms carry a high risk of rupture due to exposure to high-flow hemodynamic stress near the SMA origin.Case PresentationA 76-year-old female was incidentally diagnosed with a 1.6 cm saccular splenomesenteric aneurysm during investigation for sepsis. The patient underwent successful endovascular exclusion using a combination of a microvascular plug and coil embolisation to address the aneurysm 'front' and 'back' doors, while a covered stent was deployed in the SMA to prevent coil prolapse and preserve mesenteric perfusion. Follow-up at 3 months confirmed successful exclusion with preserved visceral flow.DiscussionDue to the rarity of this anatomical variant, documented in less than 60 cases in English literature, no standardised treatment algorithm exists. This study adds to the literature by demonstrating procedural innovation, refining management strategies and advocating for early intervention for such conditions.

items.title: Resident to Urgent Eye Clinic Transformation and Association With Health Equity and Resident Education.

sections.objective: US ophthalmology residency programs are divided between traditional resident clinic-based models with a separate faculty practice, and universal practice-based models. Little data exist comparing these educational models. To evaluate the association of changing a traditional resident clinic training model to a universal practice plus urgent eye clinic-based residency training model with sociodemographic disparities and resident education.
sections.methods: This was a cross-sectional study conducted at a US academic medical center. All patients presenting to the University of Rochester Flaum Eye Institute between the period July 1, 2017, to June 30, 2019, and the period July 1, 2022, to June 30, 2024, were divided into 4 cohorts for retrospective analysis as follows: resident clinic 2017-2019, faculty practice 2017-2019, urgent eye clinic 2022-2024, and universal practice 2022-2024.
sections.results: Participants were divided into the following 4 cohorts: resident clinic 2017-2019 (6819 patients), faculty practice 2017-2019 (61 847 patients), urgent eye clinic 2022-2024 (5124 patients), and universal practice 2022-2024 (79 001 patients), for a total of 118 459 patients (mean [SD] age, 47 [25] years; 65 186 female [55%]). Pretransition, compared with faculty practice patients, greater proportions of resident clinic patients used Medicaid insurance (62.1% vs 19.4%; difference, 32.0%; 95% CI, 30.9%-33.1%; P < .001) and identified as Asian, Black or African American, multiracial, native (ie, American Indian or Alaska Native), or other (51.9% vs 23.6%; difference, 28.3%; 95% CI, 27.1%-29.5%; P < .001). Posttransition, compared with universal practice patients, similar proportions of urgent eye clinic patients used Medicaid insurance (26.8% vs 27.8%; difference, 0.4%; 95% CI, -0.7% to 1.6%; P = .42) and identified as Asian, Black or African American, multiracial, native, or other (29.6% vs 26.8%; difference, 2.8%; 95% CI, 1.5%-4.1%; P < .001). A greater proportion of urgent eye clinic patients presented with high-acuity disease (37.6%) compared with resident clinic patients (20.9%; difference, 16.7%; 95% CI, 15.0%-18.4%; P < .001). Median graduating resident primary cataract surgery volume increased from 148 to 228 cases (difference, 80; 95% CI, 49 to 122; P < .001).
sections.conclusion: Results of this cross-sectionals study show that transforming resident clinic into urgent eye clinic was associated with reduced sociodemographic disparities, enhanced resident exposure to high-acuity disease, and increased resident procedural experience. These results suggest that changes in resident clinic structure may improve both health equity and resident education.
sections.other: The resident clinic was transitioned to urgent eye clinic in July 2022. All former patients from resident clinic were reassigned to the new universal practice. Patient cohorts were compared regarding insurance payor(s) and self-identified race. Level of disease acuity in resident clinic and urgent eye clinic were compared. Graduating resident procedural volumes were compared.

items.title: Incidence and Risk Factors of Recurrent Visual Field Progression in Glaucoma.

sections.objective: A confirmed visual field progression event in glaucoma typically prompts intensification of intraocular pressure (IOP)-lowering therapy, yet the factors associated with recurrent progression after that first event remain poorly characterized. To evaluate the incidence of recurrent visual field progression after an initial Guided Progression Analysis (GPA) likely-progression event and the factors associated with a recurrent event.
sections.methods: This cohort study was conducted among patients receiving routine ophthalmic care between 1998 and 2025 at a single tertiary academic center (Bascom Palmer Ophthalmic Registry). Data were analyzed from February 2026 to August 2026.
sections.results: A total of 7457 eyes of 5086 patients with open-angle glaucoma or suspected glaucoma were included, with a mean (SD) follow-up of 12.4 (4.6) years. Mean (SD) patient age was 60.5 (13.1) years, and 4468 eyes (59.9%) were from female patients. By self-reported race and ethnicity, 203 eyes (2.7%) were from Asian patients, 1718 (23.0%) from Black patients, 1677 (22.5%) from Hispanic patients, and 5536 (74.2%) from White patients. A total of 1951 eyes (26.2%) developed initial GPA likely progression; 635 eyes had adequate follow-up after first progression and IOP data. Among those, 167 (26.3%) recurred. Kaplan-Meier cumulative recurrence was 13.8% at 3 years (95% CI, 11.6%-17.1%) and 43.5% at 10 years (95% CI, 35.8%-52.1%). In multivariable Cox analysis, faster mean deviation (MD) loss before first progression (HR, 1.73 per 1 decibel [dB]/y; 95% CI, 1.39-2.15), higher mean IOP after the first event (HR, 1.09 per 1 mm Hg; 95% CI, 1.05-1.13), less negative MD at first progression (HR, 1.08 per 1 dB; 95% CI, 1.04-1.12), and older age (HR, 1.11 per 5 years; 95% CI, 1.03-1.19) were independently associated with recurrence. Each 10% greater IOP reduction was associated with lower hazard (HR, 0.89; 95% CI, 0.83-0.94). Among eyes with pre-event MD slopes faster than -1.0 dB/y, recurrence occurred in 42.7% of eyes vs 23.4% in slower-progressing eyes (difference, 19.3%; 95% CI, 8.8%-29.9%).
sections.conclusion: Findings from this cohort study suggest that recurrent visual field progression after a first GPA progression event is common; eyes at highest risk had faster pre-event visual field loss, less advanced damage at first progression, higher postevent IOP, and older age. These results may help target intensified monitoring and IOP lowering toward higher-risk eyes.
sections.other: The primary outcomes were the cumulative probability of recurrent visual field progression and hazard ratios (HRs) for factors associated with recurrence.

items.title: Long-term efficacy and safety for the complement factor B inhibitor iptacopan in IgA nephropathy.

sections.objective: Iptacopan, a factor B inhibitor, targets alternative complement pathway overactivation, a key driver of glomerular inflammation in IgA nephropathy. In the phase 3 APPLAUSE-IgAN trial (NCT04578834), iptacopan significantly slowed kidney function decline versus placebo over 24 months (difference in total estimated glomerular filtration rate [eGFR] slope: 3.02 ml/min per 1.73 m2 per year [95% confidence interval (CI) 2.02, 4.01; P < 0.001]).
sections.methods: Patients who completed APPLAUSE-IgAN or the phase 2 iptacopan trial (NCT03373461) could enter an open-label rollover extension program (REP) (NCT04557462). Patients in this REP receive oral iptacopan 200 mg twice daily alongside supportive care. Patients from the phase 2 trial were not included in efficacy analyses.
sections.results: Overall, 194 and 174 patients from the APPLAUSE-IgAN iptacopan and placebo arms, respectively, entered the REP. In patients who received iptacopan for up to 48 months, the total annualized eGFR slope was -3.49 ml/min per 1.73 m2 per year (95% CI -4.17, -2.80). Urine protein-to-creatinine ratio from first morning void (UPCR-FMV) reduction was sustained through 48 months with iptacopan (geometric mean ratio to baseline: 0.61 [95% CI 0.50, 0.75]). Before receiving iptacopan, the total eGFR slope over 24 months in APPLAUSE-IgAN placebo arm patients who entered the REP was -5.29 ml/min per 1.73 m2 per year (95% CI -6.09, -4.49). After switching to iptacopan, the total eGFR slope improved to -2.11 ml/min per 1.73 m2 per year (95% CI -3.08, -1.13) over the next 24 months. UPCR-FMV decreased after switching (geometric mean ratio to baseline at month 48: 0.74 [95% CI 0.59, 0.91]). Long-term safety up to 5 years (median treatment duration: 29.9 months) was consistent with the known profile of iptacopan.
sections.conclusion: Long-term treatment with iptacopan led to sustained slowing in eGFR decline and proteinuria reduction that were also observed after switching from placebo. No new safety signals were observed.

items.title: Circulating Immune and Cancer Driver Gene Biomarkers Precede Prostate Cancer Diagnosis by over 10 yr.

sections.objective: Prospective proteomic and proteogenomic studies may enhance the understanding of proteins associated with prostate cancer (PCa) development.
sections.methods: In a case-cohort study within the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition (EPIC), baseline plasma samples from 982 incident PCa cases and 1573 subcohort participants were profiled using the SomaScan 7k platform (over 6000 proteins). Associations were estimated using Prentice-weighted Cox models. The coprimary end points were incident overall PCa and aggressive PCa (n = 290). Findings were evaluated in the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities (ARIC) study and supported by Mendelian randomization (MR) and exome gene-burden analyses.
sections.conclusion: Prospective plasma proteomic analyses identified circulating proteins associated with future PCa risk, including proteins related to immune, adhesion, angiogenesis, and PCa driver-gene pathways. These findings identify candidate protein risk factors for overall and clinically significant PCa, and warrant further validation and mechanistic evaluation.
sections.other: ACP3, FLT4, and KLK3 were associated with overall PCa risk (hazard ratio [HR] per 1 standard deviation [SD] increase were 1.20 [1.10-1.31], 1.26 [1.13-1.40], and 2.28 [1.96-2.65], respectively). Seven proteins were associated with aggressive PCa risk, with ANKRD1 consistently associated across multiple clinically relevant disease subtypes. Twelve proteins were associated with PCa diagnosed >15 yr after blood draw, including ANXA2, GZMK, and OSCAR. ACP3, ANXA2, APOC2, and KLK3 showed consistent associations in both EPIC and ARIC. Additionally, four proteins had support from MR analyses and eight from rare-variant burden tests. Circulating products of established PCa driver genes, including ERBB3, KRAS, and NRAS, were associated with future aggressive disease. Limitations include incomplete external replication and differences in end point availability across cohorts.

items.title: Bacteriophage-derived ectolysin: a promising antimicrobial against fluoroquinolone-resistant MRSA.

sections.objective: Microbial keratitis remains one of the leading causes of blindness globally. With the rising threat of antimicrobial resistance, there is an urgent need for the development of novel antimicrobial agents with innovative mechanisms of action.
sections.results: P128 demonstrated potent antibacterial activity against multidrug resistant S. aureus strains collected from patients with infectious keratitis, with minimum inhibitory concentrations ranging from 0.5 µg/mL to 16 µg/mL. Topical instillation of P128 to an injured cornea did not interfere with the re-epithelialisation rates nor cause any adverse effects. In a rabbit S. aureus keratitis model, P128 showed similar therapeutic efficacy to standard of care antibiotic, gatifloxacin. In a mouse model of fluoroquinolone-resistant methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA) keratitis, P128 decreased the bacterial bioburden as well as corneal oedema. P128 displayed potent synergism with membrane active antimicrobial peptides, and their combination eradicated the preformed 96 hours biofilms.
sections.conclusion: These results demonstrate the therapeutic potential of P128 for the management of drug-resistant MRSA keratitis and its combination with antimicrobial peptides may expand the antimicrobial armamentarium against biofilm-associated infections.
sections.other: Antibacterial properties of P128, a peptidoglycan degrading enzyme derived from bacteriophage K, was determined against multi-drug resistant Staphylococcus aureus clinical strains. P128 was tested for its ocular safety in a rabbit corneal wound healing model. The antibacterial efficacy of P128 was investigated in in vivo rabbit and mouse infectious keratitis models.

items.title: Clinical characteristics and ompA serovar correlation in adult inclusion conjunctivitis: a cohort study in China.

sections.objective: Adult inclusion conjunctivitis (AIC) caused by non-trachomatous Chlamydia trachomatis is often under-recognised due to variable and non-specific clinical features. This study aimed to describe its clinical and laboratory characteristics, ompA serotype distribution, and their association with clinical presentation and outcome.
sections.methods: This retrospective cohort study included 22 patients with laboratory-confirmed AIC diagnosed at a tertiary eye centre between February 2023 and January 2026. Clinical signs were graded using a structured conjunctival scoring system. Diagnosis was based on conjunctival cytology, nucleic acid amplification testing and cell culture. C. trachomatis ompA genotyping was performed by PCR and sequencing with phylogenetic analysis. Patients were classified into serovar D and non-D groups, and clinical severity scores and time to resolution were compared using the Mann-Whitney U test.
sections.results: Patients presented with subacute or chronic conjunctivitis with variable conjunctival hyperaemia, follicular reaction, papillary hypertrophy and discharge. ompA genotyping revealed a heterogeneous serovar distribution, with serovar D predominating. Overall clinical scores at presentation were higher in patients with non-D serovars than in those with serovar D (p<0.05), while only papillary reaction differed among individual signs. Time to clinical resolution after standard antibiotic therapy varied but did not differ significantly between groups.
sections.conclusion: This study provides a clinical and molecular profile of AIC and highlights variability across ompA serotypes. By generating data from a Chinese cohort, it helps address the limited evidence base in this setting and may support improved clinical recognition and future genotype–phenotype research.

items.title: Clade-specific ophthalmic manifestations of mpox: an umbrella review and meta-analysis of systematic reviews.

sections.objective: On 14 August 2024, the WHO redesignated Monkeypox (mpox) as a Public Health Emergency of International Concern. Ocular disease is under-recognised and can cause irreversible vision loss. Clarifying its burden, clade-specific patterns and HIV-related risks is essential for clinical care and public health.
sections.methods: We conducted an umbrella review and meta-analysis, systematically searching PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science and the Cochrane Library from inception to September 2025. Eligible studies were systematic reviews reporting ophthalmic manifestations in laboratory-confirmed mpox cases, stratified by viral clades I, II and IIb. Pooled proportions were estimated using random-effects meta-analysis, with clade-stratified subgroup analyses. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251137180).
sections.results: Five systematic reviews (36 primary studies; 28 139 patients) were included. The pooled proportion of conjunctivitis was 8.9% (95% CI 4.8 to 13.9), highest in clade I (21.9%) and lowest in clade IIb (2.7%). Keratitis (1.5%), eyelid lesions (3.3%), conjunctival lesions (8.4%) and corneal ulceration (3.3%) varied by clade. Visual impairment occurred in 4.5% overall; unilateral (0.9%) and bilateral (0.4%) blindness were reported only with clade I. Across reviews, people living with advanced HIV experienced disproportionately higher rates of severe and persistent ocular complications than HIV-negative individuals.
sections.conclusion: Mpox-related ophthalmic disease can cause substantial—and potentially preventable—visual disability. Clade I infection is associated with a greater burden of ocular complications than clade II—particularly IIb. Improved access to eye health services, early recognition and integration of HIV and mpox care are critical to reducing vision loss, especially in resource-limited settings.

items.title: Cardiac Resynchronization Therapy Using a Conduction System Pacing Defibrillation Lead in Patients Meeting CRT-D Indications: Six-Month Clinical Outcomes Results From the ASCEND CSP Study.

sections.objective: Conduction system pacing (CSP) via left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP) is a physiologic alternative to conventional biventricular (BiV) pacing for cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT), but prospective data using purpose-built implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) leads are limited. The purpose of this study was to evaluate procedural success, defibrillation efficacy, safety, and 6-month clinical outcomes of left bundle branch-optimized cardiac resynchronization therapy (LOT-CRT) delivered with a purpose-built CSP ICD lead and compare outcomes to conventional BiV-CRT.
sections.methods: A total of 52 CRT defibrillator patients (age 66 ± 10 years, 31.4% female, left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) 29.5 ± 6.7%, left bundle branch block [LBBB] 66.7%, QRSd 164.6 ± 25.3 milliseconds, 29.4% ischemic) in the ASCEND CSP IDE (A Stylet-Driven ICD Lead Intended for Conduction System Pacing IDE Study) study underwent attempted implantation of a CSP ICD lead and a coronary sinus lead (LOT-CRT). Implant success, safety and efficacy outcomes, electrocardiographic characteristics, echocardiographic remodeling, heart failure status, patient-reported quality of life, and CRT response were assessed through 6 months. Outcomes were compared with a propensity-matched conventional CRT cohort (BiV-CRT).
sections.results: Implantation succeeded in 98.1% (51 of 52), with LBBAP capture achieved in all (51 of 51). Freedom from CSP lead-related serious adverse device effects through 6 months was 98.1% (95% CI: 87.1%-99.7%). Defibrillation was successful in all tested patients (100%). Compared with baseline, QRS narrowed by 30.4 ms and LVEF increased by 10.4 points (both P < 0.0001), with a CRT response (≥5%) in 71.1% and super-response (≥14.5%) in 34.2%. Compared with matched BiV-CRT patients from the MORE-CRT MPP (MORE response on Cardiac Resynchronization Therapy with MultiPoint Pacing) study, lead-related events were similar (2.0% vs 2.5%; P = 1.0), LVEF increase was greater (10.4 points vs 4.6 points; P = 0.0005) with more responders (≥5%) and super-responders (≥14.5%) (71.1% vs 48.5%; P = 0.0107 and 34.2% vs 7.8%; P < 0.0001, respectively), and more patients improved by clinical composite score (76.5% vs 52.0%; P = 0.0016). Significant improvements were seen with LOT-CRT in both LBBB and non-LBBB patients.
sections.conclusion: LOT-CRT with a dedicated CSP ICD lead achieved high implant success, preserved defibrillation efficacy, and had favorable safety, with greater left ventricular systolic function and clinical improvement than matched conventional CRT, supporting CSP-based CRT defibrillator therapy.

items.title: Payments for ecosystem services and their effects on health and wellbeing: a systematic review.
items.abstract: Payments for ecosystem services, often funded through carbon offsetting, seek to improve environmental conservation and reduce poverty by paying individuals or communities for maintaining the environment. Following previous registration (PROSPERO CRD42024591264), we searched the EconLit, Medline, CAB Abstracts and Global Health (accessed via Web of Science), GreenFILE, and 3ie databases and grey literature. We systematically reviewed quantitative and qualitative studies assessing the effects of payments for ecosystem services on the health or subjective wellbeing of individuals. We assessed risk of bias using Risk of Bias tool for randomised trials 2, Risk Of Bias In Non-randomized Studies-of Interventions, and Critical Appraisal Skills Programme, with certainty assessed using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation. Synthesis without meta-analysis, effect direction plots, and thematic synthesis were conducted. 19 (7·7%) of 5615 screened articles met the inclusion criteria, with very high or high risk of bias in most studies. Two randomised controlled trials, eight natural experiments, and nine qualitative studies were included. The synthesis without meta-analysis and effect direction plots indicated heterogeneous effects, with both beneficial and adverse effects across outcomes. Thematic synthesis suggested that payment for ecosystem services resources were often invested in health care. The reported benefits included perceived gains in happiness and pride linked to conservation activities. However, the participants also reported stress related to conditionalities or delayed payment. Community-level payments compared with individual-level payments appeared more conducive to equitable and positive health outcomes. The effects of payments for ecosystem services on health and subjective wellbeing were highly variable, depending on context and programme design. Available evidence remains scarce and has very low certainty; therefore, robust health evaluations are needed.

items.title: Endometrial ablation plus levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system versus endometrial ablation alone in women with heavy menstrual bleeding in The Netherlands (MIRA2): a multicentre, open-label, randomised, controlled, superiority trial.

sections.objective: Endometrial ablation is an established and effective treatment for women with heavy menstrual bleeding, but many patients require further treatment, with approximately 10% ultimately undergoing a hysterectomy within 2 years. The insertion of a levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system (LNG-IUS) immediately after endometrial ablation might inactivate residual untreated endometrium or prevent its regeneration, thereby preventing recurrent symptoms necessitating a hysterectomy. The aim of the study was to assess whether LNG-IUS insertion immediately after endometrial ablation in women with heavy menstrual bleeding reduced the need for subsequent hysterectomy within 2 years compared with endometrial ablation alone.
sections.methods: This multicentre, open-label, randomised, controlled, superiority trial was conducted in 34 hospitals in the Netherlands. Women younger than 60 years with heavy menstrual bleeding who were eligible for endometrial ablation were included and randomly assigned (1:1) to combined treatment comprising endometrial ablation plus LNG-IUS or to standard care comprising endometrial ablation alone (stratified by dysmenorrhoea and age). Masking was not applied. Endometrial ablation was done using electrical radiofrequency ablation or by transcervical resection of the endometrium. In participants allocated to combined treatment, intrauterine insertion of an LNG-IUS containing a total of 52 mg of levonorgestrel (releasing 20 μg per day in the first year) was done immediately after the ablative procedure. The primary outcome was the incidence of hysterectomy within 2 years, analysed on a modified intention-to-treat basis in all participants with available data. Serious adverse events were systematically assessed at 6 weeks, 12 months, and 24 months after the intervention. This study was registered on the International Clinical Trials Registry Platform (NL-OMON54839) and is complete.
sections.results: Between Nov 19, 2019, and April 5, 2023, 715 participants were randomly assigned to combined treatment (n=359) or endometrial ablation alone (n=356). The median age of all participants was 45 years (IQR 40-48). 42 (6%) participants had missing data for the primary outcome at 2 years of follow-up. A hysterectomy was done in 15 (4%) of 342 participants in the combined treatment group versus 34 (10%) of 331 participants in the endometrial ablation group, corresponding to a relative risk (RR) of 0·43 (95% CI 0·24 to 0·77; p=0·0050), with a risk difference of -0·06 (95% CI -0·10 to -0·02; p=0·0040). Serious adverse events were reported in 27 (8%) of 346 participants in the combined treatment group and 26 (8%) of 327 participants in the endometrial ablation alone group (RR 0·98, 95% CI 0·59-1·65; p=0·94), and there were no treatment-related deaths.
sections.conclusion: The combination of endometrial ablation and LNG-IUS significantly reduced the incidence of hysterectomy compared with endometrial ablation alone. The combined treatment appears to be a safe adjunctive strategy for heavy menstrual bleeding that does not increase the risk of complications.

items.title: Disease-free survival and overall survival after neoadjuvant immunotherapy in mismatch repair-deficient colon cancer in the Netherlands: results of the single-arm, multicentre, phase 2, NICHE-2 trial.

sections.objective: Neoadjuvant immune checkpoint blockade induces high pathological response rates in patients with locally advanced mismatch repair-deficient (dMMR) colon cancer, yet long-term survival outcomes have not been established. Previously, we reported safety (a primary endpoint) and pathological response (a secondary endpoint) data from the NICHE-2 trial. Here, we report the primary efficacy endpoint of 3-year disease-free survival and the exploratory endpoint of 5-year overall survival.
sections.methods: In this single-arm, multicentre, phase 2, NICHE-2 trial, patients with previously untreated, clinical stage 2 or 3, resectable dMMR colon cancer received a single dose of intravenous ipilimumab (1 mg per kg) on day 1, and two doses of intravenous nivolumab (3 mg per kg) on days 1 and 15, followed by surgery in one of the six participating hospitals in the Netherlands. Here, we report the independent primary efficacy endpoint of 3-year disease-free survival (time from surgery until disease recurrence or death from any cause) and the secondary endpoint of circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) analysis. Overall survival (time from study enrolment until death from any cause) is reported as an exploratory post-hoc analysis. All endpoints were assessed in the per-protocol population (patients who met the eligibility criteria and received at least one cycle of therapy). The study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT03026140, and has completed accrual.
sections.results: From July 4, 2017, to July 18, 2022, 123 patients were screened, of whom 115 were treated and 111 were included in the per-protocol population. At the data cutoff (June 19, 2026), the postoperative median follow-up was 58·7 months (IQR 49·0-72·9). The 3-year disease-free survival was 100% (97·5% CI 100-100). After a median follow-up of 60·4 months (IQR 50·6-74·1), calculated from time of study enrolment, the 5-year overall survival was 100% (95% CI 100-100). In patients with available plasma samples, ctDNA was detected in 99 (92%) of 108 patients at baseline, and ctDNA clearance was observed in 44 (45%) of 98 patients after the first cycle in week 2 and in 80 (82%) of 97 patients after the second cycle before surgery. In patients with a pathological near-complete response and complete response, presurgery ctDNA clearance was observed in 19 (70%) of 27 patients and 60 (92%) of 65 patients, respectively. Assessment for minimal residual disease after surgery revealed that all patients were ctDNA negative.
sections.conclusion: In patients with locally advanced dMMR colon cancer, treatment with ipilimumab and nivolumab before surgery resulted in a 3-year disease-free survival and 5-year overall survival of 100%. These findings support neoadjuvant nivolumab plus ipilimumab as a potential standard of care for patients with locally advanced dMMR colon cancer.

items.title: Programmable design of functional proteins from natural language.
items.abstract: Programming biological function-designing bespoke proteins to perform specified molecular tasks-is a foundational goal of molecular engineering. However, current design models remain fundamentally limited1-3: they typically require either natural proteins as starting points for optimization or manual reformulation of functional goals as geometric and sequence-level constraints to guide candidate generation. Here we introduce Pinal, a 16-billion-parameter foundation model that designs candidate proteins from natural-language descriptions of desired function. Trained on 1.7 billion synthetically annotated protein-text pairs, Pinal links functional intent to protein sequence and structure. In computational evaluations, generated candidates combined high predicted foldability with functional-description alignment and sequence diversity, providing a basis for prioritizing experimentally testable designs. We applied Pinal to four distinct design tasks-a fluorescent protein, a polyethylene terephthalate hydrolase, an alcohol dehydrogenase and a metabolic H-protein-and experimentally observed the intended function in each case, including catalytic activity for both designed enzymes. Without iterative experimental optimization, a Pinal-designed H-protein increased product titre by 1.7-fold relative to the corresponding native Escherichia coli H-protein in a multi-enzyme CO2 fixation pathway. These findings support natural language as a high-level interface for candidate generation in protein design, enabling programmable exploration with reduced reliance on manually specified structural or sequence constraints.

items.title: Drought and disease trigger novel interactions among top predators.
items.abstract: Interactions among species are increasingly recognized as key determinants of climate change impacts on ecosystems1-5. However, we know little about how climatic perturbations affect interactions among top vertebrate predators. Here we show that, when an emergent disease caused the decline of shared prey (rabbits), after decades of neutral co-existence a mammalian carnivore (lynx) started to prey heavily on a top predatory raptor (kites). These predation bouts occurred exclusively under drought conditions and when lynx found rabbit remains under the raptor nests, consistent with the removal of a potential competitor. Drought-induced lynx predation depressed lifetime reproductive success and triggered territory abandonment and dispersal by the raptor, suggestive of a new arms race among predators. A reduction in raptor abundance was associated with an increase in an insectivorous bird (a small owl), showing that the new interaction had the potential to reach lower trophic levels. These results underline the importance of diet flexibility and mobility as important mediators of resilience to stressors. In the future, synergistic effects of multiple anthropogenic stressors may reshape the interactions and ecological roles of many apex predators, with potential cascading consequences for whole ecosystems. A key to forecasting the future impact of global change may reside in understanding how behavioural flexibility and interacting keystone species respond to interacting shocks.

items.title: Acetic acid chromoendoscopy for detection of neoplastic Barrett's oesophagus: stepped wedge cluster randomised controlled trial (ACID-trial).

sections.objective: To assess the added value of acetic acid chromoendoscopy (AAC) for the detection of dysplasia and oesophageal adenocarcinoma during Barrett's oesophagus surveillance endoscopies.
sections.methods: Prospective, open label, stepped wedge cluster, randomised trial. Patients undergoing surveillance for Barrett's oesophagus were eligible, excluding those with known or previously treated dysplasia. Hospitals randomly shifted from surveillance without AAC (control) to AAC (intervention), with endoscopists trained before implementation. Targeted biopsies were obtained if lesions were present; random four quadrant biopsies were conducted.
sections.results: 2267 participants were included, of whom 1438 (63%) were allocated to surveillance without AAC and 829 (37%) to surveillance with AAC; AAC was applied in 679 (82%) allocated participants. Overall, neoplasia was diagnosed in 163 (7.2%) participants (111 (4.9%) low grade dysplasia, 30 (1.3%) high grade dysplasia, and 22 (1.0%) oesophageal adenocarcinoma). AAC use did not increase the neoplasia detection rate (7.4% (50/679) with AAC versus 7.1% (113/1588) without AAC; odds ratio 0.97, 95% confidence interval 0.65 to 1.44; adjusted for calendar time and Barrett's oesophagus length). Suspected lesions were detected in 95 (14.0%) participants receiving AAC versus 101 (6.4%) without AAC (P<0.001), but the targeted neoplasia detection rate was not higher (2.1% (14/679) versus 1.8% (29/1588); odds ratio 1.05, 0.49 to 2.24).
sections.conclusion: Use of AAC did not improve detection of neoplasia in patients with Barrett's oesophagus undergoing endoscopic surveillance in routine clinical practice.
sections.other: 18 Dutch community hospitals. The primary endpoint was the neoplasia detection rate, defined as the percentage of participants with low grade dysplasia, high grade dysplasia, and oesophageal adenocarcinoma in any biopsy, confirmed by an experienced gastrointestinal pathologist. The secondary endpoint was the neoplasia detection rate in targeted biopsies.

items.title: Retatrutide Once Weekly for Treatment of Obstructive Sleep Apnea.

sections.objective: Retatrutide, an investigational triple agonist of glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide, glucagon-like peptide 1, and glucagon receptors, may be useful for treating obstructive sleep apnea (OSA).
sections.methods: In two phase 3, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trials nested within larger basket trials of once-weekly subcutaneous retatrutide, we assigned adults with moderate-to-severe OSA and a body-mass index (the weight in kilograms divided by the square of the height in meters) of at least 27, without (TRIUMPH-1-OSA) or with (TRIUMPH-2-OSA) type 2 diabetes, to receive retatrutide (4, 9, or 12 mg) or placebo. The primary end point was the change in the apnea-hypopnea index (AHI, the average number of apneas and hypopneas per hour of sleep) at 80 weeks with 9 mg and 12 mg of retatrutide. For OSA-related end points, a hybrid-treatment estimand was applied, with a hypothetical strategy used for participants who had intercurrent events suggesting treatment failure and a treatment-policy strategy used elsewhere. We also report intention-to-treat (ITT) results.
sections.results: A total of 243 participants underwent randomization in TRIUMPH-1-OSA and 448 in TRIUMPH-2-OSA. The baseline mean AHI was 58.6 and 55.9 events per hour, respectively, and the mean body weight was 119.6 and 115.9 kg. At 80 weeks, the mean changes in the AHI (hybrid-treatment estimand) with retatrutide in TRIUMPH-1-OSA were -22.9 (4 mg), -34.3 (9 mg), and -31.7 (12 mg) events per hour, versus -9.9 with placebo (difference vs. placebo, -13.0 [95% confidence interval {CI}, -23.0 to -3.0], -24.4 [95% CI, -34.1 to -14.7], and -21.9 [95% CI, -32.2 to -11.5], respectively). The changes with retatrutide in TRIUMPH-2-OSA were -19.2 (4 mg), -24.7 (9 mg), and -25.4 (12 mg) events per hour, versus -10.3 with placebo (difference vs. placebo, -8.9 [95% CI, -15.9 to -2.0], -14.4 [95% CI, -21.6 to -7.2], and -15.1 [95% CI, -22.5 to -7.7]). For the ITT estimand, the corresponding differences from placebo were -13.2 (95% CI, -22.6 to -3.9), -24.7 (95% CI, -34.1 to -15.3), and -22.5 (95% CI, -31.9 to -13.1) in TRIUMPH-1-OSA and -8.8 (95% CI, -15.8 to -1.7), -13.9 (95% CI, -21.3 to -6.6), and -15.0 (95% CI, -22.5 to -7.4) in TRIUMPH-2-OSA. The mean percent change in body weight with retatrutide (key secondary end point) was -12.5 to -22.2% in TRIUMPH-1-OSA and -12.1 to -18.5% in TRIUMPH-2-OSA, versus -4.8% and -5.6% with placebo (treatment-regimen estimand). The most common adverse events were gastrointestinal.
sections.conclusion: In adults with OSA and obesity or overweight with or without type 2 diabetes, retatrutide resulted in significantly greater decreases in the AHI than placebo. (Funded by Eli Lilly; TRIUMPH-1 and -2 ClinicalTrials.gov numbers, NCT05929066 and NCT05929079.).

items.title: Hydrus microstent combined with cataract surgery or used alone: cost-utility analysis for UK.

sections.objective: Minimally invasive glaucoma surgery (MIGS) has the potential to become standard of care for patients with primary open angle glaucoma (POAG), whether combined with cataract surgery (CS) or as a standalone procedure. This study provides evidence of cost-effectiveness for Hydrus Microstent for both indications in UK healthcare settings.
sections.methods: A cohort Markov model simulated the natural history of POAG to assess costs and quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) over a 15-year horizon, comparing Hydrus Microstent + CS with CS alone, and Hydrus Microstent to iStent standalone. Patient progression across glaucoma severity health states was modelled using a rate of progression (RoP) derived from 5-year visual field loss data in HORIZON trial (for mild to moderate POAG) and by trial-based annual number of medications from COMPARE trial (for moderate POAG), respectively. Conducted from the public healthcare payer perspective, model inputs were derived from UK publicly available sources and/or publications. Both deterministic and probabilistic analyses (PA) were performed.
sections.results: When compared with CS alone, Hydrus + CS was estimated to generate 0.334 more QALYs but £604 higher costs over the 15-year time horizon. When comparing Hydrus to iStent, Hydrus had £534 in projected savings and generated 0.068 more QALYs. The PA showed that the probability of Hydrus + CS being cost-effective compared to CS alone is 87.6%, and about 71.5% when compared to iStent. The results were consistent across scenario analyses.
sections.conclusion: Hydrus implantation is a cost-effective strategy both in combination with CS (for mild-to-moderate POAG) and as a standalone procedure (for moderate POAG) in UK healthcare settings.

items.title: Artificial intelligence in diabetic retinopathy: From deep learning to foundation models, clinical translation, and real-world deployment.
items.abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) remains a leading cause of preventable vision impairment worldwide, with its burden increasing in parallel with the global diabetes pandemic. As a progressive microvascular disorder with neurovascular unit involvement, DR is driven by retinal ischemia, inflammation, and pathological neovascularization, while diabetic macular edema (DME) continues to represent a principal cause of vision loss. This structured narrative review provides a critical synthesis of advances in diabetic retinopathy diagnosis, retinal imaging, treatment strategies, and artificial intelligence(AI)-enabled screening published from January, 2020, through March, 2026, while selectively incorporating earlier landmark studies to provide clinical and methodological context. We summarize contemporary screening pathways and emerging retinal imaging modalities, including ultra-widefield photography (up to ∼200° field of view), optical coherence tomography (OCT), and OCT angiography, examining how complementary structural and vascular biomarkers are reshaping disease severity assessment and DME characterization. We then review the evolution of AI methodologies, highlighting a transition from task-specific convolutional neural network pipelines toward transformer-based and self-supervised representation learning, including retina-specific foundation models designed to reduce annotation burden and improve robustness and generalizability under domain shift. Beyond algorithmic performance on curated benchmarks, we emphasize key translational requirements for clinical adoption, including model calibration, uncertainty-aware triage, image quality control, and external validation across imaging devices and diverse populations. Recent prospective and implementation studies across diverse healthcare systems demonstrate that the real-world effectiveness of AI-enabled DR screening depends not only on diagnostic accuracy but also on image gradability, clinically appropriate operating thresholds, uncertainty management, external validation, referral capacity, and integration with established care pathways. Evidence from the Asia-Pacific region provides important examples of these implementation challenges in heterogeneous and resource-constrained screening environments. Specific attention is given to the identification and mitigation strategies for fundus pigmentation-related performance disparities and the governance of autonomous versus hybrid human-AI screening models within evolving regulatory frameworks. Finally, we examine emerging work in oculomics for systemic risk stratification and propose a pragmatic clinical readiness framework centered on validation hierarchy, safety monitoring, and workflow integration. Particular emphasis is placed on the translational readiness of foundation models, multimodal retinal intelligence, and emerging technologies for large-scale screening, therapeutic decision-making, and longitudinal disease monitoring.

items.title: Peripheral exudative hemorrhagic chorioretinopathy: A comprehensive review of clinical features, differential diagnosis, pathogenesis-related disease spectra, and management.
items.abstract: Peripheral exudative hemorrhagic chorioretinopathy (PEHCR is a peripheral chorioretinopathy characterized by retinal pigment epithelium detachment with either blood, exudation, or both, and may present with macular hemorrhage, macular exudation, and vitreous hemorrhage. PEHCR exhibits a variety of features on fundus fluorescein angiography, indocyanine green angiography, and ultrasound examinations. The hemorrhagic type PEHCR may greatly resemble malignant melanoma, whereas the exudative type can mimics primary vitreoretinal lymphoma making differential diagnosis of great importance. The pathogenesis may involve choroidal neovascularization. Early studies suggested a link to age-related macular degeneration, while subsequent research has revealed a close association with polypoidal choroidal vasculopathy and pachychoroid disease spectrum. Most cases of PEHCR are self-limiting and may be observed alone. For those complicated by, or at risk of, macular exudation, macular hemorrhage, as well as vitreous hemorrhage, management strategies include intravitreal anti-vascular endothelial growth factor injections, vitrectomy, laser photocoagulation, photodynamic therapy, and cryotherapy.
keywords: Intravitreal anti-vascular endothelial growth factor therapy

items.title: Subretinal fibrosis in neovascular age-related macular degeneration: From clinical features to fibrotic mechanisms and therapeutic opportunities.
items.abstract: Neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD) is a leading cause of irreversible central vision loss worldwide. Although intravitreal anti-vascular endothelial growth factor therapy has substantially improved short-term outcomes, long-term vision is frequently limited by the development of subretinal fibrosis. This progressive scarring process occurs in a substantial proportion of patients and represents a major determinant of permanent visual impairment during long-term follow-up. Subretinal fibrosis arises from a complex interaction among structural injury, inflammatory signaling, and cellular reprogramming. Clinical and imaging characteristics are associated with fibrotic progression. Experimental studies have also provided insights into the underlying biological mechanisms. To organize heterogeneous evidence across clinical, cellular, and experimental studies, this review adopts a dual-axis framework as a working model for subretinal fibrosis in nAMD. The injury-inflammation axis describes processes that establish and maintain a persistent profibrotic microenvironment, whereas the cellular reprogramming axis describes phenotypic transitions of retinal and immune cell types, including epithelial-mesenchymal transition in retinal pigment epithelium cells, macrophage-to-myofibroblast transition, endothelial and pericyte plasticity, and glial remodeling, that may generate or contribute to extracellular matrix -producing effector cell populations. These axes' crosstalk through secretory signaling and matrix-dependent mechanical feedback may contribute to the persistence of fibrotic remodeling. Emerging therapeutic approaches include interventions targeting inflammatory pathways, fibrogenic signaling, and maladaptive cellular reprogramming, including transitions toward mesenchymal and matrix-producing phenotypes, as well as gene-based and bioengineered delivery strategies. This working model may help organize current evidence, identify unresolved causal links, and inform stage-specific therapeutic strategies.

items.title: A GABAergic preoptic-raphe circuit mediates paradoxical coupling of anxiety and social preference after comparative social deficit.
items.abstract: Social disconnection is a major risk factor for anxiety disorders, the most prevalent mental illnesses worldwide, yet its neural substrates remain unclear. Here, we establish a comparative social deficit (CSD) model in adult male mice that induces a paradoxical phenotype of increased anxiety-like behavior together with heightened social preference, a pattern conceptually similar to human loneliness. Mechanistically, CSD increases the excitability of medial preoptic GABAergic (mPOAGad2) neurons, which bidirectionally regulate CSD-induced behavioral changes. Transcriptomic and electrophysiological analyses identify downregulation of the Kv4.3 potassium channel (Kcnd3) as a molecular driver of mPOAGad2 hyperexcitability. Furthermore, mPOAGad2 neurons exert monosynaptic inhibition onto dorsal raphe serotonergic (DRN5-HT) neurons. This inhibitory projection, strengthened by CSD, mediates CSD-induced behavioral effects. These findings define a molecular and circuit mechanism by which social disconnection remodels mPOA-DRN interactions to drive the paradoxical coupling of anxiety and elevated social preference, providing a translational framework for understanding loneliness-related psychiatric vulnerability.

items.title: Approaches to Inferior Vena Cava Reconstruction in the Setting of Leiomyosarcoma.
items.abstract: IntroductionPrimary vascular leiomyosarcomas (PVLs) are rare, aggressive tumors arising from the smooth muscle cells of large veins, most commonly the inferior vena cava (IVC). Fewer than 500 cases have been reported worldwide, and outcomes remain poor without complete surgical resection. Treatment often requires complex venous and multivisceral reconstruction, but data on operative strategies and outcomes remain limited.MethodsWe reviewed four cases of IVC PVL resected at our institution between 2020 and 2023.
