Each case involved a distinct anatomic segment of the IVC, requiring individualized approaches to resection and vascular reconstruction.ResultsPatient 1 underwent infrarenal IVC resection with en bloc removal of bilateral renal veins and right renal artery, followed by complex reconstruction using cryopreserved cadaveric vein grafts to preserve bilateral renal function. Patients 2 and 3 presented with pararenal and suprarenal IVC tumors, respectively, and underwent en bloc resection with patch venoplasty using bovine pericardium, avoiding luminal narrowing and preserving caval flow. Patient 4 had a large pararenal IVC tumor with suprarenal atriocaval extension requiring cardiopulmonary bypass and patch venoplasty. She subsequently developed two recurrences, the second requiring thoracoabdominal exposure and interposition IVC bypass with a biologic tube graft. All patients recovered well postoperatively, with patent reconstructions and preserved organ function on surveillance imaging. At follow-up ranging from 12 months to 3 years, three patients remained disease-free, while one experienced recurrence managed with repeat resection.ConclusionsIVC leiomyosarcomas present unique surgical challenges requiring patient-specific operative strategies. Complete resection with negative margins remains the cornerstone of treatment, with vascular reconstruction essential to preserve renal function and venous return. This series contributes to the limited literature by demonstrating the feasibility of both standard (patch venoplasty) and complex (renal vein preservation, interposition grafting) reconstructions, highlighting the importance of individualized, multidisciplinary operative planning to optimize outcomes.

items.title: OCT to Assess Risk of Progression of Multiple Sclerosis: A Report by the American Academy of Ophthalmology.

sections.objective: To review the current published literature on the utility of OCT of the retina in peripapillary and macular regions to predict or assess risk of disease activity in adult patients with multiple sclerosis (MS) and MS precursors (radiologically isolated syndrome and clinically isolated syndrome).
sections.methods: A literature search of the PubMed database was last performed in September 2025. Articles were limited to original research in the English language that included adult patients. The search yielded 275 articles that were examined in abstract form to exclude reviews, and 71 were reviewed in full text. Twenty-one articles were selected for inclusion in this assessment and were assigned a level of evidence rating by the panel methodologist.
sections.results: Two studies were rated level I, 8 studies were rated level II, and 11 studies were rated level III. Baseline measurements (lower thickness, faster thickness decline, and larger interocular thickness differences) of the peripapillary retinal nerve fiber layer (pRNFL) and macular ganglion cell-inner plexiform layer (GC-IPL) from OCT scans in patients with MS and precursors of MS were associated with future progression of MS as measured by disability, clinical relapses, and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) changes. Multiple variable models support the independent association of OCT metrics and MS progression.
sections.conclusion: Evidence supports the development of OCT-derived pRNFL and macular GC-IPL thickness measurements as biomarkers for future progression of MS in patients with MS or MS precursor syndromes. Future work is needed to improve generalizability by studying demographically heterogeneous cohorts and should include determining the comparability of metrics obtained from different OCT manufacturers' hardware and software. Future research is also needed to guide interpretation of OCT in the context of other predictors of future disease activity such as MRI.
sections.other: Proprietary or commercial disclosure may be found in the Footnotes and Disclosures at the end of this article.

items.title: Prostatic Artery Embolization in a Patient With Bilateral Internal Iliac Artery Occlusions.
items.abstract: Background: Prostatic artery embolization (PAE) is an established treatment for lower urinary tract symptoms due to benign prostatic hyperplasia but can be challenging in complex anatomy. Study Sample: An 86-year-old male with history of abdominal aortic aneurysm repair and aortobifemoral bypass presented with gross hematuria and urinary retention. Imaging and clinical evaluation confirmed BPH-related clot retention as the etiology. Careful review of preprocedural CT angiography revealed occluded bilateral internal iliac arteries, a right aberrant obturator artery (AOA) (corona mortis variant), arising from the inferior epigastric artery, which itself originated from the native right external iliac artery. The AOA supplied the entire prostate, perfusing both lobes and contributing to the contralateral pelvic circulation as well. Cone-beam CT and angiography confirmed the perfusion to both prostatic lobes. PAE was performed by accessing the native common femoral artery and selectively catheterizing the AOA. Embolization of the prostatic parenchyma was completed successfully while preserving flow to adjacent pelvic structures, avoiding non-target embolization. Results: The patient had complete resolution of hematuria and urinary retention and remained catheter-free at 1-year follow-up. Conclusions: This case highlights the importance of pre-procedural evaluation and planning, demonstrating that PAE can be safely and effectively performed even in variant vascular anatomy.

items.title: Symptomatic Superior Vena Cava Lipoma Causing Near-Complete Venous Obstruction: A Case Report and Literature Review.
items.abstract: BackgroundLipomas are common benign mesenchymal tumors; however, intravascular localization is exceedingly rare. Superior vena cava (SVC) involvement represents an exceptional entity, with only a limited number of cases reported in the literature. Intravascular lipomas are frequently detected incidentally but may present with symptoms related to venous obstruction, including superior vena cava syndrome. We report a rare case of SVC-origin intravascular lipoma extending into the right brachiocephalic vein, accompanied by a focused review of previously published upper extremity cases.Case PresentationA 77-year-old male presented with facial and cervical edema, dyspnea exacerbated in the supine position, and distended cervical veins. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography revealed a 5-cm elongated, fat-attenuation mass within the SVC extending into the right brachiocephalic vein, causing near-total (approximately 99%) luminal occlusion. Transthoracic echocardiography supported the diagnosis. The patient underwent surgical resection via median sternotomy under cardiopulmonary bypass. Following longitudinal venotomy of the SVC extending to the brachiocephalic vein, the tumor-adherent to the posterior venous wall-was completely excised with preservation of vascular integrity. Primary venous repair was performed. The diagnosis of lipoma was histopathologically confirmed. The patient initially showed marked symptomatic improvement; however, on postoperative day 5, sudden-onset dyspnea necessitated reintubation, followed by multiorgan failure and death. The precise cause of the acute deterioration could not be definitively established.Literature review identified only 21 previously reported upper extremity intravenous lipomas, with this case representing the 16th involving the SVC and the oldest reported patient.ConclusionUpper extremity intravenous lipomas are rare and may lead to significant venous obstruction. Cross-sectional imaging is essential for diagnosis and surgical planning. In symptomatic patients, complete surgical excision provides definitive treatment and symptom relief. Management of incidentally detected asymptomatic cases remains controversial and should be individualized.

items.title: Tau-induced mitochondrial reverse electron transport drives neurodegeneration.
items.abstract: Hyperphosphorylation and aggregation of tau are pathological hallmarks of tauopathies. Mitochondrial dysfunction is also a common feature of tauopathies. The mechanistic link between tau abnormalities and mitochondrial dysfunction and its relationship to the physiological function of tau, however, is unclear. Here, we demonstrate that tau regulates mitochondrial reverse electron transport (RET), which produces excess reactive oxygen species (ROS), reduces the NAD+/NADH ratio, and is activated by aging or stress. In flies, mice, and human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC)-derived neurons, tau depletion eliminates stress-induced RET and confers resilience. Mechanistically, tau enters mitochondria and directly interacts with the complex I subunit NDUFS3 to promote RET in a phosphorylation-dependent manner. Elevated RET further drives tau hyperphosphorylation, establishing a self-perpetuating pathological loop. Inhibition of RET ameliorates tau toxicity across species. RET regulation thus represents a previously unrecognized normal function of tau that becomes pathological in disease, providing a therapeutic target for various conditions characterized by tau abnormalities and mitochondrial dysfunction.

items.title: Pharmacokinetics and safety of dolutegravir in term neonates exposed to HIV-1 (IMPAACT 2023): a phase 1, open-label, multicentre study.

sections.objective: Safe and effective antiretroviral options are needed for neonates exposed to HIV-1, but data supporting dolutegravir use from birth are scarce. The aim of this study was to evaluate dolutegravir pharmacokinetics, safety, and tolerability in term neonates, and to identify an appropriate dosing regimen.
sections.methods: IMPAACT 2023 was a phase 1, open-label, multicentre study conducted at 15 IMPAACT sites in South Africa, Thailand, and the USA from Oct 5, 2022, to May 22, 2025. Full-term neonates weighing at least 2 kg born to women living with HIV-1 were enrolled between birth and 5 days of life. In cohort 1, infants received two single dolutegravir doses using liquid suspension or 5 mg dispersible tablets. In cohort 2, infants received dolutegravir 5 mg every 48 h until day 14 of life, then every 24 h up to week 4-6 depending on duration of local standard-of-care antiretroviral prophylaxis. In both cohorts, participants were stratified by antepartum maternal dolutegravir exposure. Intensive pharmacokinetic sampling was done around each of the two single doses in cohort 1 and at 7 days post initial dose and at week 4 of life in cohort 2. Safety and tolerability were assessed up to week 16. Primary pharmacokinetic outcomes were the last observed concentration of dolutegravir after each dose and area under the observed single-dose concentration-time curve in cohort 1, and concentration of dolutegravir at the end of the dosing interval (Ctrough) and area under the concentration-time curve over one dosing interval (AUC0-τ) in cohort 2. Pharmacokinetic parameters were estimated by non-compartmental analysis in infants who received the dolutegravir dose under evaluation and had evaluable pharmacokinetic data from intensive sampling. Primary safety outcomes were study drug-related safety failure and safety failure from initial dosing up to 2 weeks after permanent study drug discontinuation. Safety outcomes were assessed in all infants who received at least one dose of dolutegravir and were summarised descriptively. The study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05406583, and is complete.
sections.results: Of 73 screened mother-infant pairs, 48 were enrolled between Oct 5, 2022, and Jan 21, 2025. All 48 infants started the study drug and were safety-evaluable; 41 were pharmacokinetic-evaluable. In cohort 1, concentration-time profiles showed prolonged elimination and wide interindividual variability, with substantial overlap between neonates with and without antepartum maternal dolutegravir exposure. In cohort 2, geometric mean Ctrough and AUC0-τ at the day 7 post initial dose visit were within target ranges. At week 4 of life, geometric mean AUC0-τ remained within target range, whereas Ctrough exceeded the target range but remained acceptable. No infants in either cohort had a study drug-related safety failure during the primary safety window. Safety failure occurred in zero of 18 infants in cohort 1 and four of 30 infants in cohort 2. Two of 48 infants had grade 1-2 adverse events that were considered related to dolutegravir.
sections.conclusion: These findings support dolutegravir as an option from birth for presumptive therapy or early treatment in term infants weighing at least 2 kg.

items.title: Effectiveness of a structured template to improve completeness of reporting randomised trial protocols: randomised controlled trial.

sections.objective: To evaluate whether providing authors with a manuscript template structured according to the Standard Protocol Items: Recommendations for Interventional Trials (SPIRIT) 2025 reporting guideline for use during revision improves the completeness of reporting in randomised trial protocols.
sections.methods: Randomised controlled trial. Handling editors asked the intervention group authors to use a SPIRIT based manuscript template when preparing their first revision. The template included structured subheadings corresponding to SPIRIT 2025 items, along with guidance on reporting. Editorial decisions were not conditional on use of the template. Control group manuscripts underwent standard peer review.
sections.results: Of the 70 manuscripts randomised (35 in each group), all were analysed, with no loss to follow-up. In the intervention group, completeness of reporting in randomised trial protocols improved by 0.61 points (95% confidence interval 0.20 to 1.01) compared with the control group, with mean (standard deviation) scores increasing from 5.42 (1.07) to 6.70 (1.23) and 5.77 (1.19) to 6.32 (0.94), respectively. The largest improvements were observed for recruitment, data collection methods, and access to data. Median time to submission of the first revision was similar between the intervention and control groups (27.10 v 29.86 days, respectively). Data on harms were not systematically collected. Among 14 of 35 survey respondents (40%), many (8/13, 62%) reported the template as time consuming and some (5/13, 39%) as burdensome. Most respondents, however, found it easy to use (10/13, 77%), helpful for improving the manuscript (9/13, 69%), and reassuring for adherence to SPIRIT (13/13, 100%).
sections.conclusion: Providing authors of randomised controlled trials with a SPIRIT based template during manuscript revision modestly improved the completeness of reporting in the trial protocols without extending revision times.
sections.other: BMJ Open. 70 of 74 manuscripts screened between 29 April and 27 May 2025 that reported randomised controlled trial protocols with a decision of minor or major revision after the first round of peer review were randomly allocated (1:1) using an R generated sequence. Authors were not informed of the study. The primary outcome was completeness of reporting score in the revised manuscript (adjusted for baseline), calculated as the mean of 11 SPIRIT items that are frequently inadequately reported (each scored 0, 0.5, or 1) and linearly rescaled to a 0-10 score. After submission of their first revision, authors in the intervention group completed an online survey. The survey included both fixed response and open ended questions designed to capture the authors' perceptions of ease of use, helpfulness, and any challenges encountered when using the template. Secondary outcomes included mean completeness of reporting scores for each item, median time to submission of the revised manuscript, and authors' experiences of using the template. Outcome assessors, but not editors or investigators, were masked.

items.title: Intravascular Lithotripsy of Aortic and Renal Lesions as a Therapeutic Tool for Pickering Syndrome: A Case Report.
items.abstract: We report the case of a 73-year-old woman admitted with Pickering syndrome, a life-threatening condition characterized by recurrent flash pulmonary edema secondary to severe renovascular disease. Computed tomography angiography demonstrated an atrophic left kidney, a heavily calcified visceral aorta with a coral-reef morphology, and a near-occlusive stenosis of the right renal artery. Urgent endovascular treatment was performed with intravascular lithotripsy for plaque modification of the suprarenal aorta and the right renal artery, followed by renal artery stenting. The patient showed prompt clinical recovery, with resolution of pulmonary edema, stabilization of blood pressure, and improvement of renal function. This case illustrates the potential role of intravascular lithotripsy as a minimally invasive adjunct for managing severely calcified aorto-renal disease in high-risk patients, enabling endovascular treatment in otherwise challenging anatomy.

items.title: Efficacy and safety of QY201, an oral dual Janus kinase 1/tyrosine kinase 2 inhibitor, in adults with moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis: a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 2 dose-finding trial.

sections.objective: QY201 is a novel oral Janus kinase 1 and tyrosine kinase 2 inhibitor. To evaluate the efficacy of multiple QY201 doses in moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis (AD), and to inform dose selection for phase 3 studies.
sections.methods: In this phase 2, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 200 adults with moderate-to-severe AD were randomized 1:1:1:1 to receive QY201 (5 mg, 10 mg, or 20 mg twice daily [BID]) or placebo for 12 weeks. The primary endpoint was the proportion of patients achieving ≥75% improvement in Eczema Area and Severity Index (EASI-75) at week 12.
sections.results: EASI-75 response rates at week 12 were 72.9%, 84.7% and 81.4% in the 5 mg BID, 10 mg BID, and 20 mg BID groups, respectively, compared with 18.5% in the placebo group (all P<0.0001). Investigator's Global Assessment response rates were 44.7% (P=0.0011), 64.3% (P<0.0001), and 71.3% (P<0.0001), respectively, versus 12.4% with placebo. Treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 74.0%, 75.5%, and 90.4% of patients receiving QY201, compared to 69.4% with placebo; most were mild or moderate.
sections.conclusion: The phase 2 findings support further evaluation of QY201 at doses of 10 mg BID and 20 mg BID in confirmatory phase 3 trials.
sections.other: Short follow-up and single-country population.

items.title: Peritoneal dialysis induces hepatic metabolic stress as an instigator for systemic inflammation.

sections.objective: Peritoneal dialysis (PD) is a lifesaving therapy in patients with kidney failure, but results in daily intraperitoneal glucose administration corresponding to 50% of the recommended energy intake, most of which enters the portal circulation. As the impact of this glucose exposure on liver and metabolic health remains unclear, we explored hepatic and systemic metabolic effects of PD.
sections.methods: Healthy mice and mice with chronic kidney disease (5/6 nephrectomy C57BL/6 aged 12-14 weeks) underwent seven weeks of PD. Combining morphologic studies, untargeted tissue proteomics, targeted plasma metabolomics and spatial transcriptomics, we assessed hepatic molecular and metabolic effects of PD. Gut- and gut-vascular barriers, systemic and hepatic lipopolysaccharide abundance and zonal transcriptional changes were assessed with multiplexed spatial single-cell analysis and transcriptomics.
sections.results: Intraperitoneally administered glucose during PD was rapidly taken up by the liver and induced hepatic metabolic inflammation. Portal-venous glucose overload bypassing the gastrointestinal tract resulted in increased glucose-to-cholesterol shunting with elevated plasma cholesterol levels, despite the absence of hepatic steatosis or glycogen storage. Increased oxidative stress and endotoxin load were associated with reduced hepatic Kupffer cell numbers without increased gut permeability.
sections.conclusion: Ours study found chronic hepatic metabolic stress induced by PD. Evidence of hepatic glucotoxicity and oxidative stress as instigators for systemic metabolic inflammation induced by PD suggests that similar pathologic mechanisms could also contribute to increased cardiometabolic risk on chronic PD.

items.title: Safety outcomes of semaglutide by chronic kidney disease severity in the FLOW trial.

sections.objective: People with type 2 diabetes (T2D) and chronic kidney disease (CKD) often experience medication intolerance and side effects that worsen with lower estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR). This prespecified secondary analysis assessed the safety of semaglutide by baseline eGFR.
sections.methods: FLOW (NCT03819153) was a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial testing the efficacy of subcutaneous semaglutide 1.0 mg once-weekly on a primary kidney outcome (50% or more eGFR reduction, kidney failure, or death due to kidney or cardiovascular causes) in participants with T2D and CKD. Safety data were collected selectively and included serious adverse events (SAEs), AEs leading to treatment discontinuation, and prespecified AEs of special interest (AESIs). In this descriptive assessment, systematically collected safety data were reported numerically by baseline eGFR.
sections.results: Of 3533 participants, 1767 received semaglutide and 1766 received placebo. Fewer SAEs were reported with semaglutide than placebo across baseline eGFR subgroups (45.1% versus 50.4% in the 60 or more ml/min per 1.73 m2 subgroup, and 56.4% versus 60.4% in the under 30 ml/min per 1.73 m2 subgroup). SAEs related to infections and infestations; cardiac disorders; respiratory, thoracic and mediastinal disorders; and metabolism and nutrition disorders were generally less frequent with semaglutide than placebo, regardless of baseline eGFR. Treatment discontinuations due to AEs were higher with lower baseline eGFR across treatment groups (60 or more ml/min per 1.73 m2: semaglutide 11.2%, placebo 11.3%; under30 ml/min per 66 1.73 m2: semaglutide 18.8%, placebo 18.7%). Discontinuations specifically due to gastrointestinal AEs were reported more frequently with semaglutide (4.5%) than placebo (1.1%), regardless of baseline eGFR. Frequencies of AESI were similar between treatment groups across baseline eGFR subgroups.
sections.conclusion: In this safety assessment, SAEs were reported less frequently with semaglutide than placebo, with corresponding patterns observed for treatment discontinuations and AESIs. No unexpected safety concerns were identified across the spectrum of eGFR represented in the FLOW trial.

items.title: A study using the REIN registry suggests a statin therapy benefits for secondary prevention in patients receiving dialysis.

sections.objective: While statins are effective for cardiovascular prevention in the general population, their benefit in patients with CKD G5D (kidney failure treated by dialysis) remains uncertain. Previous randomized controlled trials included mixed populations for primary and secondary prevention while excluding patients with recent cardiovascular events, leaving a knowledge gap regarding statin effectiveness for secondary prevention immediately following an atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) event. Here, we address this gap by providing real-world evidence.
sections.methods: We conducted a landmark-based observational study, informed by the target trial framework using the French Renal Epidemiology and Information Network (REIN) registry and merged with data from the French national healthcare system database from 2010 to 2023. We included adults with CKD G5D who experienced an ASCVD event. We used inverse probability of treatment weighting to balance baseline characteristics between statin initiators and non-initiators, thereby estimating the average causal effect on all-cause mortality. Results focus on the relative and absolute risk difference and the life expectancy gain using delta restricted mean survival time (dRMST).
sections.results: The study cohort included 5534 patients (median age: 75 years; 67% male). During the ten years of follow-up, statin use was associated with a reduced risk of mortality. The survival curves reached a maximum absolute difference at year four (risk difference -6.2% (95% CI: -10.2; -2.2); relative risk 0.88 [95% CI: 0.81; 0.96]). Life expectancy extended significantly over time with a mean survival gain of 69 days at five years (95% CI: 14-125) and reaching 135 days at ten years (95% CI: 31-239). No difference was identified between groups regarding hospitalizations for rhabdomyolysis or toxic hepatitis.
sections.conclusion: In patients receiving dialysis, statin initiation following an ASCVD event is safe and associated with a modest-to-moderate ten-year cumulative survival benefit. While interpreted within observational limitations, this real-world evidence supports their use in this secondary prevention setting.

items.title: Mastering the eye: Clinical paradigm shifts from optical restoration to genomic correction.
items.abstract: Historically, the main operation for cataract was couching, and the interior of the living eye could not be examined until Hermann von Helmholtz introduced the ophthalmoscope in 1851. Since the mid-twentieth century, seven advances have reshaped ophthalmic care. Harold Ridley implanted the first intraocular lens in 1949, and the ophthalmologist Charles Kelman and the engineer Anton Banko developed phacoemulsification, reported in 1967. Robert Machemer performed the first pars plana vitrectomy in 1970, while David Huang and colleagues described optical coherence tomography in 1991. Endothelial keratoplasty, developed by Gerrit Melles and others between 1998 and 2006, replaced only the failing corneal endothelium instead of the full thickness of the cornea. Anti-VEGF therapy followed the purification of VEGF by Napoleone Ferrara and colleagues in 1989 and the approval of ranibizumab in 2006. Minimally invasive glaucoma surgery has spread since 2012, and in 2017 voretigene neparvovec became the first approved gene therapy for an inherited retinal disease. Five of these advances enabled a new type of intervention, whereas endothelial keratoplasty and minimally invasive glaucoma surgery made existing operations safer. For each advance we summarize the best available evidence of benefit to patients and its certainty, which is high for some, such as anti-VEGF therapy, and low for others, such as the effect of imaging on patient outcomes. Each advance created new burdens, from chronic injections to dependence on donor tissue, and routine adoption depended on manufacturing, regulation, cost, reimbursement, and health-system capacity.

items.title: Joint American Academy of Dermatology-Hidradenitis Suppurativa Foundation guidelines of care for the management of hidradenitis suppurativa.

sections.objective: Hidradenitis suppurativa affects 0.7% to 1.5% of the global population and causes substantial disability and meaningfully impairs quality of life. To provide evidence-based recommendations for the management of hidradenitis suppurativa.
sections.methods: A workgroup conducted a systematic review and applied the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation approach to assess the certainty of evidence and to develop recommendations.
sections.results: This guideline presents 37 evidence-based recommendations. Strong recommendations are made for adalimumab, bimekizumab, infliximab, secukinumab, and routine pain assessment. Conditional recommendations are made for topical clindamycin, resorcinol, and ruxolitinib; oral doxycycline, tetracycline, and clindamycin with rifampin; intravenous ertapenem; spironolactone; short-term systemic corticosteroids; upadacitinib; specific procedural interventions; tobacco cessation; supportive pain management; and zinc supplementation and vitamin D repletion.
sections.conclusion: These guidelines provide evidence-based recommendations for the management of hidradenitis suppurativa.
sections.other: Analysis is limited to best evidence available from systematic review.

items.title: Physiological Left Atrial Staging and the Risk of New-Onset Atrial Fibrillation in Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy.

sections.objective: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is pervasive and an independent driver of stroke and death in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM). Despite guideline recommendations for AF surveillance, effective risk stratification remains elusive, and the hemodynamic and functional states of the left atrium (LA) preceding AF onset remain poorly characterized. We aimed to delineate the hemodynamic and functional states of the LA in HCM, derive a novel LA staging system, and evaluate its prognostic performance for new-onset atrial fibrillation (NOAF).
sections.methods: This multicenter retrospective study included consecutive HCM patients with normal left ventricular systolic function from January 2007 to February 2024 at 2 academic referral centers. Patients with valvular heart disease or prior AF were excluded. Patients were categorized by combining the presence of elevated LA pressure (hemodynamic load) and LA contractile strain (intrinsic LA function): stage 1 (normal LA pressure and function), stage 2 (relative contractile augmentation for a given LA pressure), stage 3 (loss of relative contractile augmentation despite elevated LA pressure), stage 4 (elevated LA pressure with decreased LA contractile strain), and isolated LA contractile dysfunction. The primary outcome was NOAF. External validation was conducted in an independent HCM cohort.
sections.results: Of 1,856 patients screened, 705 were eligible (mean age 57.6 ± 13.0 years, 30.1% female). During a median follow-up of 7.5 years (Q1-Q3: 3.6-11.0 years), NOAF occurred in 101. The staging system was independently associated with a significant, stepwise increase in the risk of NOAF (adjusted HR: 1.83 per increment; 95% CI: 1.42-2.37; P < 0.001) and conferred incremental predictive value beyond established risk models (CHARGE-AF and HCM-AF). Consistent results were demonstrated in 1-year landmark and competing-risk analyses, as well as in an external validation cohort (n = 425; age 59.7 ± 13.5 years, 33.9% female). Importantly, serial echocardiography performed in 217 patients 4 to 6 years after baseline revealed a predominantly unidirectional evolution of the proposed LA stage, with most patients remaining stable (39.6%) or progressing to higher stages or AF (43.8%).
sections.conclusion: The proposed LA staging framework offers mechanistic insights into how the LA adapts to progressive diastolic dysfunction in HCM. It is associated with a graded risk of NOAF and may help tailor AF surveillance strategies.

items.title: Effectiveness of respiratory syncytial virus immunisation in practice.
items.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) affects all ages, with infants and older adults most affected by severe disease. The RSV prevention landscape includes 39 candidates in clinical development, alongside setbacks such as the discontinuation of a promising paediatric live-attenuated vaccine candidate. Several products have been approved, including a maternal vaccine, infant monoclonal antibodies, and vaccines for older adults and adults at high risk. Due to high cost, implementation of these products remains limited to higher-income settings. Real-world evidence confirms high effectiveness, with emerging benefits beyond respiratory disease, including reduced cardiovascular events in older adults. Despite comparable effectiveness of maternal vaccination and monoclonal antibodies, differences in uptake highlight that product availability alone will not ensure population impact. Achieving uptake requires integration into accessible routine care, recommendation by trusted providers, and context-sensitive delivery strategies. This Review summarises RSV preventive products, real-world effectiveness and uptake, and the opportunity of using communication in translating RSV prevention into impact.

items.title: Anatomical Insight Into Idiopathic Ventricular Arrhythmias Originating From the Papillary Muscles.
items.abstract: The papillary muscles (PAMs) are important sites of origin of idiopathic ventricular arrhythmias (VAs). Although catheter ablation of idiopathic PAM VAs has proven to be an effective treatment, these arrhythmias remain challenging compared with other idiopathic VAs despite advances in technologies and techniques. This is related to the unique anatomical challenges of these structures. PAMs are anatomically unique in their location, morphology, histologic composition, and connections with surrounding structures. Electrophysiological studies and catheter ablation of PAM VAs have revealed specific electrocardiographic and electrophysiological characteristics of idiopathic PAM VAs, such as inconsistent precordial transition, discordant QRS axis, multiform VA morphologies, and preferential conduction. Anatomical studies with the aid of imaging modalities, such as intracardiac echocardiography, computed tomography, and cardiac magnetic resonance, have helped define the anatomical background underlying these electrocardiographic and electrophysiological characteristics. This article reviews the unique anatomy of PAMs from an electrophysiological standpoint to better understand the anatomy of the PAMs and thereby improve the outcomes of catheter ablation of idiopathic PAM VAs.

items.title: NON-INVASIVE HemodynamicS of Non-Thrombotic Iliac Vein Lesions ARE DISTURBED IN PATIEnTS with A HiSTORY OF Deep Venous Thrombosis.

sections.objective: Non thrombotic iliac vein lesions (NIVL) are thought to be associated with deep vein thrombosis (DVT), yet most individuals with NIVL never develop thrombotic complications. This study assessed whether ultrasound-derived hemodynamic measurements differ between NIVL patients with and without a history of DVT, and whether these hemodynamic measurements better discriminate DVT history than percent stenosis alone.
sections.methods: We performed a retrospective case-control study of patients evaluated at a tertiary academic referral center between 2022 and 2025 who underwent pelvic venous duplex ultrasound imaging. Patients with left common iliac vein stenoses greater than 20 percent were included and categorized by history of left lower extremity DVT. Exclusion criteria included concurrent DVT or prior venous stenting. Ultrasound images were digitized to obtain vessel diameters and spectral Doppler velocities in the iliac veins. Mean velocity, peak velocity, flow rate, shear rate, and ipsilateral and contralateral ratios were calculated. Continuous variables were compared using Welch t tests, with statistical significance defined as p<0.05.
sections.results: 45 patients were included, comprising 9 with prior DVT and 36 without. Amongst all metrics, velocity-based metrics at the compressed left common iliac vein showed the strongest associations with a history of prior DVT, including ipsilateral velocity ratio (log2 fold change -1.539, p=0.007), peak velocity (log2 fold change -0.999, p=0.002), and mean velocity (log2 fold change -0.989, p=0.002). Differences in percent stenosis were statistically significant but less discriminative than velocity-based metrics (log2 fold change 0.363, p=0.033). Composite metrics such as flow rate and shear rate demonstrated weaker discrimination. Dimensionality reduction analysis revealed distinct clustering based on multivariate hemodynamic features between patients with and without a history of DVT.
sections.conclusion: Among patients with NIVL, decreased velocity through the left common iliac vein at the compression point was the strongest predictor of prior DVT whereas percent stenosis was less discriminative. This study suggests that ultrasound-derived hemodynamic assessment can potentially provide a functional framework for risk stratification in patients with NIVL, but further prospective studies are needed to validate its clinical utility.

items.title: A pilot study of the InVera Infusion Device: Twelve-month outcomes in the treatment of incompetent saphenous veins.

sections.objective: The InVera Infusion Device is a novel catheter designed for the delivery of sclerosant agents during non-thermal, non-tumescent (NTNT) ablation of incompetent superficial truncal veins of the lower extremity. This device pilot study aimed to evaluate the technical success, safety, and 12-month clinical outcome.
sections.methods: A single-center, prospective pilot study enrolled 10 patients with primary symptomatic axial reflux who underwent chemical ablation procedures with sclerosant delivery using the InVera Infusion Device. Primary outcomes assessed were technical procedural success, adverse events, Revised Venous Clinical Severity Score (rVCSS), patient-reported outcomes (PROs) based on a HASTI (Heaviness, Achiness, Swelling, Throbbing, Itching) symptom questionnaire and anatomical success rates from duplex ultrasound examination at baseline, 1 week, 8 weeks, 3, 6, and 12 months post procedure. Baseline and 12 months post procedure were compared for both the rVCSS and the HASTI results using a paired t-test and a Wilcoxon signed-rank test respectively RESULTS: Technical procedural success was 100%. There were no device-related adverse events or serious adverse events including no deep vein thrombosis recorded throughout the follow-up period. Clinician assessed rVCSS and patient reported HASTI scores both showed statistically significant reductions from baseline to 12 months (adjusted p = 0.03 for both). Ultrasound-based anatomical assessment at 12 months demonstrated elimination of abnormal reflux and complete or partial occlusion in 90% of patients.
sections.conclusion: The InVera Infusion device provides a safe and effective technique for the delivery of sclerosant agents as part of the management of incompetent saphenous veins, demonstrating favorable 12-month anatomical, clinical and patient reported outcomes in this pilot cohort.

items.title: Systematic Review of Devices, Designs, and Trials for the Treatment of Deep Venous Reflux.

sections.objective: Chronic venous insufficiency (CVI) is driven primarily by venous reflux and affects nearly one-third of adults. While superficial reflux is effectively treated with ablation, therapeutic options for deep venous reflux (DVR) remain limited. Despite decades of innovation, no prosthetic or bioprosthetic venous valve has achieved U.S. regulatory approval. We systematically reviewed device strategies, clinical and hemodynamic outcomes, complications, and barriers to translation for devices designed to treat DVR.
sections.methods: We conducted a PROSPERO-registered systematic review (CRD420251101761) of six databases from inception through February 2026, including in vivo animal and human studies evaluating prosthetic or bioprosthetic devices for DVR. Studies of native valve repair or autotransplantation were excluded. The primary outcome for human studies was clinical improvement, and secondary outcomes included patency, procedural complications, valvular function, and thrombosis.
sections.results: Of 516 records identified, 15 met inclusion criteria: 8 human and 7 animal studies. Two principal strategies were identified: intraluminal valve restoration (VR) and external compression (EC), with approximately 40% of devices delivered percutaneously or endovenously. In human studies, technical success ranged from 87.7%-100%, patency from 67%-100%, and perioperative complication rates from 0%-44%, consisting primarily of bleeding, wound infection, and valve thrombosis. Valve occlusion occurred in up to 28% of animal implants and 18%-22% of select human cohorts. Two perioperative deaths occurred in animal studies; none were reported in human studies. Among human studies, valve competency assessment methods varied substantially. Reported competency ranged from 0%-92%, reflecting heterogeneity in imaging modalities and definitions. Discordance between anatomic patency, duplex-derived reflux reduction, and clinical improvement was frequently observed. In contemporary multicenter trial data, fewer than half of patients met predefined reflux-reduction endpoints despite high device patency and substantial clinical improvement, highlighting discordance between anatomic, hemodynamic, and patient-centered outcomes. By one year, pain had improved in 75%-97% of patients; rVCSS decreased by 37%-81%, with clinically meaningful (≥3-point) improvement in up to 84.6%; and ulcer healing ranged from 67%-100%. Longer follow-up extended to 2 years in animal studies and up to 11 years in human series with various outcomes reported.
sections.conclusion: Several devices developed for DVR have demonstrated technical feasibility and symptom improvement. However, the risk of thrombosis, the marginal impact on valvular function, and the lack of standardization and selection of adequate endpoints in the measurement of results remain major barriers to regulatory approval. Standardized composite endpoints integrating objective hemodynamic measures with patient-centered outcomes are essential to advance durable DVR device development and clinical translation.

items.title: Nail disorders in pediatric patients: Part 1. Clinical overview, diagnosis and management of physiological variants, and congenital, hereditary, and infectious etiologies.
items.abstract: Nail disorders in children are relatively common and anxiety-provoking for families, yet frequently underrecognized in clinical practice. Many nail disorders in children require no treatment or are readably treatable; however, unfamiliarity may lead to unnecessary, inappropriate, or delayed treatment. In this part 1 of a 2-part continuing medical education series we review physiological variants and congenital, hereditary, and infectious nail disorders, and provide diagnostic and management tips for dermatologists managing these conditions.
keywords: congenital hypertrophy of the nail folds
congenital malalignment of the great toenail

items.title: Psoriasis: Which therapy for which patient, updated, part I. Focus on Psoriasis Comorbidities and Preferred Systemic Agents.
items.abstract: Patients with psoriasis (PsO) may have various comorbidities, that are either related to or unrelated to the disease itself. Selection of the appropriate treatment modality has evolved substantially with the rapid expansion of available options that can be individualized based on patients' comorbidity profiles, extent of disease, prior therapeutic response, and treatment preferences. This first article of a two-part series focuses on selecting systemic therapy for PsO patients with specific inflammatory comorbidities or a history of malignancy.

items.title: Nail disorders in pediatric patients: Part 2. Clinical overview, diagnosis and management of inflammatory, pigmentary, and neoplastic etiologies.
items.abstract: Nail disorders represent a relatively uncommon but diverse group of conditions seen in pediatric patients. Management varies largely by etiology. Some inflammatory nail disorders in children are self-limited, whereas others may lead to permanent nail loss if not recognized and treated early. In addition, certain nail disorders may present differently in children than adults and may suggest increased systemic disease burden. In Part 2 of this two-part continuing medical education series, we review inflammatory, pigmentary, and neoplastic nail disorders in children and propose clinical approach algorithms for pediatric nail psoriasis and longitudinal melanonychia.

items.title: Updated treatment targets in inflammatory bowel disease (STRIDE-III): an initiative of the International Organization for the Study of IBD.
items.abstract: Since Selecting Therapeutic Targets in Inflammatory Bowel Disease-II (STRIDE-II), new evidence has become available across inflammatory and patient-centred outcomes. We aimed to update the STRIDE recommendations for Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis. We searched MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane CENTRAL for studies published after the STRIDE-II search period. Findings were integrated with surveys of International Organization for the Study of IBD (IOIBD) members and paediatric gastroenterologists from the Porto group of the European Society for Paediatric Gastroenterology, Hepatology and Nutrition. Statements were subsequently voted on using a modified Delphi approach; consensus was defined as ≥75% of participants rating a statement 7-10 on a 10-point scale. Of 13 071 records identified in the systematic review, 1018 were included. Surveys were completed by 60 of 79 IOIBD gastroenterologists and 23 of 30 paediatric gastroenterologists in the Porto group. STRIDE-III defines three conceptually distinct categories of treatment targets. Actionable targets include clinical response and remission, which reflect patient priorities, and objective inflammatory targets (C-reactive protein normalisation, faecal calprotectin within target range, and endoscopic remission), supported by interventional evidence demonstrating benefits of target-guided treatment modification. Adjunctive targets (ie, urgency, histological remission in ulcerative colitis, transmural remission in Crohn's disease, and growth) are supported by studies showing association with favourable outcomes and guide treatment optimisation and tighter monitoring but do not necessarily require a change in therapeutic class. Patient-centred targets (ie, disability, fatigue, and quality of life) directly reflect patients' well-being and are impaired in a substantial proportion of patients with inflammatory bowel disease; impairment should prompt assessment of inflammation and alternative causes and management through shared decision-making. Targets are further classified as immediate, short-term, intermediate, and long-term. STRIDE-III also defines treatment-specific times to target achievement, new faecal calprotectin thresholds, and adaptations for resource-limited settings. STRIDE-III distinguishes targets that should prompt treatment change from those that primarily guide optimisation and monitoring, while establishing a separate patient-centred pathway based on shared decision-making. This framework supports consistent, evidence-based treat-to-target care.

items.title: The development of obesity pharmacotherapy: from early challenges and setbacks to recognition by WHO.
items.abstract: Obesity is a chronic, progressive disease associated with disability, increased morbidity, and reduced life expectancy. Global prevalence has risen sharply in recent decades, yet obesity and its treatment-particularly pharmacotherapy -have been highly stigmatised. A legacy of early medications withdrawn over safety concerns, together with poor efficacy, and widespread lack of recognition of obesity as a chronic disease contributed to persistent underuse of obesity pharmacotherapy. This underuse changed in the 2020s with GLP-1 receptor agonists and, later, multiagonist therapies, with their substantially greater efficacy, safety, and disease-modifying benefits compared with older agents. Reflecting this paradigm shift, WHO issued global guidelines and included GLP-1 receptor agonists in the Essential Medicines List, albeit for a narrowly defined population. We take a critical historical perspective, charting the highs and lows of obesity medication development and examining the scientific, regulatory, and societal factors that have slowed or impeded the translation of pharmacological advances into safe, effective, and widely accepted treatments for obesity.

items.title: Addressing threats to future global health-what is the right timeframe?
items.abstract: Our decisions today can support or threaten future human health. Insofar as we protect the planet or invest in fruitful research on pandemic countermeasures, we promote future wellbeing and health, sometimes at the present generation's expense. As we warm the planet, accelerate antibiotic resistance, or consume finite natural resources, we might serve present-day wellbeing or health at the expense of future generations. To decide which such trade-offs are legitimate or advisable, we need to know how to balance the health interests of future generations against each other and against our own. Should concerns for future health be confined to the 21st century as per the stated mission of the Lancet Commission on 21st century global threats to health? If not, how far into the future should they extend, and why? Population ethics is a branch of ethics that considers future populations' wellbeing. This Review, a part of the Lancet Commission on 21st century global threats to health, applies general insights from population ethics to future populations' health, and shows why that application is more complex than meets the eye.

items.title: 8 weeks versus 12 weeks of sofosbuvir-velpatasvir for treatment-naive, non-cirrhotic, chronic hepatitis C (RESOLVE): a multicentre, open-label, non-inferiority, randomised controlled trial in India.

sections.objective: Chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection without cirrhosis can be treated with 12 weeks of sofosbuvir-velpatasvir combination therapy. We aimed to assess whether a shorter 8-week treatment regimen of this combination was non-inferior to the standard 12-week regimen in successfully clearing HCV infection in HCV-infected patients without evidence of cirrhosis.
sections.methods: RESOLVE was a multicentre, open-label, non-inferiority, randomised controlled trial, conducted in five publicly funded hospitals in India. We randomly assigned (1:1) treatment-naive adults (aged ≥18 years) with non-cirrhotic HCV mono-infection to receive sofosbuvir 400 mg and velpatasvir 100 mg (orally, daily) for either 8 weeks or 12 weeks. The primary outcome was the proportion of participants with sustained virological response-ie, absence of quantifiable HCV RNA at 12 weeks after treatment completion (SVR12), with 95% assumed proportion with 12-week treatment, 5% non-inferiority margin, 2·5% one-sided alpha error, and 90% study power in the per-protocol population. The trial was registered with the Clinical Trial Registry of India, CTRI/2022/03/041368, and is complete.
sections.results: Between May 15, 2022, and Sept 10, 2024, we screened 1620 participants, of whom 880 (54·3%) were enrolled in the study and randomly assigned to the 12-week (n=437 [50%]) or 8-week (n=443 [50%]) groups. 455 (52%) participants were women, 425 (48%) were men, and the median age was 35 years (IQR 28 to 47). 816 (93%) participants completed the intended 12-week (401 [92%] of 437) or 8-week (415 [94%] of 443) treatment and SVR12 testing. On per-protocol analysis, the proportion reaching SVR12 with 8-week treatment (410/415; 98·8% [95% CI 97·2 to 99·6]) was non-inferior to 12-week treatment (397/401; 99·0% [97·5 to 99·7]), with a risk difference of 0·2% (-1·5 to 1·9). Further, on intention-to-treat analysis, the proportion of participants reaching SVR12 with 8-week treatment (414/443; 93·5% [90·9 to 95·5]) was non-inferior to 12-week treatment (401/437; 91·8% [88·8 to 94·2]) with a risk difference of -1·7% (-5·2 to 1·9). No participant had any drug-related serious adverse event or drug discontinuation due to an adverse event.
sections.conclusion: An 8-week regimen of sofosbuvir-velpatasvir was similar in efficacy to the standard 12-week treatment in individuals with chronic HCV infection without cirrhosis. This finding supports shortening the duration of treatment in such patients.

items.title: Cardiovascular safety of orforglipron versus insulin glargine in adults with type 2 diabetes at increased cardiovascular risk (ACHIEVE-4): a phase 3, event-driven, randomised, open-label, non-inferiority, active comparator trial.

sections.objective: Orforglipron is an oral, non-peptide GLP-1 receptor agonist. While some peptide GLP-1 receptor agonists have established cardiovascular benefit, the cardiovascular safety of non-peptide GLP-1 receptor agonists has not been studied. This study aimed to compare the effect of orforglipron with insulin glargine on the incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events in individuals with type 2 diabetes and obesity or overweight who are at increased risk for cardiovascular events.
sections.methods: This event-driven, phase 3, multicentre, randomised, open-label, active comparator, parallel-group study was conducted in 317 sites across 16 countries and territories. Adults with type 2 diabetes at increased cardiovascular risk with glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c) concentrations between 7·0% and 10·5% (53-91 mmol/mol) and a BMI of 25 kg/m2 or more, treated with up to three glucose-lowering medications (metformin, a sulfonylurea, and/or an SGLT2 inhibitor), were randomly assigned (1:1) to oral orforglipron maximum tolerated dose (up to 36 mg capsule [equivalent to 17·2 mg tablet]) or injectable titrated insulin glargine, each administered once daily. All participants had established cardiovascular or chronic kidney disease. The primary outcome was time to occurrence of four-component major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE-4), including cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, non-fatal stroke, or hospitalisation for unstable angina. Non-inferiority of orforglipron to insulin glargine was declared if the upper limit of the two-sided 95% CI for the hazard ratio (HR; orforglipron vs insulin glargine) was less than 1·8. The primary endpoint and other safety endpoints were assessed in all participants who took at least one dose of assigned treatment using all datapoints from baseline until withdrawal or study completion, regardless of treatment adherence. This trial was registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05803421) and is completed.
sections.results: Between May 1, 2023, and Sept 5, 2024, 2749 participants were randomly assigned (1371 to orforglipron and 1378 to insulin glargine). 1032 (38%) participants were female and 1717 (62·5%) male. 2362 (85·9%) participants had established cardiovascular disease and 1033 (37·6%) had chronic kidney disease. Mean baseline age, HbA1c, and BMI were 63·1 years (SD 9·9), 8·2% (1·0), and 33 kg/m2 (6·2), respectively. Over a median follow-up of 2 years, the primary outcome occurred in 57 (4·2%) of 1358 orforglipron participants and 67 (5·0%) of 1343 insulin glargine participants, showing non-inferiority to insulin glargine for MACE-4 (HR 0·84; 95% CI 0·59-1·20; p<0·0001 for non-inferiority). Gastrointestinal adverse events were reported in 851 (62·1%) of 1371 orforglipron participants and 193 (14·2%) of 1355 insulin glargine participants; clinically significant or severe hypoglycaemia (glucose <3 mmol/L [54 mg/dL]) occurred in 93 (6·8%) of 1371 orforglipron participants and 260 (19·2%) of 1355 insulin glargine participants. 62 deaths were reported during the study: 19 (1·4%) of 1371 participants receiving orforglipron and 43 (3·2%) of 1355 participants receiving insulin glargine; all deaths except one (in the insulin glargine group) were deemed unrelated to treatment.
sections.conclusion: In people with type 2 diabetes at increased cardiovascular risk, the cardiovascular safety of orforglipron was confirmed by demonstrating non-inferiority to insulin glargine for MACE-4. Gastrointestinal adverse events were the most frequent adverse event and most common reason for orforglipron treatment discontinuation with orforglipron, while clinically significant hypoglycaemia occurred less frequently with orforglipron than with insulin glargine. These findings support orforglipron as a potential once-daily, oral treatment option with established cardiovascular safety in people with type 2 diabetes and increased cardiovascular risk.

items.title: Efficacy and safety of garetosmab, an activin A-blocking antibody, in fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (OPTIMA): a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial.

sections.objective: Fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP) is an ultrarare genetic disorder resulting in progressive heterotopic ossification of ligaments, tendons, and muscles, leading to disability and early mortality. FOP is caused by heterozygous gain-of-function mutations in the activin receptor type 1A, allowing this receptor to be aberrantly activated by activin A (ActA), which normally inhibits this receptor, thus driving heterotopic bone formation. In preclinical models and an earlier phase 2 trial (LUMINA-1) in FOP, an antibody blocking ActA (garetosmab) prevented heterotopic ossification. We aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of garetosmab in adults living with FOP.
sections.methods: OPTIMA is a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial conducted at 18 study sites across 16 countries and regions. Participants aged 18 years or older with FOP were randomly assigned (1:1:1) to monthly intravenous placebo, garetosmab 3 mg/kg, or garetosmab 10 mg/kg. Randomisation was stratified by baseline Cumulative Analogue Joint Involvement Scale score and previous participation in the LUMINA-1 study. The primary efficacy and safety endpoints were total number of new heterotopic bone lesions at week 56 and treatment-emergent adverse events of special interest (AESIs) through week 56, analysed in all randomised participants who received at least one dose of the study drug. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05394116); the trial is active (completed primary endpoint) but not recruiting participants.
sections.results: Between Nov 21, 2022, and July 4, 2024, 63 participants were enrolled and randomly assigned (placebo, n=21; garetosmab 3 mg/kg, n=19; garetosmab 10 mg/kg, n=23). The mean age was 26·6 years (SD 6·8); 38 (60%) participants were female and 25 (40%) male. 62 participants completed 56 weeks of treatment; one participant in the placebo group discontinued at 53 weeks. The total number of new heterotopic bone lesions was significantly lower with garetosmab: there were 19 lesions with placebo versus one lesion with garetosmab 3 mg/kg (rate ratio vs placebo: 0·06 [95% CI 0·00-0·73]; p=0·027) and two lesions with garetosmab 10 mg/kg (rate ratio vs placebo: 0·10 [0·01-0·76]; p=0·026). Treatment-emergent AESIs occurred in one (5%) of 21 participants receiving placebo, zero of 19 receiving garetosmab 3 mg/kg, and four (17%) of 23 receiving garetosmab 10 mg/kg; all were considered treatment-related. No deaths occurred.
sections.conclusion: Garetosmab substantially reduced the number of new heterotopic bone lesions, providing robust evidence of its potential to be an efficacious and generally well tolerated disease-modifying therapy for FOP.

items.title: Artificial intelligence (AI) and the choroidal challenge: A comprehensive review of AI applications in choroidal imaging.
items.abstract: The choroid is a densely vascular layer that sustains the outer retina and may reflect systemic microvascular health. With the advent of new imaging techniques, choroidal imaging has become increasingly detailed, generating vast data volumes. Conventional analytic tools often fall short in managing these high-dimensional datasets. Artificial intelligence (AI) automatically enhances, segments, and analyzes choroidal images, facilitating the discovery of choroidal biomarkers relevant to ocular and systemic disease. Yet, anatomical complexity, heterogeneous protocols, and a lack of large, annotated datasets hinder AI adoption. Overcoming these barriers is essential to assess AI-derived choroidal biomarkers as reliable diagnostic and prognostic tools.

items.title: Midterm Outcomes of the Minos Ultralow Profile Endograft: Results from the Multicentre MINER Registry.

sections.objective: The aim of this study was to assess midterm outcomes of the ultralow profile Minos endograft in a physician initiated registry.
sections.methods: A non-sponsored registry collected consecutive patients treated with the Minos device in 20 Italian centres (2021 - 2025). Elective patients (the primary analysis population) were stratified by access quality (hostile vs. standard access); hostile iliac-femoral access was defined by a narrowest iliac diameter 1.6, aortic bifurcation diameter < 16 mm, or severe circumferential calcification. Proximal neck features were covariates only; urgent and emergent procedures were analysed separately. Outcomes were thirty day technical success, mortality, and major adverse events (MAEs), and midterm freedom from rupture, limb occlusion, type I or III endoleak, and re-intervention.
sections.results: Of 310 patients (mean aneurysm diameter 54.8 ± 10.0 mm), 288 (92.9%) were elective. Among these, 154 (53.5%) had a standard access and 134 (46.5%) a hostile access. The latter were more frequently women (16.4% vs. 6.0%; p = .009) and more frequently had peripheral arterial disease (31.6% vs. 16.8%; p = .006). Elective technical success was 100%, with no thirty day deaths. The thirty day MAE rate was higher with hostile access (8.2% vs. 1.3%; p = .032), mainly from access related events and blood loss > 1 000 mL (3.7% vs. 0.0%; p = .021), as was early re-intervention (3.7% vs. 0.0%; p = .021). At 3 years there were no aneurysm related deaths; freedom from limb occlusion was 97% vs. 100% (p = .025) and from type I OR III endoleak was 98% vs. 100% (p = .18) in the standard and hostile access groups, respectively.
sections.conclusion: The Minos ultralow profile endograft was safe and effective for the treatment of elective abdominal aortic aneurysms. Peri-operative morbidity was higher when the iliac-femoral access was hostile, and limb occlusion, type I - III endoleak, and re-intervention were more evident compared with standard access anatomy. An ultralow profile platform can extend endovascular repair to unfavourable access vessels without affecting midterm device performance.

items.title: Cilostazol and Risk of Major Adverse Limb and Cardiovascular Events after Revascularisation for Peripheral Artery Disease.

sections.objective: Patients with peripheral artery disease (PAD) remain at high risk of major adverse limb events (MALE) and cardiovascular events (MACE) after revascularisation. Cilostazol, a phosphodiesterase-3 inhibitor with antiplatelet and antiproliferative effects, reduces re-stenosis but its real world impact on clinical outcomes is uncertain. This retrospective, nationwide, propensity score matched cohort study evaluated the effectiveness and safety of cilostazol on MALE, MACE, and all cause mortality after lower limb revascularisation for PAD.
sections.methods: Using the Taiwan National Health Insurance Research Database, patients who underwent lower limb revascularisation for PAD from 2010 - 2023, with follow up through 2024 were identified. Patients with prior cilostazol use were excluded. 1:1 propensity score matching (n = 5 464 per group) adjusted for baseline differences. Cox regression and Fine-Gray competing risk models were used to evaluate outcomes. The comparison reflects cilostazol used with or without background antithrombotic therapy.
sections.results: Cilostazol use was associated with significantly lower risks of MALE (78.7 vs. 154.0 events/1 000 person-years; subdistribution hazard ratio [SHR] 0.50; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.46 - 0.53) and MACE (97.9 vs. 117.1 events/1 000 person-years; hazard ratio [HR] 0.84; 95% CI 0.79 - 0.89). All cause mortality was also reduced (116.0 vs. 127.6 events/1 000 person-years; HR 0.91; 95% CI 0.86 - 0.96). Major bleeding did not differ significantly between groups (SHR 0.90; 95% CI 0.81 - 1.00), although the absolute rate was high in both groups (12.1% vs. 13.1%). Subgroup analysis showed greater limb benefit in patients not on other antiplatelet agents.
sections.conclusion: Cilostazol after PAD revascularisation was associated with lower risks of limb and cardiovascular events and mortality. These effects were observed without any increase in the rate of major bleeding, although this rate was high in both groups. Randomised trials focused on cardiovascular events are needed.

items.title: Differences in Clinical Presentation of Chronic Pelvic Pain Caused by Iliac Vein Obstruction Impacts Referral Pathway, Time to Diagnosis, and Post-stenting Pain Resolution.

sections.objective: Iliac venous stenting improves chronic pelvic pain (CPP) caused by iliac vein obstruction (IVO). Signs and symptoms vary, but this pain is reproducible and easily identifiable. However, patients can experience significant delays in diagnosis and treatment. This study aimed to determine associations between the referral history, clinical presentation, pain characteristics, and stenting outcomes among women with CPP due to IVO.
sections.methods: This was a retrospective analysis of prospectively collected data of women who were referred to a vascular surgeon with signs and symptoms of IVO, including CPP, and who underwent iliac venous stenting. Associations between clinical presentation (signs, symptoms, pain severity), medical and referral history, and stenting outcomes were compared between three patient groups based on number of other specialist consultations prior to stenting (none, one, or at least two).
sections.results: Data were for 113 women (46.5 ± 15.7 years) who had CPP for 6.3 ± 6.6 years with initial severity of 6.7 ± 2.3 (out of 10). CPP was reproducible for all women, with exercise, standing, and intercourse being the most common triggers. More than two thirds had lower limb pain, oedema, and varicose veins. At a median of 7 years post-stenting, the latest pain score was 0.8 ± 1.6, and approximately 80% had full pain resolution. Women who had seen at least two other specialists had the worst initial pelvic pain, the most prescription pain medication, back pain, other abdominopelvic signs and symptoms, and previous interventions, and the fewest varicose veins. These women had 8.5 ± 7.9 years to diagnosis, but 99% still had significant improvement in, and 66% had full resolution of, their pelvic pain.
sections.conclusion: All patients had a reproducible pattern of venous origin pelvic pain, but those with worse CPP, more abdominopelvic symptoms, and less varicose veins had a more complex and delayed referral pathway and the lowest pain resolution.

items.title: Thyroid hormone receptor-β agonist simedeutirom (HSK31679) for Chinese patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis: a 52-week, multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 2b trial.

sections.objective: Simedeutirom is a selective thyroid hormone receptor-β agonist that has previously been shown to reduce hepatic fat content in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease. We assessed the efficacy and safety of simedeutirom in patients of Asian descent with biopsy-confirmed metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) and F2 or F3 fibrosis.
sections.methods: This multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 2b trial was conducted at 42 clinical sites in China. Adults (aged 18-74 years) with biopsy-confirmed MASH, a non-alcoholic fatty liver disease activity score (NAS) of at least 4, F2 or F3 fibrosis, and MRI-proton density fat fraction liver fat content of at least 8% were randomly assigned (1:1:1) by block randomisation (block size of six; no stratification) via a centralised web-based system to receive once-daily simedeutirom 80 mg, simedeutirom 160 mg, or placebo for 52 weeks. Participants and study personnel were masked to treatment assignment. The primary endpoint was MASH improvement (ie, two-point or more reduction in NAS, one-point or more improvement in hepatocellular ballooning, and no increase in steatosis score) without worsening of fibrosis (ie, no increase in fibrosis stage) at week 52. Efficacy was analysed in the full analysis set, which included all randomly assigned participants who received at least one dose and had at least one efficacy assessment after baseline; participants without liver biopsy data after treatment or who used prohibited medications affecting efficacy were considered non-responders. The trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06168383) and is complete.
sections.results: Between Jan 5, 2024, and Jan 16, 2026, 186 participants were randomly assigned (62 per group). In the full analysis set (n=179), the median age was 42·0 years (IQR 35·0-54·0), 116 (65%) participants were men, and 63 (35%) were women. 22 (37%) of 59 participants in the 80 mg group, 18 (30%) of 60 in the 160 mg group, and six (10%) of 60 in the placebo group had MASH improvement without worsening of fibrosis at week 52. ORs versus placebo were 4·87 (95% CI 1·76-13·48; p=0·0023) in the 80 mg group and 5·24 (1·74-15·72; p=0·0032) in the 160 mg group, with absolute differences of 27·3 percentage points (95% CI 12·2-41·1) and 20·0 percentage points (5·7-33·6), respectively. Grade 3 treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in three (5%) of 61 participants in the simedeutirom 80 mg group, five (8%) of 62 in the simedeutirom 160 mg group, and three (5%) of 62 in the placebo group; no individual grade 3 event affected more than one participant, and no grade 4-5 treatment-emergent adverse events occurred. Serious adverse events occurred in three (5%) participants in the simedeutirom 80 mg group, four (6%) in the simedeutirom 160 mg group, and three (5%) in the placebo group; none were treatment related. No deaths or adverse events leading to treatment discontinuation occurred.
sections.conclusion: Simedeutirom led to higher rates of MASH improvement without worsening of fibrosis than placebo after 52 weeks, warranting further investigation in phase 3 trials.

items.title: Prevalence, management, and outcomes of urinary tract infections in older adults living in care homes versus older adults living outside care homes in the UK: a propensity score-matched case-control analysis.

sections.objective: Globally, rising drug-resistant urinary tract infections (UTIs) affect older populations disproportionally. We aimed to assess the incidence, management, and patient outcomes of UTIs in English care homes.
sections.methods: Using linked primary, secondary, social care, and pathology data covering 2·5 million patients in London between 2018 and 2023, we matched older adults with UTIs living in care homes with older adults living outside care homes using propensity scores. We performed a time-series analysis of incidence and compared urine culture turnaround time and results (including antimicrobial resistance). We assessed UTI-related patient outcomes, including death, complications, recurrent infection, and antibiotic re-prescription within 60 days, using generalised estimating equations, adjusted for demographic and other risk factors.
sections.results: We identified 91 501 UTI cases, including 6648 (7·3%) in care homes. In care homes, 4678 (70·4%) of the 6448 UTIs occurred in women and 3779 (56·8%) involved individuals aged 85 years or older. The older adults living in care homes were older (median age: 86 years [IQR 80-91] vs 76 years [71-83]) and more frequently White (70·3% vs 56·7%) than older adults living outside care homes. The incidence rate of community-acquired UTIs was 1909·4 per 100 000 person-months in care homes (increasing by 3·7 [95% CI 0·8-6·6] per month), as compared with 543·5 outside care homes (decreasing by 1·3 [-1·8 to -0·7] per month). Urine cultures were used less (1366 [20·5%] of 6648 [95% CI 19·6-21·5] vs 24 699 [29·1%] of 84 853 [28·8-29·4]), were more likely to be polymicrobial (suggesting contamination; 416 [30·4%] of 1366 [28·1-32·9] vs 4325 [17·5%] of 24 699 [17·0-18·0]), and had a longer turnaround time (52·9% turnaround in 1 day [50·3-55·6] vs 66·2% [65·6-66·8]) in care homes than outside care homes. Escherichia coli UTIs had higher resistance to trimethoprim (46·4% [95% CI 41·0-51·9] vs 32·0% [30·9-33·1]) and nitrofurantoin (7·5% [4·9-10·8] vs 2·4% [2·0-2·8]) in care homes than outside care homes. Care home cases had significantly worse 60-day outcomes, with higher risk of death (1·99 [95% CI 1·67-2·36]; p<0·001), presenting to general practitioners (1·38 [1·01-1·89]; p=0·042) and to hospitals (1·15 [1·01-1·32]; p=0·041) with complications, recurrent infections (1·22 [1·08-1·36]; p=0·001), and antibiotic re-prescription (1·11 [1·01-1·21]; p=0·024).
sections.conclusion: Older adults residing in care homes had higher UTI infection burden and worse clinical outcomes than matched older adults residing outside care homes. Possible explanatory factors include inadequate care, discordant prescribing decisions, and disconnect with diagnostic capabilities, in addition to the exacerbating effects on infection management during the COVID-19 pandemic. These findings highlight the need for improvement in infection management in care home settings.

items.title: Patient-Level Perivascular Adipose Tissue Density Aggregation and Plaque Progression: Plaque-Free vs Plaque-Adjacent Segments.

sections.objective: Perivascular adipose tissue (PVAT) density on coronary computed tomography angiography (CTA) reflects pericoronary inflammation, but measurements adjacent to existing plaques may be confounded by local inflammatory signaling from the plaque itself-a form of reverse causation. Whether systematically comparing patient-level PVAT aggregation approaches (including measurements restricted to plaque-free segments) can identify a more robust inflammatory biomarker has not been evaluated. The authors aimed to compare the predictive performance of 4 patient-level PVAT aggregation approaches for coronary plaque progression.
sections.methods: From the PARADIGM serial coronary CTA registry, 412 patients with baseline coronary plaque who underwent serial coronary CTA at identical tube voltages were included (mean age: 61.1 ± 9.3 years; 61.7% male; mean interval: 3.2 ± 1.2 years). Four patient-level PVAT measures were compared: proximal right coronary artery (pRCA), whole-coronary, plaque-free, and plaque PVAT. Multivariable regression models were constructed for annualized plaque volume (PV) progression with adjustment for clinical risk factors and imaging covariates.
sections.results: Annualized increases in pRCA PVAT (β = 0.804; P = 0.033), whole-coronary PVAT (β = 1.142; P = 0.022), and plaque-free PVAT (β = 1.419; P = 0.007) were each independently associated with total PV progression, whereas plaque PVAT did not reach significance (β = 0.755; P = 0.083). For noncalcified PV progression, plaque-free PVAT was the only significant measure (β = 1.086; P = 0.026). None of the 4 baseline PVAT measures were significantly associated with plaque progression (all P > 0.50). Pairwise comparisons revealed no significant differences among the 4 measures.
sections.conclusion: Changes in pRCA, whole-coronary, and plaque-free PVAT were each independently associated with total PV progression. For noncalcified PV progression, plaque-free PVAT change was the only significant measure. (Progression of AtheRosclerotic PlAque DetermIned by Computed TomoGraphic Angiography Imaging [PARADIGM]; NCT02803411).
